p: [כו] מִשְׁמוֹר ג': תִּינוֹק יוֹנֵק וְאִשָּׁה מְסַפֶּרֶת. שְׁנֵיהֶם יַחַד זֶהוּ רַק בְּמִשְׁמָר ג' שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כֻּלָּם נֵיעוֹרִים בִּזְמַן אֶחָד.
During the third watch an infant nurses and a woman converses with her husband. Both occurring together happens only in the third watch, when everyone awakens at the same time.
וְכֵן בַּנִּמְשָׁל: יְנִיקַת תִּינוֹק מִשְּׁדֵי אִמּוֹ הַתּוֹרָה כַּאֲשֶׁר אִשָּׁה מְסַפֶּרֶת, וְיִהְיֶה גַּם הָאָב
And so too in the spiritual metaphor: the nursing of the child from the breasts of his mother, the Torah, takes place when the woman converses, so that the Father as well
[הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כֵּיצַד מְבָרְכִין]
the Holy One, blessed be He, as stated at the beginning of the chapter Keitzad Mevarkhin (Berakhot 35b)
מִשְׁתַּעֲשֵׁעַ בִּינִיקַת הַתִּינוֹק, זֶהוּ רַק בְּמִשְׁמוֹר ג' שֶׁכְּבָר שָׁלֵם בַּמַּעֲשִׂים וּבַעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב.
delights in the nursing of the child, which occurs solely in the third watch, when one has already reached perfection in physical deeds and in the interior service of the heart.
וְהִנֵּה בַּמַּעֲשֶׂה הִקְדִּים תִּינוֹק יוֹנֵק, שֶׁהוּא הַמְּעוֹרֵר קוֹדֶם לָאֵם, וְהִיא מְעוֹרֶרֶת לַבַּעַל.
Now in practical reality, the text placed the nursing infant first, for he awakens the mother first, and she in turn arouses the husband.

אֲבָל לְהַלָּן בִּשְׁמִיעָה לַאֲחֵרִים, לְמַאן דְּגָנֵי וְכוּלֵי, אָמַר לְהֵיפֶךְ: "אִשָּׁה מְסַפֶּרֶת", שֶׁקּוֹלָם נִשְׁמָע וְשׁוֹמֵעַ קוֹדֶם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁמַּטֶּה אָזְנוֹ שָׁמַע קוֹל תִּינוֹק יוֹנֵק.

But further on regarding hearing by outside observers—for one sleeping in a dark room—it stated the reverse: "a woman converses," because their spoken voice carries far and is heard first, and only afterward, when leaning his ear, does he detect the soft sound of the nursing infant.
וְהַנִּמְשָׁל: יְנִיקַת תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן מִשְּׁדֵי אִמָּם
And the spiritual parallel: the suckling of school children from the breasts of their mother
[כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כֵּיצַד מְבָרְכִין],
the Congregation of Israel, as stated at the beginning of the chapter Keitzad Mevarkhin (Berakhot 35b),
רָאשֵׁי הַדּוֹר, וְהֵם אָז מְסַפְּרִים כְּבוֹד אֵל וּשְׁכִינָה מְדַבֶּרֶת מִתּוֹךְ גְּרוֹנָם
namely the leaders of the generation, who at that hour recount the glory of God while the Shechinah speaks through their throat
[וְזֶהוּ בְּמִשְׁמוֹר ג' שֶׁל גָּלוּת הַדּוֹמֶה לְלַיְלָה].
and this corresponds to the third watch of the exile, which is likened to night.
בֶּאֱמֶת תִּינוֹק יוֹנֵק קוֹדֶם,
In essential reality, the infant suckling precedes;
רַק לְהַרְגָּשַׁת עֵין בְּנֵי אָדָם אִשָּׁה מְסַפֶּרֶת קוֹדֶם.
yet to the outward perception of human eyes, the woman conversing appears first.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר תּוֹלְדוֹת יַעֲקֹב יוֹסֵף עַל פָּסוּק "גָּמַר חָסִיד כִּי פַסּוּ אֱמוּנִים" בְּשֵׁם רַבִּי לֵיבּ פִּיסְטִינֶער, דְּהַאי קְרָא מֵרֵישֵׁיהּ לְסֵיפֵיהּ וּמִסֵּיפֵיהּ לְרֵישֵׁיהּ מִדְרַשׁ.

And as written in Sefer Toledot Yaakov Yosef on the verse "The pious man has ceased, for the faithful fail" (Psalms 12:2) in the name of Rabbi Leib Pistiner, that this verse may be expounded from its beginning to its end, and from its end to its beginning.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֲרָכִין יז.): פַּרְנָס לְפִי הַדּוֹר, דּוֹר לְפִי פַּרְנָס, וְהֵי קָדִים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
And as they said (Arachin 17a): "A leader is according to the generation, and a generation is according to its leader," and which one precedes depends on the perspective, as noted above.

paragraphs.text: Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Berakhot 3:5: “At first the Gemara puts the infant before the woman, while at the end, concerning one who is sleeping, it puts the woman first. In the actual event, the infant comes first: his need awakens them from sleep. But another person first perceives the sound of the woman speaking. Understand the meaning of the analogy well: those who awaken are the people of Israel. Through their yearning, the teacher is raised to receive Torah from Hashem and convey it to them, even though human beings perceive and experience the order in the reverse way.”

paragraphs.text: Toldot Yaakov Yosef, Shemot 2–3, reports Rabbi Yehudah Leib of Pistina’s two readings of ‘the pious person has ceased’ and ‘the faithful have vanished’: either can explain the other, because leaders and people are joined. The resulting counsel is that scholars and ordinary people should each attribute the failure to themselves rather than blame the other. This preserves both directions of influence and the ethical purpose of the teaching.

, reports Rabbi Yehudah Leib of Pistina’s two readings of ‘the pious person has ceased’ and ‘the faithful have vanished’: either can explain the other, because leaders and people are joined. The resulting counsel is that scholars and ordinary people should each attribute the failure to themselves rather than blame the other. This preserves both directions of influence and the ethical purpose of the teaching.

sections.en: Praying Over Exile at Daybreak and Nightfall

p: [כז] צָרִיךְ בִּתְחִלַּת יוֹם וְכֵן בִּתְחִלַּת לַיְלָה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל הַגָּלוּת
At the beginning of the day and likewise at the beginning of the night, one must pray over the exile
[שִׁעְבּוּד וְכוּלֵי וּשְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה שְׁקוּלִים, וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד],
for physical subjugation and the inner leaven in the dough are equivalent, being all one,
וְעַיֵּין בְּמָגֵן אַבְרָהָם רֵישׁ סִימָן א' בְּשֵׁם שְׁלָ"ה.
and see Magen Avraham at the beginning of Siman 1 in the name of the Shelah.
לְפִי שֶׁאָז הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹאֵג וְכוּלֵי
For at those transition points the Holy One, blessed be He, roars over the destruction
[וּכְדִיָלֵיף בְּהָרֹא"שׁ עַל סוֹף כָּל מִשְׁמָר מִזֶּה],
as the Rosh derived concerning the end of each watch from this,
כִּדְמַשְׁמָע מִלְּשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא: סִימָנָא לְמַאי לִי? אוּרְתָּא סִימָנָא לְמַאי לִי? יְמָמָא הוּא!
as implied by the wording of the Gemara (Berakhot 3a): "Why do I need a sign? For the evening, why do I need a sign? It is daytime!"

דְּקָשֶׁה, הָא מָצִינוּ בְּיוֹמָא (כח.) שֶׁטָּעוּ בִּמְאוֹר הַלְּבָנָה שֶׁהוּא אוֹר הַיּוֹם, וְכֵן מָצִינוּ לְהַלָּן (כז עַמּוּד ב) בְּיוֹם הַמְּעוּנָּן הִתְפַּלְּלוּ שֶׁל שַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, וְאִם כֵּן שַׁפִּיר צָרִיךְ סִימָנָא כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר.

for this poses a difficulty: do we not find in Yoma (28a) that they mistook the moonlight for the break of day, and do we not find below (27b) that on an overcast day they prayed the Shabbat prayer on Friday afternoon, showing that one indeed requires a sign when it is not obvious?
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּהַךְ סִימָן פֵּירוּשׁ סִימָן עַל אֲמִירַת הַשְּׁאָגָה,
Therefore perforce this Talmudic sign refers to identifying the precise moment of the Supernal Roar;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר דְּלַיְלָה וִימָמָא הוּא, וְאִם כֵּן אֵין צָרִיךְ סִימָן טְפֵי
and to this the Gemara responded that night and day are inherently distinct, so that one requires no additional sign
[נִיכָּר לְמַטָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְעֵיל אוֹת כג],
discernible below, as explained above in Section 23,

כִּי וַדַּאי בְּהַתְחָלַת הַזְּמַן דְּלַיְלָה וּדְיוֹם, שֶׁהוּא חֲלִיפוֹת זְמַן דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, אָז שׁוֹאֵג עַל הַחוּרְבָּן, שֶׁכְּבָר מַתְחִיל עוֹד זְמַן בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ מִזְּמַנֵּי הָעוֹלָם וַעֲדַיִן בֶּן דָּוִד לֹא בָּא.

because certainly at the inception of night and at the inception of day—which represent the structural shifts of this physical world—He roars over the destruction, seeing that yet another independent epoch of world-time begins while the son of David has still not arrived.

וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר נַמֵּי לְהַלָּן: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? לִמְקְרֵי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, דְּקָשֶׁה, לְמַאי לִי "לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ וְכוּלֵי", וְכִי לְעֵיל קָאָמַר נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר רַק: סִימָנָא לְמַאן דְּגָנֵי בְּבַיִת אָפֵל.

And this explains what the Gemara states further: "What is the practical difference? To recite the Shema"—which is difficult: why ask "what is the practical difference," since previously it offered no halakhic difference, and it should simply have said: "The sign is for one sleeping in a dark room"?
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ לָזֶה אֵין צָרִיךְ סִימָן, רַק הַסִּימָן הוּא שֶׁנִּיכָּר לְמַטָּה אֵיזֶה שִׁינּוּי אָז, וְזֶה לְאוֹת עַל הַשְּׁאָגָה.
Perforce, for the natural time itself one requires no sign, but the sign denotes a discernible terrestrial change occurring then, serving as a token of the divine Roar.
אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ "לְמַאן דְּגָנֵי" קָשֶׁה: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? הוּצְרַךְ לוֹמַר "לִמְקְרֵי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע".
But afterward, regarding "one who is sleeping," the Gemara challenges: what practical difference does it make? and was obliged to answer: "To recite Shema."
וְהוּא הַדִּין דְּשָׁם הֲוָה מָצֵי לְמֵימַר לְיוֹם הַמְּעוּנָּן אוֹ זְרִיחַת אוֹר הַלְּבָנָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, אֶלָּא דְּמַאי דִּשְׁכִיחַ טְפֵי נָקַט:
And the same applies that the Talmud could just as well have mentioned an overcast day or misleading moonlight as noted above, but it cited the most common scenario: one sleeping in a dark room.

sections.en: Finding Light Through the Congregation and Its Leaders

p: [כח] מַאן דְּגָנֵי בְּבַיִת אָפֵל.
"One who sleeps in a dark house"
פֵּירוּשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין צב.): "הֱוֵי קַבֵּל וְקַיֵּים, כִּדִתְנַן: בַּיִת אָפֵל וְכוּלֵי".
is explained according to Sanhedrin (92a): "Accept your lot and endure, as we learn: a dark house, etc."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין מֵאִיר בּוֹ שׁוּם אוֹר אֱלֹהוּת, וְלֹא יָדַע זְמַן קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם אֵימָתַי,
This allegorically depicts a person within whom no divine light shines, who does not perceive when the time to accept the yoke of Heaven arrives;
כֵּיוָן דְּשָׁמַע תִּינוֹק וְכוּלֵי יְצָרֵף עַצְמוֹ בַּהֲדֵי צִיבּוּרָא וּבַהֲדֵי רָאשֵׁי הָעֵדָה,
but once he hears the infant and the woman, let him attach himself to the congregation and to the leaders of the community,
וּבַהֲדַיְיהוּ גַּם הוּא יוּכַל לְקַבֵּל, כַּיָּדוּעַ כַּאֲשֶׁר נִכְלָל נַפְשׁוֹ בְּנִשְׁמַת גְּדוֹלֵי הַדּוֹר הֵם מַעֲלִים אוֹתוֹ.
and alongside them he too will become capable of accepting the yoke, for as is known, when a person binds his soul into the collective soul of the generation's leaders, they elevate him.
וְדַוְקָא כְּשֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לָצֵאת מִן הַבַּיִת אָפֵל, דְּלָא עָדִיף הַאי סִימָנָא מֵחֲזָקָה, דְּהֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא לְבָרוּרֵי מְבָרְרִינַן, וְיֵצֵא לַחוּץ לִרְאוֹת.

And this applies specifically when he cannot exit the dark house, for this sign is no greater than a legal presumption (chazakah), where if verification is possible we investigate, and he should go outside to see the light.
[וְלָכֵן לֹא נָקַט טְפֵי סוּמָא, דַּעֲדַיִן צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דְּגָנֵי בְּבַיִת סָגוּר שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לָצֵאת לִשְׁאוֹל מִבְּנֵי אָדָם].
And for this reason the Talmud did not formulate the case around a blind person, for one would still need to specify that he lies in an enclosed room unable to exit to inquire of others.
אַךְ כְּשֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל כְּלָל אַחַר כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לְהַגִּיעַ לְבָבוֹ לִמְקוֹם הָאוֹר,
But when, after all his efforts, he cannot bring his heart into the realm of light,
אָז יִצְטָרֵף בִּשְׁמִיעַת קוֹל תִּינוֹק וְאִשָּׁה,
then he should attach himself through hearing the voice of the infant and the woman;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּיָכוֹל לָצֵאת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁעַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה מִמְּשַׁל דַּחֲבוּרָה שֶׁנֶּחְלָה אֶחָד אוֹ שֶׁמֵּת, עַיֵּין שָׁם:
unlike when he is able to emerge on his own, as written in Sha'ar HaTeshuvah regarding the parable of a fellowship when one falls ill or dies, see there.

This mutual aid accompanies personal effort; the following parable still requires some living intention.

sections.en: The Inner Temple and the Order of Repentance

p: [כט] מִתְּחִלָּה הוּא חוּרְבַּן הַבַּיִת
The destruction of the inner Temple comes first
[הַפְּנִימִי, בֵּית דִּירָה, וּבוֹ דַּי רַק חוּרְבָּה שֶׁחָרַב מֵאֵין דָּרִים],
the inner residence, where ruin alone suffices, being laid waste without inhabitants,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ שְׂרֵיפַת הַהֵיכָל
and afterward the burning of the Sanctuary
[הַחִיצוֹן, וְחוּרְבָּנוֹ הַיְינוּ שְׂרֵיפָה],
the outer structure, whose destruction requires burning,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ גָּלוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and afterward the exile of Israel.
וְכֵן הַחוֹטֵא: מִתְּחִלָּה בַּלֵּב שֶׁחָרַב מִיִּרְאַת שָׁמַיִם,
And so too the sinner: first the heart is destroyed, becoming barren of the fear of Heaven,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בַּמּוֹחַ
and afterward the damage reaches the brain

[שֶׁשָּׁם אֵינוֹ מָדוֹר קָבוּעַ, כִּי "בַּיִת זוֹ אִשָּׁה" שֶׁהִיא הַלֵּב, וְהוּא נִשְׂרָף לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁאֵינֶנּוּ מָקוֹם מֵכִיל אַף לִפְרָקִים מַחֲשֶׁבֶת שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם שֶׁאוּלַי יָבוֹא הִרְהוּר תְּשׁוּבָה לַלֵּב],

for there is no permanent dwelling there, since 'a house is a woman' who is the heart; and the brain is entirely consumed by fire so that it can no longer contain even occasional thoughts of Heaven that might stir a thought of repentance in the heart,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ כָּל אֵבָרֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה גּוֹלִים לִמְקוֹם הַטֻּמְאָה.
and afterward all the limbs of physical action are exiled to a place of impurity.
וּבִתְשׁוּבָה לְהֵיפֶךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, קלד עַמּוּד א): מִתְּחִלָּה "בּוֹנֵה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם" וַהֲדַר "נִדְחֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכַנֵּס"
But in repentance it is the reverse, as written in the Zohar (Part I, 134a): first "He rebuilds Jerusalem," and only afterward "He gathers the dispersed of Israel"
[וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי (פֶּרֶק ה הֲלָכָה ב) דְּבִנְיַן הַבַּיִת עַל יְדֵי מַלְכֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם],
and in Yerushalmi Maaser Sheni (5:2) that the rebuilding of the Temple will be facilitated by the kings of the nations,
דְּמִתְּחִלָּה תִּיקּוּן הַמִּדּוֹת וְהַלֵּב וְאַחַר כָּךְ לַמַּעֲשִׂים.
because first comes the rectification of character traits and the heart, and only afterward the practical deeds.
וְנִרְאֶה דְּהֵיכָל קוֹדֵם בְּבִנְיָן לַבַּיִת, וְכֵן מִתְּחִלָּה הַמּוֹחַ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ב מֵהִלְכוֹת יְסוֹדֵי הַתּוֹרָה: "וְכֵיצַד הִיא הַדֶּרֶךְ וְכוּלֵי":

And it appears that the Sanctuary precedes the inner Temple in rebuilding, and so too the intellect precedes in rectification, as Maimonides wrote at the beginning of Chapter 2 of Hilkhot Yesodei HaTorah: "And what is the way to love and fear Him? When one contemplates His great and wondrous works..."

The contrast is whether a person follows the recipient’s immediate wishes or attends to the divine Giver within what is received. The righteous orient the heart toward the One who gives strength. This supplies the symbolic background to the relation of heart, house, and what directs them here.

sections.en: Intention and Interruption in an Imperfect Mitzvah

p: [ל] אַף מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאֵינָהּ הֲגוּנָה בְּעֶצֶם, כָּל שֶׁהִיא הֲגוּנָה כְּפִי מַחֲשַׁבַּת הָאָדָם וְהִיא מַעֲשֵׂה מִצְוָה,
Even an action that is not inherently proper, so long as it is proper according to the person's subjective intention and constitutes a performance of a mitzvah,
רַק שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ עֵצָה הַיּוֹתֵר טוֹבָה, אֵין לָנוּ לִמְנוֹעַ מִמֶּנּוּ עֲשִׂיָּתָהּ
except that he should rather have performed it in a better, more advisable way, we are not to prevent him from doing it
כִּדְמַשְׁמָע מֵאֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁהִמְתִּין עַד שֶׁסִּיֵּים תְּפִלָּתוֹ וְלֹא מְנָעוֹ תֵּיכֶף.
as implied by Elijah, who waited until Rabbi Yosei finished his prayer in the ruin and did not interrupt him immediately.
וְאוּלַי יֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּלֹא הָיָה שָׁם מָקוֹם פָּנוּי לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עוֹד,
And perhaps one could suggest that there was no other cleared spot to pray there,
וְהָיָה לוֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל בַּדֶּרֶךְ, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּכְנַס לַחָרְבָּה,
and he should have prayed on the road—meaning before entering the ruin;
וְאֵינוֹ בַּמַּשְׁמָע, אֶלָּא גַּם שֶׁהָיָה יָכוֹל לָצֵאת לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לֹא מְנָעוֹ מֵהִתְפַּלֵּל בַּחָרְבָּה.
yet that is not the implication of the text, but rather even though he could have stepped outside to pray, Elijah did not stop him from praying inside the ruin.
וְאוּלַי לְבַל יִתְבַּלְבֵּל בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ עַל יְדֵי זֶה, כֵּיוָן שֶׁכְּבָר הָיָה מוּכָן לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לֹא רָצָה לְמוֹנְעוֹ,
And perhaps lest he become distracted and confused in his prayer through an interruption, since he was already poised in prayer, Elijah chose not to stop him,
אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי עַל פִּי דִּין לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן לְכַתְּחִלָּה:
even though it is halakhically improper to act in such a manner ab initio.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 3a:12: “It was taught: Rabbi Yosei said: Once I was walking along the road, and I entered one of Jerusalem’s ruins to pray. Elijah, remembered for good, came and kept watch for me at the entrance (and waited for me) until I finished my prayer. After I finished my prayer, he said to me: ‘Peace to you, Rabbi.’ I said to him: ‘Peace to you, my rabbi and teacher.’ He said to me: ‘My son, why did you enter this ruin?’ I answered him: ‘To pray.’ He said to me: ‘You should have prayed on the road.’ I said to him: ‘I was afraid that travelers might interrupt me.’ He said to me: ‘You should have recited a short prayer.’”

sections.en: Short Prayer with True Concentration

p: [לא] אֵין לְהִתְפַּלֵּל בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְבַּלְבֵּל בָּאֶמְצַע, אֶלָּא תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה שֶׁלֹּא יִתְבַּלְבֵּל בָּהּ.
One should not pray in a place where one might become confused or interrupted in the middle, except by offering a shortened prayer in which one will not be distracted.
כִּי טוֹב מְעַט בְּכַוָּנָה מֵהַרְבּוֹת בְּלֹא כַוָּנָה.
For better is a little with heartfelt concentration than much without concentration.
וְכֵן בְּכָל עִנְיָן וּזְמַן, כְּשֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לְכַוֵּין כָּל הַתְּפִלָּה,
And likewise in every circumstance and time, when a person is unable to concentrate through the entire prayer,
וְעוֹבְרֵי דְּרָכִים – דֶּרֶךְ הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, חָלָל שְׂמָאלִי שֶׁבַּלֵּב – יַפְסִיקוּהוּ מֵעֲבוֹדָתוֹ,
and wayfarers—representing the highway of the mundane world, the left cavity of the heart—would interrupt him from his divine service,
יִתְפַּלֵּל תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה עַל כָּל פָּנִים בְּכַוָּנָה:
let him at least pray a shortened prayer with true focused intention.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 3a:12: “It was taught: Rabbi Yosei said: Once I was walking on the road and entered one of the ruins of Jerusalem to pray. Eliyahu, remembered for good, came and waited for me at the entrance until I finished my prayer. After I finished my prayer, he said to me, “Peace be upon you, my master.” I said to him, “Peace be upon you, my master and teacher.” He said to me: My son, why did you enter this ruin? I said to him: To pray. He said to me: You should have prayed on the road. I said to him: I was afraid that passersby might interrupt me. He said to me: You should have prayed a short prayer.”

sections.en: Spiritual Ruins and the Dangers of Emptiness

p: [לב] "אֵין נִכְנָסִים לַחָרְבָּה" – פֵּירוּשׁ: מָקוֹם פָּנוּי מִמּוֹשַׁב בְּנֵי אָדָם הָאֲמִתִּיִּים וּמְקוֹם מִצְוָה, רַק כָּל מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הָרְשׁוּת.

"One does not enter a ruin" (Berakhot 3a)—meaning a place devoid of the dwelling of authentic, spiritual human beings and a place of mitzvot, occupied solely by thoughts of optional, mundane pursuits.
מִפְּנֵי הַחֲשָׁד – שֶׁיַּחְשׁוֹד לְעַצְמוֹ שֶׁמָּא יֵשׁ אֵיזֶה תַּאֲוָה בַּדָּבָר.
"On account of suspicion"—meaning that a person should suspect within himself lest there be some subtle base desire motivating the matter.
וּמִפְּנֵי הַמַּזִּיקִין – דְּכָל מָקוֹם הַפָּנוּי מִקְּדוּשָׁה יֵשׁ מָקוֹם לַמַּזִּיקִין וְכֹחַ הַיֵּצֶר לְהִתְגַּבֵּר.
"And on account of harmful spirits (mazikin)"—for every place vacant of holiness leaves room for damaging spiritual forces and the power of the evil inclination to prevail.
וּמִפְּנֵי הַמַּפּוֹלֶת – דִּסְתָם חָרְבָּה רְעוּעָה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ קִיּוּם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "שֶׁקֶר אֵין לוֹ רַגְלַיִם".
"And on account of collapse"—for an ordinary ruin is precarious and lacks enduring stability, as it is written: "falsehood has no legs to stand on."
וַאֲפִילּוּ לְצוֹרֶךְ עֲבוֹדָה [לְהִתְפַּלֵּל] אֵין לִיכָּנֵס,
And even for the sake of divine service such as to pray, one should not enter,
אִם יָכוֹל [לְהִתְפַּלֵּל] בַּדֶּרֶךְ, הוּא דֶּרֶךְ הַמֶּלֶךְ, פִּילוֹן מְפוּלָּשׁ לַעֲבוֹדַת ה',
if one can pray on the road, which represents the King's highway, an open avenue for the service of Hashem;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ הַמֶּלֶךְ הוּא מָלֵא מֵעוֹבְרֵי דְּרָכִים, וְהֵם הַמַּפְסִיקִין לַהוֹלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ ה',
and even though the King's highway is full of transient passersby who disturb one walking in the path of Hashem,
מוּטָב לַעֲבוֹד שָׁם עֲבוֹדָה קְצָרָה כְּפִי הַיְּכוֹלֶת מִלִּיכָּנֵס לַחָרְבָּה וּמַחֲשֶׁבֶת חוּץ לְצוֹרֶךְ עֲבוֹדָה.
it is better to perform a brief service there according to one's ability than to enter a ruin and entertain external, peripheral thoughts for the sake of divine worship.
אִם לֹא בְּחָרְבָּא חֲדַתָּא, מְחוּדֶּשֶׁת מֵאִתּוֹ,
This applies unless it is a newly made ruin (charba chadta), freshly originated by him,
וּבִתְרֵי, שֶׁאֵינוֹ יְחִידִי בַּעֲבוֹדָתוֹ עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַזֶּה,
and in the presence of two people, such that he is not isolated in his divine service along this path,
וּכְשֵׁרֵי, שֶׁכָּל כַּוָּנָתָם לַעֲבוֹדַת ה',
and they are worthy individuals whose whole intention is directed toward the service of Hashem,
וּדְלָא קָאֵי בִּדְבָרָא, שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹמָן שֶׁל כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע:
and it is not situated out in an open field, which is the natural domain of the power of the evil inclination.

sections.en: Urgent Mitzvos and Effort Beyond the Day

p: [לג] אַף עַל גַּב דִּזְרִיזִים אֵין מַקְדִּימִין טְפֵי מִצַּפְרָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּפְסָחִים (ד.),
Although zealous individuals do not anticipate a mitzvah earlier than the morning, as taught in the first chapter of Pesachim (4a),
זֶהוּ מִצַּד הַזְּרִיזוּת לַמִּצְוָה לְבַד;
that rule applies solely from the general standpoint of alacrity toward a mitzvah;
אֲבָל בִּדְבַר מִצְוָה הַנְּחוּצָה לִשְׁעָתָהּ, צֵא וּלְמַד מִפּוֹעֵל בְּעִסְקֵי הָעוֹלָם בְּדָבָר הַנָּחוּץ.
but regarding an urgent mitzvah that is pressing for that specific hour, go forth and learn from a hired laborer engaged in urgent worldly affairs.
וּלְכָךְ סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בִּבְרָכוֹת ב' עַמּוּד ב' דִּלִמְלֶאכֶת בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הָווּ מַחְשְׁכֵי וּמַקְדְּמֵי גַּם בַּלַּיְלָה, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And for this reason, the Gemara in Berakhot (2b) initially entertained that for the construction of the Temple, workers would stay late into the night and arise early before dawn, see there.
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר גַּם לְמַאי דְּדָיֵיק מִקְּרָאֵי דְּלָא חָשְׁכֵי וְקָדְמֵי, הַיְינוּ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם הַלַּיְלָה לְמִשְׁמָר וְגַם כֵּן לֹא הָיוּ פְּנוּיִים לְכָךְ,

And one may say that even according to the conclusion derived from verses that they did not work into the night or before dawn, it was because the night was required for guard duty and they were not available for physical building;
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת דְּמַחְשְׁכֵי וּמַקְדְּמֵי, אֲבָל בְּלָאו הָכִי וַדַּאי לְמִצְוָה נְחוּצָה דְּעָבְדִינַן כֵּן כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
they therefore could not have been working into the night and before dawn. Otherwise, it is certainly established that for an urgent mitzvah one acts with such nocturnal exertion, as mentioned above.

p: [לד] "כָּל הַלַּיְלָה אִיבְרִי לְשֵׁינְתָא" לְחַד מַאן דְּאָמַר בְּעֵירוּבִין ס"ה עַמּוּד א',
"The entire night was created for sleep," according to one opinion in Eruvin (65a);
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתוֹסָפוֹת דְּהַיְינוּ לֵילֵי תְּקוּפַת תַּמּוּז.
and see there in Tosafot that this denotes the short nights of the Tammuz solstice.
וְעַיֵּין תַּעֲנִית ל"א עַמּוּד א' דְּמִטַּ"וּ בְּאָב צָרִיךְ לְהוֹסִיף, וְהַיְינוּ מֵחֲצִי תְּקוּפַת תַּמּוּז,
And see Ta'anit (31a) that from the fifteenth of Av one must add time to Torah study, which corresponds to the midpoint of the Tammuz solstice;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר דִּלְעוֹלָם הַהַתְחָלָה נִמְשָׁךְ עַד הַחֲצִי, דְּאַחַר כָּךְ רוּבּוֹ כְּכֻלּוֹ וּכְאִלּוּ כֻּלּוֹ עָבַר, וְהַלֵּילוֹת מַתְחִילִין לְהִתְגַּדֵּל.

and as I wrote elsewhere, the beginning of a period extends until its midpoint, for afterward the rule that 'the majority is like the whole' applies as if the period has entirely passed, and the nights begin to lengthen.
וְעַיֵּין בַּמִּשְׁנָה רֵישׁ בְּרָכוֹת דִּזְמַן הַהַתְחָלָה לִישַׁן עַד סוֹף הָאַשְׁמוּרָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה,
And see the Mishna at the beginning of Berakhot, that the window for beginning to sleep extends until the end of the first watch;
וְאַף רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וַחֲכָמִים מוֹדִים לָזֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה
and even Rabban Gamliel and the Sages concede to this, as written in Talmidei Rabbeinu Yonah
וְצָרִיךְ עִיּוּן אַמַּאי לֹא פֵּירְשׁוּ דִּפְלִיגֵי אַף אַזְמַן הַתְחָלַת שְׁכִיבָה, דְּאִיכָּא אֱינָשֵׁי שֶׁהוֹלְכִים לִשְׁכַּב בְּהַאי שַׁעְתָּא,
and it requires further reflection why they did not explain that they argue regarding the start of retiring to bed as well, since there are people who go to sleep at that later hour;
דְּהָא קַיְימָא לַן דְּאוֹמֵר "הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ", עַיֵּין לְקַמָּן ט' עַמּוּד א' בְּרַשִּׁ"י וְתוֹסָפוֹת דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "בִּלְבַד",
for we establish that one recites Hashkiveinu, see below on 9a in Rashi and Tosafot s.v. bilvad,
[דְּיֵשׁ שֶׁהוֹלְכִים אָז תְּחִלַּת שְׁכִיבָה.]
showing that some retire to sleep at that later time.
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא ב' עַמּוּד ב' בָּזֶה מַחֲלוֹקֶת בַּהַתְחָלָה, וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתוֹסָפוֹת דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "וְאִי":
And see there in the Gemara (2b) that this forms a dispute concerning the starting point, and see Tosafot s.v. ve-i.

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Berakhot 1:1: “From when may one recite the Shema in the evening? From the time when the priests enter to eat their terumah until the end of the first watch: these are Rabbi Eliezer’s words. The Sages say: Until midnight. Rabban Gamliel says: Until dawn. It happened that his sons returned from a feast and said to him: We have not recited the Shema. He said to them: If dawn has not risen, you are obligated to recite it. Not only this: in every case in which the Sages said “until midnight,” the mitzvah extends until dawn. The burning of sacrificial fats and limbs may be performed until dawn; and all offerings eaten for one day may be eaten until dawn. If so, why did the Sages say “until midnight”? To distance a person from transgression.”

sections.en: The Destructive Emptiness of an Abandoned House

p: [לה] לֹא יִכָּנֵס לְחָרְבָּה דִּשְׁכִיחִים מַזִּיקִין
One should not enter a ruin because harmful spirits (mazikin) are commonly found there
[וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא עוֹד שְׁנֵי טְעָמִים, עַיֵּין שָׁם הַנָּפְקָא מִינַּהּ בָּהֶם].
and see there in the Gemara two additional reasons, and examine the practical halakhic differences between them.
וְעַיֵּין בָּבָא קַמָּא כ"א עַמּוּד א' וּבְרַשִּׁ"י עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And see Bava Kamma 21a and Rashi there.
כִּי בַּיִת הוּא מָקוֹם שֶׁמַּחֲזִיק בּוֹ אֵיזֶה דָּבָר,
For a house is a structure designated to contain something,
וְכַאֲשֶׁר חָרַב מֵאֵין יוֹשֵׁב מִבְּנֵי אָדָם וְלֹא מֵחֲפָצָיו
and when it lies in ruins without human inhabitant and devoid of personal property
[וְכִדְאִיתָא בְּבָבָא קַמָּא שָׁם דְּגַם בְּמַחֲזִיק בּוֹ תִּבְנָא וְצִיבֵי סַגִּי],
and as stated in Bava Kamma there, that even if it merely stores straw and wood it is sufficient,
אִם כֵּן הוּא מָקוֹם הָפְכִּי וּמַזִּיק לְיִשּׁוּב בְּנֵי אָדָם,
then it becomes an inverted, detrimental place that opposes human settlement;
וּלְפִיכָךְ אָמְרוּ שָׁם בְּבָבָא קַמָּא דִּמְקַלְקֵל גַּם כֵּן הַבִּנְיָן,
and therefore they stated there in Bava Kamma that an empty ruin ruins the building itself as well,
שֶׁהַבִּנְיָן מִצָּרְכֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם,
because a building exists for human needs,
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁזֶּה הִיפּוּךְ הַיִּשּׁוּב, הוּא גַּם כֵּן הָפְכִּי וּמַזִּיק לַבִּנְיָן שֶׁהוּא מִכְּלַל הַיִּשּׁוּב:
and since the vacancy is the negation of civilized habitation, it is likewise contrary and destructive to the structure itself, which belongs to the realm of human civilization.

sections.en: Companionship and Safety in the Synagogue

p: [לו] לֹא יִכָּנֵס בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת יְחִידִי – בְּבָתֵּי כְּנֵסִיּוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹמְדִים בַּשָּׂדֶה וּמְסוּכָּנִים מִמַּזִּיקִים,
A person should not enter a synagogue alone—this referred to their ancient synagogues which stood out in the fields and were perilous on account of harmful spirits,
וּלְפִיכָךְ צְרִיכִים לְהַמְתִּין אֶחָד עַל חֲבֵירוֹ
and therefore worshippers had to wait one for another
תּוֹסָפוֹת שָׁם ב' עַמּוּד א' דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "מְבָרֵךְ".
Tosafot there, Berakhot 2a s.v. mevarekh.
וּבַהַמְתָּנָה סַגִּי כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב שָׁם מ"ג עַמּוּד ב' דִּלִשְׁנַיִם אֵין מַזִּיק, וְכֵן אִיתָא שָׁם ג' עַמּוּד ב' דִּבִּתְרֵי לֵיכָּא,
And waiting is sufficient, as written there on 43b that harmful spirits do not harm two people, and on 3b that in the company of two they do not appear;
וּלְכָךְ כְּשֶׁיִּשָּׁאֵר אֶחָד דַּי כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב שָׁם ה' סוֹף עַמּוּד ב': שְׁנַיִם שֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ וְכוּלֵי,
and therefore keeping one companion remaining is sufficient, as written on 5b regarding two who entered to pray, etc.;
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם ו' עַמּוּד א' תּוֹסָפוֹת דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל", וְיְעוּיַּן שָׁם שֶׁסִּיְּמוּ: וּלְכָךְ בַּלַּיְלָה וְכוּלֵי,
and see 6a in Tosafot s.v. hamitpalel, where they conclude: 'and therefore at night, etc.',
מַשְׁמָע דְּבַלַּיְלָה גַּם בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת דִּילַן שֶׁבָּעִיר יֵשׁ לָחוּשׁ.
implying that at night, even in our urban synagogues located in town, there is reason for concern.
וְכֵן מַשְׁמָע מִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתְבוּ בְּדִבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "מְבָרֵךְ" הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל: אֲבָל וְכוּלֵי אֶלָּא בַּלַּיְלָה.
And this is likewise implied from what they wrote in the aforementioned s.v. mevarekh: 'however... only at night.'
אֲבָל צָרִיךְ עִיּוּן, דְּהָא "יִרְאוּ עֵינֵינוּ" נִתְקַן רַק בַּלַּיְלָה,
But this requires study, for the blessing Yir'u Eineinu was instituted specifically at night,
וּמִלְּשׁוֹן "וְדַוְקָא וְכוּלֵי" מַשְׁמָע דְּבְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת דִּילַן אֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר "יִרְאוּ עֵינֵינוּ", וְצָרִיךְ עִיּוּן.
and from their phrasing 'and specifically, etc.' it would imply that in our urban synagogues one need not recite Yir'u Eineinu, which requires examination.
וּבָרִי"ף אַהָא דִּשְׁנַיִם שֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ וְכוּלֵי מַשְׁמָע גַּם בִּזְמַנָּם דַּוְקָא בַּלַּיְלָה,
And in the Rif on the passage of two who entered to pray, it implies that even in their day it was strictly at night,
וְיֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹסָפוֹת דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל" הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל קָאֵי בִּזְמַנָּם.
and one may explain that the words of Tosafot s.v. hamitpalel were addressed to their ancient period.

וּלְפִי זֶה יֵשׁ לְהַגִּיהַּ בְּתוֹסָפוֹת דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "מְבָרֵךְ" הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל דְּצָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת אַחַר תֵּירוּץ הַמַּזִּיקִים "בַּלַּיְלָה", וְתֵיבַת "אֶלָּא בַּלַּיְלָה" טָעוּת סוֹפֵר, וְדָחוּק.

And according to this, one would have to emend Tosafot s.v. mevarekh, placing 'at night' after the answer regarding harmful spirits, treating the phrase 'only at night' as a scribal error, which is forced.
וְעַיֵּין בְּאֹרַח חַיִּים סִימָן צ' סָעִיף ט"ו יֵשׁ לְעַיֵּין,
And see Orach Chayim 90:15 where this warrants careful analysis;
וְנִרְאֶה דְּסָבְרֵי דִּ"יִתְבַּלְבֵּל" שַׁיָּיךְ גַּם בָּעִיר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה, וְגַם זֶה דַּוְקָא בַּלַּיְלָה.
and it appears they hold that distraction (yitbalbel) applies in the city as well as written in Talmidei Rabbeinu Yonah, and this too specifically at night.

אַךְ עַל הַ"יֵּשׁ אוֹמְרִים" שֶׁבָּרַמָ"א נִרְשָׁם תַּלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה, מְבוֹאָר דִּלְתַלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה הוּא הַדִּין בַּיּוֹם, וְכֵן כָּתַב בְּבֵית יוֹסֵף לְהַתַּלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה, אַךְ לֹא יָדַעְתִּי מִנַּיִן לוֹ.

However, on the 'some say' cited in the Rema, Talmidei Rabbeinu Yonah is referenced, indicating that according to them the same applies by day; and so the Beit Yosef wrote regarding Talmidei Rabbeinu Yonah, yet I do not know his source for this.
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר תַּלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה קָאֵי עַל דִּבְרֵי הָרִי"ף דְּמַיְירֵי בַּלַּיְלָה.
And one can argue that Talmidei Rabbeinu Yonah commented on the Rif who spoke specifically of nighttime.
וְעַיֵּין בַּטּוּר מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב: "וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים דְּאַף בְּשֶׁלָּנוּ וְכוּלֵי", לִכְאוֹרָה הַךְ "יֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים" דִּבְרֵי תַּלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי.
And see the Tur where he wrote: 'And some say that even in ours, etc.,' which seemingly represents the opinion of Talmidei Rabbeinu Yonah as I suggested.

אַךְ מִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתַב בַּדֵּעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה "בַּשָּׂדוֹת אַף בַּיּוֹם" נִרְאֶה דְּזֶהוּ דַּעַת תַּלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה, וְהַ"יֵּשׁ אוֹמְרִים" הוּא דַּעַת הָרִי"ף, וְסָבַר דְּקָאֵי אַשֶּׁלָּנוּ, וְכֵן מַשְׁמָע בְּבֵית יוֹסֵף עַיֵּין שָׁם.

Yet from what he wrote in the first opinion—'in the fields even by day'—it appears that this is the view of Talmidei Rabbeinu Yonah, while the 'some say' is the view of the Rif, holding that it applies to our synagogues, and this is implied in the Beit Yosef, see there.
אֲבָל צָרִיךְ עִיּוּן, דְּהָא הָרִי"ף אֵין מְחַלֵּק, וְגַם בַּשָּׂדֶה דַּוְקָא בַּלַּיְלָה.
But this requires study, for the Rif makes no such division, holding that even in the field it applies strictly at night.
וְלָכֵן נִרְאֶה טְפֵי דְּהַ"יֵּשׁ אוֹמְרִים" דַּעַת תּוֹסָפוֹת כַּנִּרְאֶה מִדִּבְרֵיהֶם שֶׁלְּפָנֵינוּ.
Therefore it seems more probable that the 'some say' is the opinion of Tosafot as evident from their text before us.
וּלְפִי זֶה בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת שֶׁלָּנוּ בַּלַּיְלָה, אִם יֵשׁ חֲשַׁשׁ מַזִּיקִין תַּלְיָא בִּפְלוּגְתָּא.
And according to this, whether there is concern for harmful spirits in our synagogues at night depends on this dispute.
וּבְשֶׁלָּהֶם מַשְׁמָע אַף בַּיּוֹם יֵשׁ חֲשָׁשׁ, וְצָרִיךְ עִיּוּן דְּהָא "יִרְאוּ עֵינֵינוּ" תִּקְּנוּ רַק בַּלַּיְלָה.
And regarding their ancient synagogues it would imply that a concern existed even by day, which requires reflection since Yir'u Eineinu was instituted solely at night.
וְעַיֵּין בְּטוּר וְשֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ סִימָן רל"ו טַעַם אַחֵר, דְּהוּא בִּמְקוֹם תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית דְּגַם כְּשֶׁכֻּלָּם בְּיַחַד יְרֵאִים
And see Tur and Shulchan Arukh Siman 236 for an alternative rationale: that it was instituted to substitute for the evening prayer when, even together, people were fearful

[אוֹ דִּמְקוֹמָן שָׁאנֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל ג' עַמּוּד ב', אוֹ מִשּׁוּם חַיּוֹת וְלִסְטִים, עַיֵּין בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי רֵישׁ פִּרְקִין, וְעַיֵּין פְּסָחִים ב' עַמּוּד א' וּבְתוֹסָפוֹת, וְיוֹמָא כ"א עַמּוּד א'].
or perhaps their physical location was uniquely perilous as noted on 3b, or because of wild beasts and bandits, see Yerushalmi at the start of our chapter, Pesachim 2a and Tosafot, and Yoma 21a.

But the opinion of Tosafot explaining the reason to wait requires study, and in Shulchan Arukh Siman 90 which states the reason is distraction without mentioning harmful spirits also requires some reflection.

Indeed, in truth we do not find a blanket prohibition against entering alone into a house in the field by day or in the city at night

only against sleeping alone in a house,

and likewise from the phrasing on 3b 'a ruin in the field' it implies specifically a ruin, whereas a synagogue is not a ruin as I wrote above, since even housing straw and wood removes the status of a ruin

only in an open field at night is there concern, as written in Pesachim 2a, see Tosafot there.

And one can say that an outhouse is also not called a ruin since it serves human use, though one might argue an outhouse is different because harmful spirits are prevalent there, as written at the end of Berakhot.

Yet one could also say this regarding a synagogue, as written in Bava Kamma 60b that the Angel of Death deposits his weapons there.

paragraphs.text: Beit Yosef, Orach Chayim 90:20-21: ““Two people who entered a synagogue, and one finished his prayer before his fellow,” and so forth: this is discussed there, on Berakhot 5b. Rabbeinu Yonah wrote that the same applies when many people entered a synagogue, even if they did not enter together: of those remaining last, one must wait for the other. However, if someone entered alone at a time when he could not finish his prayer with them, his fellow need not wait for him. Since he saw that he could not finish with them and nevertheless entered, he showed that he entered on that understanding and is not afraid to remain alone. He further wrote: When we say that his fellow must wait for him, this applies specifically when he is not prolonging anything beyond his prayer. But if he prolongs petitions and other matters, his fellow is not required to wait for him in any circumstance. This concludes his words. What our author explained in the name of Rabbeinu Chananel was also written by Rabbeinu Yonah in his name, and Tosafot likewise wrote it in the name of Rabbeinu Tam. Rif wrote: “The rabbis explained this and established that it concerns the evening prayer; if he leaves him alone and departs, there is concern that he may come into danger.” Concerning the statement that Ri would wait even in our synagogues during the day: Tosafot’s words indicate that he did so as an additional stringency. Mordechai likewise wrote: “Ri was stringent even in our synagogues. He would prolong his prayer until everyone left; and if someone entered the synagogue in the meantime, he would study a book until that person finished his prayer. It is proper for us too to be stringent.” This concludes his words. Rabbeinu Yonah, however, wrote that this rule appears to apply even in synagogues within the city, because a person’s prayer commonly becomes unsettled when he stands alone in prayer.”

Now that they have resumed praying the evening prayer in synagogues, the original custom has not been abolished. Nevertheless, one must not interrupt with other matters. Some of the great authorities followed the practice of not reciting these verses.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 9: “‘See, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a field,’ and so forth. A field alludes to an expansion of desires. Esav was therefore called ‘a man of the field,’ because he expanded into all kinds of evil cravings and desires. Yaakov our father, however, had an expansion in holiness. This is ‘like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed’—the holy apple orchard.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach explicitly interprets ‘field’ as an expansion of desire, then distinguishes Esav's field from Yaakov's field blessed by Hashem. This helps identify the kind of expansion intended by the siman: its claim that bodily desires are uncommon concerns the spiritual state under discussion. The word ‘field’ by itself does not always signify freedom from bodily desire. This is a conceptual comparison, rather than an identification of the unnamed teaching Rav Tzadok reports hearing.

sections.en: Humility and Caution in Expressing Certainty

p: [לח] "לַמֵּד לְשׁוֹנְךָ לוֹמַר אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ, שֶׁמָּא תִּתְבַּדֶּה וְתֵאָחֵז" (בְּרָכוֹת ד' עַמּוּד א').
"Accustom your tongue to say 'I do not know,' lest you be trapped into deceit" (Berakhot 4a).
וּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר: אַף בִּדְבָרִים הַבְּרוּרִים בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה, כְּשֶׁבָּאִים לְגִלּוּי שֶׁהוּא הַלָּשׁוֹן הַמּוֹצִיא לַפּוֹעַל מַה שֶּׁבַּכֹּחַ בַּלֵּב – יִהְיוּ תְּלוּיִים בְּסָפֵק,

This means: even regarding matters that appear clear in inner thought, when they are brought into outward expression—which is the tongue actualizing that which is latent in the heart—let them be held in cautious doubt;
כִּי הָאָדָם עָלוּל הַטָּעִיּוֹת.
for man is inherently prone to errors.
וּלְכָךְ צָרִיךְ שֶׁכָּל גִּלּוּי מַעֲשָׂיו יִהְיוּ דְּבָרִים מְבוֹרָרִים לַכֹּל, וְלֹא מַה שֶּׁמְּבוֹרָר רַק לוֹ בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ;
And therefore all overt disclosures of his deeds must be matters verified and clear to all, and not merely what appears verified to him alone in his private thought;
אֲבָל בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ יָכוֹל לַחְשׁוֹב אַף דְּבָרִים הַמְּבוֹרָרִים רַק לוֹ,
though within his thought he may contemplate even matters clear only to himself,
וּבִכְגוֹן זֶה: לִבָּא לְפוּמָא לָא גַּלְיָא:
and in such an instance: the heart does not disclose its secrets to the mouth.

paragraphs.text: Context: The Midrash uses this expression for what Hashem has kept undisclosed, in its discussion of the time of redemption and Moshe’s burial place. Rav Tzadok applies the expression here to the distinction between an inward conviction and what one can responsibly express to others.

p: [לט] פְּעָמִים נִדְמֶה לָאָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ סִיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא לַדָּבָר שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה, אַל יִסְמוֹךְ עַל זֶה לוֹמַר שֶׁדָּבָר טוֹב הוּא,
Sometimes it appears to a person that he enjoys Heavenly assistance (siyata dishmaya) for the action he is undertaking; yet let him not rely upon this to conclude that it is necessarily a good thing,
דְּלוּלֵי כֵן לֹא הָיָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ, שֶׁרַק לַבָּא לִטָּהֵר מְסַיְּעִין אוֹתוֹ, אֲבָל בְּבָא לִטָּמֵא אָמְרוּ: רַק פּוֹתְחִין לוֹ וְלֹא מְסַיְּעִין.

arguing that were it not good, the Holy One would not have helped him—reasoning that only to one who comes to purify himself do they grant assistance, whereas to one who comes to defile himself they merely open the door without assisting.
דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם פְּעָמִים יֵשׁ דִּלְנִסָּיוֹן סִיְּעוּהוּ וְכַיּוֹצֵא,
For nonetheless, there are times when Heaven assists a person as a severe spiritual trial or the like,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִיכָה שֶׁאָמַר (שׁוֹפְטִים יז, יג): "עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יֵיטִיב ה' לִי, כִּי הָיָה לִי הַלֵּוִי לְכֹהֵן",
as written concerning Micah who declared: "Now I know that Hashem will prosper me, seeing I have a Levite as my priest" (Judges 17:13)
[וְשֵׁם זֶה בַּהֲוָיָ"ה שֶׁהוּא קֹדֶשׁ כִּדְאִיתָא בִּשְׁבוּעוֹת (לה:)],
and this divine Name was the Tetragrammaton which is holy, as brought in Shevuot 35b,
הֲרֵי חָשַׁב שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ סִיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא וְעֵזֶר אֱלֹהִי לְהַזְמִין לוֹ הַלֵּוִי לְכֹהֵן וּלְהֵיטִיב לוֹ.
so that Micah actually believed he had Heavenly assistance and divine aid in having the Levite arranged as his priest to bring him good fortune.
אָמְנָם רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כו) כִּי מִיכָה כָּפַר בְּ"אָנֹכִי",
True, our Sages of blessed memory stated in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu that Micah denied the principle of 'I am Hashem,'
וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר בֵּיאַרְתִּי שֶׁהוּא כְּפִירָה בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּבֵיאוּרוֹ.
and elsewhere I explained that this constitutes a denial of the intrinsic Jewish spiritual root, see there.
וְרַק בְּכָאֵלֶּה נִמְצָא זֶה, מִי שֶׁהוּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם שׁוֹרֶשׁ פּוֹרֶה וְכוּלֵי.
And this occurs only in such extreme cases, in one who is, Heaven forbid, a root producing venom and gall.
אֲבָל אַטּוּ אֲנַן מִי יָדְעִינַן מֵהֵיכָא קָאָתֵינַן וְכוּלֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב קִדּוּשִׁין עא:),
But do we know whence our soul originates? (Kiddushin 71b);
וְהָעֵצָה לָזֶה תְּפִלָּה וְתַחֲנוּנִים לְרַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם הַמּוֹעִילִים לַהֲפוֹךְ גַּם הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
and the remedy for this is prayer and supplication for Heavenly mercy which can transform even the primordial root itself,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל פָּסוּק: "לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא לִי אֱלֹהִים וְגוֹמֵר", דִּבְרִיאָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם הַיְינוּ יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן כַּנּוֹדָע.
as I explained elsewhere on the verse 'Create in me a clean heart, O God' (Psalms 51:12), for 'creation' everywhere denotes something from nothing, as is known.
וְעַיֵּין לְקַמָּן אוֹת ס"ד:
And see below, Section 64.

sections.en: Repentance and the Transformation of Sins into Merits

p: [מ] עִיקַּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה הוּא עַד שֶׁיָּאִיר ה' עֵינָיו שֶׁיִּהְיוּ זְדוֹנוֹת כִּזְכִיּוֹת,
The ultimate essence of repentance is reached when Hashem illuminates a person's eyes so that willful transgressions are transformed into merits,
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁיַּכִּיר וְיָבִין שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁחָטָא הָיָה גַּם כֵּן בִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
which means that he recognizes and understands that everything he sinned was likewise encompassed within the ultimate will of the Blessed Name,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת לא סוֹף עַמּוּד ב–לב עַמּוּד א): ג' פְּסוּקִים וְכוּלֵי, "וְאַתָּה הֲסִבֹּתָ אֶת לִבָּם אֲחֹרַנִּית", "וַאֲשֶׁר הֲרֵעֹתִי" וְכוּלֵי.
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Berakhot 31b–32a): three verses imply this, including "You have turned their heart back" (I Kings 18:37) and "whom I have afflicted" (Micah 4:6).
וּכְטַעַם יְדִיעָה וּבְחִירָה שֶׁבֵּיאַר הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל בְּסוֹף סֵפֶר אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף,
This mirrors the dynamic of divine Foreknowledge and human Free Will explained by the holy Ari at the end of Sefer Arba Meot Shekel Kesef:
שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת, כָּל אֶחָד בְּמָקוֹם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ:
that both are absolute truth, each within its own distinct domain;
בִּמְקוֹם הַבְּחִירָה שָׁם אֵין מָקוֹם לִידִיעָה,
in the realm of Free Choice there is no place for Foreknowledge,
וּבִמְקוֹם הַיְדִיעָה שָׁם בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין מָקוֹם לַבְּחִירָה.
while in the realm of Foreknowledge there is in ultimate truth no room for Free Choice.
וּכְשֶׁמַּשִּׂיג לְאוֹר זֶה הָעָצוּם,
And when a person attains this sublime, overwhelming illumination,
אָז שָׁבוּ כָּל זְדוֹנוֹתָיו בִּלְתִּי יוֹצְאִים מֵעוֹמֶק יְדִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
then all of his willful sins are seen as never having deviated from the unfathomable depth of the knowledge of the Blessed Name,
וְהוּא וְדַעְתּוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ הַכֹּל אֶחָד.
and He, His knowledge, and His will are entirely One.
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה כֵּן, הֲרֵי הַכֹּל זְכִיּוֹת,
And since the Blessed Name willed it so, behold all those deeds are converted into merits,
וְזוֹכֶה לְכַפָּרָה גְּמוּרָה שֶׁבְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
and he merits the absolute atonement of Yom Kippur,
שֶׁזֶּה סוֹד הַשָּׂעִיר לַעֲזָאזֵל,
which is the inner mystical secret of the scapegoat sent to Azazel:
שֶׁאִלּוּ עֲשָׂאוּהוּ הָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ הָיָה עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה גָּמוּר,
for had a person performed this act on his own initiative, he would be a complete idolater,
וְהוּא "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" שֶׁהוּא יְסוֹד כָּל הַמִּצְווֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וְכָל הָעֲבֵירוֹת וְהַהֲסָרוֹת מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
violating "You shall have no other gods," which is the foundation of all negative prohibitions, all sins, and all departures from the will of Hashem.
רַק שֶׁהַשָּׂעִיר הוּא עַל יְדֵי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא מִצְוָה לְשַׁלְּחוֹ לוֹ, נַעֲשָׂה עוֹד מִצְוָה וְלֹא עֲבֵירָה.
Yet because the scapegoat is dispatched through the explicit command and will of the Blessed Name, it becomes a supreme mitzvah rather than a sin.
וְכָךְ פֵּירְשׁוּהוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק מו),
And so our Sages of blessed memory explained (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 46),
וְעַיֵּין בָּרַמְבַּ"ן פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי,
and see Ramban in Parashat Acharei Mot:
שֶׁאָנוּ נוֹתְנִים חֵלֶק לַעֲזָאזֵל שֶׁהוּא הָרַע מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צִוָּה לָתֵת לוֹ,
that we offer a portion to Azazel—the side of evil—specifically because the Blessed Name commanded us to give it to him,
וְנִמְצָא הָעֲבֵירָה מִצְוָה:
and consequently the apparent sin is revealed to be a holy mitzvah.

p: [מא] "אָנֹכִי" קוֹדֵם לְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ",
"I am the Lord your God" precedes "You shall have no other gods,"
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת הַגְּמוּרָה בְּ"אָנֹכִי" מִצַּד אֱמוּנָה הַבְּרוּרָה בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא מָצוּי
for through complete and profound contemplation of "I am" arising from lucid faith in the Blessed Name that He is existent,
הוּא נִיצּוֹל מִ"לֹא יִהְיֶה" וְנִשְׁמָר מִכָּל מִינֵי הֲסָרוֹת וּנְזָקִין,
a person is saved from "You shall have no," and is preserved against all forms of spiritual departure and harm;
כִּי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא וַיֵּצֵא): עָשָׂה מִצְוָה אַחַת מוֹסְרִין לוֹ מַלְאָךְ אֶחָד לְשָׁמְרוֹ.
for our Sages of blessed memory stated (Midrash Tanchuma, Vayeitzei): "If one performs a single mitzvah, a single angel is assigned to him to guard him."
וְהִנֵּה מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה: כָּל הַמִּצְווֹת קִבְּלוּ עַל יְדֵי שָׁלִיחַ, נִמְסָר מַלְאָךְ;
And behold, it is measure for measure: for all the commandments that they received through an emissary Moses, an angel is assigned;
וְ"אָנֹכִי" וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה" שָׁמְעוּ מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה,
whereas "I am" and "You shall have no" they heard directly from the mouth of the Almighty,
לְכָךְ בִּשְׂכַר "אָנֹכִי" הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ שׁוֹמְרוֹ.
and therefore, in reward for "I am," the Holy One, blessed be He, guards him Himself.
וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר אָמְרוּ כִּי מִמִּצְוָה נִבְרָא מַלְאָךְ,
And elsewhere they stated that from a mitzvah an angel is created,
וּבְמִצְוַת "אָנֹכִי" נִבְרָא כִּבְיָכוֹל הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשְׁגָּחַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ בְּמוֹחוֹ וְדַעְתּוֹ שֶׁל זֶה,

yet through the commandment of "I am," there is created, as it were, the revelation of the personal providence of the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself within the mind and consciousness of this person,
בְּרִיאָה מַמָּשׁ יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן בְּמוֹחַ וְלֵב אָטוּם
an absolute creation of something from nothing (yesh me'ayin) within an obtuse brain and sealed heart,
לִהְיוֹת מָצוּי אֶצְלוֹ תָּמִיד
so that He is constantly present with him,
עַל יְדֵי אִתְעָרוּתָא כְּחֻדָּהּ שֶׁל מַחַט מִתַּתָּא
whereby through an awakening from below as narrow as the eye of a needle,
נִפְתַּח אַחַר כָּךְ כְּפִתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם:
it is subsequently opened wide like the portal of the Temple Hall.

Hashem’s ordering leaves repentance and mitzvot open even then.

p: [מב] בִּתְפִלָּה הוּא הָעִיקָּר הַחֵשֶׁק וְהָרָצוֹן לְהִתְפַּלֵּל וּלְהִתְחַנֵּן,
In prayer, the primary essence is the inner longing and passionate desire to pray and plead,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אַל תַּעַשׂ תְּפִלָּתְךָ קֶבַע אֶלָּא רַחֲמִים וְכוּלֵי",
as it is written: "Do not make your prayer a fixed routine, but supplications for mercy, etc." (Avot 2:13),
שֶׁהוּא עַצְמוֹ מַאֲמָרָם שִׁילְהֵי מְנָחוֹת בְּקָרְבָּנוֹת [שֶׁהַתְּפִלָּה דּוּגְמָתָן]:
which is identical to their teaching at the end of Menachot (110a) regarding sacrificial offerings which prayer mirrors:
"שֶׁלֹּא תֹאמַר אֶעֱשֶׂה רְצוֹנוֹ וְכוּלֵי, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: 'לִרְצֹנְכֶם תִּזְבָּחוּהוּ'",
"Lest you say: 'I will perform His will, etc.,' Scripture states: 'You shall slaughter it of your own free will (to your desire)'" (Leviticus 19:5),
דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כִּי אֵין הַקָּרְבָּן מִצְוָה,
meaning that the sacrificial offering is not a typical commanded obligation,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְלֹא צִוִּיתִים וְגוֹמֵר עַל דִּבְרֵי עוֹלָה וָזָבַח", וְכֵן בְּכָל מָקוֹם.
as it is written: "I spoke not unto your fathers... concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices" (Jeremiah 7:22), and likewise in numerous passages.
וְעַיֵּין בְּמוֹרֶה נְבוּכִים בְּטַעַם הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת.
And see the Guide for the Perplexed (3:32) regarding the rationale of sacrifices.
וְנוֹדַע מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב מַהֲרַ"ם אַלְשַׁקַר סִימָן קי"ז דְּכֵן הוּא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ, וְכָתַב מָשָׁל וְכוּלֵי עַיֵּין שָׁם,
And it is known what Maharam Alashkar wrote in Responsum 117 that this is found in the Midrash, citing a parable, see there:
דְּעִנְיַן הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת הוּא שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל הַתִּקְרֹבֶת נֶהֱנֶה מִמֶּנּוּ,
that the concept of sacrifices is that the recipient of an offering derives gratification from it,
וְכָל הָעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה – אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ נֶהֱנֶה וּמִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יְדֵי אוֹתוֹ קָרְבָּן כְּמוֹ אָדָם עַל יְדֵי מַאֲכָל;
and in all idolatry, that celestial force derives pleasure and gains strength through that sacrifice just as a person does through food;
וּמִתּוֹךְ שֶׁיָּדְעוּ בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כֵּן, הָיָה חֶשְׁקָם וְכָסְפָּם שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְהַהֲנוֹת כִּבְיָכוֹל לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and because they recognized this regarding idolatry, they harbored an intense yearning and desire to likewise bestow pleasure, as it were, upon the Blessed Name;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "לְמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיךָ תִכְסֹף", כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תְּצַוֶּה ב),
and concerning this it is stated: "You will yearn for the work of Your hands" (Job 14:15), as our Sages expounded (Midrash Tanchuma, Tetzaveh 2),
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִרְשָׁם בְּכָךְ שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כִּמְהַנִּים אוֹתוֹ.
and the Blessed Name permitted them to do so, that they might be considered as granting Him satisfaction.
רַק מִי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְכָךְ בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא נֶהֱנֶה בְּכָךְ, אֲבָל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין צָרִיךְ לְכָךְ,
However, one who truly needs it derives genuine nourishment from it, but the Blessed Name has no need for it;
וְלֹא תֹאמַר אֶעֱשֶׂה רְצוֹנוֹ וְכוּלֵי כִּבְכָל הַמִּצְווֹת,
so you must not say "I am doing His will, etc." as with all other commandments,
רַק "לִרְצוֹנְכֶם" – כְּפִי הָרָצוֹן וְהַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלָּכֶם, כָּךְ הוּא הַקָּרְבָּן.
but rather "to your desire"—in accordance with your own inner will and longing, so is the quality of the sacrifice.
רַק דְּמִזֶּה הוּא הַהֲנָאָה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: מֵהָרָצוֹן וְהַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁלָּהֶם לְהַהֲנוֹתוֹ.
The only gratification to the Blessed Name arises directly from this: from their heartfelt desire and longing to please Him.
וְכֵן הַתְּפִלָּה בִּמְקוֹם הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת,
So too is prayer, which stands in the place of the sacrifices:
שֶׁאֵין רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִבְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁיִּתְפַּלְּלוּ לְפָנָיו וִישַׁנּוּהוּ,
it is not the desire of the Blessed Name that human beings pray before Him to change His mind,
רַק הָרָצוֹן שֶׁלָּהֶם לְהִתְפַּלֵּל – זֶהוּ רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהָבֵן זֶה:
rather their very desire to pray—that itself is His blessed will; and understand this well.

p: [מג] פְּעָמִים יֵשׁ אָדָם עוֹמֵד בְּנִסָּיוֹן גָּדוֹל כָּל כָּךְ, עַד שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יֶחֱטָא,
At times a person faces a spiritual test of such overwhelming magnitude that it is virtually impossible for him not to sin,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר שָׁם (בְּרָכוֹת לב.): "מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה הַבֵּן וְכוּלֵי",
in the spirit of the Sages' words (Berakhot 32a): "What can the son do and not sin, etc.?",
וּבָזֶה הוּא נֶחְשָׁב אֹנֶס גָּמוּר דְּרַחֲמָנָא פַּטְרֵיהּ.
and in such a state it is legally deemed absolute duress (ones gamur), from which the Merciful One exempts him.
וְגַם בְּהַסָּתַת הַיֵּצֶר בְּתוֹקֶף עָצוּם שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְנַצְּחוֹ, שַׁיָּיךְ אֹנֶס
And even under the incitement of the evil inclination of such immense ferocity that it cannot be conquered, duress applies
[וְאִם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵסֵיב אֶת לִבּוֹ, הֲרֵי אֵין חֵטְא זֶה חֵטְא כְּלָל, רַק שֶׁרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה כָּךְ].
and if the Blessed Name turned his heart, then this sin is not a sin at all, but rather the will of the Blessed Name unfolded thus.
וְעַיֵּין מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּכְתוּבּוֹת (נא.) גַּבֵּי תְּחִלָּתוֹ בְּאֹנֶס:
And examine Ketubot (51b) regarding a violation that began under duress:
אֲפִילּוּ צוֹוַחַת לְבַסּוֹף שֶׁאִלְמָלֵא מַנִּיחָהּ הִיא שׂוֹכַרְתּוֹ, מוּתֶּרֶת לְבַעְלָהּ;
even if she cries out at the end that were he to let her go she would hire him, she remains permitted to her husband;
מַאי טַעְמָא? יֵצֶר אַלְבְּשַׁהּ;
what is the reason? Passion enclothed her;
הֲרֵי דְּזֶה מִתְחַשֵּׁב אֹנֶס גָּמוּר,
which proves that this is deemed complete duress,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מֵרְצוֹנָהּ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵצֶר גָּדוֹל כָּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר בָּאָדָם לְכָפְיוֹ, וְהוּא אֹנֶס גָּמוּר,
for even though it ended with her consent, an inclination of such ferocity is beyond human capacity to suppress, and constitutes total duress,
וְאֵין בָּזֶה עוֹנֶשׁ אַף דְּעָשָׂה אִיסּוּר, כֵּיוָן דְּהָיָה אָנוּס.
and bears no punishment even though a prohibition was transgressed, since one was under duress.
אֲבָל הָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהָעִיד עַל עַצְמוֹ בָּזֶה, כִּי אוּלַי עֲדַיִן הָיָה לוֹ כֹּחַ לִכְפּוֹת הַיֵּצֶר
However, a person cannot testify about himself in this regard, for perhaps he still possessed sufficient strength to master the inclination
[וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בָּזֶה מֵעִנְיַן זִמְרִי שֶׁטָּעָה בָּזֶה]:
as I heard concerning the episode of Zimri who erred in this very self-assessment.

p: [מד] מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ תְּשׁוּקָה גְּדוֹלָה לְתַאֲווֹת הַגּוּף, אַל יִתְעַצֵּב בָּזֶה לַחְשׁוֹב כַּמָּה פָּגוּם הוּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ תְּשׁוּקָה כָּל כָּךְ.
A person possessed of intense longing for physical pleasures must not be saddened by this, thinking how blemished he must be to harbor such desires.
כִּי אַדְּרַבָּא, הוּא כְּלִי מוּכָן לְתוֹקֶף אַהֲבַת וּתְשׁוּקַת דְּרִישַׁת הָאֱמֶת.
For on the contrary, he is a vessel ideally prepared for the intense love and passionate pursuit of the Truth.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 248:1: “The essence of a person is the desire in the heart, through which he has an advantage over the angels. This is called inclination: the good inclination and the evil inclination. When he strengthens his desire toward good, it is good; otherwise, the reverse. Our Sages said: Whoever is greater than his fellow has a greater inclination. For one person’s greatness over another is only according to the greatness of his desire for good, which is the power of inclination. The good inclination and the evil inclination stand opposite one another in the heart’s two chambers: according to the desire in his heart on the right for good, so it is on the left for evil. Therefore the evil inclination is also greater.”

p: [מה] כְּשֶׁחָטָא הַרְבֵּה עַד שֶׁנִּסְתַּם הַתְּשׁוּבָה, כִּי כְּבָר סוּגְּרוּ דַּלְתֵי לִבּוֹ,
When a person has sinned so exceedingly that the path of repentance seems blocked, because the gates of his heart have slammed shut,
עַל זֶה אָמַר: "בּוֹרֵא נִיב שְׂפָתָיִם שָׁלוֹם שָׁלוֹם",
concerning this Scripture proclaims: "He creates the utterance of the lips: Peace, peace" (Isaiah 57:19),
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בּוֹרֵא יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן הַדִּבּוּר שֶׁל "שָׁלוֹם שָׁלוֹם",
meaning that the Holy One, blessed be He, creates something from nothing the speech of "Peace, peace,"
שֶׁהוּא קַבָּלַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה, הֵיפֶךְ הַנֶּאֱמָר: "לָרְשָׁעִים אֵין שָׁלוֹם".

Rabbi Yochanan said: He has not fulfilled the commandment to be fruitful and multiply. We require ‘He formed it to be inhabited,’ and that is absent here.’

p: [מו] "וְלָרָשָׁע אָמַר אֱלֹהִים מַה לְּךָ לְסַפֵּר חֻקָּי".
"And unto the wicked God said: What right have you to recount My statutes?" (Psalms 50:16).
וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה יִדְווּ וְכוּלֵי,
And over this matter hearts faint,
כִּי הָעוֹבֵר עַל דִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים נִקְרָא רָשָׁע כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְבָמוֹת כ.).
for one who transgresses the words of the Scribes is termed wicked, as written (Yevamot 20a).
אֲבָל עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ הַקַּדְמוֹנִים מַאֲמַר חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים פו:):
Yet concerning this, the early masters applied the statement of our Sages (Pesachim 86b):
כָּל מַה שֶּׁיֹּאמַר בַּעַל הַבַּיִת עֲשֵׂה – חוּץ מִצֵּא.
"Whatever the host tells you, do—except: 'leave.'"
וְלֹא לְחִנָּם כָּתְבָה תּוֹרָה עִנְיַן הַמַּעְפִּילִים בְּפָרָשַׁת שְׁלַח,
And not in vain did the Torah record the episode of the Ma'apilim (those who presumed to ascend) in Parashat Shelach,
אֲשֶׁר כְּבָר הֶאֱמִינוּ בְּדִבְרֵי מֹשֶׁה, וְלָמָּה לֹא שָׁמְעוּ לוֹ בָּזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם "אַל תַּעֲלוּ וְגוֹמֵר"?
who already believed the words of Moses; why then did they disobey him when he instructed them "Do not go up, etc."?
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם חָשְׁבוּ שֶׁזֶּה בִּכְלַל "חוּץ מִצֵּא".
Rather, they reasoned that this fell under the rubric of "except: 'leave.'"
וְעַיֵּין בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, קס עַמּוּד א) הִמְלִיץ כָּל עִנְיַן מְרַגְּלִים עַל הַתּוֹרָה,
And see the Zohar (Part III, 160a) which allegorizes the entire episode of the Spies to the Torah,
וְהָיָה הָעוֹנֶשׁ שֶׁלֹּא יַשִּׂיגוּהָ,
where the punishment was that they would not attain it,
וְעַל זֶה הֶעְפִּילוּ לַעֲלוֹת אַף נֶגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and regarding this they dared to ascend even counter to the apparent will of the Blessed Name,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קה.): "חוּצְפָּתָא – מַלְכוּתָא בְּלָא תָּגָא"
as in the dictum of our Sages (Sanhedrin 105a): "Audacity is kingship without a crown"
[וּלְמָדוּהָ מִבִּלְעָם שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ הִסְכִּים הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי בִּלְעָם נִסְתַּכֵּל עַד עִקְבְּתָא דִּמְשִׁיחָא וּלְכָךְ יָדַע סוֹד זֶה].
which they derived from Balaam, where afterward the Blessed Name consented; for Balaam gazed unto the footsteps of the Messiah, and therefore grasped this secret.
פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּידוּעַ "מַלְכוּת" הוּא כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְ"כֶתֶר" הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
The explanation is: as is known, Malchut (Kingship) is the Congregation of Israel, while Keter (Crown) is the primordial root of Hashem's will,
וּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר: מֶמְשָׁלָה מֵעַצְמוֹ בְּלִי רְצוֹן הָרוֹצִים, וְהִתְקָרְבוּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעַצְמָם.
meaning sovereign initiative from oneself without dependent will, and the spontaneous drawing near of the Congregation of Israel on their own.
וְהֵם לֹא הִצְלִיחוּ בָּזֶה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֲכָלוּהָ פַּגָּה,
But the Ma'apilim did not succeed in this because they ate it unripe,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה מט:): "בְּעִקְּבוֹתָא דִּמְשִׁיחָא חוּצְפָּא יִסְגֵּא", שֶׁאָז הוּא הָעֵת לָזֶה
as our Sages stated (Sotah 49b): "In the footsteps of the Messiah audacity will increase," for only then is the proper hour for this
[וּלְעָתִיד: "נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר", וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ].
and in the future: "A woman shall court a man" (Jeremiah 31:21), and this is not the place to elaborate.
וּלְכָךְ אָמַר לָהֶם מֹשֶׁה: "וְהִוא לֹא תִצְלָח",
And therefore Moses said to them: "And it shall not prosper" (Numbers 14:41)—
נִרְאֶה שֶׁעֵצָה הוּא אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא תִצְלַח;
indicating that it is a valid concept, only that it would not prosper at that time;
וְדָיֵיק "וְהִוא" – שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם דָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "הִיא" וְלֹא אַחֶרֶת,
and he was precise in saying "and it" (ve-hi)—for everywhere our Sages expound: "it, but not another,"
שֶׁיֵּשׁ זְמַן אַחֵר שֶׁמַּצְלִיחַ,
teaching that there is another future time when it does prosper,
וְהוּא זְמַנֵּנוּ זֶה שֶׁהוּא עִקְבֵי מָשִׁיחַ:
and that is this present era of ours, which represents the footsteps of the Messiah.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Miketz 2:1: “As we heard from our holy master, of blessed memory, on the verse, “The Rock of Israel spoke to me: a righteous one rules over man, ruling through the fear of God”: “Rock” denotes firmness. Hashem gives firmness to the penitent’s heart, as though He had spoken to him personally, enabling him to rule over a righteous man. This means that even concerning matters of which Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said in the holy Zohar that repentance is ineffective, Heaven forbid, the penitent has the power to annul that judgment and repair them. “Ruling through the fear of God” also includes what was spoken by the Holy One, blessed be He, as when a heavenly voice declared, “Return, wayward children, except Acher.” Nevertheless, he could have repaired himself through repentance, because this is Hashem’s will. As the Shelah and Reishit Chokhmah wrote, this is what the Sages hinted at: “Do everything the master of the house tells you, except ‘Leave.’””

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 52:3-4: “This source is called “the revealed world,” “the Matron,” “the lower Mother,” and “Shekhinah,” from the expression “I shall dwell among them.” It is so called because this source is the beginning of the revelation of the light of the Infinite, which it draws down and illuminates into the worlds in a revealed manner. From this source, the particular light and vitality appropriate to each one is drawn forth, dwelling and clothing itself within them to give them life. All of them come only from the extension of vitality and light from this source called Shekhinah, like the extension of light from the sun.”

People from the border regions will wander from city to city, and no one will show them favor.’

sections.en: Directing Every Inner Faculty Toward Hashem

p: [מז] כָּל הַכֹּחוֹת הַנְּטוּעוֹת בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, אֵין לַחְשׁוֹב שֶׁהוּא רַע גָּמוּר וְשֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת הֶפְכּוֹ,
Regarding all the innate faculties planted within every soul of Israel, one must not imagine that any of them is pure evil requiring absolute eradication to its opposite;
כִּי אֵין לְךָ שׁוּם מִדָּה וְכֹחַ שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ צַד טוֹב גַּם כֵּן,
for you have no character trait or faculty that does not also possess a dimension of good,
רַק צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהּ כְּפִי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
one only needs to utilize it in accordance with the will of the Blessed Name.
וְאִם אֵינוֹ כְּפִי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, גַּם הַמִּדּוֹת טוֹבוֹת רָעוֹת,
And if it is not aligned with the will of the Blessed Name, even good traits become evil,
כְּמוֹ שָׁאוּל שֶׁנֶּעֱנַשׁ בַּעֲבוּר הָרַחְמָנוּת,
as with King Saul who was punished on account of misplaced mercy,
וּבְגִטִּין (נו.): עַנְוְתָנוּתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן אַבְקוּלַס הֶחֱרִיבָה וְכוּלֵי.
and in Gittin (56a): "The excessive humility of Rabbi Zechariah ben Avkulas destroyed our Temple, etc."
וּלְהֵיפֶךְ אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת סג.):
And conversely, our Sages stated (Shabbat 63a):
אִם רָאִיתָ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם נוֹקֵם וְנוֹטֵר כְּנָחָשׁ – חָגְרֵהוּ וְכוּלֵי,
"If you see a Torah scholar who avenges and bears a grudge like a serpent—gird him upon your loins, etc.,"
וְנָחָשׁ הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרַע בְּכַעַס.
though a serpent is the root of evil in anger.
וּבְתַלְמִיד חָכָם – רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר אֲשֶׁר כָּל מְגַמּוֹתָיו רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – אַדְּרַבָּה הוּא טוֹב מְאֹד,
But in a Torah scholar—meaning one whose entire aim is the will of the Blessed Name—on the contrary, it is "very good,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט): "טוֹב מְאֹד" – זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע.
along the lines of what our Sages said (Bereishit Rabbah 9): "'Very good'—this is the evil inclination."
וְכֵן בְּגַאֲוָה (בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דִּסְוֹטָה ה.): בְּשַׁמְתָּא מַאן דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ.
And likewise regarding pride (in the first chapter of Sotah 5a): "Under a ban of excommunication is one who possesses none of it."
וְלָכֵן הַנְּבִיאִים הָיוּ מְיַלְּלִים עַל אָבְדַן הָאֻמּוֹת: "לִבִּי לְמוֹאָב וְגוֹמֵר" וְכַיּוֹצֵא,
And therefore the Prophets wailed over the destruction of the nations: "My heart cries out for Moab, etc." (Isaiah 15:5) and the like,
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שִׁבְּחוּם עַל זֶה בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת בָּלָק).
and our Sages praised them for this in Midrash Rabbah (beginning of Parashat Balak).
וּבְוַדַּאי לֹא חָסוּ עַל אִיבּוּד גּוּפָם, כִּי "בַּאֲבֹד רְשָׁעִים רִנָּה"
And surely they did not mourn over the destruction of their physical bodies, for "when the wicked perish there is singing" (Proverbs 11:10)

[וְאוּלַי יִהְיֶה "לִבִּי" עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ה, ב): הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "צוּר לְבָבִי", וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה י:): הוּא אֵינוֹ שָׂשׂ],

and perhaps "my heart" is along the lines of the Sages' teaching (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2): the Holy One is the heart of Israel, as stated: 'God is the rock of my heart'; and the Sages stated (Megillah 10b): He Himself does not rejoice;
רַק יָדוּעַ: כָּל אֻמָּה הוּא כֹּחַ מְיוּחָד, ע' אֻמּוֹת וְע' כֹּחוֹת בַּנֶּפֶשׁ.
rather it is known: each nation represents a unique spiritual faculty, seventy nations corresponding to seventy faculties within the soul.
וּבַיּוֹם הַהוּא יִגְדַּל הַמִּסְפֵּד בְּאָבְדַן הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע גַּם כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סֻכָּה נב.),
And on that day the great lamentation will encompass the destruction of the evil inclination as well, as written (Sukkah 52a),
כִּי "יָפָה שָׁעָה אַחַת בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִכָּל [חַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא]", וְאָז יִהְיֶה בִּכְלָל.
for "better is one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than all the life of the World to Come," and then it will end.
וְאָבְדַן אֻמָּה פְּרָטִית הוּא אִבּוּד מֶמְשֶׁלֶת אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ פְּרָטִי
And the destruction of an individual nation represents the eradication of the dominion of that particular faculty
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנִּתְאוֹנֵן קֹהֶלֶת וְכֵן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שִׁילְהֵי שַׁבָּת עַל הַיַּלְדוּת,
analogous to Ecclesiastes and our Sages at the end of Shabbat lamenting the passing of youth,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ: זִקְנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים וְכוּלֵי דַּעְתָּן מִתְיַשֶּׁבֶת וְכוּלֵי,
even though we learned that elderly scholars become more settled in mind,
וּבִשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה ה) מֵחֲשִׁיבוּת הַזְּקֵנִים, וְכֵן בְּכָל מָקוֹם
and in Shemot Rabbah (end of Parashah 5) regarding the dignity of the elderly, and throughout Chazal—
אֶלָּא שֶׁפָּסַק הַחֶמְדָּה וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
merely because the youthful passion and drive of the inclination have ceased.
וְכֹחַ בִּלְעָם בַּחֲצִיפוּת שֶׁלָּמְדוּ מִמֶּנּוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קה.),
And the trait of Balaam lay in audacity, which our Sages derived from him (Sanhedrin 105a);
וְהוּא הָיָה רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם, דּוּגְמַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, קצג עַמּוּד ב),
and he was the foremost among the nations, the pagan counterpart to Moses our teacher in Israel, as taught in Zohar (Part III, 193b);
לְכָךְ הַכֹּחַ שֶׁהִשִּׂיג יְתוּקַּן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים,
therefore, the faculty that he attained will be refined and rectified within Israel in the End of Days,
וּבְעִקְבֵי מָשִׁיחַ אָז "חוּצְפָּא יִסְגֵּא" – יִתְגַּדֵּל וְיִהְיֶה בְּמַעֲלָה:
and in the footsteps of the Messiah, then "audacity will increase"—it will become elevated and transformed into a supreme holy virtue.

sections.en: Avoiding Wicked Company Even for a Mitzvah

p: [מח] לֹא יִתְחַבֵּר עִם רְשָׁעִים, וַאֲפִילּוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מִצְוָה,
One must not join with the wicked, even to perform a mitzvah;
וְכֵן הוּא מְפוֹרָשׁ בַּמְּכִילְתָּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּהִתְחַבֶּרְךָ [עִם אֲחַזְיָהוּ פָּרַץ ה' אֶת מַעֲשֶׂיךָ]" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב כ, לז),
and this is explicitly taught in the Mekhilta, as written: "Because you have joined with Ahaziah, Hashem has destroyed your works" (II Chronicles 20:37),
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְחַבֵּר עִמּוֹ לִלְחוֹם נֶגֶד אֲרָם.
even though he joined with him to wage war against Aram.
וְנֶאֱמַר: "בְּנִי, אַל תֵּלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ אִתָּם" (מִשְׁלֵי א, טו),
And Scripture warns: "My son, walk not in the way with them" (Proverbs 1:15),
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם "דֶּרֶךְ" בְּסֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵי רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר דֶּרֶךְ הַתּוֹרָה וְהַמִּצְווֹת.
and everywhere the word "way" (derekh) in Proverbs signifies the path of Torah and commandments.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא לה:) גַּבֵּי יוֹסֵף: "לִהְיוֹת עִמָּהּ" – לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And our Sages stated (Yoma 35b) concerning Joseph: "'to be with her'—in the World to Come,"
וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא הוּא רַק קִבּוּל שָׂכָר וְלֹא עוֹנֶשׁ, דְּזֶה אֵין נִקְרָא עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
and the World to Come is exclusively the reception of reward and not punishment, for punishment is not called the World to Come.
רַק שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת יוֹסֵף נָשָׂא בִּתָּהּ וּמֵהֶם יָצָא שֵׁבֶט בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף.
Only that in truth Joseph married her daughter Osnat, and from them emerged a tribe in Israel and the Messiah son of Joseph.
וְיוֹסֵף רָאָה גַּם כֵּן זֶה שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה יֵצֵא שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת גְּדוֹלָה כָּזוֹ,
And Joseph likewise foresaw that such an illustrious dynasty was destined to emerge from her;
רַק לֹא רָצָה לִהְיוֹת עִמָּהּ אֲפִילּוּ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
nevertheless, he refused to associate with her even for the sake of the World to Come.
דְּגַם שֶׁיְּהוּדָה זָנָה וְיָצָא מִמֶּנּוּ מְלָכִים וּנְבִיאִים, וְהָיָה זְנוּתוֹ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,

sections.en: The Place of Temptation and Personal Rectification

p: [מט] כָּל אֶחָד יֵדַע שֶׁבַּמֶּה שֶׁיִּצְרוֹ תּוֹקְפוֹ בְּיוֹתֵר, הוּא כְּלִי מוּכָן לְאוֹתָם דְּבָרִים בְּיוֹתֵר לִהְיוֹת נְקִיִּים וְזַכִּים אֶצְלוֹ.
Each person must know that in whatever realm his inclination attacks him most fiercely, he is a vessel specially prepared for those very matters to become exceptionally pure and refined within him.
וּבִדְבָרִים שֶׁהִרְבָּה לִפְשׁוֹעַ בָּהֶם, יֵדַע שֶׁהוּא כְּלִי מוּכָן לִהְיוֹת דַּיְיקָא בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר נָקִי וּבַר לֵבָב.
And in matters wherein he has sinned abundantly, he should know that he is a vessel prepared to become, precisely in that very thing, clean and pure of heart.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה כא) שֶׁבְּאֵבֶר שֶׁבּוֹ חָטָא, בּוֹ יַעֲשֶׂה מִצְווֹת;
And therefore they stated in Vayikra Rabbah (21:5) that with the very limb wherewith one sinned, with it he should perform mitzvot;
וְאֵין זֶה רַק תִּיקּוּן לָעֲבֵירָה הַקּוֹדֶמֶת מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה, אֲבָל הוּא גַּם תִּיקּוּן נַפְשׁוֹ בִּפְרָט,
and this is not merely a rectification for the prior transgression measure for measure, but it is also the individual rectification of his particular soul,
כִּי כָּל אֶחָד נִבְרָא לְתִיקּוּן אֵיזֶה דָּבָר פְּרָטִי אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ נִתְיַיחֲדָה נַפְשׁוֹ בִּפְרָט וְאֵין לָהּ חָבֵר
for each person was created to rectify a specific matter wherein his soul is uniquely distinguished, having no counterpart
[כְּמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִמְצָא פַּרְצוּפִים שָׁוִים, וּפַרְצוּף פָּנִים רוֹמֵז עַל צֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים דְּנֶפֶשׁ],
just as no two faces are identical, and the facial visage reflects the Divine image of the soul,
כְּנוֹדָע מַאֲמַר הַקַּדְמוֹנִים עַל מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת קיח:): "אֲבוּךְ בְּמַאי זָהִיר טְפֵי?".
as is known from the teachings of the early masters on the Talmudic query (Shabbat 118b): "In what matter was your father especially vigilant?"
וְעַל כָּזֶה אָמְרוּ (גִּטִּין מג.): אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְשַׁל,
And concerning this they said (Gittin 43a): "A person does not truly master words of Torah unless he has stumbled in them,"
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַמַּכְשֵׁלָה הוּא מֵבִין שֶׁלְּכָךְ נוֹצַר – לְתַקֵּן אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר.
meaning that through the stumbling he understands that for this purpose was he created: to rectify that specific thing.

הֲלֹא תִרְאֶה: אָחָז חָתַם הַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (קג:) וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מב) שֶׁמָּנַע תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן, אָמַר: אִם אֵין גְּדָיִים וְכוּלֵי,

Behold, consider: King Ahaz sealed the Torah, as written in Sanhedrin (103b) and in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 42) that he locked school children out of Torah study, saying: "If there are no kids, there are no goats, etc.,"
לְפִי שֶׁהוּא הָיָה כְּלִי מוּכָן לְהוֹלִיד חִזְקִיָּה שֶׁהָיָה מַרְבִּיץ תּוֹרָה בְּיוֹתֵר,
because he was the vessel prepared to father Hezekiah, who disseminated Torah to the utmost degree,
כִּדְאִיתָא סוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּבָבָא קַמָּא וּפֶרֶק ב דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כ.), וְעַד שֶׁלֹּא נִמְצָא עַם הָאָרֶץ בְּיָמָיו כִּדְאִיתָא בְּחֵלֶק (צד:) עַיֵּין שָׁם – מַמָּשׁ הַהִיפּוּךְ:

as stated at the end of the first chapter of Bava Kamma and in Sanhedrin (20a), to the extent that not an ignorant person could be found in his days, as brought in Sanhedrin (94b), see there—literally the complete opposite!

paragraphs.text: Shevet Musar 1:4 connects the particular mitzvah a person most resists with a task of repair for which that soul returned. It also treats a preferred area of Torah study as a clue to that task. The Talmudic sages’ special care for particular mitzvot illustrates recognition followed by intensified effort. The practical response to resistance is to strengthen observance, not to abandon it.

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 21:5 counsels making bundles of mitzvot corresponding to bundles of transgressions. Its examples redirect eyes, tongue, hands, heart, and feet toward their proper mitzvot, and answer false witness and strife with testimony to Hashem and pursuit of peace. The point is active repair through the same faculties that had been misused. Its further discussion urges planning opportunities for mitzvot and sustained Mishnah study.

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 16:5: “The moment of the inclination’s enticement between one spiritual level and another is the descent that the righteous undergo for the sake of ascent, as is known concerning “A righteous person falls seven times and rises.” This was the meaning of Rephidim after the splitting of the sea, when they were proceeding to the giving of the Torah, a higher level. When a person succeeds in overcoming it immediately, the descent is scarcely felt at all: he falls for only a moment and rises at once. There is only a momentary slackening; he immediately remembers, takes it to heart, and strengthens himself like a lion for Hashem’s service. The greater the subsequent ascent, however, the greater the preceding descent. For a great ascent the inclination grows stronger, one corresponding to the other, and the power that overcomes it is correspondingly greater.”

sections.en: Salvation in Its Time and Before Its Time

p: [נ] עַל כָּל מִינֵי יְשׁוּעוֹת שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לָאָדָם יֵשׁ "בְּעִתָּהּ" וַ"אֲחִישֶׁנָּה": זָכוּ – "אֲחִישֶׁנָּה", לֹא זָכוּ – "בְּעִתָּהּ".

Concerning all manner of salvations granted by the Blessed Name to man, there exists "in its time" (be'itah) and "I will hasten it" (achishenah) (Isaiah 60:22): if they merit—"I will hasten it"; if they do not merit—"in its time."
וּ"בְעִתָּהּ" הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁכְּבָר חָסֵר לוֹ הַדָּבָר וְהוּא צָמֵא וּמִשְׁתּוֹקֵק וְנִצְרָךְ לָהּ
And "in its time" means when the matter is already acutely lacking to him and he is thirsty, yearning, and in desperate need of it

[וְכֵן הוּא "בְּעִתָּהּ" לְעִנְיַן בִּיאַת מָשִׁיחַ, כַּאֲשֶׁר יִהְיוּ הַכֹּל צְמֵאִים לִישׁוּעָתוֹ וְלֹא יִהְיֶה שׁוּם עֵצָה אַחֶרֶת לִישׁוּעַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּמוּבָן לַמַּשְׂכִּיל כַּמָּה מַאֲמָרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בָּזֶה].

and likewise is "in its time" regarding the advent of the Messiah, when all will be thirsting for his salvation and no other remedy remains for Israel's deliverance, as understood to the wise from numerous rabbinic teachings.
וַ"אֲחִישֶׁנָּה" הַיְינוּ "טֶרֶם יִקְרָאוּ", שֶׁמַּקְדִּים רְפוּאָה לַמַּכָּה.
Whereas "I will hasten it" corresponds to "Before they call I will answer" (Isaiah 65:24), wherein He prepares the cure prior to the blow.
וְזֶה שֶׁרָמַז רָבָא לְרַב עִילִישׁ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קלג:) בַּמֶּה שֶׁקָּרָא עָלָיו "בְּעִתָּהּ אֲחִישֶׁנָּה",
And this is what Rava hinted to Rav Ilish (Bava Batra 133b) when applying the verse "in its time I will hasten it" to him,
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה לַ"אֲחִישֶׁנָּה",
meaning that he did not merit "I will hasten it,"
אֲבָל עַל כָּל פָּנִים לְ"בְעִתָּהּ" – לָזֶה זוֹכֶה כָּל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, אַף הַלֹּא זָכָה,
but at any rate to "in its time"—to this every soul among Israel merits, even one who has not otherwise merited;
שֶׁ"בְּעִתָּהּ" מַזְמִין לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַיְשׁוּעָה.
for "in its time" the Blessed Name unfailingly provides the salvation.
וְאִם יִרְאֶה שֶׁאֵין מַזְמִין, זֶה לְאוֹת שֶׁעֲדַיִן אֵין צָרִיךְ לָהּ וְיוּכַל לִהְיוֹת זוּלָתָהּ:
And if one perceives that He does not provide it, this serves as a sign that he does not truly need it yet, and is capable of enduring without it.
