sections.en: Divine Help Beyond the Strength of Human Effort

p: [נא] כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָדָם בִּשְׁבִירַת הַיֵּצֶר בַּתַּאֲווֹת נִקְרָא חֵן וְיוֹפִי לְבַד, שֶׁהוּא שֶׁקֶר וָהֶבֶל שֶׁאֵינוֹ קִיּוּם לָעַד,
All of man's self-effort in breaking the inclination regarding bodily desires is called mere grace and beauty, which is deceitful and vain, possessing no eternal endurance;
כִּי הַיֵּצֶר מִתְגַּבֵּר בְּכָל יוֹם, וְאוּלַי מָחָר לֹא יְנַצְּחֶנּוּ.
for the evil inclination renews its strength every day, and perhaps tomorrow he will not overcome it.
רַק הָעִיקָּר לְבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּעֶזְרוֹ, שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִבְטָח נֶאֱמָן, כִּי גוֹאֲלוֹ חָי.
Rather, the essential foundation is to plead before the Blessed Name to be his assistance, which constitutes a steadfast refuge, for his Redeemer lives.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין כ.): "שֶׁקֶר הַחֵן" – זֶה יוֹסֵף
And this is what they said (Sanhedrin 20a): "'Grace is deceitful'—this refers to Joseph"
[אֵינוֹ יוֹפִי גָּמוּר, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה לו:) שֶׁיָּצְאוּ טִפִּין, לָכֵן נִקְרָא שֶׁקֶר],
for it was not an absolute flawlessness, as our Sages stated in Sotah 36b that drops of seed emerged from his fingernails; therefore it was termed deceitful,
"וְהֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי" – זֶה בֹּעַז, שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם גַּם כֵּן שֶׁנִּתְקַשָּׁה וְהָיָה לוֹ תַּאֲוָה וְיֵצֶר, רַק הִתְאַמֵּץ נֶגְדּוֹ, וּלְכָךְ הָיָה רַק שָׁעָה אַחַת.

"'and beauty is vain'—this refers to Boaz," for they said there as well that his bodily nature hardened and he experienced desire and temptation, only that he braced himself against it, and therefore it lasted only an hour.
אֲבָל "אִשָּׁה [יִרְאַת ה' הִיא תִתְהַלָּל]" – זֶה פַּלְטִי, שֶׁהָיָה הוֹלֵךְ וּבוֹכֶה עַל מִצְוָה דַּאֲזָלָה מִינֵיהּ,
But "'a woman that fears Hashem, she shall be praised'—this refers to Palti," who went weeping over a mitzvah that had departed from him,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יוֹסֵף וּבֹעַז וַדַּאי הָיוּ רוֹצִים יוֹתֵר שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ בְּאוֹתוֹ נִסָּיוֹן;
unlike Joseph and Boaz who surely would have preferred not to have faced that trial;
כִּי הוּא נִקְרָא פַּלְטִיאֵל, שֶׁפְּלָטוֹ וְכוּלֵי, זָכָה לְסִיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא וְלֹא מֵהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ:
for he was named Paltiel because God delivered him (pelato), meriting miraculous Heavenly assistance and not merely relying on his own effort.

sections.en: Divine Providence in a Generation of Wickedness

p: [נב] אַל יִתְמַהּ הָאָדָם אִם יִרְאֶה רְשָׁעִים מִתְרַבִּים בָּעוֹלָם וְהוֹלְכִים וּמִתְגַּדְּלִים בְּכָל יוֹם,
A person must not be astonished if he sees the wicked multiplying in the world and constantly growing in prominence every day,
כִּי יֵדַע שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בַּעַל הַכֶּרֶם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פג:), וְיוֹדֵעַ טִיבוֹ שֶׁל כֶּרֶם יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנּוּ, וּמְתַקֵּן צְרָכָיו בְּכָל עֵת וָרֶגַע.

for he should know that the Blessed Name is the Owner of the vineyard (Bava Metzia 83b), and He understands the nature of His vineyard far better than man, rectifying its needs at every single moment.
וְהִנֵּה רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צח.) אָמְרוּ שֶׁבֶּן דָּוִד אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיָּבוֹא בְּדוֹר שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ חַיָּיב, דְּיַעֲמִיד מֶלֶךְ קָשֶׁה כְּהָמָן שֶׁיָּשׁוּבוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה.

And behold, our Sages of blessed memory stated (Sanhedrin 98a) that the Son of David may arrive in a generation that is entirely guilty, wherein He will set up a monarch harsh as Haman so that they return in repentance.
וַהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: אֵיזֶה דּוֹר חָבִיב מִכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת? זֶה דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁזָּכוּ לְקַבָּלַת תּוֹרָה;
And behold, our Sages asked: Which generation is most beloved of all generations? It is the Generation of the Wilderness, because they merited receiving the Torah;
וְכֵן עַל דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמְרוּ (מוֹעֵד קָטָן ט.) שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׂרוּ לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁזָּכוּ לְבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ;

and likewise regarding the generation of King Solomon, peace be upon him, they said (Moed Katan 9a) that they were assured life in the World to Come because they merited the construction of the Holy Temple;
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ וַדַּאי יִהְיֶה חָבִיב,
and it goes without saying that the generation of the Messiah will certainly be beloved,
וְאֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֻּלּוֹ חַיָּיב וְיִתְהַפְּכוּ לְדוֹר חָבִיב עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְבִיאֵם לִתְשׁוּבָה,
yet it is possible that it will be entirely guilty and subsequently be transformed into a beloved generation through the Blessed Name bringing them to repentance;
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתָם מִמָּקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת.
and perforce the primordial root of their souls stems from a loftier source than all other generations.
דְּבֶאֱמֶת כָּל חֲטָאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינָם בְּעֶצֶם,
For in truth, all sins of Israel are not part of their essential nature,
רַק הִמְשִׁילוּם רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד.) לְאָסָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּינֵי חִילְפֵי,
but our Sages compared them (Sanhedrin 44a) to a myrtle standing among briers,
וְלָכֵן הֵם הַיִּסּוּרִים עַל יְדֵי הַחֵטְא שֶׁהַחוֹחַ עוֹקְצָהּ;
and therefore the suffering brought on by sin is simply the thorn pricking it;
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁיִּשָּׂרְפוּ הַחוֹחִים שֶׁסְּבִיבוֹת, תִּשָּׁאֵר הַשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה בִּשְׁלֵימוּתָהּ,
but when the encircling thorns are burned away, the rose will remain in its full perfection,
וְאַדְּרַבָּה, שׁוֹשַׁנָּה שֶׁבֵּין הַחוֹחִים חֲשׁוּבָה יוֹתֵר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, קפט עַמּוּד ב)
and on the contrary, a rose nurtured among thorns is far more precious, as written in Zohar II:189b
[וַאֲתָאן לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה עֲדִיפֵי].
and we arrive at the opinion that penitents are greater.
וּתְשׁוּבָה אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּרֶגַע אֶחָד כִּדְמוּכָח בְּפֶרֶק ב דְּקִדּוּשִׁין (מט:),
And repentance can take place in a single split second, as demonstrated in Kiddushin 49b;
וְאָנוּ מְבַקְּשִׁים "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ וְגוֹמֵר", רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צוֹוֵחַ "שׁוּבוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה סוֹף אֵיכָה),
and we plead "Bring us back, etc.," while the Blessed Name cries out "Return unto Me, etc." (Midrash Rabbah, end of Eichah),
וּמִסְּתָמָא בְּדוֹר שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אָז "דִּידַן נָצַח",
and presumably in a generation entirely guilty, perforce the verdict "our side has triumphed" will prevail;
וּכְשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִרְצֶה, הֲרֵי בְּרֶגַע אֶחָד יִכְלוּ כָּל הַקּוֹצִים הַסּוֹבְבִים וְיִהְיֶה הַכֹּל כִּרְצוֹנוֹ,
and when the Blessed Name wills it, in one instant all the encircling thorns will be consumed, and all will be according to His will,
וְיִתְגַּלֶּה שֶׁגַּם מַה שֶּׁקּוֹדֶם הָיָה הַכֹּל לְצוֹרֶךְ:
and it will become revealed that even all that came before was necessary and purposeful.

p: [נג] דִּבּוּר שֶׁל חוֹל הַמּוּרְגָּל בְּפִי הָאָדָם וּמַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵיהּ, הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מַמָּשׁ אֲפִילּוּ אֵצֶל אִישׁ הַהֲמוֹנִי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
A mundane spoken phrase that is habitual in a person's mouth and constantly on his tongue is actual Torah, even for an ordinary, simple Jew;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּרְאֶה הַרְבֵּה בַּתַּלְמוּד מֵבִיא: "דְּאָמְרֵי אֱינָשֵׁי", וְהוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
as we repeatedly see in the Talmud where it introduces "as people commonly say," and it cites a verse of Torah;
וּבְפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (ז.) הַרְבֵּה: "הַהוּא דַּהֲוָה קָאָמַר וְאָזֵיל וְכוּלֵי, וַאֲמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: קְרָא כְּתִיב".
and in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (7a) multiple instances appear: "There was a certain man who used to say, etc., and Samuel remarked: It is explicitly written in Scripture."
כִּי כָּל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לוֹ אֲחִיזָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מְיוּחֶדֶת כַּנּוֹדָע,
For every soul of Israel has a unique grasp in a specific portion of Torah, as is known,
וּבְדִבּוּר שֶׁמַּרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵיהּ זֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ
and in the phrase habitual on his tongue lies the root of his soul

[כִּי הַדִּבּוּר הוּא יְסוֹד הַנֶּפֶשׁ, תַּרְגּוּם "נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה" – "רוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּפְסִיקְתָּא: אֵין בֵּין צַדִּיקִים הַחַיִּים לַמֵּתִים אֶלָּא הַדִּבּוּר, זֶהוּ יְסוֹד הַחַיּוּת].

for speech is the foundation of the soul, the Targum of 'a living soul' being 'a speaking spirit'; and as written in the Pesikta: between the living righteous and the deceased there is only speech, which is the bedrock of vitality.
וּמִזֶּה יוּכַל הָאָדָם לַעֲמוֹד עַל שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ לָדַעַת מַה עִנְיָנוֹ בְּזֶה הָעוֹלָם.
And from this a person can comprehend the root of his soul to discern his specific purpose in this world.

sections.en: The Name of Israel and Jewish Identity

p: (אוֹת נד חָסֵר בְּכַמָּה דְּפוּסִים וְנוֹסַף כָּאן מִכְּתַב יָד)
(Section 54 is absent in some printings and added here from manuscript)
עִיקַּר הַיַּהֲדוּת – בִּקְרִיאַת שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל.
The core essence of Jewish identity consists in bearing the name of Israel.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "זֶה [יֹאמַר לַה' אָנִי, וְזֶה יִקְרָא בְשֵׁם יַעֲקֹב, וְזֶה יִכְתֹּב יָדוֹ לַה',] וּבְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכַנֶּה" (יְשַׁעְיָה מד, ה).

As it is said: "One shall say: 'I am the Lord's'; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord, and surname himself by the name of Israel" (Isaiah 44:5).
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ רַק מַעֲלָה זוֹ שֶׁמְּכֻנֶּה בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל – דַּי.
Even if he possesses no virtue other than being titled by the name of Israel—it is sufficient.
וּמָצִינוּ בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כְּלָל גָּדוֹל (שַׁבָּת סח:) גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר בֵּין הָאֻמּוֹת, וּמֵבִיא חַטָּאת עַל הַחֵלֶב וְהַדָּם וְהַשַּׁבָּת וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,

And we find at the beginning of the chapter Klal Gadol (Shabbat 68b) concerning a convert who converted while living among the gentiles, and brings a sin-offering for consuming fat, blood, desecrating Shabbat, and idolatry;
עַיֵּין שָׁם דְּלֹא יָדַע כְּלָל שֶׁזֶּה אֲסוּרָה, וַאֲפִילּוּ עַל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְשַׁבָּת.
see there, for he did not even know that these were forbidden, including idolatry and Shabbat.
וְנִמְצָא שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע כְּלָל מִכָּל הַתּוֹרָה, וּבַמֶּה הוּא גֵּר לְהִתְחַיֵּיב חַטָּאת? רַק בִּקְרִיאַת שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל דַּי.

Thus it turns out he knew nothing of the entire Torah, yet through what was he an authentic convert to be liable for a sin-offering? Solely through calling himself by the name of Israel is it sufficient.
וּבָזֶה יוּבַן מַה דְּיֵהָרֵג וְאַל יַעֲבֹר עַל הֲמָרַת דָּת לִהְיוֹת יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
And through this one can understand why it is ruled that one must be killed rather than transgress by converting to Islam,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם אֵין עוֹבְדִים עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֲפִילּוּ בְּשִׁיתּוּף כַּנּוֹדָע, וְכֵן נִזְהָרִים עַל גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים,
even though they do not practice idolatry even in associative form (shituf), and likewise avoid forbidden sexual unions and bloodshed,
וְאֵין כּוֹפִין כְּלָל עַל אוֹתָן שָׁלֹשׁ עֲבֵירוֹת דְּיֵהָרֵג וְאַל יַעֲבֹר.
so that they do not coerce him at all regarding the classical three cardinal sins of martyrdom.
אֲבָל הֲמָרַת שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַד, זֶה שָׁקוּל כְּכָל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ וּכְנֶגֶד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים, וְעַיֵּין בָּרַדְבַּ"ז מִזֶּה.
Yet the renunciation of the name of Israel alone is equivalent to the entire Torah and balances against idolatry, sexual immorality, and murder; and see the Radbaz on this.

וְלָכֵן גַּם אֵצֶל הַהֲמוֹן הוּא פְּסוּל מִשְׁפָּחָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ מוּמָר בַּמִּשְׁפָּחָה, וְאֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין אִם יֵשׁ בָּהּ רָשָׁע גָּמוּר הָעוֹבֵר עַל כָּל עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הֵמִיר.

Therefore among the common people it is considered a genealogical flaw to have an apostate in the family, while they are not concerned if there is a wicked sinner violating all biblical prohibitions so long as he has not converted.
וְכֵן דּוֹרוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הָיוּ עוֹבְדִים עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא הֵמִירוּ,
And so the early biblical generations practiced idolatry, yet they never exchanged the name of Israel;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "חֲבוּר עֲצַבִּים אֶפְרָיִם, הַנַּח לוֹ" (הוֹשֵׁעַ ד, יז),
and concerning this it was stated: "Ephraim is joined to idols; let him alone" (Hosea 4:17),
שֶׁהֵם בְּחִיבּוּר אֻמָּה אַחַת וְלֹא נִתְפָּרְדוּ לְהִתְחַבֵּר עִם הַגּוֹיִם וְלִהְיוֹת בִּכְלָלָם:
because they remained bound as one single nation, never separating to merge with the gentiles and be counted among them.

sections.en: Remembering the Commandments in the Heart

p: [נה] עִיקַּר הָעֲבֵירוֹת בָּאִים מֵחֲמַת הַשִּׁכְחָה, שֶׁהוּא בַּלֵּב כִּדְאִיתָא בִּמְגִילָּה (יח.),
The root of sins arises from forgetfulness, which resides in the heart (Megillah 18a),
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ זוֹכֵר בַּמּוֹחַ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ זוֹכֵר בַּלֵּב;
for even if one remembers in the brain, he fails to remember in the heart;
כִּי אִלּוּ הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת זוֹכֵר בְּהַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צִוָּה עַל זֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כֵּן, אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל שֶׁהָיָה עוֹשֶׂה,
for had he truly remembered with heartfelt feeling that the Blessed Name commanded not to do this, it would be impossible for him to do it,
רַק שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר מַעֲלִימוֹ מִלִּבּוֹ, כְּעִנְיַן "שָׁמַנְתָּ עָבִיתָ וְגוֹמֵר".
only that the inclination conceals it from his heart, as in "you grew fat, you grew thick, etc." (Deuteronomy 32:15).
תֵּדַע, שֶׁמִּצְוַת צִיצִית הוּא לִזְכּוֹר עַל יָדוֹ מִצְוֹת ה',
You may know this, for the mitzvah of tzitzit is specifically to remember through it the commandments of Hashem,
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְנָחוֹת מד.) בְּמַעֲשֶׂה דְּתַלְמִיד שֶׁזָּכַר עַל יְדֵי הַצִּיצִית,
and our Sages stated (Menachot 44a) in the narrative of the student who remembered by virtue of his tzitzit;
וְשָׁם הָיָה מֵזִיד וְיוֹדֵעַ, רַק שֶׁעָמְדוּ הַצִּיצִית נֶגְדּוֹ, שֶׁנִּתְחַדֵּשׁ לוֹ הַזְּכִירָה רַק מִן הַמּוֹחַ לַלֵּב.
and there he was willful and knowledgeable, yet the tzitzit slapped him in the face so that remembrance was renewed from the brain into the heart.
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ הַקַּדְמוֹנִים דְּלָכֵן נִסְמַךְ פָּרָשַׁת צִיצִית לַמְקוֹשֵׁשׁ, שֶׁלֹּא יֶאֱרַע עוֹד כָּזֶה לִשְׁכּוֹחַ שֶׁהוּא שַׁבָּת, וַהֲרֵי מְקוֹשֵׁשׁ מֵזִיד הָיָה.

And so the early masters said that for this reason the passage of tzitzit was juxtaposed to the wood-gatherer, so that such an event of forgetting that it is Shabbat would not recur, even though the gatherer acted willfully.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּנְדָרִים (ח.): נִשְׁבָּעִים לְקַיֵּים הַמִּצְווֹת,
And therefore they said in Nedarim 8a: one may swear to fulfill a mitzvah,
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמוּשְׁבָּע וְעוֹמֵד מֵהַר סִינַי – לְזָרוֹזֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ;
and even though he is already adjured from Mount Sinai—it serves to invigorate himself;
וּמַה זֵּירוּז הוּא? אֲבָל הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ:
and what kind of dynamic is this? It is precisely as we have explained.

With the mouth.”

Although every Israelite truly believes in the reality of His providence, blessed be He, and all the details of the principles of faith, it is nevertheless not yet rooted in the heart so as to be revealed through the powers of action that issue from the heart, such that this faith will never be forgotten.”

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 220:1: “Concerning tzitzit it is explicitly stated, “You shall see it,” and “You shall not stray,” and so forth. The wording “You shall not stray” does not imply that the thought will be completely uprooted from the heart, but that one will have the strength to reject it. For as long as a person remembers the yoke of Heaven’s kingship, the yoke of Torah and the yoke of mitzvot that rest upon him, he can readily rebuke the inclination and reject every thought outside this. The inclination’s activity is only to make him forget this. As they said in Nedarim 32b, when the evil inclination is active no one remembers the good inclination, as it is said, “No person remembered,” and so forth. At that time the good thoughts of the unity of the Creator, blessed be He, are forgotten from the heart and are not recalled.”

paragraphs.text: Ramban on Numbers 30:3:1: “Oaths, however, serve only to prohibit what is otherwise permitted. They do not apply at all to a matter already commanded: neither to violating a negative commandment nor to keeping it, nor to neglecting a positive commandment, such as “I swear that I will not make a sukkah” or “I will not put on tefillin.” They do not take effect even for fulfilling a positive commandment. If someone swears to fulfill the mitzvah and does not fulfill it, he incurs no liability on account of the oath—neither lashes nor an offering. It is simply permitted to stir oneself to action, as it is written, “I have sworn and shall uphold it, to keep Your righteous ordinances.””

Rather, it makes him forget the severity of the prohibition and presents reasons why it is no transgression at all. This is why Nedarim 8a says that one may swear to fulfill the mitzvot. Vayikra Rabbah 23 and Midrash Ruth, on the verse “As the Lord lives,” say that Joseph, David and Boaz swore against their inclination. Against this the new oath is effective.”

p: [נו] הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נָתַן הַתּוֹרָה בְּעַל כָּרְחָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּשַׁבָּת פֶּרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
The Blessed Name gave the Torah against the will of Israel, as our Sages expounded in Shabbat 88a,
וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּיָד חֲזָקָה... אֶמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיכֶם"
and so in the future, as it is written: "With a mighty hand... will I rule over you" (Ezekiel 20:33)
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה פֶּרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קה.) קְרָאוּהוּ "רִתְחָא",
and our Sages in Sanhedrin 105a termed this "wrathful fervor";
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת פֶּרֶק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עַל פָּסוּק "כִּי אַתָּה אָבִינוּ" שֶׁיִּצְחָק הוּא הַגּוֹאֵל עַל יְדֵי מִדָּתוֹ.
and therefore they stated in Shabbat 89b on the verse "For You are our Father" that Isaac is the redeemer through his attribute of Gevurah.
וְכֵן אֵצֶל כָּל פְּרָט, הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹלֵחַ לוֹ הִרְהוּרֵי תְשׁוּבָה וּמַחֲשָׁבוֹת שֶׁל קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם בְּעַל כָּרְחוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא מֵרְצוֹנוֹ.
And likewise for each individual, the Blessed Name sends him stirrings of repentance and thoughts of accepting the yoke of Heaven against his will.
רַק גַּם לָזֶה צָרִיךְ הַכָנָה וְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא קְצָת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם הַכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, וְגָלוּתֵינוּ לְבִיאַת מָשִׁיחַ.
Only for this too some preparation and an awakening from below are required, just as the Egyptian exile prepared for the Giving of the Torah, and our exile prepares for the coming of the Messiah.
שֶׁלָּזֶה שֶׁל מְלוּכָה בְּעַל כָּרְחוֹ, הַהַכָנָה הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהוּא יִסּוּרִין שֶׁשּׁוֹלֵחַ.
For this forced dominion, the preparation likewise stems from the Blessed Name, namely the afflictions He sends.
וּלְכָךְ צָרִיךְ כָּל אֶחָד לְיִסּוּרִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּעֵרָכִין (טז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב).
And therefore everyone requires afflictions, as written in Arachin 16b.
וְהַיִּסּוּרִים הֵם גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד הָרִתְחָא מִמִּדַּת גְּבוּרָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
And afflictions likewise emerge from the fervor of His attribute of Gevurah.
וְיֵשׁ אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא הַמּוֹעִיל לָזֶה, וְהוּא הַיִּרְאָה, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִמִּדָּה זוֹ,
And there is an awakening from below that aids this, which is fear/awe, also deriving from this attribute,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מְעוֹרֵר לְמַעְלָה לִמְשׁוֹל עָלָיו בְּעַל כָּרְחוֹ כְּמוֹ אָדוֹן עַל עֶבֶד.
through which he arouses Above to rule over him against his will like a master over a servant.
וְזֶהוּ "מָה ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ שֹׁאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה", וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יַדְרִיכְךָ בַּתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת בְּעַל כָּרְחֲךָ.
And this is "What does Hashem your God ask of you but to fear," and subsequently the Blessed Name will guide you in Torah and commandments against your will.
וְזֶהוּ מִצְוַת צִיצִית עַל זֶה, שֶׁהִיא לְיִרְאָה כַּנּוֹדָע, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר סוֹף שְׁלַח דִּתְכֵלֶת הִיא יִרְאָה,
And this is the purpose of the mitzvah of tzitzit, which promotes fear, as written in the Zohar (end of Shelach) that techelet represents fear,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא זְכִירַת כָּל הַמִּצְווֹת אַף בְּעַל כָּרְחוֹ, כְּעוֹבָדָא דִּמְנָחוֹת:
and through this comes the remembrance of all commandments even against one's will, like the episode in Menachot.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Bo 11:1: ““Israel His dominions”: dominion denotes rule without consent, as they explain “Will you reign over us, or will you indeed rule over us?” Likewise, “For kingship belongs to Hashem, and He rules over the nations”: among them Hashem is called a ruler. It is written, “Surely with a strong hand … I will reign over you,” and at the giving of the Torah He held the mountain over them like a vat. Nevertheless, it is written, “They gathered at Your feet.” This means that at their root Israel wanted to be compelled, and at the root this is the quality of kingship.”

paragraphs.text: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 3:6: “Circumcision is the self-restraint that comes from fear, through the designation “Master,” with Hashem present before one’s eyes, as stated in the gloss at the beginning of Orach Chayim: the awareness that there is One who watches over us. Therefore the nations are called uncircumcised, but the house of Israel is not, as stated in Nedarim and as I explained above in section one. This is the level of a servant, as it is said, “If I am a master, where is My fear?” He may not deviate at all from his master’s will.”

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah 2:4:1: “Tekhelet is awe, and white indicates kindness and love, as is known. This is “You shall see it and remember all the commandments of Hashem.” Awe is the foundation of the prohibitions, and love is the foundation of the positive commandments. The testing of tekhelet with leaven, and so forth, as stated in Menachot 44a, means that through the strength of the inclination and the leaven in the dough its appearance does not depart, because of the depth of awe. We do not now possess such powerful awe; we use only white. For, as is known, from afar love is easier than awe, because from afar Hashem appears to us more in the aspect of love and attachment.”

paragraphs.text: Menachot 44a:4–7 tells of a man careful in tzitzit who deliberately arranged a forbidden encounter. At the decisive moment the fringes struck his face and he withdrew. He explained their double reminder, ‘I am Hashem your God’: the One who exacts punishment and gives reward. They appeared as four witnesses. The interruption makes the remembered command effective against his immediate desire, which is the point invoked here.

sections.en: The Atoning Power of Remorse and Shame

p: [נז] הָעָגְמַת נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם עַל עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁעָשָׂה, הֵם מַמָּשׁ יִסּוּרֵי גֵיהִנָּם עַל אוֹתָהּ עֲבֵירָה,
The anguish of soul that a person endures over the sins he committed is literally the torment of Gehenna for that transgression;
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת (יב:) דְּהַמִּתְבַּיֵּישׁ בָּהּ מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ, כִּי כְּבָר סָבַל עוֹנֶשׁ גֵּיהִנָּם.
and therefore they stated at the end of the first chapter of Berakhot (12b) that whoever feels shame over a sin is forgiven, because he has already endured the retribution of Gehenna.
וּמִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה, מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם מַזְכִּירִים לוֹ בְּכָל עֵת עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁעָשָׂה, וּמִתְמַרְמֵר עֲלֵיהֶם עַד שֶׁסּוֹבֵל שִׁיעוּר גֵּיהִנָּם הַמַּגִּיעַ לוֹ עַל זֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And he who is worthy has his transgressions brought to mind from Heaven at all times, grieving bitterly over them until he endures the measure of Gehenna due to him in this world;
וְזֶהוּ הַפֵּרָעוֹן מִן הָעֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁנִּפְרָעִים מִן הַצַּדִּיקִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
and this is the exacting of payment for sins that is collected from the righteous in this world;

כִּי בְּעָנְשֵׁי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַמָּשׁ יֵשׁ מִשְׁפָּטִים אֲחֵרִים, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מוֹעֵד קָטָן כח.): חַיֵּי, בָּנֵי וּמְזוֹנֵי לָא בִּזְכוּתָא תַּלְיָא מִלְּתָא אֶלָּא בְּמַזָּלָא.
for concerning literal worldly afflictions other rules apply, as our Sages stated (Moed Katan 28a): children, life, and sustenance depend not on merit but on heavenly constellation.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא [רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי]",
And this is what King David said: "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalms 23:4);
וַדַּאי לֹא חָשַׁב שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּגֵיהִנָּם לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת ד.) דְּקָרֵי לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ חָסִיד עַיֵּין שָׁם,
surely he did not anticipate being in Gehenna in the World to Come, since he referred to himself as pious (Berakhot 4a);
וְעַל כָּל פָּנִים לֹא הָיָה פּוֹתֵחַ פִּיו לַשָּׂטָן חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אִם חָשַׁשׁ שֶׁמָּא יִגְרוֹם הַחֵטְא.
and at any rate he would not open his mouth to the prosecutor had he worried that sin might cause it.
רַק רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כְּשֶׁהָיָה הוֹלֵךְ בְּגֵיהִנָּם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כְּשֶׁהָיָה הוֹלֵךְ בְּעַצְבוּת וּמָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה עַל חֲטָאָיו,
Rather, he meant when walking through Gehenna in this world, walking in sorrow and dejection over his sins;
וְעַל יְדֵי עַצְבוּת הַשְּׁכִינָה מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת וְיוּכַל לָבוֹא לִידֵי רַע כַּנּוֹדָע,
and through sadness the Shechinah departs and one can stumble into evil, as is known;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי".
and concerning this he said: "I will fear no evil, for You are with me."
"אַתָּה" אֵינוֹ מַדְרֵגַת הַשְּׁכִינָה הַנִּקְרָא "אֲנִי" כַּנּוֹדָע שֶׁמִּסְתַּלֶּקֶת בְּעַצְבוּת,
"You" (Attah) is not the rung of the Shechinah called "I" (Ani) which departs during sadness,
רַק מַדְרֵגַת קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא הַנִּקְרָא "אַתָּה", זֶהוּ עִמָּדִי גַּם בְּעֵת הָעַצְבוּת, שֶׁמִּצִּדּוֹ הוּא הַהִתְעוֹרְרוּת לְכָךְ:
but the level of the Holy One called "You," which remains with me even in sorrow, for from His side comes the awakening to feel this remorse.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 247:1 distinguishes ‘I,’ the Shekhinah recognized within the heart and creation, from ‘You,’ direct address to the King in prayer. In the first, a person perceives the Creator through His rule and also recognizes that the very awakening to seek Him comes from Him. The second is described as standing before the King, beyond recognition mediated through created things.

p: [נח] בְּדָבָר שֶׁהָאָדָם נָקִי מִמֶּנּוּ וְאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם נְגִיעָה וְתַאֲוָה, נִקְרָא צַדִּיק לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר
In a matter wherein a person is completely pure and harbors no selfish interest or lust, he is termed righteous regarding that specific thing
[כִּדְבָרֵי הָרַשְׁבָּ"א בְּנִדָּה (יד.) לְעִנְיַן גַּמָּלִין כֻּלָּם רְשָׁעִים, וּבְסוֹף קִדּוּשִׁין (פב.) אִיתָא רוּבָּם כְּשֵׁרִים, דִּלְגַבֵּי זֶה רְשָׁעִים וּלְגַבֵּי זֶה כְּשֵׁרִים]

as the Rashba explained in Niddah 14a that camel drivers are called wicked, while in Kiddushin 82a they are termed fit, meaning relative to one trait they are wicked and relative to another they are fit
לְעִנְיַן שֶׁעָלָיו הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר: "לֹא יְאֻנֶּה [לַצַּדִּיק כָּל אָוֶן]" (מִשְׁלֵי יב, כא) בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר.
in the sense that concerning him Scripture states: "No harm shall befall the righteous" regarding that specific area.
וּלְכָךְ הַשּׁוֹגֵג נִקְרָא חוֹטֵא וְצָרִיךְ כַּפָּרָה, שֶׁמֵּאַחַר שֶׁהָאֱלֹהִים אִנָּה לְיָדוֹ, הוּא לְאוֹת כִּי עֲדַיִן אֵינֶנּוּ נָקִי.

And therefore an inadvertent transgressor (shogeg) is termed a sinner and requires atonement, for since God caused it to happen through his hands, it indicates he is not yet entirely pure in that domain.
וּבְסוֹטָה (כח.): בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין הָאִישׁ מְנוּקֶּה מֵעָוֹן, אֵין הַמַּיִם בּוֹדְקִים אִשְׁתּוֹ
And in Sotah 28a: when the husband is not free from guilt, the bitter waters do not test his wife
[וְלָכֵן תָּנֵי נָזִיר וְאַחַר כָּךְ סוֹטָה, עַיֵּין רֵישׁ סוֹטָה, כְּלוֹמַר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא תְּחִלָּה מְנוּקֶּה מֵעָוֹן],
which is why the Mishnah places Nazir before Sotah, to teach that he must first be free from iniquity,
כְּדֵי שֶׁיָּבוֹא לוֹ בֵּירוּר מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם לְשָׁמְרוֹ מֵעֲבֵירָה.
so that clarity from Heaven may come to preserve him from sin.
וְכֵן דָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "כִּי כָשַׁלְתָּ בַּעֲוֹנֶךָ" – בָּאוּ לְךָ מִכְשׁוֹלִים בַּעֲוֹנֶךָ;
And so our Sages expounded: "'For you have stumbled in your iniquity'—obstacles have come upon you on account of your iniquity";
וּמִן הַמִּכְשׁוֹלִים שֶׁאֵירַע לָאָדָם, יוּכַל לָדַעַת דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵינֶנּוּ נָקִי מֵהֶם עֲדַיִן בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי לִבּוֹ.
and from the mishaps that occur to a person, he can recognize the matters from which he is not yet cleansed in the recesses of his heart.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מא) עַל לוֹט: מִי שֶׁלָּהוּט וְכוּלֵי סוֹף וְכוּלֵי.
And our Sages stated (Bereishit Rabbah 41) regarding Lot: he who is passionate for lust will ultimately be fed it.
וְלִפְעָמִים הַמִּכְשׁוֹלִים בִּמְכֻוָּון כְּדֵי לְעוֹרְרוֹ עַל יְדֵי כֵן שֶׁיָּשׁוּב עַל אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר:
And sometimes obstacles are deliberately engineered from Above to stir him up so that he repents for that very flaw.

sections.en: The Light of Torah That Guides the Heart

p: [נט] תּוֹרָה נִקְרָא לְשׁוֹן מוֹרֶה דֶּרֶךְ, שֶׁהִיא מוֹרָה וּמְלַמֶּדֶת לָאָדָם.
Torah is called an expression of guiding the way (moreh derekh), for it instructs and teaches man.
וְאֵין רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר בַּמֶּה שֶׁמְּלַמֶּדֶת הַחֻקִּים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִים, שֶׁהֲרֵי גַּם כְּשֶׁלּוֹמֵד סֵדֶר קָדָשִׁים נִקְרָא עוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה;
And it does not merely mean that it teaches statutes and laws, for even when studying sacrificial orders (Kodashim) one is engaged in Torah;
רַק כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּמִּדְרָשׁ אֵיכָה (פְּתִיחָה ב): "הַמָּאוֹר שֶׁבָּהּ מַחֲזִירוֹ לְמוּטָב".
but as our Sages stated in the Midrash on Eichah (Petichta 2): "The illumination within it returns him to good."
וְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה
And the illumination of the Torah
[הוּא אַגּוֹנֵי וּמַצּוֹלֵי מִן הַחֵטְא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסוֹטָה (כא.) וְזֶהוּ מַחֲזִיר לְמוּטָב]
which shields and saves from sin as written in Sotah 21a, and this is what returns one to the good
הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי מַיְמִינִים בָּהּ, שֶׁהוּא סַמָּא דְחַיֵּי, וְחַיִּים וְאוֹר הַכֹּל אֶחָד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי עִמְּךָ מְקוֹר חַיִּים, בְּאוֹרְךָ נִרְאֶה אוֹר".

is achieved only by those who engage it on the right side, for it is an elixir of life, and life and light are one, as written: "For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light do we see light" (Psalms 36:10).
אֲבָל שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ אֵינוֹ מַשִּׂיג הָאוֹר, וּמִמֵּילָא אֵינָהּ מוֹרָה לוֹ וּמַחֲזִירָתוֹ לְמוּטָב, וְאֵין עַל זֶה שֵׁם תּוֹרָה,
But when studying not for its own sake, he does not attain the light, and consequently it does not guide him or return him to good, nor does the true title of Torah apply to it,
רַק הוּא בִּכְלַל "פִּטְטַיָּא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא" דְּאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי (סוֹף בְּרָכוֹת) דְּטָבִין.
but rather it belongs to "idle chatter of the Torah" which the Yerushalmi (end of Berakhot) praises as beneficial.
וּלְכָךְ אָנוּ מְבָרְכִין "לַעֲסוֹק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה" וְלֹא "בַּתּוֹרָה", דְּמַאן סָפֵין וּמַאן רָקֵיעַ לִהְיוֹת בָּטוּחַ שֶׁיַּעֲסוֹק בָּהּ;
And therefore we formulate the blessing "to engage in the words of Torah" and not "in Torah," for who is worthy to be confident that he will truly engage in its essence;
רַק עַל כָּל פָּנִים הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּפִטְטַיָּא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, שֶׁאוֹתָם הַדִּבּוּרִים הֵם תּוֹרָה בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
rather at any rate they are words of Torah and conversational Torah talk, those very words being Torah elsewhere.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצְוָה, וּמְבָרֵךְ "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ", שֶׁמַּכְנִיס קְדוּשָּׁה בַּלֵּב כְּכָל הַמִּצְווֹת.
And this is likewise a mitzvah over which one recites "Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us," instilling holiness into the heart like all commandments.
וְהוּא נִלְמָד מִצִּיוּוּי "וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם", שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּיוֹמָא (יט.): וְלֹא בִּדְבָרִים בְּטֵלִים;
And it is derived from the command "and you shall speak of them," which our Sages expounded in Yoma 19b: "and not of idle matters";
וַהֲרֵי זֶה מִצְוָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ לְדַבֵּר דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, רַק רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר אֲפִילּוּ דִּבּוּרִים שֶׁאֵינָם אֶלָּא לְאַפּוֹקֵי דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים.
and this is a mitzvah in its own right to speak words of Torah, meaning even speech aimed merely at avoiding idle chatter.
וּלְכָךְ אוֹמְרִים אַחַר כָּךְ "וְהַעֲרֶב נָא וְגוֹמֵר", מְבַקְּשִׁים עַל עֵסֶק לִשְׁמָהּ עַל יְדֵי הַהַעֲרָבָה וּמִיתּוּק שֶׁל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָתְךָ בְּפִינוּ,
And therefore we pray immediately afterward "And make sweet, etc.," beseeching to attain study for its own sake through the sweetness and pleasantness of the words of Your Torah in our mouth,

p: [ס] כָּל מִינֵי צַעַר וְיִסּוּרִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם עַל יְדֵי אָדָם אַחֵר, בֵּין מִדַּעְתּוֹ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ, רַק בִּגְרָמָא דִילֵיהּ נִגְרַם צַעַר לְאַחֵר,
Every type of grief and suffering a person experiences through another person, whether intentionally or unintentionally, wherein sorrow was merely caused indirectly through him,
וְכֵן אֲפִילּוּ מוֹכִיחוֹ וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִצְטַעֵר, הוּא הָרְצוּעָה מַרְדּוּת לוֹ עַל עֲוֹנוֹ
and likewise even if one rebukes him and he feels pain from it, that person serves as the chastising rod for his sin
[כִּי גַּם הַבּוּשָׁה וְהַצַּעַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם בַּעֲוֹנוֹ כְּשֶׁמּוֹכִיחִין אוֹתוֹ, גַּם זֶה הוּא לְיִסּוּרִין עַל עֲוֹנוֹ].
for the shame and sorrow a person feels over his sin when rebuked also counts toward suffering for his iniquity.
וְלָכֵן יֵשׁ לָאָדָם לִיזָּהֵר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא נָקִי בָּזֶה,
Therefore, a person must be vigilant that he himself remains completely clear in this,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּפָקַדְתִּי אֶת דְּמֵי יִזְרְעֶאל עַל בֵּית יֵהוּא", וְכֵן נֶאֱמַר גַּבֵּי בַּעְשָׁא, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִּׁ"י;
as it is written: "And I will visit the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu" (Hosea 1:4), and likewise regarding Baasha, see Rashi there;
וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר: "הִתְקוֹשְׁשׁוּ וָקוֹשּׁוּ" – קְשׁוֹט [עַצְמְךָ וְאַחַר כָּךְ קְשׁוֹט אֲחֵרִים] (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּבָא מְצִיעָא קז:), דִּבְלָאו הָכִי נֶעֱנָשׁ עַל כָּךְ.
and therefore it is said: "Gather yourselves together and assemble"—first adorn yourself and only then adorn others (Bava Metzia 107b), for otherwise one is punished for doing so.
וְיִסּוּרִין הַבָּאִים לְאַחֵר עַל יָדוֹ שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ, אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְבִיאָם אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי מִי שֶׁנָּקִי בַּדָּבָר,
And suffering brought upon another unintentionally is brought by the Holy One only through someone who is personally pure in that matter,
כִּי אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רוֹצֶה לְהָבִיא תַּקָּלָה לְאִישׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
for the Holy One does not desire to bring a stumbling block to any Jew

[אִם לֹא שֶׁגַּם לוֹ יֵשׁ מִשְׁפָּט בָּזֶה שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל הָעוֹנֶשׁ עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּעֱנַשׁ זֶה עַל יָדוֹ, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמַכּוֹת (י:): הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַזְמִינָם לְפוּנְדָּק זֶה וְכוּלֵי וְזֶה וְכוּלֵי].
unless he too faces a heavenly judgment to receive punishment for causing the other's penalty, as they said in Makkot 10b: the Holy One arranges them at the same inn, etc..
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה: כְּשֶׁאֵין הָאִישׁ מְנוּקֶּה מֵעָוֹן, אֵין הַמַּיִם בּוֹדְקִים אִשְׁתּוֹ:
And therefore they stated in Sotah: when the husband is not free from iniquity, the testing waters do not check his wife.

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef extends the parapet beyond physical construction to responsibility for the effects of one's avodah on another person. This sharpens Rav Tzadok's demand to correct oneself before correcting others: even an act presented as religious service needs a safeguard against causing another person's fall. The other's need for correction does not by itself justify the manner of rebuke.

sections.en: Priestly Holiness and the Sanctifying Power of Mitzvos

p: [סא] הַכֹּהֲנִים נִקְרְאוּ קְדוֹשִׁים,
The priests are termed "holy,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַיִּבָּדֵל אַהֲרֹן לְהַקְדִּישׁוֹ" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כג, יג),
as it is written: "And Aaron was set apart, that he should be sanctified" (I Chronicles 23:13),
וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְאֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ וְהִקְרִיב אֵלָיו" (בַּמִּדְבָּר טז, ה).
and it is said: "even him whom He has chosen will He cause to come near unto Him" (Numbers 16:5).
וּבְכָל זַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו יֵשׁ מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ,
And throughout all of his descendants after him this spiritual level exists,
רַק שֶׁחֲלוּקִים בֵּין מְעַט וְרַב, עַד אַהֲרֹן שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית מַדְרֵגַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה.
differing only in degree between less and more, culminating in Aaron who represents the ultimate peak of the level of holiness.
וְלָכֵן הָעֲבוֹדָה לַכֹּהֲנִים,
Therefore the Temple service is entrusted to the priests,
וְכֵן רִבָּה בָּהֶן הַכָּתוּב מִצְווֹת יְתֵירוֹת,
and likewise Scripture multiplied for them additional, specific commandments,
כִּי הַמִּצְווֹת מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת הֵם הַנּוֹתְנִים קְדוּשָּׁה בָּאָדָם,
for practical commandments of action are what infuse holiness into a person,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ",
as we express: "Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us,"
וְנֶאֱמַר: "קַדְּשֵׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ",
and as we say: "Sanctify us with Your commandments,"
וְנֶאֱמַר: "וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֶת כָּל מִצְוֹתָי וִהְיִיתֶם קְדֹשִׁים" (בַּמִּדְבָּר טו, מ).
and as it is written: "and do all My commandments, and be holy unto your God" (Numbers 15:40).
וּלְכָךְ: כֹּהֲנִים זְרִיזִים בְּמַעֲשֶׂה – הִכְנִיס הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּהֶם מִדָּה זוֹ שֶׁל זְרִיזוּת בְּמַעֲשֶׂה כְּדֵי לְהַכְנִיס קְדוּשָּׁה בַּלֵּב.

And for this reason, priests are zealous in physical deed (Shabbat 20a)—the Blessed Name instilled within them this character trait of energetic alacrity in action in order to implant holiness deep in the heart.
וְעִנְיַן הַקְּדוּשָּׁה הוּא הַבְדָּלָה מִכָּל עִנְיְנֵי חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, רַק לִהְיוֹת עוֹבֵד ה'.
And the true nature of holiness (kedushah) is separation and detachment from all worldly pursuits and lusts, existing exclusively to be a servant of Hashem.
וְנֶאֱמַר בַּכֹּהֲנִים: "לִי" (שְׁמוֹת כח, מא), שֶׁהוּא קַיָּים לְעוֹלְמֵי עוֹלָמִים, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ב);
And concerning the priests Scripture states: "unto Me" (Li), which denotes an enduring covenant for all eternity, as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Vayikra Rabbah 2:2);
וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּכֹהֵן הַיּוֹתֵר פָּחוּת בְּמַעֲלָה, כָּל שֶׁהוּא מִזֶּרַע אַהֲרֹן,
and even regarding the cohen of the lowliest spiritual stature, so long as he descends from Aaron's seed,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין נִיכָּר בּוֹ שֶׁמֶץ קְדוּשָּׁה
even though not a trace of holiness appears visible upon him—
"הָאָדָם יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם וַה' יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב" (שְׁמוּאֵל א טז, ז),
"for man looks on the outward appearance, but Hashem looks on the heart" (I Samuel 16:7),
וּכְבָר הִבְטִיחַ: "אִם תָּפֵרוּ אֶת בְּרִיתִי הַיּוֹם וְגוֹמֵר" (יִרְמְיָה לג, כ) עַל בְּרִית הַכְּהֻנָּה:
and He has already promised: "If you can break My covenant of the day and My covenant of the night, etc." (Jeremiah 33:20–21) concerning the eternal covenant of the priesthood.

p: [סב] מַעֲלוֹת הַרְבֵּה יֵשׁ, וְכֻלָּם זָכוּ כְּבָר גְּדוֹלֵי הַדּוֹרוֹת וּנְטָלוּם וְזָכוּ לִבְנֵיהֶם אַחֲרֵיהֶם.
There are many spiritual virtues, and the giants of the early generations already merited and acquired them all, bequeathing them unto their descendants after them.
כְּמוֹ מַעֲלַת שֵׁם "יִשְׂרָאֵל" זָכָה יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ וּנְטָלָהּ וְזָכָה לְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו
Just as our father Jacob merited the title and stature of "Israel," acquired it, and transmitted it to his seed after him

[וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן כַּמָּה מַדְרֵגוֹת בִּלְתִּי סָפֵק כְּמוֹ בְּכָל הַמַּעֲלוֹת, מִן הַפָּחוּת שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַד תַּכְלִית הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַיּוֹתֵר עֶלְיוֹנָה בְּמַעֲלָה זוֹ שֶׁהוּא יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם];

and within this title there are undoubtedly various gradations, as in all virtues, from the lowliest person in Israel up to the ultimate supreme peak of this virtue, which is our father Jacob, peace be upon him;
אֲבָל הַגֵּרִים אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהֶם לִזְכּוֹת לְמַעֲלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב,
yet converts cannot achieve the essential biological level of Israel since they do not descend from Jacob's seed,
רַק כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (אָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן פֶּרֶק לו) עַל פָּסוּק "וּבְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכַנֶּה" – אֵלּוּ גֵּרֵי הַצֶּדֶק,
rather as our Sages expounded (Avot DeRabbi Natan 36) on the verse "and surname himself by the name of Israel" (Isaiah 44:5)—these are righteous converts,
שֶׁהוּא רַק כְּמוֹ כִּנּוּי וְלֹא עֶצֶם הַשֵּׁם.
meaning that it is merely an adopted surname and appellation, and not the intrinsic, inherited name itself.
וּמַעֲלַת שֵׁם "צַדִּיק" זָכָה יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק וּנְטָלוֹ וְזָכָה לְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו,
And the virtue of the title "Tzadik" (Righteous) Joseph the Righteous merited, acquired, and endowed unto his seed after him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בֵּיאוּר מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג:): "אֵין עֲמָלֵק נוֹפֵל וְכוּלֵי",
as I explained elsewhere regarding the teaching of our Sages (Bava Batra 123b): "Amalek falls only at the hand of Rachel's descendants,"
וּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת כ.): "בְּזַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף לָא שָׁלְטָא עֵינָא בִישָׁא",
and the teaching (Berakhot 20a): "The evil eye has no power over the offspring of Joseph";
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים", מִכָּל מָקוֹם עִיקָּרוֹ בְּזַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף.
and even though it is written "and your people are all righteous" (Isaiah 60:21), its primary root is anchored in the seed of Joseph.
וְשֵׁם "חָסִיד" זָכָה דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּנְטָלוֹ, וְכֵן זַרְעָא דְּדָוִד אַחֲרָיו, בֵּית דָּוִד לְבַד.
And the title "Chasid" (Pious) King David, peace be upon him, merited and acquired, and likewise the seed of David after him—the House of David exclusively.
וְלֵוִי זָכָה לְשֵׁם "טָהוֹר" וְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו.
And Levi merited the title "Tahor" (Pure), bequeathing it to his seed after him.
וְאַהֲרֹן וְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו – לְשֵׁם "קָדוֹשׁ", עַיֵּין בַּזֹּהַר רֵישׁ קֹרַח.
And Aaron and his seed after him merited the title "Kadosh" (Holy), see the Zohar at the beginning of Parashat Korach.
וְכֵן שְׁאָר מַעֲלוֹת.
And so it is with the remaining virtues.
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זָכָה לְמַעֲלַת הַתּוֹרָה וְהַחָכְמָה וּלְשֵׁם "תַּלְמִיד חָכָם", וְלֹא זָכָה לְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו,

But Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, merited the supreme virtue of Torah and Wisdom and the title of "Talmid Chacham" (Torah Scholar), yet did not transmit it as a bodily inheritance to his seed after him,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כא) שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ שֶׁיִּנָּתֵן גְּדוּלָּתוֹ לְזַרְעוֹ וְלֹא נִתְּנוּ,
as our Sages noted (Bemidbar Rabbah 21:14) that he requested his mantle of leadership be given to his sons, but it was not granted;
כִּי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אֵין מְצוּיִים לִהְיוֹת בְּנֵיהֶם תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּנְדָרִים (פא.),
for with Torah scholars it is uncommon that their children naturally become scholars, as written in Nedarim 81a;
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא עב:): כֶּתֶר תּוֹרָה מוּנָּח לַכֹּל.
and therefore they said (Yoma 72b): "the Crown of Torah lies open and accessible to all."
וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא מֹשֶׁה "אָב בַּתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי" (מְגִילָּה יג.),
Therefore Moses is termed "a father in Torah, etc." (Megillah 13a),
כִּי תּוֹאַר "אָב" אַף לְשֶׁאֵין בָּנָיו, עַיֵּין בְּפֶרֶק ב דִּבְרָכוֹת (טז:) "אֵין קוֹרִין אָבוֹת וְכוּלֵי, אִי מֵרָחֵל וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם,
for the designation of "father" applies even to one who has no biological sons in that matter—see Berakhot 16b, "we do not refer to any as Patriarchs, etc."—
רַק הוּא אֲבִי כָּל הַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
but rather he is the spiritual father of all Torah scholars throughout Israel.
וַחֲלוּקַּת מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַשְּׁבָטִים שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה הוּא כְּפִי חֲלוּקַּת הַמַּעֲלוֹת שֶׁזָּכָה כָּל אַב מִשְׁפָּחָה וּמִשְׁפָּחָה וּנְטָלָהּ לְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו.
And the demarcation of the tribal families in the Torah corresponds directly to the distribution of virtues which each patriarch of a family acquired and bequeathed to his offspring after him.
וּמִזֶּה הֵם חֲלוּקַּת הַכִּתּוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל: אֵלּוּ בַּעֲלֵי מִדָּה זוֹ וְאֵלּוּ חֲפֵצִים בָּזוֹ,
And from this stems the divergence of pathways within Israel: these master this spiritual quality, and those desire that one;
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ עַל כָּל הַמַּחֲלוֹקֶת שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל: "אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים":
and therefore they proclaimed concerning all legitimate halakhic disputes in Israel: "Both these and those are the words of the living God."

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 47:1 explains how a forefather’s acquired virtue becomes an inherited spiritual root. Avraham first established faith through his own effort, but Yitzchak’s circumcision at eight days showed that attachment to God could already be present before understanding. His son’s condition revealed the depth of Avraham’s own transformation. The surrounding discussion distinguishes this inherited root from faith’s full expression in the heart, which still requires personal effort.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 48:2 grounds disagreement for the sake of Heaven in the different spiritual qualities God created. Avraham’s love and Yitzchak’s fear are both true and must coexist; in their descendants these shared qualities appear in different proportions, producing different judgments about the same matter. The discussion also distinguishes this legitimate diversity from Korach’s angry dispute. Its opening qualification, “for the sake of Heaven,” is essential to the parallel.

grounds disagreement for the sake of Heaven in the different spiritual qualities God created. Avraham’s love and Yitzchak’s fear are both true and must coexist; in their descendants these shared qualities appear in different proportions, producing different judgments about the same matter. The discussion also distinguishes this legitimate diversity from Korach’s angry dispute. Its opening qualification, “for the sake of Heaven,” is essential to the parallel.

p: [סג] הַבָּנִים דּוֹמִים לָאֵם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּפְסָחִים (מט.): יִשָּׂא בַּת תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁאִם וְכוּלֵי בָּנָיו תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים;
Sons resemble the mother, as written in Pesachim 49a: let a man marry the daughter of a Torah scholar, for then his sons will be scholars;
וְאִילּוּ אִם הוּא תַּלְמִיד חָכָם אֵין בָּנָיו תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּנְדָרִים (פא.),
whereas if he alone is a Torah scholar, his sons are not guaranteed to be scholars, as written in Nedarim 81a,
וְנֶאֱמַר: "בֵּן כְּסִיל תּוּגַת אִמּוֹ" (מִשְׁלֵי י, א), וְלֹא אָבִיו.
and it is written: "a foolish son is the grief of his mother" (Proverbs 10:1), and not his father.
וְזֶהוּ בִּזְכָרִים, אֲבָל הַנְּקֵבוֹת דּוֹמוֹת לָאָב, שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַעֲלַת בַּת תַּלְמִיד חָכָם,
And this rule applies to male offspring; female offspring, however, resemble the father, which is the exact spiritual virtue of the daughter of a Torah scholar;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּנִדָּה (לא.): תָּלָה הַכָּתוּב הַזְּכָרִים בִּנְקֵבוֹת וּנְקֵבוֹת בִּזְכָרִים.
and as written in Niddah 31a: Scripture attributed male offspring to the female, and female offspring to the male.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, מִצַּד הָרְגִילוּת הַבַּת אֵצֶל אִמָּהּ, הִיא דּוֹמָה גַּם כֵּן לְאִמָּהּ מִצַּד הַהֶרְגֵּל וְלֹא מִצַּד הַתּוֹלָדָה,
Nonetheless, by virtue of constant habituation where a daughter is raised alongside her mother, she also resembles her mother out of habit, though not out of genetic conception,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (כְּתוּבּוֹת סג.): "רְחֵילָא בָּתַר רְחֵילָא וְכוּלֵי",
as stated in Ketubot 63a: "a ewe follows a ewe, etc.";
לְכָךְ הַנּוֹשֵׂא אִשָּׁה יִבְדּוֹק בְּאַחֶיהָ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קי.).
therefore one who marries a woman should examine her brothers (Bava Batra 110a).
וּלְעוֹלָם הָאָבוֹת נִיכָּרִים בִּבְנֵיהֶם,
And fathers are forever recognized within their children,
כִּי מַה שֶּׁהוּא סָתוּם בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב שֶׁל הָאָבוֹת, מִתְגַּלֶּה לַפּוֹעַל בַּבָּנִים,
for that which is concealed in the innermost depths of the fathers' hearts breaks forth into tangible actuality within the sons,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי מִזֶּה בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
as I have written concerning this elsewhere;
וְכָךְ קִבַּלְתִּי: כִּי הַבָּנִים – מַעֲמַקֵּי לֵב הָאָבוֹת:
and thus I received as a tradition: children are the externalized depths of their fathers' hearts.

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah 2:30:1 distinguishes three formative influences: character learned from others, qualities received through family, and inborn disposition. It reads Avraham’s departure from land, family, and birthplace as a call to direct each influence according to God’s guidance. Departure does not mean mechanically adopting the opposite quality; an apparently deficient trait may itself have a proper use. This extends the present distinction between upbringing and origin. The supplied passage’s reference for “A father endows his son” is corrected here to Mishnah Eduyot 2:9.

The contrast between father and son thus clarifies their common inward purpose.

p: [סד] פְּעָמִים שֶׁרוֹאֶה בְּבֵירוּר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְסַיְּיעוֹ וּמַסְכִּים עִם מַעֲשָׂיו, עַל כָּל פָּנִים אֵינוֹ רְאָיָה כִּי מַעֲשָׂיו יְשָׁרִים בֶּאֱמֶת,
At times a person clearly sees that the Blessed Name assists him and agrees with his actions; yet despite this, it is no definitive proof that his deeds are truly righteous in objective truth;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "מַדְרִיכֲךָ בְּדֶרֶךְ תֵּלֵךְ" (יְשַׁעְיָה מח, יז),
and regarding this it is stated: "Who leads you by the way that you should go" (Isaiah 48:17),
וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַכּוֹת י:): בְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָדָם רוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ – מוֹלִיכִין אוֹתוֹ
which our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Makkot 10b): "In the path that a man desires to go, along that path they lead him"
וְאָמַר "בְּדֶרֶךְ", דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר בְּסֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵי דֶּרֶךְ הַתּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת מ"ח,
and Scripture uses the word "way" (derekh), which in Proverbs denotes the way of Torah, as I wrote above in Section 48,
כִּי אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְסַיֵּיעַ אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהוּא עַל פִּי דַעְתּוֹ הוֹלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ הַתּוֹרָה;
for the Blessed Name grants assistance only when the person genuinely believes in his own mind that he is walking in the way of the Torah;
וּמַה שֶּׁלָּמְדוּ מִבִּלְעָם, גַּם לְפִי דַעְתּוֹ שֶׁל בִּלְעָם, כְּפִי סִטְרָא דִילֵיהּ, הָיָה דֶּרֶךְ זֶה יָשָׁר לוֹ כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא, וּמוּבָן.
and what they derived from Balaam was because in Balaam's own distorted mind, from his corrupt perspective, that path appeared correct to him according to what he was, which is understood.
הֲלֹא תִרְאֶה בְּאֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קיג.) שֶׁהָיָה קָשֶׁה לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ עֲצִירַת הַגְּשָׁמִים,
Behold, consider Elijah, concerning whom our Sages stated (Sanhedrin 113a) that the withholding of the rain was grievous before the Blessed Name;
וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן אָמַר לוֹ לְאֵלִיָּהוּ: "לֵךְ... וְנִסְתַּרְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר", וְעֲזָרוֹ לְהִסָּתֵר מִפְּנֵי אַחְאָב בְּדֶרֶךְ נֵס,
and nonetheless He commanded Elijah: "Go... and hide yourself, etc." (I Kings 17:3), miraculously assisting him to hide from Ahab through an overt miracle,
וְאִלּוּ סִיעַת אַחְאָב מוֹצְאוֹ הָיָה מַכְרִיחוֹ לְבַטֵּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה אַחַר כָּךְ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁעָשָׂה יְהוֹרָם לֶאֱלִישָׁע.
whereas had Ahab's men discovered him, they would have forced him to revoke the decree, as happened later and as Jehoram did to Elisha.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא" (דְּבָרִים ל, יב),
And concerning this it is stated: "It is not in heaven" (Deuteronomy 30:12);
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעֲזָרוּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּדֶרֶךְ נֵס לְהַרְאוֹת שֶׁהַדִּין עִמּוֹ, לֹא סָמְכוּ עַל זֶה (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא נט:),
and even though they assisted Rabbi Eliezer through supernatural miracles to show the law was according to him, the Sages did not rely upon it (Bava Metzia 59b),
שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ שֶׁהוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה.
for they reasoned that the miracle occurred merely because he desired to walk in that path.
וְזֶה הָיְתָה גַּם כֵּן תְּלוּנַּת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: "אַתֶּם הֲמִתֶּם אֶת עַם ה'" (בַּמִּדְבָּר יז, ו),
And this was likewise the complaint of the children of Israel: "You have killed the people of Hashem" (Numbers 17:6);
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרָאוּ הַפְלָגַת הַנֵּס בְּאָבְדָם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם חָשְׁבוּ עַל זֶה כִּי "לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא",
for even though they witnessed the staggering miracle in their destruction, they nonetheless argued that "it is not in heaven,"
וְאֵין לִסְמוֹךְ עַל זֶה שֶׁהַדִּין עִם מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן נֶגֶד קֹרַח וַעֲדָתוֹ,
and one cannot prove from miraculous occurrences that the halakhah stood with Moses and Aaron against Korah and his assembly,
רַק: אַתֶּם רְצִיתֶם לֵילֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה וּזְכוּתְכֶם גָּדוֹל, וּלְכָךְ הֲמִתֶּם וְגוֹמֵר:
but rather: you desired to walk in this path, and your personal merit was vast, and therefore you brought about their death.

sections.en: Surrendering the Soul in Nefilas Apayim

p: [סה] הָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לִמְסוֹר נַפְשׁוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁאִם אֵינוֹ כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – אָז מוּסְכָּם לֵילֵךְ מִן הָעוֹלָם,
A person must surrender his very soul to the Blessed Name, resolving that if his life does not conform to the will of the Blessed Name, he wholeheartedly accepts to depart from this world,
כְּדִכְתִיב: "וּרְאֵה אִם דֶּרֶךְ עֹצֶב בִּי, וּנְחֵנִי בְּדֶרֶךְ עוֹלָם" (תְּהִלִּים קלט, כד),
as it is written: "And see if there be any grievous way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting" (Psalms 139:24),
וּכְעִנְיָן זֶה אָמַר יוֹנָה: "טוֹב מוֹתִי מֵחַיָּי" (יוֹנָה ד, ג).
and in this vein Jonah proclaimed: "it is better for me to die than to live" (Jonah 4:3).
וְזֶה עִנְיַן נְפִילַת אַפַּיִם אַחַר כָּל תְּפִלָּה,
And this is the inner meaning of falling upon one's face (nefilat apayim / Tachanun) following each prayer,
וְאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר רֵישׁ קֹרַח כִּי נְפִילַת אַפַּיִם הוּא מְסִירַת עַצְמוֹ לְמִיתָה,
for the Zohar states at the beginning of Parashat Korach that falling on one's face represents the surrender of oneself unto death,
וְגַם בַּפָּשׁוּט יִרְמוֹז לָזֶה.
and even in its literal posture it hints at this.
וּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן נָפְלוּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶם שְׁתֵּי פְּעָמִים שָׁם בְּפָרָשַׁת קֹרַח.
And Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces twice there in Parashat Korach.
כִּי מָאתַיִם וַחֲמִשִּׁים אִישׁ "חָטְאוּ בְּנַפְשֹׁתָם" (בַּמִּדְבָּר יז, ג),
For the two hundred and fifty men "sinned at the cost of their souls" (Numbers 17:3);
וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ: קֹרַח שֶׁפִּקֵּחַ הָיָה וְכוּלֵי;
and our Sages remarked: "Korah, who was astute, what did he see?";
וְהִנֵּה גַּם הַמָּאתַיִם וַחֲמִשִּׁים אִישׁ לֹא שׁוֹטִים הָיוּ, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁהָיוּ רָאשֵׁי סַנְהֶדְרָאוֹת,
and behold, those two hundred and fifty men were likewise no fools, for our Sages noted that they were heads of Sanhedrin courts,
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה) שֶׁהָיוּ בִּכְלָלָם הַשְּׁנֵים עָשָׂר נְשִׂיאִים,
and the Midrash relates that among them were the twelve tribal princes;
וְכֵן מוֹרֶה לְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב: "אַתֶּם הֲמִתֶּם אֶת עַם ה'", וְהֵם רַק יְחִידִים, וּקְרָאוּם "עַם ה'" לְפִי שֶׁשְּׁקוּלִים כְּנֶגֶד כָּל הָעָם;

and so the scriptural phrase demonstrates: "You have killed the people of Hashem"—though they were few individuals, they called them "the people of Hashem" because they weighed equally against the entire nation;
וְהֶאֱמִינוּ לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְהַעֲנִישָׁם,
and they fully believed Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, that he possessed the power to punish them,
אֲבָל הֵם חָטְאוּ בְּנַפְשׁוֹתָם, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּנָזִיר: "חָטָא עַל הַנָּפֶשׁ" – פֵּירוּשׁ מִתְחַיֵּיב בְּנַפְשׁוֹ.
but they sinned at the hazard of their souls, just as the Sages said concerning a Nazirite: "he sinned against the soul"—meaning he staked his very life.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיָּדְעוּ כִּי לֶעָתִיד לֹא יְלַמְּדוּ אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ, וְיִהְיֶה מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ שֶׁ"כָּל הָעֵדָה כֻּלָּם קְדֹשִׁים",
This means that they knew that in the ultimate future "no man will teach his neighbor" (Jeremiah 31:33), and the state where "all the congregation are holy" will be attained;
וְחָשְׁבוּ שֶׁכְּבָר הִגִּיעוּ לְכָךְ
and they presumed that they had already reached that elevated stature
[כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת לוּלֵי שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא הָיוּ עַל מַדְרֵגַת לֶעָתִיד, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה],
for in truth, had not sin intervened, they would indeed have stood at that future messianic level, as our Sages taught;
וּמֵרוֹב הִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּתָם לָזֶה, עַד שֶׁנִּתְרַצּוּ בֶּאֱמֶת שֶׁאִם בֶּאֱמֶת אֵינָם בְּמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ – אָז טוֹב מוֹתָם מֵחַיֵּיהֶם, וּמוּסְכָּמִים לָמוּת בֶּאֱמֶת
and out of their overwhelming yearning for this, they consented in truth that if they were not genuinely at that level, then death was preferable to life, and they truly accepted death

[וְזֶהוּ: קֹרַח שֶׁפִּקֵּחַ הָיָה – פֵּירוּשׁ, "פִּקֵּחַ" בְּכָל מָקוֹם בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עָרוּם, כְּמוֹ "אִי פִּקֵּחַ הוּא וְכוּלֵי" (כְּתוּבּוֹת פח.), שֶׁטָּעַם מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ עוֹד].

and this is: 'Korah, who was astute'—where 'astute' throughout the Sages' words means shrewdly cunning, like 'if he is astute, etc.' (Ketubot 88a), having tasted of the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, and this is not the place to elaborate further.
וּלְכָךְ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ חוֹטְאִים בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה בְּנַפְשׁוֹתָם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַעֲלָה גְּדוֹלָה הוּא,
And therefore, even though they were termed sinners on this account at the cost of their souls, it was nonetheless an immense spiritual level,
וּלְכָךְ זָכוּ שֶׁהַמַּחְתּוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם נַעֲשׂוּ צִפּוּי לַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
and therefore they merited that their fire-pans were hammered into a sacred plating for the Altar.
וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר לְמֹשֶׁה וּלְאַהֲרֹן: "הִבָּדְלוּ וְגוֹמֵר", וְכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ: "הֵרֹמּוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
And therefore God commanded Moses and Aaron: "Separate yourselves, etc." (Numbers 16:21), and subsequently: "Get you up, etc." (ibid. 17:10);
וְהִקְשָׁה הָרַמְבַּ"ן: וְכִי אֵין בְּיַד ה' לְהַצִּילָם וְהֵם תּוֹךְ הָעֵדָה?
and the Ramban challenged: Is it not in Hashem's power to save them while remaining in the midst of the congregation?
אֲבָל לְפִי שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ בְּדָבָר זֶה גְּדוֹלִים בְּעִנְיַן הַמְּסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ, לְכָךְ הֻוצְרְכוּ לְהִבָּדֵל לְבַל יִלְקוּ עִמָּהֶם.
But because Korah's men were towering in this specific virtue of self-sacrifice, Moses and Aaron had to withdraw lest they be struck down along with them.
וּלְכָךְ תֵּיכֶף לְמַאֲמַר "הִבָּדְלוּ" וְ"הֵרֹמּוּ" הִרְגִּישׁוּ בָּזֶה, "וַיִּפְּלוּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶם",
And therefore immediately upon the commands "Separate yourselves" and "Get you up," Moses and Aaron sensed this, "and they fell upon their faces,"
וְאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר דִּמְסַרוּ גַּרְמַיְיהוּ לְמִיתָה
and the Zohar states that they surrendered their own lives unto death—
רָצוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת בָּזֶה כְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם:
seeking through this act to match their standard of self-sacrifice.

paragraphs.text: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Vayera 39:2 reads Psalms 139:23–24 as a condition within prayer: the petitioner desires the requested benefit insofar as it increases Heaven’s honor, and relinquishes it if it would draw him away from God. The conclusion affirms that God desires Avraham’s life, answering his devotion measure for measure. This illuminates the inward surrender of one’s preferred outcome after prayer while retaining both the reality of the request and the preciousness of life.

paragraphs.text: Tiferet Yosef, Korach 3 reads Moses and Aharon’s falling on their faces as intercession for Israel. Their surrender appeals to the root of the people’s life above their sin, while “God of the spirits of all flesh” invokes compassion for human frailty. The aim is that none of the congregation be cast away. The parallel thus joins their self-surrender to a plea for the community’s preservation.

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar Rabbah 18:8: “But Korach, who was astute, what led him to this foolishness? His eye misled him. He saw a great lineage arising from him: Shmuel, who is equal to Moshe and Aharon, as it is stated, “Moshe and Aharon among His priests, and Shmuel among those who call His name”; and twenty-four divisions arising from his descendants, all prophesying with the holy spirit, as it is stated, “All these were sons of Heman.” He said: Could such greatness be destined to arise from me, and I remain silent? But he did not see correctly: his sons repented, and these descendants arose from them. Moshe, however, did see. That is why Korach joined in, relying on the assurance he had heard from Moshe’s mouth that all would perish and one would survive: “The man whom Hashem chooses—he is the holy one.””

Its identification rests on the matching biblical descriptions: those “summoned from the congregation,” the ancestral leaders designated by name, correspond to the “leaders of the congregation” and “men of renown” who opposed Moses. This is the midrashic basis for the present reference to the twelve princes.

paragraphs.text: Taanit 11a:14–17 records opposing assessments of abstinence. Shmuel, following Rabbi Elazar HaKappar, calls the faster a sinner by extending the nazir’s sin of self-affliction beyond abstention from wine. Rabbi Elazar instead calls him holy, extending the nazir’s holiness. Each interprets the other verse accordingly: holiness refers to the hair, or sin to becoming impure. Rav Tzadok invokes the first reading of sin “against the soul”; the passage also preserves the contrasting view.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Korach 1:2 explains Korach’s mistake as treating a future perfection as continuously present. Sinai had opened the possibility of the future revelation in which all stand equally before God, as in a circle; the sea likewise disclosed an exceptional equality of vision. That level was subsequently lost. Korach’s appeal to the congregation’s holiness therefore confused a true revelation and future destiny with the generation’s present state.

sections.en: Prayer Even After a Divine Decree

p: [סו] תְּפִלָּה צָרִיךְ לְכָל דָּבָר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּגְזַר מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
Prayer is required for every matter, even when it has already been decreed by the Blessed Name.
הֲלֹא תִרְאֶה בְּאֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ ה': "הֵרָאֵה אֶל אַחְאָב וְאֶתְּנָה מָטָר" (מְלָכִים א יח, א),
Behold, consider Elijah, to whom Hashem explicitly promised: "Go, show yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain" (I Kings 18:1);
וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן נֶאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁעָלָה לְרֹאשׁ הַכַּרְמֶל "וַיִּגְהַר וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁהִרְבָּה בִּתְפִלָּה עַד שֶׁבָּא גֶּשֶׁם.
and nonetheless it is related afterward that he ascended to the top of Carmel, "and bowed himself down, etc." (ibid. 18:42), praying intensely until the rain arrived.
וַחֲכָמִים דְּאָמְרוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (טז.) דִּגְזַר דִּין הוּא בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, לֹא פְּלִיגֵי אַאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ סֵדֶר תְּפִלּוֹת בְּכָל יוֹם.

And the Sages who stated in Rosh Hashanah 16a that the final decree is sealed on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur do not dispute the Men of the Great Assembly who instituted the order of prayer every day.
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא: "כְּמַאן מְצַלֵּינַן הָאִידְנָא אַקְצִירֵי וּמָרִיעֵי? כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי",
And that which the Gemara asks: "In accordance with whom do we pray today for the sick and the afflicted? In accordance with Rabbi Yosi,"
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁמַּה שֶּׁהֵם הָיוּ מִתְפַּלְּלִים וּמַרְבִּים בִּתְפִלָּה לִקְרוֹעַ גְּזַר דִּין – זֶהוּ אֱלִיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
means that their intense praying to tear up a sealed decree follows the view of Rabbi Yosi.
וְהוּא מַאֲמָר יְגִיעִיִי, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁאָמְרוּ כֵּן לַהֲלָכָה בִּמְכֻוָּון,
And this was an intentionally formulated halakhic decree, meaning that they deliberately established the ruling thus,
שֶׁרְצוֹנָם הָיָה כָּךְ שֶׁתְּפִלָּתֵנוּ הָאִידְנָא יִהְיֶה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, שֶׁיּוֹעִילוּ אַף לִקְרוֹעַ גְּזַר דִּין דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה:
for their will was that our prayers today should follow Rabbi Yosi, possessing the power even to tear up the sealed decree of Rosh Hashanah.

paragraphs.text: Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 16a:13:1 asks how the established prayers accord with judgment sealed annually. Rabbeinu Tam distinguishes preventing illness, which follows Rabbi Yosei, from seeking recovery, which all permit because the time of recovery was not fixed. The blessing over the years can ask that an allotted rainfall arrive at useful times. A second answer distinguishes communal prayer, which can overturn a decree; prayer for an individual together with Israel’s sick shares that character. These are alternative approaches to the difficulty Rav Tzadok addresses here.

sections.en: Renewed Repentance with Every Spiritual Ascent

p: [סז] בְּכָל מַדְרֵגָה שֶׁהוּא עוֹלֶה, יֵשׁ לוֹ לַחֲזוֹר וְלָשׁוּב עַל חֲטָאָיו,
At every higher spiritual level to which a person ascends, he must return and repent anew for his past sins;
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן "וְחַטָּאתִי נֶגְדִּי תָמִיד" (תְּהִלִּים נא, ה),
and this is the meaning of "and my sin is ever before me" (Psalms 51:5),
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֶאֱמִין שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְקַבְּלָה תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ,
even though he firmly believed that his repentance had already been accepted;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, לְפִי שֶׁהוּא לֹא הָיָה עוֹמֵד, וּבְכָל יוֹם הָיָה עוֹלֶה מִמַּדְרֵגָה לְמַדְרֵגָה.
nevertheless, because he was not spiritually stagnant, but was ascending each day from level to level.

וְנוֹדַע דִּבְרֵי הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל כִּי בְּגַן עֵדֶן, כָּל עֵת שֶׁמַּעֲלִין לְמַדְרֵגָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה, מוֹסִיפִין לְדַקְדֵּק עָלָיו בַּחֲטָאָיו וּלְהַעֲנִישׁוֹ עַל כָּל חֵטְא קָטָן, וְכֵן הוּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.

And the teaching of the holy Ari of blessed memory is known: that in Gan Eden, whenever a soul is elevated to a loftier rung, they judge him with greater precision regarding his past sins, chastising him over every minute flaw, and so it is in this world.
וְזֶהוּ טַעַם "יְרִידָה לְצוֹרֶךְ עֲלִיָּה" הַמְּבוֹאָר בַּסְּפָרִים,
And this is the rationale for "descent for the sake of ascent" expounded in holy works:
שֶׁעֵת שֶׁמְּדַקְדְּקִים בּוֹ הוּא עֵת הַיְּרִידָה,
the period when they scrutinize him with exacting judgment is the time of descent,
וְאָז צָרִיךְ תְּשׁוּבָה,
and then he requires renewed repentance,
וְעָגְמַת נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מֵחֲטָאָיו הוּא הָעוֹנֶשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת נ"ז,
and the anguish of soul he experiences over his sins constitutes the punishment, as I wrote above in Section 57,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִזְכֶּה לַעֲלִיָּה:
and through this he merits the higher ascent.

sections.en: The Heart as the Goal of Divine Service

p: [סח] כָּל הָעֲבוֹדוֹת שֶׁבְּאֵבְרֵי הַגּוּף וְהַמִּצְווֹת שֶׁבָּהֶם הֵם רַק לְהַיְשִׁיר הַלֵּב,
All forms of divine service performed through the bodily limbs and their commandments exist solely to rectify and align the heart;
וְהָעִיקָּר הוּא הַלֵּב שֶׁשָּׁם מְעוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and the principal core is the heart, which is the dwelling place of the Blessed Name,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב): הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "צוּר לְבָבִי וְגוֹמֵר".
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2): "The Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel, as it is stated: 'God is the rock of my heart, etc.'" (Psalms 73:26).
וּלְכָךְ לֹא יִהְיֶה זֶה הַמְּכֻוָּון מִן הָאָדָם, רַק כָּל אֵלֶּה דְּבָרִים הַמְּבִיאִים אֶל הַמְּכֻוָּון,
Therefore the physical act itself should not be man's ultimate objective, but rather all these deeds are instruments leading to the ultimate goal,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, פב עַמּוּד ב) עַל תַּרְיַ"ג מִצְווֹת – תַּרְיַ"ג עֵיטִין.
as written in the Zohar (Part II, 82b) concerning the 613 commandments: they are 613 counsels of holy advice.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "וְאַחַר הָרוּחַ רַעַשׁ – לֹא בָרַעַשׁ ה', וְאַחַר הָרַעַשׁ אֵשׁ וְגוֹמֵר" (מְלָכִים א יט, יא–יב),
And regarding this Scripture states: "and after the wind an earthquake, but Hashem was not in the earthquake; and after the earthquake a fire, etc." (I Kings 19:11–12),
כִּי כְּבוֹד ה' אֵינוֹ בְּדָבָר הַנִּרְגָּשׁ וּמַרְעִישׁ, רַק "בְּקוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה",
for the glory of Hashem is not found in sensational, noisy display, but in "a still small voice,"
וְהוּא הַלֵּב שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִרְגָּשׁ לְשׁוּם בְּרִיָּה.
which is the inward heart, unfelt and unseen by any created being.
וְלָמְדוּ מִזֶּה בִּבְרָכוֹת (נח.) לְמַלְכוּתָא דְאַרְעָא,
And from this they derived in Berakhot 58a regarding earthly monarchy;
וּמַאן מַלְכֵי? רַבָּנָן, שֶׁהֵם הַמּוֹלְכִים עַל עַצְמָם, הַמּוֹשְׁלִים בְּיִצְרָם, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (עח:),
and who are kings? The Rabbis, who reign sovereignly over themselves and master their inclinations (Bava Batra 78b);
גַּם הַמְּלוּכָה בַּיֵּצֶר לֹא בְּרַעַשׁ, רַק קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה.
and mastery over the inclination is likewise not achieved through noisy tumult, but through a still small voice.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, "גּוּנְדָּא קַמַּיְיתָא חָלֵיף כִּי קָא אָוְושָׁא",
However, "the first troop passes with noisy clamor,"
כִּי לוּלֵי זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר, רַק מִקּוֹדֶם צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּרַעַשׁ וְתוֹקֶף נֶגְדּוֹ,
for without that preliminary stage it is impossible, and initially one must confront the inclination with forceful tumult,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ה.): לְעוֹלָם יַרְגִּיז אָדָם וְכוּלֵי.
as our Sages stated (Berakhot 5a): "A person should always stir up his good inclination against the evil inclination."
אֲבָל אֵין זֶה הַמֶּמְשָׁלָה הַגְּמוּרָה עֲדַיִן,
Yet that noisy struggle is not yet the complete dominion;
רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בְּלִי רַעַשׁ,
rather, full dominion occurs when it operates without noise,
רַק כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "וְלִבִּי חָלַל בְּקִרְבִּי" (תְּהִלִּים קט, כב),
along the lines of what King David, peace be upon him, stated: "and my heart is slain within me" (Psalms 109:22),
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק ט הֲלָכָה ה) שֶׁהֲרָגוֹ לְיֵצֶר הָרָע בְּתַעֲנִית
and our Sages expounded (Yerushalmi Berakhot 9:5) that he slew his evil inclination through fasting
[שֶׁהוּא הָרַעַשׁ נֶגֶד הַתַּאֲוָה],
which represented the tempestuous tumult waged against physical desire,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא הַמֶּמְשָׁלָה:
and through that quiet slaying is ultimate, absolute dominion attained.

paragraphs.text: Rabbeinu Bahya, Devarim 21:10:2: “It is well known that all the limbs of the body follow the heart and the eyes, and the heart is the essential thing. If the heart is whole with the blessed God, everything is at peace; if the heart is deficient toward Him, everything is deficient. Our Sages expounded: “The Merciful One desires the heart.” They said in the Midrash: “My son, give Me your heart”—if you give Me your heart and your eyes, I know that you are Mine; if not, you are not Mine.”

paragraphs.text: Tiferet Yosef, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 3 asks what the Zohar’s “613 counsels” lead toward, since love and fear of God are themselves among the commandments. Its answer is the alignment of the embodied person with God’s will, so that the heart harbors no contrary inclination. This complements the present teaching that bodily acts prepare inward mastery; their aim extends beyond an isolated feeling of devotion.

sections.en: Israel's Influence Among the Nations and Its Protection

items.h: Editorial note. This entire entry (אות סט) was originally censored and omitted from the first printed edition of Tzidkas HaTzaddik. It was later restored in subsequent editions based on a handwritten manuscript transcribed directly from the holy hand of the author, Rav Tzadok HaKohen of Lublin, by one of his close disciples (as brought in Tzidkas HaTzaddik HaMaleh edited by Rabbi Avraham Eliyahu Mokotowski).

p: כַּאֲשֶׁר אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מְקַבְּלִים וּלְמֵידִים אֵיזֶה מִדָּה טוֹבָה וְדָבָר טוֹב מִיְּהוּדִים,
When the nations of the world receive and learn any good character trait or good matter from Jews,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה יְכוֹלִים הַיְּהוּדִים לְנַצְּחָם,
through this, the Jews are able to overcome and defeat them,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יְכוֹלָה הַכִּבְשָׂה לְהִתְקַיֵּם בֵּין הַזְּאֵבִים,
and through this, the sheep is able to endure and survive among the wolves,
עַל יְדֵי רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דַּיְקָא הַמִּתְחַבְּרִים לְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
specifically through the sinners of Israel who associate with the nations of the world,
וּמֵהֶם לְמֵדִים אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם אֵיזֶה דָּבָר טוֹב.
and from whom the nations of the world learn some good thing.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 57:1 describes Israel’s capacity to draw holy elements from other nations while remaining inwardly rooted in its own holiness. It also emphasizes the danger of the reverse influence: even an initially worthy intention can be compromised through association, as in the example of Ahaziah. The passage therefore requires unusual vigilance rather than treating all contact as spiritually secure. Against this background, the present siman describes providence transmitting some good even through compromised association.

And this is why Hashem, blessed be He, said to him afterward:
"אִישׁ חֶרְמִי"
regarding Ahab releasing Ben-Hadad, 'the man whom I devoted to destruction' –
כַּמָּה מְצוּדוֹת וַחֲרָמִים פֵּרַשְׂתִּי וְכוּלֵי,
meaning: 'how many nets and snares did I spread to deliver him into your hand,' etc.,
כִּי לֹא הָיָה בַּמִּשְׁפָּט לְהִמָּסֵר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁבִיל חֲטָאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
for according to strict judgment, he was not meant to be handed over to Israel because of the sins of Israel,
הוּצְרַךְ לְכַמָּה עֵצוֹת שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ עַל פִּי מִשְׁפָּט
so it required various heavenly strategies so that it would come about according to divine justice
שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל יְנַצְּחֵם.
that Israel should overcome them.

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ, עַל יְדֵי שֶׁאָמַר "אָחִי הוּא",
And afterward, because Ahab said of Ben-Hadad 'he is my brother,'
נִתְקַלְקְלָה הַמְּצוּדָה עַל יְדֵי הָאַחֲוָה שֶׁעָשָׂה אוֹתוֹ עִמּוֹ,
the snare was ruined through the fraternity that he established with him,
מִמֵּילָא לֹא הָיָה הַמִּשְׁפָּט שֶׁיְּנַצְּחוּ, וּבַמִּשְׁפָּט נִיצַּל.
and consequently it was no longer justified by judgment that they should prevail, and by judgment Ben-Hadad was spared.
וּמָרְדֳּכַי שֶׁנִּצַּח לְהָמָן,
And likewise Mordechai, who triumphed over Haman,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה:
as our Sages of blessed memory taught:
"אֵין עֲמָלֵק נוֹפֵל אֶלָּא בְּיַד זַרְעָהּ שֶׁל רָחֵל",
'Amalek falls only at the hand of the offspring of Rachel,'
וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר אָמְרוּ:
and elsewhere they taught:
זֶה נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "וְלֹא יָרֵא אֱלֹהִים",
regarding this one (Amalek) it is stated: 'and he did not fear God,'
וְזֶה נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים אֲנִי יָרֵא",
while regarding this one (Joseph) it is stated: 'I fear God';
וְלָאו דַּוְקָא יוֹסֵף,
and this does not refer strictly to Joseph himself,
אֶלָּא כָּל זַרְעֵיהּ מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה גּוֹבֵר בָּהֶם,
rather, among all of Rachel's descendants the attribute of divine awe/fear is dominant,
וּלְכָךְ "וְרַבִּים מֵעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מִתְיַהֲדִים כִּי נָפַל פַּחַד מָרְדֳּכַי עֲלֵיהֶם",
and therefore Scripture states: 'And many of the peoples of the land became Jews, for the fear of Mordechai fell upon them,'
וְקִבְּלוּ יִרְאָה מִמֶּנּוּ,
meaning they received awe/fear from him,
וּמִצַּד זֶה הִגִּיעַ מִשְׁפַּט נִצּוּחוֹ.
and from that vantage point, the heavenly judgment of his victory arrived.

p: [ע] בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר שֶׁבּוֹ הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁל אָדָם, בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר וְעַל יָדָהּ עַצְמוֹ הוּא מַעֲלָתוֹ,
In that very matter in which a person's deficiency lies, in that exact thing and through it itself is his true spiritual virtue,
כְּעִנְיַן שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין ע.) עַל "וַיִּתְפְּרוּ עֲלֵה תְאֵנָה": בַּדָּבָר שֶׁקִּלְקְלוּ בּוֹ נִתְקָנוּ.
in the spirit of what our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Sanhedrin 70a) on "and they sewed fig leaves": through the very medium in which they corrupted were they rectified.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק ב סוֹף הֲלָכָה ד): בַּיּוֹם שֶׁנֶּחְרַב הַבַּיִת נוֹלַד מָשִׁיחַ.
And along these lines is likewise what our Sages of blessed memory stated (Yerushalmi Berakhot 2:4): On the very day the Temple was destroyed, the Messiah was born.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צא:): מִנַּיִן לִתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים מִן הַתּוֹרָה
And our Sages said (Sanhedrin 91b): From where is the resurrection of the dead derived from the Torah
[רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁכָּל דָּבָר שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם יֵשׁ לוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר דְּבֵיקוּת בִּמְקוֹר הַחַיִּים שֶׁהוּא אֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ].
meaning that every matter in the world possesses a root in the Torah, signifying cleaving unto the Source of Life which is the absolute truth of the will of the Blessed Name.
וְזֶהוּ פָּרָה [אֲדֻמָּה] לְטַהֵר מִטֻּמְאַת מֵת,
And this is the red heifer (Parah Adumah) designed to purify from the defilement of death,
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה חֻקַּת): תָּבֹא אֵם וּתְקַנַּח צוֹאַת בְּנָהּ;
and our Sages expounded (Bemidbar Rabbah, Chukat 19:8): "Let the mother come and wipe away the excrement of her son";
הָעֵגֶל הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמִּיתָה, זֶהוּ צוֹאַת בְּנָהּ
the Golden Calf is the primordial root of death, representing the excrement of her son
וּלְכָךְ נַעֲשָׂה גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי יָרָבְעָם שֶׁהוּא הָיָה בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף שֶׁיָּצָא מִזַּרְעוֹ מֵאֲבִיָּה (זֹהַר חָדָשׁ בָּלָק) שֶׁהָיָה מְעוּתָּד לֵהָרֵג,

and therefore it was similarly repeated by Jeroboam, who contained within him the spiritual root of Mashiach ben Yosef emerging from his seed through Aviyah (Zohar Chadash, Balak 56a), who was destined to be slain;
וְרַק מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד נֶאֱמַר: "חַיִּים שָׁאַל מִמְּךָ נָתַתָּה לּוֹ"
whereas regarding Mashiach ben David alone is it stated: "He asked life of You, You gave it to him" (Psalms 21:5)
וּפָרָה הוּא הָאֵם (בִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב) הַמּוֹלֶדֶת זֶה,
and the cow is the Mother (Binah residing in the heart) which gives birth to this,
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁהַכֹּל מִן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, מִמֶּנּוּ יָצָא הַכֹּל,
meaning the realization that everything originates from the Blessed Name, from Him all has emerged;
עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא קִנּוּחַ אוֹתָהּ צוֹאָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
through this consciousness comes the cleansing of that foul waste, as mentioned above.
