sections.en: Praying for Others and the Limits of Judgment

p: [עא] אֵין לְבַקֵּשׁ לִרְאוֹת רָעַת אָדָם וַאֲפִילּוּ רָשָׁע,
One must not seek or pray to see the harm of any person, even a wicked one,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת י.): "יִתַּמּוּ חוֹטְאִים" – אֵין כְּתִיב [אֶלָּא חַטָּאִים].
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Berakhot 10a): "'Let sins cease' is written, not 'let sinners cease'."
וְזֶהוּ בְּרַע לַשָּׁמַיִם, אֲבָל רַע לַבְּרִיּוֹת עָנְשׁוֹ מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה, שֶׁמּוּתָּר לְבַקֵּשׁ רָעָתוֹ גַּם כֵּן;
And this applies to one who is wicked toward Heaven; but one who does evil unto created beings, his retribution is measure for measure, such that it is permissible to pray for his downfall as well;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בֶּאֱלִישָׁע שֶׁקִּלֵּל לַנְּעָרִים מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם זִלְזְלוּהוּ לְפִי שֶׁרִפָּא לַמַּיִם וְעָשָׂה טוֹבָה לַבְּרִיּוֹת, וְהֵם חֲפֵצִים יוֹתֵר בְּרָעָתָם, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה מו: וְרַשִּׁ"י שָׁם), לָכֵן הָיָה רַשַּׁאי לְקַלְּלָם.

and as we find regarding Elisha who cursed the youths because they mocked him for having healed the waters and brought benefit to the townspeople, whereas they preferred the town's plight (Sotah 46b and Rashi there), therefore he was permitted to curse them.
וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁקִּלֵּל אוֹיְבָיו בְּמִזְמוֹר ק"ט, פֵּירֵשׁ שָׁם בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁהָיוּ מְרֵיעִים לוֹ,
And likewise King David, peace be upon him, who cursed his adversaries in Psalm 109, explained there that it was because they actively harmed him,
וְאָמַר: "וַיֶּאֱהַב קְלָלָה וַתְּבוֹאֵהוּ" – מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָהַב זֶה.
stating: "He loved cursing, and it came unto him" (Psalms 109:17)—measure for measure, because he loved cursing.
וְכֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר: "וּמְקַלֶּלְךָ אָאֹר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית יב, ג), אֲבָל בְּלָאו הָכִי אֵין מְקַלֵּל לְאָדָם.
And likewise the Blessed Name proclaimed: "And him who curses you will I curse" (Genesis 12:3); but otherwise, one must not curse another person.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, גַּם בָּזֶה מָצִינוּ דֶּאֱלִישָׁע נֶעֱנַשׁ עַל זֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסוֹטָה (מז.) וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין (קז:);
Nonetheless, even in this we find that Elisha was punished for it, as written in Sotah 47a and Sanhedrin 107b;
וּמִלְּבַד זֶה גַּם כֵּן לֹא לְכָל אָדָם הוּתַּר, שֶׁהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בֶּאֱלִישָׁע (סוֹטָה שָׁם): "וַיַּרְאֵם" – רָאָה שֶׁאֵין וְכוּלֵי,
and furthermore, it is not permitted to every individual, for our Sages expounded regarding Elisha (Sotah ibid.): "'And he looked upon them'—he saw that there was no good seed in them, etc.";
וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ בַּעַל רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁהַנְּגִיעָה מְעַוֶּורְתּוֹ.
and one who does not possess the Holy Spirit (Ruach HaKodesh) might be blinded by personal bias and resentment.

וּלְכָךְ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּאוֹתוֹ מִזְמוֹר אָמַר פָּסוּק "וְלִבִּי חָלַל בְּקִרְבִּי" (תְּהִלִּים קט, כב), שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה מִזֶּה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) שֶׁהֲרָגוֹ לְיֵצֶר הָרָע,

And therefore King David, peace be upon him, in that very psalm uttered the verse "and my heart is slain within me" (Psalms 109:22), which our Sages expounded (Avodah Zarah 4b) to mean that he had completely slain his evil inclination,
שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ לָחוּשׁ לְשׁוּם נְגִיעָה לְתַאֲוַת עַצְמוֹ, כִּי כְּבָר אֵין לוֹ יֵצֶר הָרָע.
declaring that he had no concern of being blinded by self-interest or personal passion, for he no longer possessed an evil inclination.

sections.en: Miracles Through Torah and Prayer

p: [עב] אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹת מוֹפְתִים עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה,
It is possible to perform supernatural miracles through the medium of Torah;

וְכָךְ הָיוּ כָּל מוֹפֵת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁפָּתַח שַׁעַר חָדָשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְעַל פִּי אוֹתוֹ אוֹר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הָיָה נִמְשָׁךְ שְׁפִיעַת אוֹר בָּעוֹלָם לִפְעוֹל אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר.

and such was every miracle wrought by Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who unlocked a new gate in the words of Torah, and through that illumination in the words of Torah, an outpouring of light was drawn down into the cosmos to effect that physical phenomenon.
וְאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹת עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה.
And it is also possible to perform miracles through the power of prayer.
וּמָצִינוּ בַּנְּבִיאִים שֶׁסִּפֵּר הַכָּתוּב כָּל הַמּוֹפְתִים שֶׁעָשָׂה אֵלִיָּהוּ וְשֶׁעָשָׂה אֱלִישָׁע, וְזוּלַת מִשְּׁאָר הַנְּבִיאִים לֹא נִזְכַּר מוֹפְתֵיהֶם.
And we find among the Prophets that Scripture explicitly recorded all the miracles wrought by Elijah and by Elisha, whereas among the other prophets their wonders are not described.
וּכְבָר אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה יד.): נְבוּאָה שֶׁהֻוצְרְכָה לְדוֹרוֹת נִכְתְּבָה, וְשֶׁלֹּא הֻוצְרְכָה לֹא נִכְתְּבָה;
And our Sages already taught (Megillah 14a): A prophecy that was necessary for future generations was transcribed, while that which was not needed for posterity was not written down;
וְאִם כֵּן עַל כָּרְחֲךָ אוֹתָם סִפּוּרֵי הַמּוֹפְתִים הֵם צְרִיכִים לְדוֹרוֹת, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיוּ רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה, הֵם פָּתְחוּ שְׁעָרִים בָּזֶה,
and if so, perforce those accounts of their miracles are eternally needed for future generations, and even though they were temporary, they opened eternal spiritual gateways in this realm,
כִּי כָּל מוֹפְתֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ הָיוּ עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה וְעַל יָדָהּ
for all of Elijah's miracles were wrought through the authority and mechanism of Torah
[דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל יְרִידַת הָאֵשׁ עַל יְדֵי חִדּוּשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁחִדֵּשׁ לְהַתִּיר הַבָּמָה],
for example, the descent of fire from heaven through the halakhic innovation he established to temporarily permit an isolated altar,
וְכָל מוֹפְתֵי אֱלִישָׁע עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּמְגִילָּה (כז.): "וֶאֱלִישָׁע דַּעֲבַד בְּרַחֲמֵי",
while all of Elisha's miracles were achieved through prayer, as stated in Megillah 27a: "And Elisha acted through prayers for divine mercy,"
וְזָכָה לְפִי שְׁנַיִם מֵאֵלִיָּהוּ, כִּי יוֹתֵר יֵשׁ לִפְעוֹל עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה.
and he merited a double portion beyond Elijah, because greater direct intervention can be effected through prayer.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, מַה שֶּׁעַל פִּי תּוֹרָה גָּדוֹל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּשַׁבָּת (י.): "מַנִּיחִים חַיֵּי עוֹלָם וְעוֹסְקִים בְּחַיֵּי שָׁעָה", וְהַמַּעֲמִיק יָבִין:

Yet nonetheless, that which is done through Torah is intrinsically greater, as written in Shabbat 10a: "They set aside eternal life and engage in transient temporal life," and the discerning mind will understand.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Megillah 3: “The matter is as my holy grandfather explained: there are two kinds of divine inspiration. One comes through a person's preparation: he prepares and disciplines himself for Hashem's will and thereby reaches divine inspiration. As the Midrash teaches, zeal leads to cleanliness, and so forth, and piety leads to divine inspiration. By preparing himself through all the stages enumerated by the Midrash, a person attains divine inspiration. This is called prophecy needed for the generations, for since it came through human preparation, it remains established for the whole world.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Tiferet Yosef distinguishes an isolated inspiration from a lasting path opened through human preparation. This helps explain the siman's question about recording miracles that served only a particular moment: what remains is not merely the report of a wonder, but an opening in avodas Hashem. The two discussions illuminate that lasting function without making every miracle identical with the prophecy discussed there.

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 11:9 describes prayer as drawing a taste of eternal life into embodied, temporal life. Its value lies in present longing, seeking, repentance, and effort; joy can exist in the seeking itself. Torah is associated with enduring vitality and contentment. The passage therefore explains prayer’s distinctive value without reversing the present siman’s concluding priority of Torah.

sections.en: Providential Opportunities as Signs of Accepted Repentance

p: [עג] כְּשֶׁהָאָדָם מְתַקֵּן מַה שֶּׁחָטָא, אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ אוֹתוֹ פֶּרֶק וְאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּהְיֶה תְּשׁוּבַת הַמִּשְׁקָל;

When a person rectifies the flaw wherein he sinned, the Blessed Name arranges for him that exact situation and that exact circumstance so that it constitutes a commensurate, counterbalancing repentance (teshuvat hamishkal);
שֶׁהֲרֵי וַדַּאי יֵשׁ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָסוּר הָאָדָם לְהָבִיא עַצְמוֹ לִידֵי כָּךְ, כְּמוֹ בְּ"אוֹתָהּ אִשָּׁה, בְּאוֹתוֹ וְכוּלֵי" יַעֲבוֹר עַל אִיסּוּר יִחוּד,

for certainly there are scenarios where it is strictly forbidden for a person to bring himself deliberately into temptation—such as intentionally putting oneself in seclusion with the same woman, which would violate the prohibition of yichud;
רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ זֶה אוֹ עִנְיָן כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ, וְאֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ זֶה אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּשֵׁל עוֹד.
rather, the Blessed Name providential arranges this or a comparable situation for him, and the Blessed Name orchestrates this only when He foreknows that the person will not stumble again.
וּלְכָךְ, כַּאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ, הוּא סִימָן שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְקַן וְנִתְקַבְּלָה תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ.
And therefore, when the Blessed Name orchestrates such an encounter, it is a sign that he has already been spiritually rectified and his repentance has been accepted.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כה.) בַּחֲזָרָתָן שֶׁל חָשׁוּד עַל טְרֵיפוֹת: שֶׁיַּחֲזִיר אֲבֵדָה וְכוּלֵי וְכַיּוֹצֵא עַיֵּין שָׁם;
And this is what our Sages said in Sanhedrin 25a regarding the repentance of one suspected of selling non-kosher meat: that he must return a valuable lost object, etc., see there;
וַהֲרֵי זֶה אֵין בְּיָדָם, אִם אֵין מוֹצְאִין אֲבֵדָה מַה יַּעֲשׂוּ?
and behold, finding a lost item is not in their power—if they do not find one, what can they do?
רַק שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר תְּשׁוּבָתָם אֱמֶת, הַסִּימָן שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לָהֶם כָּךְ, וּכְשֶׁנִּזְדַּמֵּן לָהֶם הוּא סִימָן שֶׁתְּשׁוּבָתָם אֱמֶת.

Rather, when their repentance is genuine truth, the sign is that the Blessed Name arranges this opportunity for them, and when it presents itself to them, it is a confirmation that their repentance is sincere.
וְכָךְ בְּגֵיחֲזִי, שֶׁחֶטְאוֹ הָיָה שֶׁחָמַד לְמַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ:
And so it was with Gehazi, whose sin was coveting that which was not his:
הַתְחָלַת תִּיקּוּנוֹ הִזְמִין לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּשׂוֹרַת בִּזַּת אֲרָם,
the initial stage of his rectification the Blessed Name arranged for him through the discovery of the spoils of the Aramean camp,

כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם קז:) דְּהַמְּצֹרָעִים הֵם גֵּיחֲזִי וּבָנָיו, וְלֹא חָמְדוּ לִשְׁתּוֹק וּלְהַרְבּוֹת בְּבִזָּה לְעַצְמָם כִּי חָשְׁשׁוּ לַחֵטְא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּמְצָאָנוּ עָוֹן" (מְלָכִים ב ז, ט).

as our Sages expounded (ibid. 107b) that the four lepers were Gehazi and his sons, and they did not covet to keep silent and hoard the vast spoils for themselves because they feared sin, as it is written: "and punishment will overtake us" (II Kings 7:9).
וְאָז הָיָה הַהַתְחָלָה, וְלֹא נִזְכַּר עֲדַיִן שְׁמוֹ בְּפֵירוּשׁ.
And that was the beginning, where his name was not yet explicitly mentioned.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ סִפֵּר מֵעִנְיַן הַחֲזָרַת נַחֲלָה לָאִשָּׁה עַל יָדוֹ, וְהוּא דָּבָר דְּמִמֵּילָא בָּא עַל יָדוֹ, הוּא סִימָן לִגְמַר תִּיקּוּנוֹ.

And afterward Scripture relates how the restoration of the Shunammite woman's estate occurred through his words (II Kings 8:5), which came about spontaneously through him, serving as a sign of his complete rectification.
וְאָז אַחַר כָּךְ הָלַךְ אֱלִישָׁע לַאֲרָם, וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין שָׁם): לְהַחֲזִיר גֵּיחֲזִי בִּתְשׁוּבָה;
And then subsequently Elisha went to Damascus, concerning which our Sages said (Sanhedrin ibid.): to bring Gehazi back in repentance;
זָכָה לְמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּמִדּוֹת (פֶּרֶק ב): "יִתֵּן בְּלִבָּם וִיקָרְבוּךָ", שֶׁאַף אַחַר כָּל הַתִּיקּוּן צָרִיךְ לְהִתְקָרְבוּת אֱלִישָׁע.

he merited that which our Sages stated in Middot (chapter 2): "May He place in their hearts that they draw you near," for even after all internal rectification, he still required the personal rapprochement of Elisha.
וְזָכָה שֶׁמִּי שֶׁהִרְחִיקוֹ הוּא עַצְמוֹ קֵירְבוֹ;
And he was privileged that the very master who had pushed him away personally came to draw him close;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה מְנָאוּהוּ בְּאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא וְאָמְרוּ שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לָשׁוּב,
and even though our Sages of blessed memory enumerated him among those who have no portion in the World to Come and stated that he refused to repent,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת וְכוּלֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ:
nonetheless the interpreters of esoteric traces maintained that he indeed has a portion in the World to Come.

The source does not require seeking temptation. Rav Tzadok discusses providential encounters that disclose repair, while explicitly excluding an encounter arranged through a prohibited act.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 9:1 distinguishes repentance in the heart from the evidence needed to restore public trust. Sincere regret and resolve are known to God; confession remains a separate commanded duty, and a resolve to return stolen property does not remove the obligation to return it. Concrete changes and protective boundaries help establish credibility and prevent renewed failure. This explains the evidentiary role of the present opportunities without making an engineered temptation necessary for repentance.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Metzora 7:1: “We read as the haftarah, “Four men were lepers.” The Gemara says that these were Gehazi and his three sons. Since it is written, “Upon you and your offspring forever,” this implies that his offspring were never healed. Nevertheless, this great salvation came about through them, and merit is brought about only through one who is meritorious. This proves that at their root they have a remedy, as the interpreters of scriptural hints said about all six who descend from Yaakov: they have a share in the World to Come. For everyone descended from Yaakov is bound at the root to the blessed God: “Your people are all righteous.””

items.h:
Editorial Note on the Missing Section
The text of Section 74 is not present in the editions consulted. Har Bracha proceeds directly from Section 73 to Section 75; Ne'imos HaTzedek and Biur Meshulav both explicitly mark Section 74 as missing. Other passages of Tzidkas HaTzadik, including Section 75, were omitted from early printings and later restored from manuscript copies. No verified source establishes why Section 74 in particular remains absent. Accordingly, no text is reconstructed here; the original numbering is preserved.
Sources: Har Bracha ed., pp. 28-29; Ne'imos HaTzedek, vol. I, p. 178; Biur Meshulav, vol. I, p. 175; Josh Rosenfeld, The Seforim Blog, May 31, 2016.

sections.en: Incidental Sin and the Enduring Sanctity of Mitzvos

p: הָעֲבֵירוֹת בְּנֶפֶשׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי אֵינָם קִנְיַן עַצְמִי רַק מִקְרִי,
Transgressions within the soul of an Israelite are not an essential acquisition, but merely incidental,
וּלְכָךְ יֵשׁ לָהֶם פְּדִיָּה,
and therefore they are subject to redemption,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהוּא יִפְדֶּה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִכֹּל עֲוֹנֹתָיו".
as it is stated: 'And He shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities' (Psalms 130:8).
כְּמוֹ קְדוּשַׁת דָּמִים יֵשׁ לָהּ פִּדְיוֹן,
Just as monetary sanctity (kedushat damim) is subject to redemption,
שֶׁדָּבָר אַחֵר נִתְפָּס תְּמוּרָתוֹ וְחָלָה עָלָיו הַקְּדוּשָּׁה,
wherein another object is seized in its stead and the sanctity takes effect upon it,
כָּךְ הוּא מְחַלֵּל אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּאֲחֵרִים,
so does He desanctify / transfer the blemish of Israel onto others,
כְּעִנְיַן "וְאֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּיךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
in the manner of: 'And I will give people in your place, etc.' (Isaiah 43:4),
וְחָל עֲלֵיהֶם הָעֲבֵירוֹת.
and the transgressions take effect upon them.
וּכְעִנְיַן "וְנָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר עָלָיו אֶת כָּל עֲוֹנֹתָם",
And similar to: 'And the he-goat shall bear upon itself all their iniquities' (Leviticus 16:22),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁנּוֹתֵן הָעֲווֹנוֹת עַל רֹאשׁ עֵשָׂו.
and as our Sages of blessed memory taught, that He places the sins upon the head of Esau.

They compared the sins surrounding a person to thorns surrounding a rose. They do not come from the person’s essence, but surround and encompass him on the side of his outward extension. From the essence of the Israelite soul, however, there is no sin at all. Differences in the levels of attachment are differences in the souls themselves, for in the upright arrangement there are degrees among souls.”

p: אֲבָל הַמִּצְווֹת הֵם קְדוּשַׁת הַגּוּף וְאֵין לָהֶם פִּדְיוֹן.
However, the mitzvot possess bodily sanctity (kedushat haguf), and they are not subject to redemption.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אִם יִתֵּן אִישׁ אֶת כָּל הוֹן בֵּיתוֹ [בָּאַהֲבָה בּוֹז יָבוּזוּ לוֹ]".
And as it is written: 'If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, it would be utterly scorned' (Song of Songs 8:7).
וְעַיֵּין בִּתְשׁוּבוֹת רַב הַאי גָּאוֹן שֶׁהֵבִיא מַהֲרַ״ם אַלְשַׁקַּר בְּעִנְיַן אֶחָד שֶׁמָּכַר מִצְווֹתָיו דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And see the Responsa of Rav Hai Gaon cited by Maharam Alashkar regarding one who sold his mitzvot, that it is completely ineffective, see there.
וְעִנְיַן מְכִירַת הַבְּכוֹרָה דְּעֵשָׂו לְהַקְרִיב קָרְבָּנוֹת, שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כִּמְכִירַת דָּבָר קְדוּשָׁה,
And regarding the sale of the birthright by Esau to offer sacrifices, which appears like the sale of a sacred matter,
שָׁמַעְתִּי לְפִי שֶׁהוּא הָיָה בְּכוֹר בְּדִמְיוֹן וְלֹא בֶּאֱמֶת,
I heard: because he was a firstborn only in illusion and not in truth,
לְפִיכָךְ הוֹעִילָה מְכִירָה בְּדִמְיוֹן.
therefore a sale within the realm of illusion was effective.

paragraphs.text: Rav Hai Gaon, quoted in Responsa Maharam Alashkar 101, distinguishes enabling another’s Torah and mitzvot from purchasing that person’s already-earned reward. A supporter receives reward for his own assistance; money or a gift does not transfer another’s spiritual reward to him. The response invokes Song of Songs 8:7 and the contrast between legitimate support and Shevna’s proposed sharing with Hillel. This is the distinction behind Rav Tzadok’s rejection of a sale of mitzvot.

paragraphs.text: Yisrael Kedoshim 7:1: “He [Yitzchak] considered him [Esav] a vessel prepared for holiness, since he had been formed as a firstborn. Although the firstborn had not yet been sanctified, the forefathers fulfilled the whole Torah and he knew that the firstborn would be sanctified in the future. In truth, however, Yaakov took the birthright and the blessings from him, for everything truly belonged to Yaakov. The birthright came first, even though holiness follows blessing, because the birthright at that time was not holiness itself but a preparation for holiness. He had to take all this from Esav indirectly, because from the appearance of this world everything initially seemed to belong to Esav. For this is the order of the world: first darkness and then light, as they said at the beginning of Berakhot.”

However, the sale of transgressions is effective and he (the buyer) becomes his replacement,
וּלְכָךְ פּוֹרְעָנוּת הַבָּאָה לָעוֹלָם הוּא בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל (יְבָמוֹת סג.),
and therefore tribulation that comes into the world comes only on account of Israel (Yevamot 63a),
שֶׁכָּל אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם פִּדְיוֹנָם לִסְבּוֹל גַּם כֵּן,
for all the nations of the world are their redemption to suffer as well,
אֲבָל טוֹב הַמַּגִּיעַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׂכַר הַצָּפוּן אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק.
yet in the good that reaches Israel in the hidden supernal reward, they possess no share.

p: וּבְאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לְהֵיפֶךְ,
And among the nations of the world it is the reverse:
הַחֲטָאִים אֶצְלָם קִנְיַן הַגּוּף בְּעֶצֶם וְאֵין לוֹ פִדְיוֹן,
sins with them are an intrinsic acquisition of the body and have no redemption,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַטּוֹב יֵשׁ לוֹ פִדְיוֹן,
whereas the good does have redemption,
וְעַל זֶה הוּא הַגָּלוּת שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל קוֹלְטִים אוֹתוֹ.
and it is for this that the exile exists, so that Israel may absorb that good.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 57:2: “All their association with the nations, in its deepest truth, is only to absorb holy sparks from them. As the Sages said: Israel went into exile only so that converts would be added to them. This does not mean only actual converts, but the additional absorption of the nations’ powers, returning them little by little to holiness, until the final time when everything returns to holiness. Although this is not yet revealed outwardly, in the inward heart this light is revealed and shines clearly, and nevertheless accomplishes its work.”

sections.en: The Potential for Ascent at Moments of Failure

p: [עו] בְּעֵת כִּשְׁלוֹן הָאָדָם, יֵדַע שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ עֵת הוּא הֲכָנָה לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר לְטוֹב;
At the moment of a person's stumbling, he should know that this very time is a preparation for that exact matter toward the good;
וְאִם יִזְכֶּה בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה, יוּכַל לַעֲלוֹת לְמַדְרֵגָה גְּדוֹלָה מְאֹד.
and if he merits at that crucial hour, he can ascend to an exceedingly exalted spiritual rung.
כְּפִי גּוֹדֶל הַחֵטְא שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר מְסִיתוֹ, כָּךְ הוּא גּוֹדֶל הַטּוֹבָה שֶׁיּוּכַל לִקְלוֹט אָז,
Commensurate with the magnitude of the sin to which the evil inclination incites him, such is the magnitude of the goodness he can absorb then,
אִם יַהֲפֹךְ תְּשׁוּקָה זוֹ וְחֶמְדָּה זוֹ לְטוֹב,
if he will invert this intense longing and desire toward the good,
וּמֵאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן מַמָּשׁ הוּא הַטּוֹבָה – הֵיפֶךְ הָרָעָה.
and from that very same essence springs the goodness, as the exact antithesis of the evil.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (פִּינְחָס רטז סוֹף עַמּוּד א), כִּי בְּעֵת הַמַּבּוּל הָיוּ רְאוּיִים לְקַבֵּל הַתּוֹרָה,
And as written in the Zohar (Pinchas 216a end), that at the time of the Deluge they were originally worthy to receive the Torah,
וְהָיָה אָז מֹשֶׁה כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֻלִּין קלט:) עַל "בְּשַׁגַּם", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and Moses was already latent then, as our Sages expounded (Chullin 139b) on the word beshagam (Genesis 6:3), see there.
וּמַיִם הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה, וְהֵם הֲפָכוּהוּ לַ"מַּיִם הַזֵּידוֹנִים";
And water signifies Torah, yet they perverted it into "the raging waters" (Psalms 124:5);
וְהַתּוֹרָה הִיא תַּכְלִית קִיּוּם הָעוֹלָם וְשֶׁבִּשְׁבִילוֹ נִבְרָא, וְאִלְמָלֵא וְכוּלֵי, וְהֵם גָּרְמוּ אָבְדָנוֹ;
and the Torah is the ultimate purpose of the world's existence for whose sake it was created—and were it not for it, etc.—yet they caused the world's destruction;
וְאוֹתוֹ עֵת הָיָה מוּכָן, אִלּוּ זָכוּ, מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ, שֶׁהוּא יְרִידַת מֵימֵי הַתּוֹרָה לְקִיּוּם הָעוֹלָם.
whereas that exact hour was prepared, had they merited, for the absolute opposite: the descent of the waters of Torah for the enduring preservation of the cosmos.
וְכֵן בְּעֵת הַחוּרְבָּן נוֹלַד מָשִׁיחַ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק ב דִּבְרָכוֹת הֲלָכָה ד),
And likewise, at the moment of the Temple's destruction the Messiah was born (Yerushalmi Berakhot 2:4),
כִּי אוֹתוֹ עֵת הָיָה מוּכָן, אִם זָכוּ, לְבִיאַת מָשִׁיחַ וּבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הַנִּצְחִי וְקַיָּים לָעַד;
for that very hour was primed, had they merited, for the advent of the Messiah and the building of the eternal Holy Temple that endures forever;
וְזֶה הָיָה טָעוּת אַנְשֵׁי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם וּנְבִיאֵי הַשֶּׁקֶר, שֶׁהָיוּ חוֹשְׁבִים כִּי אַדְּרַבָּה יֵיטִיב ה' לָהֶם, שֶׁרָאוּ הָעֵת מוּכָן לְכָךְ אִם זָכוּ:

and this was the tragic error of the people of Jerusalem and the false prophets who imagined that, on the contrary, Hashem would bestow great favor upon them, since they saw the hour primed for it had they only merited.

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, On Book of Joshua 23 describes stumbling as potentially preparing later Torah understanding through repentance. The opportunity is not automatically realized by the sinner; another may receive the understanding he failed to attain. The source also insists on continuing human acknowledgment of sin, while forgiveness and transformation of the past come from God. The possibility of repair therefore supplies a call to return, not a declaration that the failure was already harmless.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan:2 reads the Flood’s first rain as merciful: through repentance it could have become blessing, associated with Torah. Continued corruption turned that same prepared flow into destructive waters. The passage then connects Cheshvan’s rains and forty-day reception period with accepting renewed Torah after Tishrei. A promising spiritual moment thus requires a faithful response; its potential alone does not ensure its outcome.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 171:1 explains that a time, place, or soul described as prepared for punishment is prepared to receive divine payment. Abundant good can overwhelm an unready recipient, as in the image of vessels broken by excess light; one who is ready receives the good itself. The siman connects this with the cherubim at the destruction, Yechezkel’s visions, and Mashiach’s birth on the Ninth of Av. It distinguishes the influx from the capacity to receive it.

p: [עז] אֲפִילּוּ אָדָם גָּדוֹל בְּיוֹתֵר, אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ פְּגָם בְּמִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ, אֵין לְהִתְדַּבֵּק בּוֹ,
Even regarding an exceptionally great person, if there is a flaw in his family lineage, one should not bind oneself to him in marriage;
כִּי אִם הוּא מִפְּנֵי גָּדְלוֹ אֵין זֶה מַזִּיק לוֹ – יַזִּיק לְזַרְעוֹ,
for even if on account of his personal greatness it causes no harm to him, it will harm his future offspring,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּיבָמוֹת (מה.): אֲפִילּוּ נֶהֱוֵי כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן לָא יָהֵיבְנָא לֵיהּ בְּרַתָּא.
as written in Yevamot (45a): "Even were he to be like Joshua son of Nun, I would not give him my daughter."
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם דִּקְדֵּק וְאָמַר "כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן" וְלֹא "כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם"
Nonetheless, he was precise in saying "like Joshua son of Nun" and not "like Moses our teacher, peace be upon him"
[וְהַפּוֹסְקִים הוֹכִיחוּ מִזֶּה דְּאָסוּר לוֹמַר "כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם", וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם טַעַם יֵשׁ בַּדָּבָר],
and halakhic authorities deduced from this that it is forbidden to say 'like Moses our teacher,' yet there is an intrinsic rationale in the matter,
כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַתּוֹרָה, וּמִצַּד כֶּתֶר הַתּוֹרָה אֵין לָחוּשׁ לְמִשְׁפָּחוֹת,
for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, is the root of Torah, and from the perspective of the Crown of Torah one is not concerned with ancestral lineage,
וְכֶתֶר תּוֹרָה מוּנָּח לַכֹּל, וְאָמְרוּ (הוֹרָיוֹת יג.): "מַמְזֵר תַּלְמִיד חָכָם קוֹדֵם וְכוּלֵי",
and the Crown of Torah lies open to all, and they taught (Horayot 13a): "A scholar born of illicit union precedes a high priest who is ignorant,"
וּלְכָךְ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם קִבֵּל הָעֵרֶב רַב.
and therefore Moses our teacher accepted the Mixed Multitude (Erev Rav).
וּלְכָךְ אִלּוּ הֲוָה כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר תַּלְמִיד חָכָם גָּדוֹל בַּדּוֹר, שֶׁזֶּהוּ כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
Therefore, had he been like Moses our teacher—meaning the supreme Torah scholar of the generation, who embodies Moses our teacher,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת קא:): "מֹשֶׁה, שַׁפִּיר קָאָמְרַתְּ" – הֲוָה יָהֵיב.
as in the rabbinic dictum (Shabbat 101b): "Moses, you have spoken well"—he would indeed have given him his daughter.
רַק "כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן", רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר צַדִּיק
Rather, he said "like Joshua son of Nun," meaning a righteous master (tzadik)
[מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף]
of the seed of Joseph
מוֹשֵׁל בְּיִרְאַת אֱלֹהִים.
who rules through the fear of God.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא כב:): אֵין מַעֲמִידִין פַּרְנָס עַל הַצִּיבּוּר אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן קֻפָּה וְכוּלֵי,
And our Sages stated (Yoma 22b): We do not appoint a communal leader unless a box of creeping creatures ancestral blemishes hangs behind him,
וְנֶאֱמַר: "בִּי מְלָכִים יִמְלֹכוּ", וְאַדְּרַבָּה, הַלָּלוּ רְאוּיִים יוֹתֵר לְכָךְ,
and it is stated: "By Me kings reign" (Proverbs 8:15), and on the contrary, such individuals are better suited for it,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (נְדָרִים פא.): הִזָּהֲרוּ בִּבְנֵי עֲנִיִּים שֶׁמֵּהֶם תֵּצֵא תוֹרָה,
and as written (Nedarim 81a): "Be heedful of the children of the poor, for from them Torah emerges,"
כִּי מְקוֹם הַתּוֹרָה דַּוְקָא בְּכֵלִים שְׁבוּרִים
for the dwelling place of the Torah is specifically within broken vessels
וִיסוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, וְהוּא מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת גֵּרִים.
and the bedrock of the Oral Torah was Rabbi Akiva, who stemmed from a family of converts.
וְכֵן רַבִּי מֵאִיר אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין יג:) שֶׁלֹּא יָכְלוּ חֲבֵירָיו לַעֲמוֹד עַל סוֹף דַּעְתּוֹ.
And likewise regarding Rabbi Meir, our Sages said (Eruvin 13b) that his colleagues could not fathom the depth of his mind.
וְכֵן מִבְּנֵי קֵינִי חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה עָלוּ מֵעִיר הַתְּמָרִים, כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קד:):
And likewise the descendants of the Kenite, father-in-law of Moses, ascended from the City of Palm Trees to teach Torah, as our Sages expounded (Sanhedrin 104a).

sources.ref: Turei Zahav on Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De'ah 242:20

paragraphs.text: Turei Zahav on Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De’ah 242:20 discusses the prohibition cited here. Beit Yosef explains that comparing another person to Moses disrespects Moses’ unique stature, and supports this from the Gemara’s use of Joshua instead. Maharshal questions the reported flogging for a customary exaggeration lacking insulting intent, though he still recommends corrective fasting. The Taz prefers Beit Yosef’s explanation and also cites the marriage passage in Yevamot. The authorities’ disagreement is therefore part of the source, while Rav Tzadok develops an additional inward explanation.

paragraphs.text: Rabbi Akiva and the recovery of concealed Torah

rich.text: Rabbi Akiva and the recovery of concealed Torah

paragraphs.text: The Torah's emergence through broken vessels is connected with the release of holiness from concealment.

rich.text: The Torah's emergence through broken vessels is connected with the release of holiness from concealment.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Ki Tavo 11:2: “It is taught in the name of the holy Ari that Moses our teacher was the root of the Written Torah, while Rabbi Akiva was the root of the Oral Torah. For this reason Rabbi Akiva came from Sisera and the wife of Heber the Kenite: within them were sparks belonging to the aspect of the Oral Torah, while Sisera was the husk surrounding this holiness.”

rich.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok ·
Peri Tzadik, Ki Tavo 11:2

: “It is taught in the name of the holy Ari that Moses our teacher was the root of the Written Torah, while Rabbi Akiva was the root of the Oral Torah. For this reason Rabbi Akiva came from Sisera and the wife of Heber the Kenite: within them were sparks belonging to the aspect of the Oral Torah, while Sisera was the husk surrounding this holiness.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: In Ki Tavo, Rav Tzadok treats the tradition about Rabbi Akiva's ancestry as the emergence of Oral Torah from a place where its holiness had been enclosed. This gives a mechanism for the present siman's striking example of Torah in ‘broken vessels’: the apparent distance of the vessel does not determine the depth of the Torah hidden within it. The passage concerns a spiritual root and does not erase the distinctions in the siman's opening discussion.

p: [עח] פְּעָמִים גַּם בָּנִים רְשָׁעִים אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִצְמָח אֵיזֶה טוֹבָה לָאָב,
Sometimes even through wicked children it is possible that some benefit sprouts forth for the father,
כְּעִנְיַן אַבְרָהָם שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ יִשְׁמָעֵאל וּבְנֵי קְטוּרָה, שֶׁיָּצָא הַפְּסֹלֶת עַל יְדֵיהֶם.
like Abraham from whom emerged Ishmael and the sons of Keturah, through whom the inner dross was purged.
אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּזֶה צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה הָאָב שֶׁיֻּפְקַע תּוֹרַת זַרְעוֹ מֵהֶם,
However, in this the father must merit that the legal status of his spiritual lineage be completely severed from them,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאַבְרָהָם: "כִּי בְיִצְחָק יִקָּרֵא לְךָ זָרַע",
as written concerning Abraham: "for in Isaac shall seed be called to you" (Genesis 21:12),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים סוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּיבָמוֹת (יז.): לֹא זָזוּ מִשָּׁם עַד שֶׁעֲשָׂאוּם כְּגוֹיִם גְּמוּרִים,
and as written regarding the Ten Tribes at the end of the first chapter of Yevamot (17a): they did not depart from there until they designated them as complete gentiles;
וְיָדוּעַ דִּבְרֵי רַמְבַּ"ן עַל פָּסוּק "שֹׁרֶשׁ פֹּרֶה רֹאשׁ", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and the words of the Ramban on the verse "a root bearing gall" (Deuteronomy 29:17) are well known, see there.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ לְחִזְקִיָּהוּ פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת (י.): בַּהֲדֵי כַּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא לְמָא לָךְ?
And concerning this they said to Hezekiah in the first chapter of Berakhot (10a): "Why do you meddle in the secrets of the Merciful One?";
וַהֲרֵי מְנַשֶּׁה מֵאוֹתָן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה נֶאֱבַד חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד וְכָל הַשַּׁלְשֶׁלֶת הַקְּדוֹשָׁה מִן הָעוֹלָם אִלּוּ לֹא נוֹלַד.

for behold, Manasseh was counted among those who have no share in the World to Come, yet nonetheless the Messiah son of David and the entire holy lineage would have been lost from the world, Heaven forbid, had he not been born.
וּמָצִינוּ "וַיִּקֹּד הָעָם וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ" בְּפָרָשַׁת בֹּא, וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י: שָׂמְחוּ עַל בְּשׂוֹרַת הַבָּנִים;
And we find "and the people bowed their heads and worshipped" in Parashat Bo (Exodus 12:27), where Rashi explains: they rejoiced over the tidings of future children;
וַהֲרֵי שָׁם הוּא בִּשְׁאֵלַת "מָה הָעֲבֹדָה הַזֹּאת לָכֶם", שֶׁהוּא שְׁאֵלַת בֵּן רָשָׁע כִּדְאִיתָא בַּהַגָּדָה: "וְאַף אַתָּה הַקְהֵה וְכוּלֵי",
yet there it is framed in the question "What is this service to you?", which is the question of the wicked son as brought in the Haggadah: "you too blunt his teeth, etc.",
וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי שָׂמְחוּ עַל בְּשׂוֹרַת לֵידָתוֹ.
and even so, they rejoiced over the tidings of his birth.
וּמִיהוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (תַּנְחוּמָא תְּרוּמָה ט) מְפוֹרָשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ עַיֵּין שָׁם,
However, in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Terumah 9) it is explicitly stated to the contrary, see there:
דִּתְפִלַּת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁאִם יְבַקֵּשׁ בֵּן וְהוּא יִהְיֶה רָשָׁע – לֹא יִתֵּן לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ:
that King Solomon, peace be upon him, prayed that if he should request a son who would turn out wicked, the Blessed Name should not grant him one.

paragraphs.text: Sifrei Devarim 312:1: “Thus, when Avraham our father came into the world, dross emerged from him: Yishmael and all the sons of Keturah. When Yitzchak came into the world, dross emerged from him: Esav and all the chiefs of Edom. They became worse than the earlier ones. When Yaakov came, no dross emerged from him; rather, all his sons were born worthy, as it is stated, “Yaakov was a wholehearted man, dwelling in tents.” Through whom does the Omnipresent recognize His portion? Through Yaakov, as it is stated, “For Hashem’s portion is His people; Yaakov is the allotment of His inheritance,” and, “For Yah has chosen Yaakov for Himself.””

When Yaakov came, no dross emerged from him; rather, all his sons were born worthy, as it is stated, “Yaakov was a wholehearted man, dwelling in tents.” Through whom does the Omnipresent recognize His portion? Through Yaakov, as it is stated, “For Hashem’s portion is His people; Yaakov is the allotment of His inheritance,” and, “For Yah has chosen Yaakov for Himself.””

paragraphs.text: Divrei Soferim 38:3 makes an essential distinction between the patriarchal stages. After Yaakov, his descendants retain the name Israel despite grave wrongdoing; that root cannot be uprooted by their sins. The exclusion of Yishmael and Esav belongs to the earlier clarification of Avraham’s and Yitzchak’s offspring, completed through Yaakov. The present discussion of severed spiritual lineage must therefore be read alongside Rav Tzadok’s express affirmation of the continuing identity of Yaakov’s descendants.

p: [עט] עִנְיַן הַפְּגָם לְמַעְלָה עַל יְדֵי עֲווֹנוֹת הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָנוּ אוֹמְרִים שֶׁהַחַמָּה לוֹקָה;
The concept of a spiritual blemish Above caused by sins operates along the lines of what we say when the sun suffers an eclipse;
וּבֶאֱמֶת הַחַמָּה בְּעַצְמוּתָהּ וּמִצִּידָּהּ אֵינָהּ לוֹקָה כְּלָל, רַק הֶעְדֵּר אוֹרָהּ לָאָרֶץ – זֶה מִקְרֵי לַקּוּת לַחַמָּה,
for in truth, the sun in its own essence and from its own perspective suffers no eclipse whatsoever, only that the withholding of its light from reaching the earth is termed an eclipse of the sun,
שֶׁהֲרֵי עִנְיַן תַּכְלִיתָהּ שֶׁל חַמָּה לְהָאִיר לָאָרֶץ, וְזֶה לַקּוּת מִצִּידָּהּ.
seeing that the ultimate purpose of the sun is to illuminate the earth, and this constitutes a failure from its functional side.
וְכֵן בְּכָל לַיְלָה הוּא לַקּוּת הַחַמָּה, שֶׁגַּם זֶה הוּא מִצַּד מָסָךְ הַמַּבְדִּיל, דּוּגְמַת לַקּוּתָהּ בַּיּוֹם.
And so every night is functionally an eclipse of the sun, for this too stems from a separating barrier, analogous to its daytime eclipse.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם, כְּשֶׁהַלְּבָנָה מְאִירָה, אֵינוֹ לַקּוּת גָּמוּר לַחַמָּה,
Nonetheless, when the moon shines, it is not an absolute eclipse of the sun,
כִּידוּעַ שֶׁאוֹר הַלְּבָנָה הוּא מֵאוֹר הַחַמָּה וּבְרַק אוֹרוֹ;
for it is known that the light of the moon derives from the light of the sun and the sparkle of its radiance;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָנוּ קוֹרִים אוֹתוֹ אוֹר לְבָנָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַמְּבִינִים יוֹדְעִים כִּי הִיא בֶּאֱמֶת אוֹר חַמָּה וְלֹא לָקְתָה לְגַמְרֵי.
and even though we call it moonlight, those who understand know that it is truly solar light, so that the sun has not suffered a total eclipse.
אֲבָל בְּסוֹף חֹדֶשׁ אוֹ בְּעֵת לִקּוּיָהּ, שֶׁגַּם הַלְּבָנָה אֵין מְאִירָה, אָז הוּא לִקּוּת הַגָּמוּר לַחַמָּה.
But at the end of the month or during a lunar eclipse, when the moon likewise ceases to shine, that is an absolute eclipse of the sun.
וְזֶה מַמָּשׁ דּוּגְמָא שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (פְּסָחִים קיב.): יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁעֵגֶל וְכוּלֵי,
And this is an exact mirror of what transpires Above, as written (Pesachim 112a): "More than the calf wishes to suckle, the cow wishes to nurse";
וְתַכְלִית הִשְׁתַּלְשְׁלוּת הָאֲצִילוּת לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל;
and the ultimate purpose of the unfolding of divine Emanation is to channel spiritual influx unto Israel;
וּכְשֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל חוֹטְאִים, שֶׁאֵין מְקַבְּלִים אוֹר יְדִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל בּוּרְיוֹ,
and when Israel sins, failing to receive the light of the knowledge of the Blessed Name in its pristine clarity,
אָז נֶחְשָׁב כִּבְיָכוֹל תְּשִׁישׁוּת לְפַמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה;
then it is accounted, as it were, as a weakening of the Heavenly Host;
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן הַחוּרְבָּן דִּלְעֵילָא, וְגָלוּת הַדּוֹמֶה לְלַיְלָה, וּמַדְרֵגוֹת בַּגָּלוּת עַצְמוֹ, וְהָבֵן כָּל זֶה.
and this is the inner secret of the destruction Above, and exile which resembles night, and the varied gradations within exile itself; and understand all this.
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ: "רָאָה וַיַּתֵּר גּוֹיִם",
And therefore Scripture states: "He looked, and released the nations" (Habakkuk 3:6),
כִּי מֵעֵת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ מֹשֶׁה שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָה בְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים, אֵין מְקַבְּלִים אוֹר כְּלָל וְאֵין כָּאן לַקּוּת:

for from the time of the Giving of the Torah, when Moses requested that the Shechinah not dwell among the gentiles, they receive no direct divine light at all, and no celestial eclipse occurs on their account.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 1:18:1: “Alternatively: when the moon is eclipsed, the light is absent in the moon itself. This is an unfavorable sign for Israel, as it says, ‘I am with him in distress’ (Psalms 91:15), and when the Temple was destroyed the heavenly retinue was diminished. But an eclipse of the sun is an absence of light for those who see it, rather than in the sun. This is an unfavorable sign for the nations: the flow remains complete in its own place, but is lacking for them.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kometz HaMinchah explicitly develops the same source-and-recipient distinction. Its alternative explanation treats the sun's eclipse as an absence of light for observers while the light remains complete at its source. paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah 1:19:1 uses “impairment of the sun” broadly for night, an intervening cloud, obstruction by the moon, and visible spots in the luminary. It maps these respectively to the loss of a court’s leader without adequate eulogy, sexual wrongdoing that blocks receptivity, bloodshed between brothers, and a disruption of the received divine flow. Further mappings follow. The parallel shows that the present term includes ordinary night and screening, not only an astronomical eclipse.

sections.en: Rectifying Anger Through a Change of Place

p: [פ] תִּיקּוּן לְכַעַס – שִׁינּוּי מָקוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרָה תּוֹרָה גָּלוּת לְרוֹצֵחַ
The spiritual rectification for anger is change of place, just as the Torah prescribed exile for an unintentional murderer
וְהָיָה עִיר מִקְלָט וְלֹא נָע וָנָד לְעוֹלָם, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת יֵשׁ פַּחַד יִצְחָק וּגְבוּרוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת שֶׁטּוֹב,
and he was granted a City of Refuge rather than wandering aimlessly forever, for in truth there is the holy 'Fear of Isaac' and sacred Gevurot which are good,
כְּעִנְיַן הַאי צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנָן דְּרָתַח (תַּעֲנִית ד.), וְזֶהוּ הָעִיר מִקְלָט.
in the manner of a young Torah scholar who flares up in holy wrath (Ta'anit 4a), and this is the City of Refuge.
וּבְגִלְעָד וּשְׁכֶם דִּשְׁכִיחֵי רוֹצְחִים הִרְבּוּ עָרֵי מִקְלָט כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמַכּוֹת (ט סוֹף עַמּוּד ב),
And in Gilead and Shechem, where murderers were rampant, they multiplied Cities of Refuge, as written in Makkot 9b,
כִּי אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּא בִּטְרוּנְיָא;
for the Blessed Name does not act tyrannically;
מֵאַחַר שֶׁבְּטֶבַע הַתּוֹלָדָה שָׁם שְׁכִיחֵי רוֹצְחִים, מִסְּתָמָא שָׁם שְׁכִיחַ דָּבָר זֶה בִּקְדוּשָׁה דְּרִתְחָא, דְּהַיְינוּ עָרֵי מִקְלָט,
since by innate nature murderers were prevalent there, presumably that trait was originally prevalent there in holy fervor—which corresponds to the Cities of Refuge—
וּכְשֶׁבָּא לְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בָּא לִרְצִיחָה הָרָעָה.
and when it degenerated into outward excess, it devolved into evil murder.
וְגִלְעָד וּשְׁכֶם שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּנַחֲלַת יוֹסֵף, כִּי "לֹא תִרְצַח" וְ"לֹא תִנְאָף" שְׁנֵיהֶם הֲפָכִים כַּנּוֹדָע.
And Gilead and Shechem are both situated within the tribal heritage of Joseph, for "You shall not murder" and "You shall not commit adultery" are exact polar counterparts, as is known.
וְשָׁמַעְתִּי: "שַׂעְרֵךְ וְגוֹמֵר מֵהַר גִּלְעָד" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ד, א), כִּידוּעַ שֵׂעָר הוּא הַדִּינִים וּגְבוּרוֹת שֶׁבָּאָדָם, וְהֵם קְדוֹשׁוֹת מֵהַר גִּלְעָד.

And I heard expounded: "Your hair is like a flock of goats that stream down from Mount Gilead" (Song of Songs 4:1)—for hair represents judgments and rigorous powers in man, and their root is holy from Mount Gilead.
וְשֶׁזֶּהוּ מַה שֶּׁאָמַר אַחְאָב: "הֲיָדַעְתֶּם כִּי לָנוּ רָמֹת גִּלְעָד" (מְלָכִים א כב, ג),
And this is what Ahab meant: "Do you know that Ramoth-gilead is ours?" (I Kings 22:3),
כִּי יָדַע שֶׁאֵין דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לְתַקֵּן רַק הֲרִיגַת הַנְּבִיאִים,
for he knew that there was no sin he could not rectify except the slaying of the prophets,
וְרָמוֹת בְּגִלְעָד הוּא עִיר מִקְלַט הָרוֹצֵחַ, לוֹמַר שֶׁהָיָה זֶה בִּקְדוּשָׁה, וְזֶהוּ "כִּי לָנוּ", אֲבָל לֹא הִצְלִיחַ.
and Ramoth-gilead was the City of Refuge for the killer, so he sought to claim that his deed was rooted in holiness, hence "it is ours," yet he did not succeed.
וְנֶאֱמַר בְּקַיִן: "נָע וָנָד תִּהְיֶה"
And concerning Cain Scripture decreed: "A fugitive and a wanderer shall you be" (Genesis 4:12)
[וְלֹא הָיָה לוֹ עִיר מִקְלָט כְּלָל, שֶׁהוּא רַק לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל].
having no City of Refuge at all, which belongs exclusively to the children of Israel.
וְתִיקּוּן לְתַאֲוָה – שִׁינּוּי מַעֲשֶׂה, שֶׁבָּא דְּבַר עֲבֵירָה לְיָדוֹ וְנִיצּוֹל הֵימֶנָּה, בָּזֶה נִתְקַן הַקּוֹדֵם.
And the rectification for illicit desire is change of deed: when an opportunity for sin comes into his hand and he is rescued from it, through this the past is rectified.
וְתִיקּוּן לְכָבוֹד – שִׁינּוּי הַשֵּׁם,
And the rectification for the pursuit of honor is change of name;
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁמּוֹעִיל לַחוֹלֶה, כִּי לִפְעָמִים אִידְּחֵי גַּבְרָא מִקַּמֵּי גַּבְרָא כַּנּוֹדָע, כִּי אֵין מַלְכוּת נוֹגַעַת בַּחֲבֶרְתָּהּ וְכוּלֵי;
and this is why changing a name helps a sick person, because sometimes one man is pushed aside before another, for one kingdom does not overlap another by even a hairsbreadth;
וּמַלְכוּת נִקְרָא כָּל עִנְיַן כָּבוֹד וּמֶמְשָׁלָה
and "kingdom" denotes any form of honor and authority
[אֲפִילּוּ עַל אִשְׁתּוֹ וּבָנָיו],
even within his home over his wife and children,
שֶׁאֵין לְךָ אָדָם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִקְרָא בֶּן מֶלֶךְ כַּנּוֹדָע,
for you have no Jew who is not called a prince, as is known,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִגְזַר עָלָיו לִפְעָמִים, וְהַתִּיקּוּן לָזֶה שִׁינּוּי הַשֵּׁם, וְאֵינֶנּוּ הַאי גַּבְרָא כְּלָל:
and on account of this judgment is sometimes decreed upon him, the remedy for which is a change of name, declaring that he is no longer that original man at all.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Matot 12:1 connects Gilead’s refuge cities and Moses’ burial there with the purification of anger. It distinguishes Moses’ exceptional freedom from anger—where even a slight departure concealed a law from him—from Pinchas’s particular task of zeal. The holy counterpart of severity therefore does not justify every angry act. This helps explain why Ahab’s claim to the holiness of his killing failed.

paragraphs.text: Makkot 10a:11-13: “Rabbi Yochanan said: If a teacher goes into exile, his academy is exiled with him. Is that so? Did Rabbi Yochanan not say: From where do we know that words of Torah provide refuge? For it is stated, “Betzer in the wilderness,” and afterward, “This is the Torah.” There is no difficulty: one statement concerns the time when he is engaged in it, and the other the time when he is not engaged in it. Alternatively, what does “provide refuge” mean? From the Angel of Death. Thus Rav Chisda was sitting and studying in the academy, and the messenger of the Angel of Death could not approach him because his mouth never ceased its study. The messenger went up and sat upon the academy’s cedar tree; the cedar cracked, Rav Chisda fell silent, and the messenger was able to reach him.”

sections.en: Overcoming Envy When Another's Light Rises

p: [פא] פְּעָמִים נִגְזַר עַל אָדָם לָמוּת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מִשּׁוּם "אֵין מַלְכוּת וְכוּלֵי", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם;
Sometimes it is decreed upon a person to die, Heaven forbid, because "one kingdom does not overlap another," as found with King David and Moses our teacher;
וְהָעֵצָה לָזֶה – הֶעְדֵּר הַקִּנְאָה, וְשֶׁיַּסְכִּים שֶׁיַּאֲפִיל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹרוֹ בְּחַיָּיו וְיִזְרַח אוֹר אַחֵר,
and the spiritual counsel for this is the eradication of envy, willingly consenting that the Blessed Name dim his light during his lifetime while another light shines forth,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא וָאֶתְחַנַּן וּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה וַיֵּלֶךְ, עַיֵּין שָׁם) בְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
as written (Midrash Tanchuma, Va'etchanan; Midrash Rabbah, Vayeilech) regarding Moses our teacher,
שֶׁנִּסְתַּמּוּ מִמֶּנּוּ מַעְיְנוֹת הַחָכְמָה וְעָמַד לִפְנֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
that the springs of wisdom were stopped from him and he stood deferentially before Joshua,
אֶלָּא שֶׁהוּא אָמַר: מֵאָה מִיתוֹת וְלֹא קִנְאָה אַחַת
except that Moses exclaimed: "A hundred deaths rather than a single pang of jealousy!"
[אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין קה:) "בַּכֹּל מִתְקַנֵּא חוּץ וְכוּלֵי", זֶהוּ לְאַחַר מִיתָה כְּהָרְאָיָה דְּשָׁם],
even though they said (Sanhedrin 105b) that in everyone a person is jealous except his son and disciple, that applies after death as the proof shows there,
מִשּׁוּם דְּאַכַּתֵּי לָא עָבַר יַרְדְּנָא, כִּדְאִיתָא בִּנְדָרִים (כב.) עַיֵּין שָׁם,
because he had not yet crossed the Jordan, as brought in Nedarim 22a, see there,
כִּי קִנְאָה נִמְשָׁךְ מִלֵּב רַגָּז;
for jealousy stems from an agitated heart;
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁמִּדַּבֵּק עַצְמוֹ בִּקְדוּשַׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הָאִידְנָא, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שָׁם
but when one attaches himself to the holiness of the Land of Israel nowadays, wherein every Jew possesses four cubits there
[וְכֵן מְקוֹם רַגְלָיו בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְזֶהוּ "וְהִתְפַּלְלוּ אֵלֶיךָ דֶּרֶךְ אַרְצָם", וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],
and likewise a foothold in the Holy Temple, which is 'and they shall pray to You by way of their land,' and this is not the place to elaborate,
יוּכַל לָזֶה
he is capable of overcoming this
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּגְלָה אֵלַי בַּחֲלוֹם (אוֹר לְיוֹם ב' רְאֵה כ"ה מְנַחֵם) פֵּירוּשׁ "לְמַעַן יִרְבּוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
and as was revealed to me in a dream (eve of Monday, Parashat Re'eh, 25 Menachem-Av) explaining 'that your days may be multiplied, etc.',
כִּי אָמְרוּ בִּמְגִילָּה (כח.) לְרַבִּי: יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁתַּגִּיעַ לַחֲצִי יָמַי, אֲבָל לְכוּלְּהוּ לָא, דְּהַבָּאִים אַחֲרֶיךָ בְּהֵמָה יִרְעוּ?
for they said in Megillah 28a to Rebbe: 'May it be His will that you reach half my days, but not all of them, for what shall those who follow after you do—graze cattle?';
וְכִי הַאי גַּוְונָא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ה.): אִלְמָלֵא אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁחָטְאוּ אָנוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בָּאנוּ לָעוֹלָם, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
and similarly Reish Lakish said in Avodah Zarah 5a: 'Were it not for our ancestors who sinned, we would be as though we never came into the world,' see there;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִבְטִיחַ עַל שְׁנֵיהֶם יַחַד, וְאֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר, וַהֲרֵי זֶה חִסָּרוֹן לַבָּנִים?
and the Blessed Name promised longevity for both fathers and sons together, yet how is that possible, since prolonged life of fathers seems a loss to the sons' prominence?
רַק "כִּימֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁקַּיָּימִים לְעוֹלָם, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם פְּעָמִים מִתְכַּסִּים בְּעָבִים וְנֶאֱפָלִים וְאֵין נִרְאֶה רָקִיעַ בְּטָהֳרָתָהּ,
Rather, 'as the days of the heavens above the earth'—which endure forever, yet at times are veiled in clouds and obscured so that the firmament is not seen in its pristine clarity;
אֲבָל זֶהוּ רַק "עַל הָאֲדָמָה וְגוֹמֵר", דִּבְלָאו הָכִי אֵין זֶה בְּרָכָה, כִּי מֵאָה מִיתוֹת וְלֹא קִנְאָה אַחַת:
but this is specifically 'upon the land' of Israel, for otherwise it would be no blessing, since a hundred deaths are preferable to a single pang of jealousy.

p: [פב] כְּשֶׁאָדָם נָע וָנָד, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּדַמֶּה שֶׁהוּא צָרִיךְ לְכָךְ לְטוֹבָתוֹ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם וַדַּאי חָטָא בִּרְצִיחָה
When a person wanders as a fugitive and vagabond, even though he imagines that he needs this journey for his own benefit, nonetheless he certainly sinned in an aspect of murder
[דּוּגְמַת קַיִן],
exemplified by Cain, regarding whom it was decreed: "A fugitive and a wanderer shall you be",
וְלָאו דַּוְקָא רְצִיחָה מַמָּשׁ, אֶלָּא דּוּגְמָתוֹ: כְּגוֹן אַחְוָורֵי אַפֵּי שֶׁדִּמּוּהוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא נח:) לִרְצִיחָה,
and not necessarily literal murder, but something akin to it: such as blanching the face of one's fellow in public shame, which our Sages compared to bloodshed (Bava Metzia 58b),
וְכֵן מֵצֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ צַעַר קָשֶׁה כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ,
and likewise causing one's fellow severe emotional distress or the like,
וְכֵן "הַנֵּחָמִים בָּאֵלִים" כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (נִדָּה יג.).
and likewise the waste of seed alluded to in "inflaming yourselves among the terebinths," as expounded by our Sages (Niddah 13a).
וּכְשֶׁנִּשְׁקַט וְנִקְבַּע בְּמָקוֹם, יֵדַע כִּי תִּיקֵּן זֶה.
And when he settles down and becomes firmly established in a place, let him know that he has rectified this flaw.
וְלִפְעָמִים תְּפִלָּה מְכַפֶּרֶת מֶחֱצָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּקַיִן: "וַיֵּשֶׁב בְּאֶרֶץ נוֹד" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה י);
And sometimes prayer atones for half the decree, as written regarding Cain: "and he dwelt in the land of Nod (wandering)," as expounded in Vayikra Rabbah (10:5);
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי "חֵן מָקוֹם עַל יוֹשְׁבָיו",
that is, because "the grace of a place is upon its inhabitants" (Sotah 47a),
וְכַאֲשֶׁר אֵין חֵן מְקוֹמוֹ עָלָיו וְהוּא כְּגֵר וְנוֹדֵד שָׁם, עֲדַיִן לֹא נִתְכַּפֵּר הַכֹּל עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה חֵן מָקוֹם עָלָיו

and when the grace of his dwelling place does not rest upon him and he feels like a transient stranger and wanderer there, the sin has not yet been fully atoned until the charm of the place settles upon him
[כִּי כְּשֶׁאֵין חֵן מְקוֹמוֹ עָלָיו, אָז עֲדַיִן הוּא נָע וָנָד בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה, וְהוּא סִימָן שֶׁתִּיקֵּן הַמַּעֲשֶׂה אֲבָל לֹא תִיקֵּן עֲדַיִן הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה]:
for when the charm of his place is not upon him, he is still wandering and unsettled in thought, which is a sign that he rectified the physical deed, but has not yet rectified the inner thought.

p: [פג] כְּמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּקִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה פְּעָמִים שֶׁאָדָם מוֹצֵא מְצִיאָה – הוֹן רַב, אוֹ זוֹכֶה בְּגוֹרָל לָאטֶע"רִיעַ וּמִתְעַשֵּׁר בְּלֹא שׁוּם יְגִיעָה,
Just as in the acquisitions of this world there are times when a person finds a lost treasure—vast wealth—or wins a lottery and becomes wealthy without any labor,
כָּךְ יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן בְּקִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַבָּא
so too is it regarding the spiritual acquisitions of the World to Come
הֲגַם שֶׁאָמְרוּ פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּמְגִילָּה (ו.): "לֹא יָגַעְתָּ וּמָצָאתָ – אַל תַּאֲמֵן",
although they taught in the first chapter of Megillah (6b): "If one says: 'I did not labor and I found,' do not believe him,"
הָא אַסְקֵיהּ שָׁם: הָנֵי מִילֵּי וְכוּלֵי, אֲבָל לְאוֹקְמֵי גִּירְסָא – סִיַּעְתָּא מִן שְׁמַיָּא;
behold, the Talmud concludes there: this applies to delving into analysis, but to retain one's learning requires Heavenly assistance;
וּבְוַדַּאי לֹא קָאֵי רַק אַ"יָגַעְתָּ וְלֹא מָצָאתָ" לְחוּד,
and surely this reservation applies not only to 'you labored and did not find,'
שֶׁהֲרֵי מִדָּה טוֹבָה מְרֻבָּה, וְאִם אֶפְשָׁר יָגַעְתָּ וְלֹא מָצָאתָ – כָּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּאֶפְשָׁר לֹא יָגַעְתָּ וּמָצָאתָ עַל יְדֵי סִיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא,

for the divine measure of reward is far greater than punishment, and if it is possible to labor and not find, all the more so is it possible that without prior labor one finds through Heavenly assistance,
וּכְעִנְיַן "וְנֹחַ מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי ה'",
and along the lines of "And Noah found grace in the eyes of Hashem" (Genesis 6:8),
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כט): הוּא מָצָא, אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לֹא מָצָא;
concerning which our Sages expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 29:1): he found grace, but the Holy One, blessed be He, did not find grace in him;
הַיְינוּ כִּי פְּעָמִים אָדָם זוֹכֶה בְּלֹא שׁוּם יְגִיעָה שֶׁהוּא שָׁמוּר מִן הָעֲבֵירָה וְנִקְרָא צַדִּיק, וְזֶהוּ מַדְרֵגַת נֹחַ
that is, because sometimes a person merits without any strenuous effort to be preserved from sin and is titled a righteous man, which was the level of Noah
[שֶׁמִּדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה הָיָה שָׁמוּר מִן הַפּוּרְעָנִיּוֹת].
who, measure for measure, was preserved from the cataclysmic punishment.
וּפְעָמִים אָדָם זוֹכֶה לְהַשִּׂיג הַשָּׂגוֹת מִידִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאוֹרוֹ, וְזֶהוּ מְצִיאַת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָצָא,
And at other times a person merits to attain profound perceptions of the knowledge of the Blessed Name and His light, and this is the "finding" of Israel which the Holy One, blessed be He, found,
שֶׁבָּזֶה מְיוּחָס גַּם כֵּן הַמְּצִיאָה לְמַעְלָה, כִּי יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁעֵגֶל וְכוּלֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת ע"ט.
in which this discovery is likewise attributed to Above, for "more than the calf desires to suckle, the cow desires to nurse," as I wrote above in Section 79.
וּמְצִיאָה אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צז.) שֶׁאֵינָהּ בָּאָה אֶלָּא בְּהֶסַּח הַדַּעַת;
And a found treasure, our Sages stated (Sanhedrin 97a), comes only through distraction of the mind;
אֲבָל מִי שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב וּמְצַפֶּה לְכָךְ, לֹא יִמְצָא לְעוֹלָם.
but one who sits passively awaiting it will never find it.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מָצִינוּ בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא יב:) שׂוֹכֵר פּוֹעֵל לִלְקוֹט מְצִיאוֹת,
Nonetheless, we find in the words of our Sages (Bava Metzia 12b) one who hires a laborer to gather found objects,
וְהֵם בִּדְבָרִים קְטַנִּים, וְגַם בִּדְבָרִים גְּדוֹלִים
and these occur both in minor things and in major windfalls,
כְּמוֹ יְהֵיב אַרְבַּע זוּזֵי לְסַפְּוָונָאֵי בְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַב גַּמְדָּא בִּנְדָרִים דַּף נ':
such as giving four zuz to sailors in the stories of Rabbi Akiva and Rav Gamda in Nedarim 50b.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Sefer Kedushat Shabbat 7:2 explains why attainment after labor is still a “find”: one could not previously direct effort toward an insight not yet known. Torah study prepares the recipient, while God grants wisdom beyond the person’s prior understanding. This complements the present distinction between working and passively awaiting a windfall; preparation does not give control over the particular disclosure.

sections.en: Righteousness and the Danger of Awakening Another's Envy

p: [פד] פְּעָמִים יֵשׁ "נִסְפֶּה בְּלֹא מִשְׁפָּט" (מִשְׁלֵי יג, כג), הַיְינוּ עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "יֵשׁ צַדִּיק אֹבֵד בְּצִדְקוֹ" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, טו) – עַל יְדֵי צִדְקוּתוֹ,

Sometimes there is one who is "swept away without justice" (Proverbs 13:23), which operates along the lines of "there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness" (Ecclesiastes 7:15)—specifically on account of his righteousness,
כְּמוֹ הֶבֶל שֶׁהֲרָגוֹ קַיִן בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁקִּבֵּל ה' מִנְחָתוֹ;
like Abel whom Cain murdered because Hashem accepted his offering;
וּבְוַדַּאי הָיָה הֲרִיגָה זוֹ מִמִּשְׁפַּט הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and certainly this slaying was part of the ultimate judgment of the Blessed Name.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי לֹא רָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בָּעוֹלָם נִבְרָא מַזִּיק לְנִבְרָא אַחֵר.
That is, because the Blessed Name does not desire that there exist in the world a creature who causes harm to another creature.
וְכָךְ עָשָׂה אוֹתוֹ חָסִיד בְּתַעֲנִית (כד.) שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ עַל בִּתּוֹ שֶׁתָּשׁוּב לַעֲפָרָהּ שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּשְׁלוּ בָּהּ בְּנֵי אָדָם;
And thus acted that pious man in Ta'anit 24a Rabbi Yosi of Yukrat who prayed that his daughter return to her dust so that men would not stumble into sin because of her;
וְכָךְ בִּקְשָׁה אוֹתָהּ בְּתוּלָה דְּסוֹטָה (כב.) שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּשְׁלוּ בָּהּ בְּנֵי אָדָם,
and so pleaded that maiden in Sotah 22a that men should not stumble through her beauty,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שַׁבָּת קמט:): כָּל שֶׁחֲבֵירוֹ נֶעֱנָשׁ עַל יָדוֹ וְכוּלֵי.
as written in Shabbat 149b: "Anyone on whose account his fellow is punished, etc."
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק ד הֲלָכָה ב, וְשָׁם הַגִּרְסָא: קִנְאָתֵינוּ עַל לֵב אָדָם, עַיֵּין שָׁם): "וְלֹא תַעֲלֶה קִנְאַת אָדָם עָלַי",

And this is what Rabbi Elazar prayed (Yerushalmi Berakhot 4:2, where the reading is: "nor jealousy of us into the heart of any man," see there): "and let not jealousy of me rise into any person's heart,"
שֶׁגַּם זֶה מַזִּיק לוֹ, כְּשֶׁעַל יְדֵי צִדְקוּתוֹ מִתְקַנְּאִים בּוֹ וְנֶעֱנָשׁ חֲבֵירוֹ עַל יָדוֹ, אָז גַּם הוּא נֶעֱנָשׁ.
for this too causes him harm: when on account of his righteousness others envy him and his fellow is punished through him, then he too is punished.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט, כִּי מִסְּתָמָא הָיָה בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב אֵיזֶה נְגִיעָה לְהִתְפָּאֲרוּת נֶגֶד חֲבֵירוֹ בְּצִדְקוּתוֹ,
Nevertheless, all unfolds in true justice, for presumably there was in the deep recesses of the heart some slight bias toward self-aggrandizement over his fellow regarding his piety,
וְ"הַנִּסְתָּרֹת לַה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ", אֲבָל בַּנִּגְלוֹת הוּא שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִשְׁפָּט.
and "the secret things belong to Hashem our God" (Deuteronomy 29:28), even though in external appearance it seems unjust.
כִּי יֵשׁ נִסְתָּרוֹת שֶׁנִּסְתָּר גַּם לָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ, רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יוֹדֵעַ,
For there are hidden faults concealed even from the person himself, which only the Blessed Name knows,
וְאֵין לָזֶה שׁוּם עֵצָה רַק תְּפִלָּה וְרַחֲמִים;
and for this there is no remedy except prayer and divine mercy;
כִּי מִי שֶׁנָּקִי בֶּאֱמֶת, אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹמְרוֹ וְ"לֹא יְאֻנֶּה לוֹ כָּל אָוֶן" שֶׁאֵין אַחֵר נִכְשָׁל עַל יָדוֹ
for one who is truly pure, the Blessed Name preserves him and "no iniquity shall befall him" such that no other person stumbles because of him

[וּלְכָךְ תְּפִלַּת רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנֶה כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס לַתּוֹרָה, דְּשָׁם הוּא בְּיוֹתֵר כַּנּוֹדָע, דְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם תִּיקּוּן הֶבֶל וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְקַן, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ]:

and therefore was the prayer of Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah instituted upon entering the house of study, for there this danger is greatest, as Moses our teacher was the rectification of Abel and through Torah this was healed, and this is not the place to elaborate.

sections.en: The Hidden Pride of Spiritual Accomplishment

p: [פה] כְּשֶׁאָדָם חוֹשֵׁב בְּנַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁעָשָׂה הַרְבֵּה בַּעֲבוֹדַת ה', יֵדַע שֶׁלֹּא נָגַע בָּהּ כְּלוּם,
When a person thinks to himself that he has accomplished much in the service of Hashem, let him know that he has not touched it at all,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (קִדּוּשִׁין מט:): סִימָן לְגַסּוּת הָרוּחַ – עֲנִיּוּת דְּתוֹרָה;
as written (Kiddushin 49b): "A sign of arrogance is poverty in Torah knowledge";
כִּי "אִסְטִירָא בִּלְגִינָא קִישׁ קִישׁ קָרְיָא", מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כִּיס מָלֵא.
for "a single coin in an empty pitcher rattles loudly," whereas a full purse makes no sound.
וְכֵן אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, קצג עַמּוּד ב): סִימָן דְּלָא יָדַע כְּלוּם – שְׁבוּחֵי;
And so it is in the Zohar (Part III, 193b): "A sign that one knows nothing is that he boasts";
וְלָאו דַּוְקָא שְׁבוּחֵי וְגַסּוּת בִּפְנֵי הַבְּרִיּוֹת, רַק גַּם בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין עַצְמוֹ וּבְלִבּוֹ בִּלְבַד
and this does not mean only outward boasting and arrogance before people, but even between himself and his own conscience within his heart alone
כִּי עִיקַּר הַגַּאֲוָה בְּלִבּוֹ לְבַד, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "גְּבַהּ לֵב" כְּשֶׁסָּבוּר כֵּן.
for the essence of pride resides in the heart alone, as written: "an haughty heart" (Proverbs 16:5) when he presumes this about himself.
וְקַיִן הִקְרִיב דָּבָר גָּרוּעַ וְחָשַׁב שֶׁעָשָׂה עֲבוֹדָה גְּדוֹלָה, שֶׁלְּכָךְ חָרָה לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַבֵּל.
And Cain offered an inferior gift yet imagined he had performed a great service, which is why he was furious when it was not accepted.
וְטָעוּת זֶה נִמְשָׁךְ מִצַּד שֶׁשּׁוֹכֵחַ עִנְיַן הַיֵּצֶר וְכֹחוֹ, וְחוֹשֵׁב שֶׁכָּל מַחְשְׁבוֹת לִבּוֹ רַק טוֹב וְאֵין לוֹ נְטִיָּה לְרָע;
And this error stems from forgetting the nature of the evil inclination and its stealthy power, presuming that all thoughts of his heart are purely good without any inclination toward evil;
וּלְכָךְ הוֹדִיעוֹ אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵעִנְיַן הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע: "כִּי לַפֶּתַח [חַטָּאת רֹבֵץ] וְכוּלֵי",
and therefore the Blessed Name informed him then of the reality of the inclination: "sin crouches at the door, etc." (Genesis 4:7),
וּכְשֶׁיֵּדַע זֶה וְיָשִׂים עֵינָיו בְּחַדְרֵי לִבּוֹ, אָז יֵדַע כִּי לֹא פָּעַל מְאוּמָה בֶּאֱמֶת גָּמוּר בְּלִי שׁוּם פְּנִיָּה וּנְגִיעָה

and when a person knows this and casts his gaze into the chambers of his heart, he will realize that he has accomplished nothing in absolute purity of truth devoid of ulterior motive and personal bias
[וְהוֹדָעַת "וְאַתָּה תִּמְשָׁל בּוֹ" – שֶׁגַּם זֶה מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהָבֵן]:
and the declaration "yet you may rule over it" informs that even this mastery is granted from the Blessed Name; and understand this.

rich.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok ·
Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 2:4

: “Jacob our father merited Torah through his smallness in his own eyes, as it says, ‘I am diminished by all the kindnesses …,’ and, ‘Jacob, for he is small.’ Words of Torah leave a high place and go to a low place. A sign of arrogance is poverty in Torah; and they said, ‘Words of Torah endure only in someone who makes himself like one who does not exist.’”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: The Chanukah passage uses the same saying about arrogance and poverty in Torah, but supplies its positive counterpart in Yaakov’s smallness in his own eyes. Humility makes the person a place where Torah can settle and endure. This helps explain why the present siman examines even unspoken pride: the obstacle is an inward sense of having already achieved enough, which prevents the honest recognition of bias and dependence described at the siman’s conclusion.

sections.en: Family and Possessions as Reflections of the Soul

p: [פו] כָּל מַה שֶּׁהוּא מִקִּנְיַן הָאָדָם: אִשְׁתּוֹ וּבָנָיו, עַבְדּוֹ וַאֲמָתוֹ, שׁוֹרוֹ וַחֲמוֹרוֹ, אָהֳלוֹ וְכַסְפּוֹ וּזְהָבוֹ וְכָל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ – הַכֹּל הוּא מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ,

Everything that belongs to a person's possessions—his wife and children, his manservant and maidservant, his ox and donkey, his tent, his silver and gold, and all that he owns—all derives from the root of his soul;
כִּי גַּם כָּל הַדּוֹמֵם, צוֹמֵחַ, חַי מְשׁוֹרָשִׁים בְּנֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ חַיּוּתָם מִמֶּנּוּ כַּנּוֹדָע.
for all inanimate matter, vegetation, and animal life are rooted in the human soul, and the source of their vitality stems from him, as is known.
וּמַה שֶּׁקָּנוּי לוֹ הוּא שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ חַיּוּתָם מִמֶּנּוּ,
And that which is acquired by him is because the root of their vitality flows directly from his soul;
וְקִנְיָנִים שֶׁהֵם הֶפְקֵר וְכָל חַיְתוֹ יָעַר הוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא תִיקֵּן כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ חַיּוּתוֹ,
whereas creatures that are ownerless in the wild and all the beasts of the forest remain unacquired because he has not yet rectified the entirety of his vital soul-root,
כִּי וַדַּאי גַּם כֵּן שַׁיָּיךְ לָאָדָם, וּלְעָתִיד נֶאֱמַר: "וְגָר זְאֵב עִם כֶּבֶשׂ",
for surely they too ultimately belong to man, and concerning the messianic future it is written: "And the wolf shall dwell with the lamb" (Isaiah 11:6),
וְכֵן הַנָּחָשׁ הָיָה קוֹדֶם הַחֵטְא שַׁמָּשׁ לָאָדָם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סַנְהֶדְרִין נט:).
and likewise the serpent prior to the primal sin was a servant to man (Sanhedrin 59b).
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהוּא הָאָדָם, כָּךְ קִנְיָנָיו,
And as the person is, so are his possessions,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (חֻלִּין ז.): בְּהֶמְתָּן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵבִיא תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדָם – מֵחֲמוֹרוֹ דְּרַבִּי פִּינְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר;
as written (Chullin 7a): through the animals of the righteous the Holy One brings no stumbling block—demonstrated by the donkey of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair;
וְכֵן בְּנֹחַ, כָּל הַמִּינִים שֶׁהָיוּ בַּתֵּבָה שֶׁהוּא זָנָם מִסְּתָמָא הָיוּ מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, לְכָךְ אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁלֹּא קִלְקְלוּ דַּרְכָּם.
and so with Noah, all the species in the Ark whom he sustained were presumably linked to his soul-root as noted above, which is why our Sages taught that they had not corrupted their ways.
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר "אֵשֶׁת חָבֵר כְּחָבֵר", וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ: נִשֵּׂאת לְעַם הָאָרֶץ וְהָיְתָה וְכוּלֵי (בְּכוֹרוֹת ל סוֹף עַמּוּד ב),
And it goes without saying that "the wife of an associate (chaver) is like an associate," and conversely: if she married an ignoramus she assumes his status (Bekhorot 30b),
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר הַבָּנִים, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ן עַל פָּסוּק "שֹׁרֶשׁ פֹּרֶה",
and it goes without saying regarding children, as the Ramban wrote on the verse "a root bearing gall" (Deuteronomy 29:17),
וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב דְּעֵדֻיּוֹת): הָאָב זוֹכֶה לַבֵּן.
and as our Sages stated (Eduyot 2:9): "A father endows his son."
וְאִם הַבֵּן רָשָׁע, עַל כָּרְחֲךָ הָיָה אֵיזֶה פְּסֹלֶת בָּאָב
And if the son turns out wicked, perforce there was some dross within the father
[וְזֶהוּ "פֹּקֵד עֲוֹן אָבוֹת וְגוֹמֵר", וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין כז:) כְּשֶׁאוֹחֲזִין מַעֲשֵׂה וְכוּלֵי, וְהוּא עֲוֹן אָבוֹת מַמָּשׁ וְאֵינוֹ חוּץ מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין]

and this is "visiting the iniquity of the fathers, etc.," which our Sages in Sanhedrin 27b explained: when they grasp the deeds of their fathers, which is truly the father's iniquity and is not outside strict justice
הַנֶּעְלָם;
which was concealed;
וְכֵן יוּכַל לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן הָאָדָם מִכָּל קִנְיָנָיו:
and thus a person can spiritually reflect upon himself from all his possessions.

We have explained this several times.”

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Bereshit 3 describes humanity as receiving powers from the inanimate, growing, and animal worlds. Service to God can elevate all those received powers, connecting creation with its source. The relation is reciprocal: the creatures share in human good and harm, illustrated by the Flood. This supplies a mechanism for the present account of associated creatures as a reflection on one’s own service.

paragraphs.text: Rabbeinu Bahya, Shemot 35:1:2: “It is known that the lower creatures have four divisions, one above another: the inanimate, the growing, the living, and the speaking. The inanimate are mountains and hills; this division has no soul at all, neither a vegetative soul nor a soul of movement, and certainly no intellectual soul. Above it is the growing: it has an advantage over the inanimate because it has a vegetative soul. Above the growing are the other living creatures, which have a soul of movement and a vegetative soul. Above the living creatures that do not speak is the human being, who includes them all through his vegetative soul and his soul of movement, and has an advantage over them all through his intellectual soul.”

p: [פז] אֵין גְּזֵירָה יוֹצְאָה מִפִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶלָּא בְּהַסְכָּמַת צַדִּיקֵי הַדּוֹר
No decree goes forth from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, except with the consent of the righteous of the generation
[שֶׁהֵם בֵּית דִּינוֹ],
who constitute His heavenly court on earth,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאִדְרָא רַבָּא (קמב עַמּוּד ב): "סוֹד ה' לִירֵאָיו", וְעַד דְּלָא אַסְכִּימוּ לָא נָחֲתִין דִּינִין לְעָלְמָא.
as written in the Idra Rabba (Zohar III:142b): "The secret of Hashem is to those who fear Him," and until they give assent, judgments do not descend upon the world.
וְאֵיךְ יִהְיֶה זֶה, וַהֲלֹא הֵם אַדְּרַבָּה מִתְפַּלְּלִים בַּעֲדָם?
But how can this be, seeing that on the contrary they pray to avert disaster?
רַק שֶׁהוּא בְּעִנְיָן אַחֵר הַדּוֹמֶה לוֹ, כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁהָיָה בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בַּכִּבְשָׂה
Rather, it is drawn out through another analogous scenario, like what occurred with King David, peace be upon him, regarding the ewe

[וְיִרְמְיָה הָיָה בִּבְנֵי עֲנָתוֹת, וְגָלוּת עֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים הָיָה יְשַׁעְיָה בְּשֶׁבְנָא, וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ בִּסְדוֹם הוּא בַּמֶּה שֶׁהִפְרִיד לוֹט מִקּוֹדֶם, וְכֵן הַכֹּל, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ].

and Jeremiah through the men of Anathoth; and the exile of the Ten Tribes occurred when Isaiah condemned Shebna; and Abraham regarding Sodom was through his separating Lot earlier; and so throughout, which is not the place to lengthen.
וּלְכָךְ צָרִיךְ שְׁמִירָה בָּזֶה שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא לְעוֹלָם דָּבָר רַע מִפִּיו.
And therefore great vigilance is required so that a harsh word never escapes one's mouth.
וּלְכָךְ הַצַּדִּיק נִתְפָּס, וּ"בַהֲדֵי הוּצָא לָקֵי כְּרָבָא";
And therefore the righteous person is caught, and "along with the thorn the cabbage is struck" (Bava Kamma 92a);

sections.en: Sincerity of Heart and the Straight Path

p: [פח] אֵין דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ עֲקַלְקַלּוֹת, רַק שֶׁבְּעֵינָיו הוּא יָשָׁר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִשְׁלֵי (כא, ב): "[כָּל דֶּרֶךְ אִישׁ יָשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו]";
There is no personal path that does not contain crooked turns, only that in a man's own eyes it appears straight, as written in Proverbs 21:2: "Every way of a man is right in his own eyes";
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַתַּאֲווֹת צָרִיךְ לְעַקֵּם דְּרָכָיו, שֶׁהֵם פְּחָתִים שֶׁבֵּינְתַיִם שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִישׁוֹר,
for through physical desires one inevitably twists his pathways, which form hidden pits making the road uneven,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה יב) עַל פָּסוּק "יִתְהַלֵּךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִים":
as written in Vayikra Rabbah (12:1) on the verse "it goes down smoothly" (Proverbs 23:31):
כִּי הַמִּתְהַלֵּךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִים כָּל הָעֲרָיוֹת דּוֹמוֹת עָלָיו כְּמִישׁוֹר (יוֹמָא עה.),
for to one who walks uprightly, all illicit temptations appear like a level plain (Yoma 75a),
לוּלֵי כֵן אִי אֶפְשָׁר לֵילֵךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִים.
whereas without that moral rectitude it is impossible to walk straight.
וּמִי שֶׁבְּעֵינָיו הוּא יָשָׁר, מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה? וַהֲלֹא לְפִי דַעְתּוֹ הוֹלֵךְ בְּיֹשֶׁר!
And if in a man's own eyes his way appears straight, what can he do, since according to his own judgment he is walking uprightly?
עַל זֶה אָמַר: "וְתֹכֵן לִבּוֹת ה'",
Concerning this Scripture concludes: "but Hashem weighs the hearts" (Proverbs 21:2):
מִי שֶׁלִּבּוֹ שָׁלֵם אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁגֵּהוּ לְהַטְעוֹתוֹ, וְאֵינוֹ בָּא בִּטְרוּנְיָא,
one whose heart is wholly sincere, the Blessed Name will not mislead into error, nor does He act tyrannically;
רַק עַקְמוּמִית שֶׁבַּלֵּב הוּא הַגּוֹרֵם הַטָּעוּת:
rather, an unrectified crookedness within the heart is what triggers the intellectual mistake.

This directly illuminates the present appeal to the One who weighs and prepares hearts.

paragraphs.text: Rabbeinu Bahya, Devarim 29:18:3 begins by asking how a person can be responsible for an unwilled thought. His answer distinguishes a thought’s sudden arrival from allowing it to remain, and emphasizes sustained preparation through good thought and action. He treats unwanted intrusions as an occasion to improve that preparation and reject the thought. Continued effort invites divine assistance in directing the heart toward good. This is one explanation within his discussion; further interpretations follow. The distinction between arrival and entertained thought must remain part of the parallel.

sections.en: The Art of Silence and Righteous Speech

p: [פט] דָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּחֻלִּין (פט.) עַל פָּסוּק "הַאֻמְנָם אֵלֶם וְגוֹמֵר":
Our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Chullin 89a on the verse "Do you indeed speak righteousness in silence?" (Psalms 58:2):
אֻמָּנוּתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה – יָשִׂים עַצְמוֹ כְּאִלֵּם.
"A person's craft in this world should be to make himself like a mute."
וּפֵירוּשׁ לְשׁוֹן "אֻמָּנוּת" – דָּבָר גָּדוֹל שֶׁאֵין כָּל אֶחָד יָכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ,
And the term "craft" (ummanut) denotes an extraordinary mastery that not everyone can achieve,
כִּדְאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי שִׁילְהֵי סֻכָּה: "בֶּאֱמוּנָתָם – בְּאֻמָּנוּתָם, אֻמָּנוּת גְּדוֹלָה וְכוּלֵי".
as they said in the Yerushalmi at the end of Sukkah: "'in their faith'—meaning in their craft, a great craft, etc."
וְאֵימַת הוּא אֻמָּנוּת? רַק כְּשֶׁ"צֶדֶק תְּדַבֵּרוּן",
And when is silence an artful craft? Only when "you speak righteousness,"
שֶׁלָּזֶה צָרִיךְ אֻמָּנוּת גָּדוֹל, כַּאֲשֶׁר מְדַבֵּר וּמַפְסִיק בָּאֶמְצַע שֶׁעַד פֹּה הוּא הַדִּבּוּר צֶדֶק,
for this requires immense mastery: to speak and deliberately stop in the middle when speech reaches the boundary of righteousness,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שֶׁלֹּא לְדַבֵּר כְּלָל.
unlike staying completely silent, which is simple.
אִי נַמֵּי: עֵצָה הוּא אֵיךְ יוּכַל לְאֻמָּנוּת זוֹ כְּשֶׁ"צֶדֶק תְּדַבֵּרוּן",
Alternatively, it provides counsel on how to acquire this craft of speaking righteousness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּעֵרָכִין (טו:) וּבִדְבָרִים רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה א) שֶׁדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מַרְפֵּא הַלָּשׁוֹן;
as written in Arachin 15b and Devarim Rabbah 1:1, that words of Torah heal the tongue;
וְשָׁם בִּדְבָרִים רַבָּה: שֶׁמַּתִּיר הַלָּשׁוֹן, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא מַתִּירוֹ לְדַבֵּר הַכֹּל,
and there in Devarim Rabbah: that Torah unties the tongue, meaning it permits one to speak freely,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֻכָּה (כא:): עֲלֵיהוּ – אֲפִילּוּ שִׂיחַת חֻלִּין וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁכָּל שִׂיחָתָן תּוֹרָה;
as written in Sukkah 21b: "its leaf"—even the casual conversation of Torah scholars is Torah;
וְזֶהוּ דְּמַיְיתֵי שָׁם: סְפָרִים נִכְתָּבִים בְּכָל לָשׁוֹן, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר אֲפִילּוּ שִׂיחַת חֻלִּין כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא תּוֹרָה,
and this is why the Talmud brings there: holy books may be written in any language, meaning even everyday vernacular when imbued with Torah,
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דִּבְרָכוֹת (סוֹף פֶּרֶק ט): פִּטְטַיָּא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא טָבִין
and this aligns with the Yerushalmi at the end of Berakhot: "casual conversations of Torah are precious"
וּמַאן דְּאָמַר: אֶלָּא יְוָנִית, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ (יִתְרוֹ) דְּאִינּוּן קְרִיבִין לְאָרְחֵי מְהֵימְנוּתָא עַיֵּין שָׁם,
and the authority who limits this to Greek, as written in Zohar Chadash (Yitro) that they were close to the paths of faith, see there;
מִזֶּה זָכוּ לַלָּשׁוֹן, וּבְבָבָא קַמָּא (פג.) מְחַלְּקִים בֵּין לָשׁוֹן לְחָכְמָה עַיֵּין שָׁם.
from this they merited their language, and in Bava Kamma 83a they distinguish between the Greek language and Greek wisdom, see there.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ (בִּמְגִילַּת תַּעֲנִית) דְּנֶחְשַׁךְ הָעוֹלָם בַּיּוֹם שֶׁנֶּעְתַּק הַתּוֹרָה לִיוָנִית וְשִׁנּוּ י"ג דְּבָרִים, וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר בֵּיאַרְנוּם,
Nonetheless, they recorded in Megillat Ta'anit that darkness fell upon the world on the day the Torah was translated into Greek and they altered thirteen matters, which we explained elsewhere;
וְשָׁם בֵּיאַרְנוּ כִּי הֵם זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה נֶגֶד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, לְכָךְ הָיוּ "פֻּם מְמַלִּל רַבְרְבָן",
and there we showed that they were the demonic counterpart facing the Oral Torah, speaking boastful arrogance,
וּלְכָךְ סְפָרִים נִכְתָּבִים בִּלְשׁוֹנָם, אֲבָל חָכְמָתָן שֶׁלָּהֶן בְּעַצְמָן אָסוּר לִלְמוֹד, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ:
therefore sacred scriptures could be written in their tongue, but studying their secular wisdom is forbidden, and this is not the place to lengthen.

The verse therefore says, ‘Speak righteousness.’ Could he then become arrogant? The verse therefore says, ‘Judge uprightly, sons of man.’”

paragraphs.text: Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 1:4 explains a scholar’s ordinary conversation as Torah when deliberate devotion has so shaped the person that even unplanned speech issues from that orientation. It expressly rejects treating such holiness as an inborn status without choice. The parallel explains how Torah can heal and open the tongue by changing its inward source, while preserving the possibility of failing to fulfill that role.
