paragraphs.text: Rabbeinu Bahya, Devarim 32:1:2: “The righteous person is compared to a tree, as it is written, “He shall be like a tree planted beside streams of water, which gives its fruit in its season, and whose leaf does not wither.” A tree produces leaf and fruit; this is a natural property implanted in it on the third day by the utterance, “Let the earth sprout.” The leaf has a purpose, for its shade protects the fruit from the sun’s heat, while the fruit is the essential thing. So too, the righteous person has leaf and fruit. His leaf is his speech about ordinary matters—the affairs of this world, his instruction, and his accounts of events. These are greatly beneficial, just as the leaf that shelters with its shade is beneficial. This is what our Sages expounded: “His leaf does not wither”—even the ordinary conversation of Torah scholars requires study. His fruit is his speech in Torah and wisdom, which is the essential thing, just as fruit is the essential thing in a tree.”

paragraphs.text: Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 1:8: “Our Sages said of Torah scholars that all their conversation is words of Torah. Since words of Torah are expressed in speech, all their speech becomes words of Torah. For wherever all a person’s thoughts are immersed, that immersion of thought is recognizable in every activity he undertakes, as is known. Similarly, the body’s eating and drinking, which resemble ordinary conversation, also become words of Torah and food and drink for the soul. Since through this the body is joined to the soul, and the body too derives benefit through a word of Torah, the body is then also included in holiness. Precisely through this comes holy inspiration; there is no room here to elaborate further.”

These, however, are permitted disciplines, and there is no prohibition in them; they are from the shell of nogah. As the Zohar Chadash says in Yitro, when enumerating the four shells: “Brightness around it” is the kingdom of Greece, which is surrounded by brightness, because among all the kingdoms none are as close to the path of faith as it is. This means that in Greek wisdom some attained an intellectual understanding of upright qualities. Yet “what wisdom have they,” since they are only from the shell of nogah: the brightness is not within them, but only around them, as stated in the Zohar Chadash.”

p: [צ] הַתּוֹרָה הוּא מַפַּת הָעוֹלָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה א בַּמָּשָׁל דְּדִיפְתְּרָאוֹת וּפִנְקְסָאוֹת;
The Torah is the architectural blueprint of the universe, as written in Bereishit Rabbah 1:1 in the parable of the monarch's parchments and drafting plans;
וְכֵן יִשְׂרָאֵל
and likewise Israel
[שֶׁהֵם וְאוֹרַיְיתָא חַד כַּנּוֹדָע, כִּי אוֹר הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא עַצְמוֹ אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב דְּיֵשׁ שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא אוֹתִיּוֹת לַתּוֹרָה]
who are one with the Torah, as the light of Jewish souls is identical with the light of Torah, there being 600,000 letters in the Torah corresponding to 600,000 souls
שֶׁבְּכָל דּוֹר הֵם מַפַּת הָעוֹלָם בְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר;
in every generation are the blueprint of the world in that generation;
כְּפִי הַהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת שֶׁבַּנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל דּוֹר, כֵּן הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת הָעוֹלָם בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן,
in accordance with the novel spiritual developments within the souls of Israel in each generation, so unfolds the renewal of world events in that era,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּיבָמוֹת (סג.): אֲפִילּוּ סְפִינוֹת וְכוּלֵי בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
as written in Yevamot 63a: even merchant ships travel only for the sake of Israel.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִשְׁתַּנּוֹת מִדּוֹר לְדוֹר, כֵּן הַתּוֹרָה, וְהַיְינוּ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁמִּתְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל דּוֹר חֲדָשׁוֹת עַל יְדֵי חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל;
And just as souls change from generation to generation, so does the Torah—namely the Oral Torah wherein new insights are revealed in every generation by the sages of Israel;
וְעַל יְדֵי כָּל חֲדָשׁוֹת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה יוֹצֵא לָאוֹר נְפָשׁוֹת חֲדָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
and through each novel revelation of the Oral Torah, new souls emerge into the light,
וְעַל פִּיהֶם נִתְחַדֵּשׁ גַּם כֵּן עִנְיָנִים בָּעוֹלָם.
and through them worldly events and circumstances are likewise transformed.
וּמִמַּצַּב הָעוֹלָם בְּכָל דּוֹר נוּכַל לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן עַל מַצַּב נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבַּדּוֹר,
And from the geopolitical condition of the world in every era, we can discern the spiritual stature of the souls of Israel in that generation,
וְכֵן עַל מַצַּב הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּפִיּוֹת תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הָאֲמִתִּיִּים שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ דּוֹר
and likewise the status of the Torah residing in the mouths of authentic scholars in that era
[וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ בְּחֲגִיגָה (ה:): "אָבְדָה עֵצָה מִבָּנִים – נִסְרְחָה חָכְמָתָם", עַיֵּין שָׁם וּמוּבָן]:
and therefore they stated in Chagigah 5b: "If counsel is lost from the children, their wisdom becomes corrupted," see there, and it is understood.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 73a: “For we have learned: Three levels are interconnected with one another—the Holy One, blessed be He, Torah, and Israel. Each, level upon level, is concealed and revealed. The Holy One, blessed be He: level upon level, concealed and revealed. Torah likewise: concealed and revealed. Israel likewise: level upon level. This is as it is written: “He tells His words to Yaakov, His statutes and judgments to Israel.” There are two levels—Yaakov and Israel—one revealed and one concealed.”

It expressly acknowledges that the ordinary number of Torah letters does not match six hundred thousand; the correspondence depends on letters dividing into sparks. New Torah teachings then correspond to the increase of souls. The number here therefore expresses a spiritual correspondence, not an unqualified count of written characters.

Divine governance clothed in storm appears in the righteous person’s zeal and in an opposing storm of self-assertion. When governance turns toward gentleness, those former modes cannot simply persist. The passage invokes the same saying from Chagigah 5b used here, providing a concrete model of the changing inward and outward forms of a generation.

sections.en: The Soul's Vitality Within Possessions and Livelihood

p: [צא] כָּל קִנְיָנֵי הָאָדָם הוּא מֵחֶלְקֵי חַיּוּתוֹ הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בַּבְּרוּאִים,
All possessions of a person derive from the sparks of his vital soul-force distributed throughout created beings,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּרֵאשִׁית" – בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵי;
as written: "In the beginning"—for the sake of Israel, etc.;
וְאָמְרוּ: הַמְּחַדֵּשׁ בְּטוּבוֹ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית,
and we declare in prayer: "Who in His goodness renews daily the work of Creation,"
וּבְכָל יוֹם הַחִדּוּשׁ הוּא בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל;
and each day's cosmic renewal unfolds for the sake of Israel;
וְכָל חֵלֶק מִן הָעוֹלָם שַׁיָּיךְ לְנֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁאוֹר חַיּוּתוֹ הוּא הַמְּקַיֵּים אוֹתָם הַנִּבְרָאִים.
and every segment of the universe belongs to an individual Jewish soul, meaning that the radiance of his vital force sustains those specific creations.
מִמַּעֲשִׂים הַטּוֹבִים מִתְקַיְּימִים בְּרוּאִים הַטּוֹבִים וְהַטְּהוֹרִים
From good deeds, good and pure creatures are sustained
[וּמִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת הֵם מַלְאָכִים וְרוּחָנִיִּים],
and from holy thoughts and divine desires, angels and spiritual entities are formed,
וּמֵהָרָעִים נַעֲשִׂים הָרָעִים
while from evil deeds, destructive forces are generated
[וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עֵירוּבִין (יח:) מִשִּׁכְבַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה: רוּחִין וְשֵׁדִין וְלִילִין]
along the lines of Eruvin 18b that from wasted seed demons and night-spirits are formed:
הַחַיּוֹת הַמַּזִּיקוֹת, וְכֵן עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים הָרוֹצְחִים,
dangerous wild beasts, murderous gentiles,
וְכֵן בַּדּוֹמְמִים: אֶבֶן שֶׁנִּסְקַל בָּהּ וְעֵץ שֶׁנִּצְלַב בּוֹ
and likewise among inanimate objects: the stone with which one was stoned and the gallows on which one was hung
וְזֶה סוֹד מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כד): מִן הַכֹּל עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהִפָּרַע, אֲפִילּוּ מִן אֶבֶן וְכוּלֵי.
and this is the secret of what our Sages said in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu: from everything the Holy One will exact retribution, even from a stone, etc.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "חַטָּאִים תְּרַדֵּף רָעָה", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְאָנֹכִי בָּרָאתִי מַשְׁחִית לְחַבֵּל",
And this is "evil pursues sinners" (Proverbs 13:21), and "I have created the waster to destroy" (Isaiah 54:16),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ו: אֵשׁ יוֹצְאָה מִגּוּפָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים וּמְלַהֶטֶת אוֹתָן,
and as written in Bereishit Rabbah 6: fire issues from the bodies of the wicked and consumes them,
וּבַצּוֹמְחִים: סַם הַמֵּמִית רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן וְכַיּוֹצֵא.
and among plants: lethal poison, may the Merciful One spare us, and the like.
וּכְפִי מֶרְחַק הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת אוֹרוֹ וְחַיּוּתוֹ בָּהֶם, כָּךְ הֵם עִנְיָנָם וְיַחְסָם לוֹ:
And in proportion to the closeness or distance of the extension of his light and vitality within them, such is their relationship to him:
מֵהֶם קִנְיָנִים לוֹ, וּמֵהֶם הָיוּ בְּיָדוֹ אֵיזֶה זְמַן וּמְכָרָם,
some remain his permanent possessions; some were in his possession for a time and he sold them;
וּמֵהֶם רַק בִּשְׁאֵלָה אוֹ שְׂכִירוּת זְמַן מוּעָט,
some are merely borrowed or rented for a brief interval;
וּמֵהֶם רָאָם אֵצֶל אֲחֵרִים אוֹ נִסְתַּכֵּל בָּהֶם מִדֵּי עָבְרוֹ בְּאֵיזֶה מָקוֹם,
some he merely saw in the possession of others or gazed upon as he passed by;
וּמֵהֶם שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה מִיָּמָיו רַק חָשַׁק בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ לָהֶם,
and some he never saw in his life, yet yearned for them in his private thoughts;
וְכַיּוֹצֵא יֵשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת לְאֵין שִׁיעוּר.
and like this there are countless gradations without end.
וְהַמֵּבִין עַל דָּבָר יוּכַל לָדַעַת וּלְהִתְבּוֹנֵן לְתַקֵּן כָּל אֵלֶּה,
And he who discerns these matters can understand and reflect on how to rectify all of them,
וְהַתִּיקּוּן הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי הַהֲשָׁבָה לַמָּקוֹר
and this rectification is achieved solely by returning them to the Source:
שֶׁיֵּדַע שֶׁהַכֹּל הוּא מֵעֶצֶם חַיּוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמְּחַיֵּיהוּ וּמְקַיְּימוֹ, זוּלַת זֶה הָיוּ כְּלֹא הָיָה
recognizing that everything exists exclusively through the essential vitality of the Blessed Name Who animates and preserves it, without which it would vanish into nothingness
וְזֶה סוֹד מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עג שֶׁהָיָה לְיַעֲקֹב שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא עֶדְרֵי צֹאן,
and this is the mystical secret of Bereishit Rabbah 73 that Jacob possessed 600,000 flocks of sheep,
כִּי נַפְשׁוֹ הָיְתָה כּוֹלֶלֶת שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא נְפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הַכְּלוּלָה כָּל אֶחָד מִפְּרָטֵי דּוֹרוֹתֵיהֶם,
for his soul encompassed the 600,000 root souls of Israel, each comprising the individual souls of all generations,
וְנִתְפַּשְּׁטוּ אָז חֶלְקֵי אוֹרוֹת נַפְשׁוֹ בַּצֹּאן שֶׁהוּא בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה,
and the rays of his soul-lights were then extended into sheep, which are pure animals,
כִּי אָז עֲדַיִן נִקְרָא יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵגַת עַם הָאָרֶץ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק אֵלּוּ מְצִיאוֹת,
for he was then still called Jacob—the level of simple folk, as noted at the end of chapter Elu Metziot—
וְגַם יִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשְׁלוּ לְצֹאן, וְהָיָה קִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁנִּתְפַּרְנֵס מֵהֶם,
and Israel too are likened to sheep; and they were his property from which he derived livelihood,
כִּי מִמַּה שֶּׁהוּא פַּרְנָסַת הָאָדָם שָׁם גָּנוּז עִיקַּר חַיּוּתוֹ,
for within that which provides a person's sustenance lies the core of his vitality,
שֶׁהֲרֵי הַפַּרְנָסָה הִיא עִיקַּר קִיּוּם חַיּוּתוֹ,
since livelihood is the literal preservation of life;
שֶׁלָּכֵן אָמְרוּ (בָּבָא קַמָּא צב:): בֵּירָא דִּשְׁתֵית מִנֵּיהּ מַיָּא לָא תִּשְׁדֵּי בֵּיהּ קָלָא,
which is why they said (Bava Kamma 92b): 'Into a well from which you drank water, do not cast a stone,'
שֶׁאֵין לְבַזּוֹתוֹ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ:
showing that one must not denigrate the vessel of his sustenance, and this is not the place to lengthen.

paragraphs.text: Tiferet Yosef, Rosh Hashanah 13 describes food as a garment for the divine utterance that gives life. Treating the garment as an independent source conceals that life; returning the received power to God through the omer opens recognition of its inward meaning. The promised blessing is therefore more than continued possession. This explains how livelihood can be returned to its source while the person still receives and uses it.

sections.en: Passing Illumination and the Call to Repentance

p: [צב] לִפְעָמִים נִפְתָּח לָאָדָם מַדְרֵגוֹת, וְאִם הוּא רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נֶעְלָם מִמֶּנּוּ וְהוּא חוֹזֵר לְסוּרוֹ לִהְיוֹת מְשׁוּקָּע בַּתַּאֲווֹת – יֵשׁ לוֹ לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן וְלִדְאוֹג פֶּן הוּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קח:) בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל, שֶׁהִטְעִימָן מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא;

Sometimes spiritual levels are opened unto a person, and if it is only temporary and afterward vanishes from him so that he returns to his waywardness, becoming immersed in desires—he must reflect and worry lest he be, Heaven forbid, in the category of what our Sages said in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 108b) regarding the Generation of the Flood, that He gave them a foretaste of the World to Come;
וַהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק הָיָה קוֹרֵא שֶׁהָעוֹלָם הַבָּא אֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם הֲנָאָה וְחֶמְדָּה מֵעִנְיְנֵי תַּאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, רַק נֶהֱנִין מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה,
and behold, they said in the chapter Hayah Koreh (Berakhot 17a) that the World to Come contains no pleasure or lust of worldly matters, but only delighting in the radiance of the Shechinah,
וְאַחַר פְּתִיחַת אוֹר כָּזֶה הֲרֵי לֹא הָיוּ עוֹד בְּנֵי מַבּוּל, רַק עַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁנִּפְתַּח לָהֶם לְשָׁעָה וְנֶעְלַם;
and after the opening of such an illumination they should no longer have been corrupt, so perforce it opened to them for a brief hour and then vanished;

וְהוּא אֶחָד עִם הַדָּבָר אַחֵר דְּשָׁם דְּקָאָמַר: "זְמַן קָטָן אַחַר זְמַן גָּדוֹל", שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה זְמַן אוּלַי יָשׁוּבוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁפָּתַח לָהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹר כָּזֶה, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן הֶעְדֵּר הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הֶעֱלִימוֹ כְּרֶגַע וְחָזְרוּ לְתַאֲוָתָם.

and this is synonymous with the alternative interpretation there that says: "a short time after a long time," meaning an interval wherein perhaps they would repent through the Blessed Name opening such light to them—which also removes the evil inclination—and afterward He concealed it in an instant and they returned to their lust.
וְאִידַךְ לִישָּׁנָא: שֶׁהֵם יְמֵי אֶבְלוֹ דִּמְתוּשֶׁלַח, וְהַיְינוּ דְּמִיתַת צַדִּיקִים מְכַפֶּרֶת כְּשָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ (יוֹמָא מב.),
And the other Talmudic formulation holds that these were the days of mourning for Methuselah, which means that the death of the righteous atones like the scapegoat (Yoma 42a),
וְקַיְימָא לַן (שְׁבוּעוֹת יג.) גַּם בְּשָׂעִיר צָרִיךְ תְּשׁוּבָה,
and we establish (Shevuot 13a) that even with the scapegoat repentance is required,
רַק הַחִלּוּק בָּזֶה: הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פּוֹתֵחַ הַפֶּתַח לִתְשׁוּבָה וּמֵאִיר אוֹרוֹ בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא קוֹדֶם וְכַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
the only distinction being that the Blessed Name opens the portal to repentance and radiates His light through an awakening from Above (itaruta de-le'ela) first, as noted above;
וּלְכָךְ בְּאוֹתָם יְמֵי אֶבְלוֹ הָיָה כֵּן אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא מִקּוֹדֶם, אַחַר זְמַן גָּדוֹל שֶׁהָיָה קוֹדֶם לִהְיוֹת שׁוּבוּ וְכוּלֵי בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא:

and therefore during those days of his mourning there was such an awakening from Above first, after the long period that preceded it to bring about "return unto Me, etc." through an awakening from below.

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 1:1 distinguishes the intensity of gifted understanding from its permanence. The expanded state granted first on Pesach can be forgotten when received without labor; understanding acquired through effort, although called constricted, becomes fixed in the heart. This explains why the Flood generation’s opening called for a lasting response beyond the experience itself.

paragraphs.text: Poked Akarim 3:1 distinguishes God’s desire for an awakening from below from our request that He first awaken us. In Egypt, Moses’ announcement of divine remembrance introduced faith into hearts submerged in forgetfulness; that faith then became the corresponding human response. Even when initiative comes from above, response from below must follow. An offered opening therefore does not dispense with the person’s own return.

sections.en: Seeking Lost Illumination Through the Depths of Torah

p: [צג] תְּחִלָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאִיר לָאָדָם, וְהָאָדָם אֵין רָגִיל בָּזֶה עֲדַיִן וְקָשֶׁה עָלָיו לְקַבְּלוֹ כְּיָתֵד קָבוּעַ בְּמָקוֹם נֶאֱמָן שֶׁלֹּא יִמּוֹט, וּמְאַבְּדוֹ;

Initially, the Blessed Name illuminates a person, but the person is not yet accustomed to this and finds it difficult to secure it as a nail driven into a firm place so that it will not give way, and he loses it;

וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָאָדָם נוֹהֶה אַחֲרָיו וּמְבַקְּשׁוֹ, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וּפוֹתֵחַ לוֹ, כְּטַעֲנַת "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ וְכוּלֵי", אִם לֹא בְּקֹשִׁי גָּדוֹל, כְּעִנְיַן "כְּשֶׁרָצִיתִי לֹא רָצִיתָ, עַכְשָׁו וְכוּלֵי" (בְּרָכוֹת ז.).

and afterward the person yearns after Him and seeks Him, but the Blessed Name does not readily reopen it to him, parallel to the plea of "Bring us back, etc.," unless with great difficulty, in the manner of: "When I desired, you did not desire; now, etc." (Berakhot 7a).
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, הָיָה בִּכְפִיַּת הַר כְּגִיגִית, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָדָר קִבְּלוּהָ בִּימֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ בְּרָצוֹן;
And this is the concept of the Giving of the Torah: it occurred through overturning the mountain like a vat (Shabbat 88a), and afterward they re-accepted it willingly in the days of Ahasuerus;
אֲבָל לֹא נַעֲשָׂה לָהֶם נֵס בִּימֵי עֶזְרָא כְּבִימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן, שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא כִּדְאִיתָא בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת (ד.), רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר חֵטְא הַקּוֹדֵם;
but a miracle was not performed for them in the days of Ezra as in the days of Joshua son of Nun, because sin caused it (Berakhot 4a), meaning the prior sin;
וְלֹא שָׁרְתָה שְׁכִינָה בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי.
and the Shechinah did not dwell overtly in the Second Temple (Yoma 21b).

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אִיתָא בְּסוֹף סֵפֶר הֵיכָלוֹת שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְּנָה תּוֹרָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל מַעֲלוֹתֶיהָ, עַיֵּין שָׁם י"ז מַעֲלוֹת דְּחָשֵׁיב, לֹא הָיוּ עַד הַבַּיִת שֵׁנִי, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁרְתָה בּוֹ שְׁכִינָה.

And nonetheless, it is stated at the end of Sefer Heikhalot that even though the Torah had been given, all its sublime virtues—see there seventeen virtues enumerated—did not exist until the Second Temple, despite the Shechinah not dwelling overtly therein.
וְעַיֵּין עוֹד שָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁלֹּא הִנִּיחוּ אֶבֶן עַל אֶבֶן בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי עַד שֶׁכָּפוּ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְגִלָּה לָהֶם רָזֵי כָּל דָּבָר, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
And see further there that they did not lay stone upon stone in the Second Temple until they coerced the Holy One, blessed be He, and He revealed to them the mysteries of every matter, see there;
וְ"כָפוּ" הוּא נֶגֶד כְּפִיַּת הַר כְּגִיגִית דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
and "they coerced" stands corresponding to the coercion of the mountain like a vat at the Giving of the Torah

[וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר דִּכְפִיָּה זוֹ הוּא בִּיטּוּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (סט:) שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַאֲשֶׁר הֲרֵעֹתִי", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּפֶרֶק אֵין עוֹמְדִין וּבְהֶחָלִיל].

and one may say that this coercion represents the nullification of the evil inclination of idolatry (Yoma 69b), which was seemingly counter to the initial divine plan, as in "whom I have afflicted" (Micah 4:6).
וְהָעֵצָה בְּהֶעְלֵם הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ אֵיכָה): "הַלְוַאי אוֹתִי עָזָבוּ וְתוֹרָתִי שָׁמָרוּ";
And the remedy in times of spiritual concealment is words of Torah, as in: "Would that they had forsaken Me but kept My Torah" (Midrash Rabbah, introduction to Eichah);
וְכֵן בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי הֵחֵלּוּ חַכְמֵי הַמִּשְׁנָה, וְעַל זֶה אָמַר שֶׁכָּל מַעֲלוֹת הַתּוֹרָה הָיוּ שָׁם יוֹתֵר,
and so in the Second Temple the Sages of the Mishnah began, and concerning this it said that all virtues of Torah were greater there,
וְזֶה בֶּאֱמֶת גָּדוֹל יוֹתֵר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (יב.): "חָכָם עָדִיף מִנָּבִיא":
and this is in truth greater, as written in Bava Batra 12a: "A sage is superior to a prophet."

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 7:5 explains why the authors of Megillat Ta’anit are called lovers of the troubles: adversity became the setting for a greater illumination of Torah. It invokes the same Heikhalot contrast between the Second Temple’s concealed Shechinah and expanded Torah, locating the opening of Oral Torah’s illumination in the Hasmonean period. The gain lies in Torah acquired through renewed effort, not in suffering considered by itself.

paragraphs.text: What remains after Torah study

rich.text: What remains after Torah study

paragraphs.text: The lasting effect of study is distinguished from drawing Torah into the heart at the outset.

rich.text: The lasting effect of study is distinguished from drawing Torah into the heart at the outset.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Simchat Torah 7:1: “The meaning of a blessing after it is what remains permanently in a person’s heart after he engages in Torah. A blessing before it concerns the person’s drawing words of Torah into his heart. But the result of those words of Torah that he has drawn into himself should remain in his heart permanently, like a peg that will never move. That permanence is called the blessing after it.”

rich.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin ·
Sod Yesharim, Simchat Torah 7:1

: “The meaning of a blessing after it is what remains permanently in a person’s heart after he engages in Torah. A blessing before it concerns the person’s drawing words of Torah into his heart. But the result of those words of Torah that he has drawn into himself should remain in his heart permanently, like a peg that will never move. That permanence is called the blessing after it.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: The Ishbitz teaching defines permanence by what remains after the act of learning. That distinction illuminates the siman’s opening difficulty: receiving light does not yet make it a fixed possession. The comparison supplements the existing historical explanation of the Second Temple with a description of the inward result sought by the learner.

paragraphs.text: Rabbeinu Bahya, Bereshit 46:27:2 expressly rejects taking the absence of the Shechinah from the Second Temple as absolute. He distinguishes the First Temple’s constant dwelling from a more intermittent or hovering presence, and distinguishes Glory from Tiferet. paragraphs.text: Derekh Hashem, Part Four, On Torah Study 6 distinguishes Torah’s full influence upon a prepared person from its gradual restorative effect upon one whose conduct is deficient. Even when fuller influence is blocked, the words retain their holiness and repeated engagement can awaken a return. Ramchal excludes study undertaken in mockery or to distort the law: at least serious engagement, comparable to studying another field of wisdom, is required. This is his explanation of the light that brings one back.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 52:7 distinguishes wisdom’s reach from prophecy’s clarity. Inward wisdom can have contact with roots beyond what prophetic vision reveals, yet its mode of attainment does not equal that vision, especially Moses’ prophecy. The passage also denies complete speculative mastery of what lies beyond human inquiry. Thus “a sage is greater” concerns a particular advantage in access through concealment, not an unqualified ranking of later inspiration above Moses.

p: [צד] פְּעָמִים מַשִּׂיג הָאָדָם הֶאָרָה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מַגִּיעַ לְיִרְאָה, וְהוּא פָּנִים שֶׁל זַעַם;
Sometimes a person attains an illumination, and through it reaches awe/fear, which is the aspect of a severe, wrathful countenance (panim shel za'am);
וּכְשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ עַל יָדוֹ לְאַהֲבָה, הוּא פָּנִים שֶׁל רָצוֹן;
and when through it he ascends to love, it is a countenance of favor (panim shel ratzon);
וְעַל יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ, הוּא מְתַקֵּן הַזַּעַם שֶׁבַּפָּנִים וּמִתְהַפֵּךְ לְרָצוֹן, וּבָא אַחַר כָּךְ לְאַהֲבָה.
and through the awe he possesses, he rectifies the wrath of the countenance, transforming it into favor, subsequently arriving at love.
אֲבָל אִם מַדְחֶה אָז מִפָּנָיו עַל יְדֵי הוֹלֵלוּת וּמַחֲשָׁבוֹת אֲחֵרוֹת, אָז אֵין נִתְקַן חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וְאָז הוּא "וְנָתַתִּי פָנַי בָּאִישׁ הַהוּא וְגוֹמֵר", רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן.

But if he banishes it from his face through frivolousness and extraneous thoughts, then it is not rectified, Heaven forbid, and it becomes: "And I will set My face against that man, etc." (Leviticus 20:5), may the Merciful One preserve us.
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם "פָּנִים" הוּא פְּתִיחוּת אוֹרוֹ.
And in every place, "panim" (face/countenance) signifies the opening of His light.
כִּי לְעוֹלָם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא פּוֹתֵחַ שַׁעַר לִתְשׁוּבָה, וּבִשְׁעַת מִיתָתוֹ אָדָם רוֹאֶה שְׁכִינָה, זֶה נִקְרָא פָּנִים שֶׁל זַעַם;
For the Holy One, blessed be He, forever opens a gate for repentance, and at the hour of his death a person beholds the Shechinah, which is termed a severe countenance;
כִּי לְעוֹלָם פָּנִים הוּא הֶאָרָה כַּאֲשֶׁר מַגִּיעַ לָאָדָם, כִּי כְּשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן פָּנָיו בּוֹ וּמִסְתַּכֵּל אֵלָיו – הֲרֵי "בְּאוֹרְךָ נִרְאֶה אוֹר";
for "panim" is always an illumination when it reaches man, since when the Blessed Name turns His face toward him and gazes upon him, behold: "in Your light do we see light" (Psalms 36:10);
וְאָמַר: "פָּנַי יֵלֵכוּ וַהֲנִחֹתִי לָךְ", כִּי יִרְאָה אֵינֶנָּה נִיחָא כַּנּוֹדָע:
and Scripture says: "My presence (Panai) shall go with you, and I will give you rest" (Exodus 33:14), for awe is not restful composure, as is known.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Resisei Layla 36:1: “These three kinds of repentance proceed from below upward. First a person has compassion on himself; this is easy for anyone to awaken on his own. Afterward he begins to feel awe before Hashem and the splendor of His majesty, and through this he sighs over his sins. Afterward he comes to love of Hashem and weeps before Him over what has already passed and is no longer.”

Resisei Layla 36:1

Afterward he comes to love of Hashem and weeps before Him over what has already passed and is no longer.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Resisei Layla describes the movement that the siman compresses into a few lines: self-concern gives way to awe before Hashem, and awe can lead to love. The quoted sequence explains why the first alarming illumination is an opening that requires a response, rather than a condition in which the person is meant to remain.

paragraphs.text: Pardes Rimmonim 23:17:13: “Sometimes there is a face of wrath, as in “The face of Hashem dispersed them.” There is also a face of favor, as in “Shine Your face upon Your servant.” Everything depends upon the source from which it draws: when it draws from Chesed, there is a face of favor and mercy; when it draws from Gevurah, then, Heaven forbid, there is a face of wrath. In this way Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai explained in Raaya Mehemna, Ki Tetze, page 282a: the faces of the sun are Gedulah and Gevurah; the faces of the moon are Netzach and Hod. Those on the right are of mercy, and those on the left are of wrath. Everything depends upon the influence reaching the sun or the moon.”

p: [צה] בִּימֵי הַנְּעוּרִים רְתִיחַת הַתַּאֲוָה מִתְגַּבֶּרֶת, וְאָז מַרְבֶּה חֲטָאִים מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן, וְהֵם חַטֹּאת נְעוּרִים;
In the days of youth, the boil of passion surges, and then one multiplies sins from the side of the evil inclination, may the Merciful One preserve us, which are the sins of youth;
וְזֶה הָיָה בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם: "כִּי יֵצֶר [לֵב הָאָדָם רַע] מִנְּעֻרָיו".
and this occurred in the Generation of the Flood, as written there: "for the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth" (Genesis 8:21).
וְגַם כֵּן מְסַגֵּל טוֹב הַרְבֵּה מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר הַטּוֹב וְחַשְׁקוּת לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְזֶה הָיָה דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְזָכַרְתִּי לָךְ חֶסֶד נְעוּרַיִךְ";

And likewise, one amasses much good from the side of the good inclination and burning passion for words of Torah, and this was the Generation of the Wilderness, as written: "I remember for you the kindness of your youth" (Jeremiah 2:2);

וְהֵם עַצְמָם אוֹתָם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר פִּינְחָס (רטז סוֹף עַמּוּד א, עַיֵּין שָׁם) דְּהָיוּ רְאוּיִים לְקַבֵּל תּוֹרָה בַּמַּבּוּל אִלּוּ זָכוּ, וְנִשְׁמַת מֹשֶׁה הָיְתָה שָׁם.
and they were identical souls, as written in the Zohar (Pinchas 216a end, see there) that they were fit to receive the Torah during the Flood had they merited, and the soul of Moses was there.
וְדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ, אָז יִהְיֶה פַּעַם שְׁלִישִׁית אוֹתוֹ דּוֹר, בְּסוֹד מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: "תִּתְחַדֵּשׁ כַּנֶּשֶׁר נְעוּרָיְכִי";
And the generation of the Messiah will be that same generation for a third time, in the mystery of: "your youth is renewed like the eagle" (Psalms 103:5);
וְאָז יִהְיֶה הַתִּיקּוּן הַגָּמוּר, שֶׁבָּאוֹת בְּעִרְבּוּבְיָא חַטֹּאת נְעוּרִים וְחֶסֶד נְעוּרִים, וְהַטּוֹב יִתְגַּבֵּר עַל הָרַע וִיהַפְּכוֹ לְטוֹב.
and then complete rectification will take place, when the sins of youth and the kindness of youth arrive intermingled, and the good will overpower the evil and transform it into good.

for the rainbow is the sign of the Covenant counter to the retributions of the sins of youth,

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Noach 5 reads cloud as awe and concealment, and rainbow as confident assurance within them. Luminous colors signify a promise made clear enough to be recognized. Its account of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai distinguishes constant from occasional perception of that assurance and identifies Shema as Israel’s strengthening declaration. This explains the present revealed covenantal sign, beyond an inference drawn from outward calm.

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah 2:16:1: ““And it shall be, when I bring a cloud”—a cloud of water, which was the principal element in the generation of the Flood; although there was a flood of fire and water, the principal element stated in Scripture is a flood of water. The Lord promised that there would no longer be a flood, such an overwhelming intensification of desire. This is the meaning of the rainbow appearing: restraint against desire, in the sense of “His bow remained firm.” This is why no rainbow appeared in Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s generation: he was on the level of a chasid and did not need restraint, and he was then the foundation of the world, as is stated repeatedly in the Zohar. “Like the appearance of the rainbow in the cloud” is “the appearance of the glory of the Lord.” Glory refers only to Torah, which restrains a person. This is the Lord’s glory: when a person bends his nature and struggles for the sake of the Lord’s will. This is the appearance of the rainbow in the cloud.”

One who guards the Covenant and never experienced a nocturnal emission in his days is termed "fair of form" (yefeh to'ar) in Scripture, as in the case of Joseph: "fair of form" (Genesis 39:6);
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "שֶׁקֶר הַחֵן וְהֶבֶל הַיֹּפִי",
and regarding this it is said: "Grace is deceitful and beauty is vain" (Proverbs 31:30),
כִּי מָצִינוּ גַּם כֵּן בְּאֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁהָיוּ נְקִיִּים מִזֶּה, כְּמוֹ עוֹג שֶׁפָּלַט מִדּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל, וּבְלֹא תֵּבָה כְּלָל;
for we find even among gentile nations those who were clean of this, such as Og who escaped from the Generation of the Flood, and that without an ark at all;
וַדַּאי לֹא הָיָה נִיסָא לְשִׁקְרָא, רַק שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בֶּן מַבּוּל, דְּהַיְינוּ מַשְׁחִית זֶרַע, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק כָּל הַיָּד (נִדָּה יג:),
surely a miracle would not occur for falsehood, but rather he was not subject to the Flood decree because he did not spill seed, as written in Niddah 13b,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר אַגְּמָרָא דְּנִדָּה (סא.) שֶׁהָיָה בֶּן אֲחִיָּה בַּר שַׁמְחֲזַאי, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ
and as I wrote elsewhere on the Gemara in Niddah 61a that he was the son of Achiyah bar Shamchazai, and this is not the place to elaborate
[וּלְכָךְ נִיתְּנָה אַרְצוֹ לַחֲצִי מַטֵּה מְנַשֶּׁה מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף, שׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית].
and therefore his land was given to the half-tribe of Manasseh from the seed of Joseph, guardians of the Covenant.

וּלְכָךְ נִתְיָירֵא מֹשֶׁה מִמֶּנּוּ, כִּי מֹשֶׁה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֻלִּין קלט:): "בְּשַׁגַּם" – בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא מֹשֶׁה, וְנֶאֱמַר עָלָיו: "כִּי מִן הַמַּיִם מְשִׁיתִהוּ", שֶׁהָיָה אָז בַּמַּיִם.

And therefore Moses feared him, for Moses was likewise present in the Generation of the Flood, as our Sages expounded (Chullin 139b): beshagam shares the numerical value of Moshe, and it is said of him: "because I drew him out of the water" (Exodus 2:10), meaning he was then in the water.
וְגַם כָּל עִיקַּר עִנְיַן מֹשֶׁה הָיָה לְתַקֵּן דָּבָר זֶה הַנִּקְרָא שְׁטוּת, שֶׁלְּכָךְ הָיָה פָּרוּשׁ מִן הָאִשָּׁה וְקָבוּר מוּל בֵּית פְּעוֹר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר;
And furthermore, Moses's entire mission was to rectify this matter termed folly, which is why he separated from his wife and was buried opposite Beit Peor, as I wrote elsewhere;
וְרָאָה זֶה נָקִי כָּל כָּךְ, נִתְיָירֵא מִמֶּנּוּ, עַד שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: "אַל תִּירָא",
and seeing Og so pristine in this trait, Moses feared him, until the Holy One, blessed be He, told him: "Fear him not" (Numbers 21:34),

כִּי קַיְימָא לַן בִּנְדָרִים (לא:): הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הָעֲרֵלִים אָסוּר בְּמוּלֵי אֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמוּתָּר בְּעַרְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁאֵין הָעָרְלָה נִקְרָא אֶלָּא עַל שְׁמָם, אֲפִילּוּ הֵם מוּלִים וְשׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית.

for we establish in Nedarim 31b: one who vows against the uncircumcised is forbidden to circumcised gentiles and permitted to uncircumcised Jews, for "uncircumcision" is designated solely upon their name, even if they are physically circumcised and guard the covenant.
וְ"עַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים" וְשׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית, אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁקִּלְקְלוּ:
And "your people are all righteous" and guardians of the Covenant, even when they have stumbled.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 44:1 connects Og’s survival with freedom from the Flood generation’s particular corruption and, through that generation’s unrealized Torah potential, with a relation to Torah. Its wider discussion treats Moses and Balaam as names of recurring spiritual roots when reconciling accounts from different generations. This is Rav Tzadok’s extended interpretive parallel; Og’s ancestry itself is supplied by the separate Niddah quotation.

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, Purim 13:3 develops the same vow-law proof: Israel’s covenantal holiness is rooted before the physical act of circumcision. It nevertheless insists that the commanded act is required to disclose that holiness to the person. Rooted belonging and practical obligation are both retained. This qualifies the present distinction between outward appearance and the covenant’s root without making that root a reason to disregard the mitzvah.

sections.en: Rectifying the Covenant Through Torah Study

p: [צז] תִּיקּוּן לְמוֹצִיא זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה הוּא עֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (קִדּוּשִׁין ל:): בָּרָאתִי יֵצֶר הָרָע, בָּרָאתִי תוֹרָה תַּבְלִין;
The rectification for emitting seed in vain is engagement in Torah study, as written (Kiddushin 30b): "I created the evil inclination, I created the Torah as its antidote";
וְאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (נב.): הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא קְרָאוֹ "רָע", וְהַיְינוּ בַּעֲוֹן דְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל דְּהַיְינוּ מוֹצִיא זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה
and they stated in Sukkah 52a: the Holy One, blessed be He, called it "evil," which refers to the sin of the Generation of the Flood, namely emitting seed in vain
[וְאָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (יג.) דְּלֹא נִגְזַר עַל דָּגִים שֶׁבַּיָּם, הַיְינוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל פָּסוּק "וּרְדוּ בִּדְגַת הַיָּם"],
and they said in Kiddushin 13a that the decree did not fall upon the fish of the sea, which represent Torah scholars, as I wrote elsewhere on "and have dominion over the fish of the sea",
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר בְּרֵאשִׁית (נז עַמּוּד א) וּבְרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כָּל הַיָּד דְּנִקְרָא רַע, זֶה הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַאֲשֶׁר הֲרֵעֹתִי";
and as written in Zohar I:57a and at the beginning of chapter Kol HaYad that it is called "evil," this evil inclination that the Holy One created, as written: "and whom I have afflicted";
וּלְכָךְ יִמָּצֵא זֶה גַּם בַּחֲלוֹם, שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה נִיכָּר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִפְּעֻלַּת אָדָם.
and therefore this occurs even in dreams, showing clearly that this is not from the voluntary action of man.

וְתַבְלִין הוּא לְמַתֵּק הַמַּאֲכָל, הַיְינוּ לַהֲפוֹךְ הָרַע לְטוֹב מְאֹד כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט): זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִמְתָּק.
And an antidote/spice (tavlin) sweetens food, meaning transforming the evil into "very good" (Bereishit Rabbah 9), which is the evil inclination sweetened through words of Torah.
וּבַזֹּהַר בְּרֵאשִׁית וְנֹחַ: דְּלֵית מְסָאָבָא כְּמוֹהוּ.
And in the Zohar (Bereishit and Noach): there is no defilement like it.
וְהִנֵּה אָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק ב דִּבְרָכוֹת (טז.) דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מַעֲלִין מִטֻּמְאָה לְטָהֳרָה.
And behold, they said in the second chapter of Berakhot (16a) that words of Torah elevate from impurity to purity.

וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר נֹחַ (סב עַמּוּד א) דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה, הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יח.): בְּזֶבַח אֵין מִתְכַּפֵּר, אֲבָל מִתְכַּפֵּר בַּתּוֹרָה; הָכָא נַמֵּי כֵּן;

And what is written in Zohar Noach (62a) that repentance does not avail, is along the lines of Rosh Hashanah 18a: through sacrifice it is not atoned, but it is atoned through Torah; here too it is so;
וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שִׁילְהֵי חֲגִיגָה: תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אֵין אוֹר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֵט בָּהֶם.
and as our Sages expounded at the end of Chagigah (27a): the fire of Gehenna has no dominion over Torah scholars.
גֵּיהִנָּם גַּם כֵּן נִקְרָא "רָע", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת סא.) עַל פָּסוּק "לֹא יִנָּקֶה רָּע",
Gehenna is likewise called "evil," as written in Berakhot 61a on "he shall not be unpunished of evil" (Proverbs 11:21),
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּעֵירוּבִין (יט.) שֶׁהַכֹּל יוֹרֵד לָהּ עַל עִסְקֵי חִנָּם, הַיְינוּ שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית;
which aligns with Eruvin 19a that all descend there on account of vain pursuits, which refers to the preservation of the Covenant;
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ גַּם כֵּן: "בָּרָאתָ גֵּיהִנָּם", שֶׁגַּם כֵּן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרָאוֹ כְּמוֹ יֵצֶר הָרָע
and this is why they said: "You created Gehenna" (Bava Batra 16a), which the Blessed Name created just as He created the evil inclination

[וְאָמְרוּ שָׁם גַּם כֵּן: "בָּרָאתָ צַדִּיקִים", צַדִּיק בְּכָל מָקוֹם שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית, גַּם הוּא מִתְּחִלַּת בְּרִיאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בָּאוֹת שֶׁלִּפְנֵי זֶה, כִּי יֶשְׁנוֹ גַּם בִּרְשָׁעִים וּבְאֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים].

and they said there: "You created the righteous," where "tzadik" everywhere denotes the guardian of the Covenant, which also exists from the inception of Creation, as I wrote in the preceding section, since it exists even among the wicked and the gentiles.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי".
And regarding this it is stated: "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalms 23:4).
"רָע" הוּא דַּרְגָּא הַנִּזְכָּר, וְ"אַתָּה" פֵּירוּשׁ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁבָּרָאתָ:
"Evil" refers to this aforementioned level, and "You" means by virtue of the fact that You created it.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 21:6 directly rejects despair over this blemish. It distinguishes complete cosmic repair of the serpent’s damage, reserved for the messianic future, from real purification available now. Its present path includes guarding the heart and eyes, turning from improper thoughts, and continually occupying the heart with Torah; it invokes Rambam’s warning about a heart empty of wisdom. Torah is described as the completion of repentance and a means of repair even in this world. The future limit therefore does not close the current path of return, and the metaphor of seasoning means redirecting the heart’s powers through Torah.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 15:15 examines the Zohar’s differing formulations rather than treating the severe sentence in isolation. It reports variant wording allowing “great” or “mighty” repentance, notes its absence from older copies and addition from another manuscript, and cites Vayakhel’s express qualification concerning complete repentance. Rav Tzadok then invokes the principle that no sinner is excluded from sincere inward return. This fuller discussion is essential to reading the present passage as opening a path of repair through Torah. The textual history here is Rav Tzadok’s report, not a new collation of manuscripts.

sections.en: The Living Power Within Every Torah Verse

p: [צח] כָּל פָּסוּק שֶׁל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה יֵשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ וְחַיּוּת שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ.
Every verse of Torah contains the latent power and vitality of that specific matter of which it speaks.
תֵּדַע בִּתְפִלִּין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהָיָה לְאוֹת וְגוֹמֵר", וְלֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ אֵיזֶה פָּרָשָׁה מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת לְאוֹת,
You may know this from tefillin: Scripture states: "And it shall be for a sign, etc." (Exodus 13:9), yet it did not explicitly specify which passage of the Torah must serve as this sign,
וְהַהֲלָכָה לִכְתּוֹב אוֹתָם הַפָּרָשִׁיּוֹת שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהֶם זֶה
and the halakhic ruling is to write those exact passages in which this is stated—
מִסְּתָמָא אוֹתָהּ פָּרָשָׁה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהּ פָּסוּק "וְהָיָה לְאוֹת וְגוֹמֵר", יֵשׁ בָּהּ אוֹתָהּ עִנְיַן כֹּחַ וּסְגֻלָּה שֶׁתִּהְיֶה לְאוֹת.
presumably because that very passage contains the inherent power and spiritual virtue to serve as that sign.
וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה יָדוּעַ הַרְבֵּה לְיוֹדְעֵי הַשֵּׁמוֹת וּבְקַבָּלָה מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת, כִּי מִכָּל פָּסוּק יוֹצֵא שֵׁם הַמּוֹעִיל לְאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן הַנִּזְכָּר בַּפָּסוּק.
And similar to this is widely known to masters of holy Names and practical Kabbalah, for from every verse emerges a Name effective for the specific theme mentioned in the verse.
וְכֵן פָּסוּק "שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל", בּוֹ כֹּחַ הַקְּבִיעוּת הַשְּׁמִיעָה בַּלֵּב, וּלְכָךְ צָרִיךְ שֶׁיֹּאמַר גַּם תֵּיבַת "שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל".
And likewise the verse "Shema Yisrael": within it lies the power to embed hearing into the heart, which is why one must articulate the words "Shema Yisrael."
וְזֶה סוֹד גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל פָּסוּק "שִׂפְתֵי צַדִּיק יֵדְעוּן רָצוֹן" (מִשְׁלֵי י, לב),
And this is also the secret of what I heard on the verse "The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable" (Proverbs 10:32):
כִּי הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל כָּתַב סְגֻלָּה לְמִי שֶׁיִּצְרוֹ מְסִיתוֹ לְאֵיזֶה עֲבֵירָה – לְדַבֵּר בְּפִיו כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים פָּסוּק הַלָּאו שֶׁל הָעֲבֵירָה, עַל יְדֵי זֶה יִשְׁתַּנֶּה הָרָצוֹן;

for the holy Ari wrote an efficacious remedy for one whose inclination incites him to a transgression: to utter verbally multiple times the biblical negative prohibition of that sin, whereby the desire will be transformed;
וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן מִצְוָה וְדָבָר טוֹב:
and likewise regarding a positive commandment and a good matter.

sections.en: Forgetting Sin as a Sign of Complete Repentance

p: [צט] סִימָן לִתְשׁוּבָה גְּמוּרָה – כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֵר כְּלָל הַחֵטְא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (נח:) שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר לְבַעַל תְּשׁוּבָה: "זְכוֹר וְכוּלֵי";
A sign of complete repentance is when one no longer remembers the sin at all, as written in Bava Metzia 58b that one must not say to a penitent: "Remember your former deeds, etc.";
וְכֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין מַזְכִּיר לְבַעַל תְּשׁוּבָה הַגָּמוּר, וּמִמֵּילָא אֵינוֹ זוֹכֵר.
and so the Blessed Name does not bring it to mind for the complete penitent, and consequently he does not remember it.
כִּי כָּל כֹּחוֹת הָאָדָם מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "מִי שָׂם פֶּה וְגוֹמֵר", וְכֵן כֹּחוֹת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה וְהַזְּכִירָה, וְאִם אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹפֵעַ לוֹ וּמַזְכִּיר לוֹ – אֵינוֹ זוֹכֵר.

For all human faculties derive from the Blessed Name—"Who makes man's mouth, etc." (Exodus 4:11)—and likewise the faculties of thought and memory; if the Blessed Name does not bestow it and remind him, he cannot remember.
וּבְתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק א: שֶׁעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לוֹמַר: אֵינִי זוֹכֵר עֲווֹנוֹתָיו וְאֵין עוֹלִין עַל לִבִּי;
And in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 1: the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to say: "I do not remember his iniquities and they do not arise in My heart";
וּכְבָר אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב): הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "צוּר לְבָבִי וְגוֹמֵר",
and our Sages already taught (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2): the Holy One is the heart of Israel, as stated: "God is the rock of my heart, etc." (Psalms 73:26),
מִמֵּילָא גַּם עַל לִבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם אֵינוֹ עוֹלֶה, וְזֶהוּ מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
so naturally it does not arise in the human heart either, which is a foretaste of the World to Come.
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ אָדָם לְעֹמֶק הַתְּשׁוּבָה כָּזֶה, שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הַכַּפָּרָה, אֵינוֹ בְּנִיחָא;
And as long as a person has not reached such profound depth of repentance, which is the ultimate perfection of atonement, he is not at restful ease;

: “Conversely, if a person remembers his sin and fulfills ‘My sin is always before me’ (Psalms 51:5), then Hashem makes Himself forgetful and does not look at that sin at all.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Beit Yaakov explicitly places the two directions together: the person keeps the sin before him, while Hashem puts it aside. This comparison helps read the siman’s final sentence alongside its description of completed forgiveness. Rav Tzadok describes the peace of complete repair, while the person’s chosen task remains honest remembrance and return; ordinary loss of memory is not itself the spiritual attainment described here.

p: [ק] תְּשׁוּבָה הַיְינוּ שֶׁמֵּשִׁיב אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר אֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁהַכֹּל פּוֹעֵל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכֹחוֹ,
Teshuvah means that one returns (meshiv) that matter unto the Blessed Name, recognizing that everything is the operation and power of the Blessed Name,
אֲפִילּוּ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה טֶרֶם נוֹצְרָה בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט).
even the thought before it is formed within the heart of man (Bereishit Rabbah 9).
נִמְצָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נָתַן לוֹ כֹּחַ אָז גַּם בְּהָעֲבֵירָה,
Thus it turns out that the Blessed Name granted him the strength then even in the sin,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה, אַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה הַגְּמוּרָה, הוּא זוֹכֶה שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשִׂין זְכִיּוֹת, כִּי גַּם זֶה הָיָה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּךְ,
and through this, after complete repentance, he merits that willful transgressions become merits, for this too was the will of the Blessed Name,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת (פט:): "אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים וְכוּלֵי",
as written in Shabbat 89b on "if your sins be as scarlet, etc." (Isaiah 1:18),
וּכְעִנְיַן שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא וַיֵּשֶׁב ד) עַל פָּסוּק "נוֹרָא עֲלִילָה עַל בְּנֵי אָדָם",
and in the spirit of Midrash Tanchuma (Vayeishev 4) on "awesome in deed toward the children of men" (Psalms 66:5),
וּכְדִבְרֵי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "לְמַעַן תִּצְדַּק בְּדָבְרֶךָ", רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר לְכָךְ נִטְּלָה מִמֶּנּוּ הַסַּיַּעְתָּא,
and in King David's words: "that You may be justified when You speak" (Psalms 51:6), meaning that Heavenly assistance was withdrawn from him for this very purpose,
וְאִם כֵּן הוּא מַמָּשׁ כִּזְכִיּוֹת מֵאַחַר שֶׁגַּם זֶה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and if so, it is literally like merits, since this too was the will of the Blessed Name.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַחֲסִידֶיךָ יְרַנֵּנוּ", וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי יְשַׁעְיָה רֶמֶז רצו): אֵלּוּ רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵי,
And this is "and let Your pious ones sing for joy" (Psalms 132:9), expounded (Yalkut Shimoni, Isaiah 296) as referring to the wicked of Israel;
וְכֵן עַל פָּסוּק "אִסְפוּ לִי חֲסִידָי וְגוֹמֵר" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם).
and likewise on "Gather My pious ones unto Me, etc." (Psalms 50:5).
פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי "חָסִיד" הוּא הַנּוֹטֶה מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין לְהִתְחַסֵּד, וְכֵן רָשָׁע נוֹטֶה מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין לְהַרְשִׁיעַ;
For a "chasid" (pious one) deviates from strict justice to act with piety, and a wicked one deviates from strict justice to do wrong;
וּכְשֶׁיִּפְתַּח הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֶעָתִיד אַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה הַגְּמוּרָה, וְיַכִּירוּ הַכֹּל כֹּחַ מַלְכוּתוֹ,
and when the Blessed Name reveals in the future after complete repentance, and all recognize the power of His sovereignty,
נִמְצָא הַזְּדוֹנוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ נְטִיָּה מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין – הָיוּ חֲסִידוּת, כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ נוֹטִים מֵאֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
it will turn out that the willful sins which deviated from strict justice were acts of chasidut, since they did not deviate from the absolute will of the Blessed Name.
וְדָיֵיק "חֲסִידָי" וַ"חֲסִידֶיךָ", וְלֹא "חֲסִידִים", רַק שֶׁאֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵם קְרוּיִים חֲסִידִים, וְלֹא לְעֵינֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם.

And Scripture is precise in saying "My pious ones" and "Your pious ones," not simply "pious ones," because in the eyes of the Blessed Name they are called pious, though not in the eyes of human beings.

paragraphs.text: Akeidat Yitzchak 28:1:4: “Therefore God gives the gentle warning, “Go and see the works of God”: direct your hearts toward the sacred, and do not err in this. His attributing these events to human actions is a matter of a pretext, for those divine purposes will in any case come to pass and will not turn aside, without thereby compelling people in the details of their individual actions. Similarly, the woman was not compelled to mix her husband’s cup with lukewarm or cold water because he intended to divorce her. Her mixing it lukewarm was only a pretext on his part: had that not occurred, another reason—or many others—would not have been lacking, and all those actions remained possible for her, as we explained.”

paragraphs.text: Context: Rabbi Chaim Vital distinguishes overcoming the inclination from the settled acquisition of good character. His account concerns acquired character becoming natural; Rav Tzadok develops his own distinction here in terms of the roots of different dispositions, while retaining the teaching that righteousness and wickedness are not decreed at birth.

sections.en: Human Action and the Perfection of Divine Thought

p: [קא] בְּמַעֲשֶׂה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא מְעַט מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אֵין אָדָם צַדִּיק בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה טּוֹב וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כ);

In practical deed, it is impossible for a person not to deviate slightly from strict justice, as written: "For there is not a righteous man upon earth, that does good, and sins not" (Ecclesiastes 7:20);
וְצַדִּיק הַיְינוּ הַנִּזְהָר שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין
and a "tzadik" is one who takes meticulous care not to deviate from strict justice
[וְכַנּוֹדָע שֶׁבְּעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה רִבּוּי הַקְּלִיפּוֹת בְּכָל הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],
and as known, in the World of Action shells and husks abound across all levels, which is not to be elaborated here,
אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, רַק בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה וּרְצוֹן הַלֵּב שֶׁגּוֹמֵר בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁיִּתְנַהֵג כָּךְ וְלֹא יֶחֱטָא, שָׁם יוּכַל לִרְצוֹת וְלַחְשׁוֹק כָּךְ.

which is impossible in physical deed, but achievable only in thought and the desire of the heart, where he resolves to conduct himself thus without sinning, being capable there of purely longing for it.

כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת, כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְמַחֲשָׁבָה וְרָצוֹן שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה בָּעוֹלָמוֹת הָהֵם, שֶׁגַּם מַעֲשֵׂה הַחֵטְא הַהוּא הוּא מִן הַסֵּדֶר וְאֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה כְּלָל מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין, וְהַכֹּל בַּדִּין.

For in truth, when one ascends to the realm of thought and supernal will, even that sinful deed is seen as part of the cosmic order, never having deviated from strict justice, all being governed by law.

וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: בַּתְּחִלָּה עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה לִבְרוֹא בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁבְּמַעֲשֶׂה הוּא יְצִיאָה מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין, אֲבָל בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה הוּא בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין וְאֵין כָּאן יְצִיאָה.

And this is: "Initially it arose in Thought to create the world with the attribute of strict Judgment, etc.," for in practical deed there is a departure from strict justice, but in Thought it remains within strict Judgment without departure.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "צַדִּיק ה' בְּכָל דְּרָכָיו" (תְּהִלִּים קמה, יז) – פֵּירוּשׁ, "דְּרָכָיו" הֵם דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ קִדּוּשִׁין, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "יוֹדִיעַ דְּרָכָיו לְמֹשֶׁה", וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן מִתְנַהֵג עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה;

And as written: "Hashem is righteous in all His ways" (Psalms 145:17)—meaning His "ways" are words of Torah (Kiddushin 2b), and as written: "He made known His ways unto Moses" (Psalms 103:7), and the Blessed Name conducts Himself according to the Torah;
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְמַעֲשֶׂה הוּא "חָסִיד", דְּהַיְינוּ לִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין כִּדְאִיתָא בְּשַׁבָּת (קכ. וּבְרַשִּׁ"י),
but when it reaches practical deed He is "pious" (chasid), that is, beyond the letter of the law (Shabbat 120a and Rashi),
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְחַנֹּתִי אֶת אֲשֶׁר אָחֹן" וְגוֹמֵר.
matching: "and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, etc." (Exodus 33:19).
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם זֶה פָּסוּק בַּתּוֹרָה וְאֶחָד מִדְּרָכָיו שֶׁנּוֹדַע,
And nonetheless, this too is a scriptural verse in the Torah and one of His known ways,
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ "עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה' הֵפֵרוּ תּוֹרָתֶךָ" הוּא גַּם כֵּן הֲלָכָה קְבוּעָה;
parallel to: "It is time to work for Hashem; they have made void Your Torah" (Psalms 119:126), which is itself an established halakhah;
וְזֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי: כְּשֶׁחוֹזֵר לְמַחֲשָׁבָה, גַּם זֶה מִן הַסֵּדֶר וְהַשּׁוּרָה הָרְאוּיָה:
and this is as I wrote: when returning to Thought, even this belongs to the proper order and appropriate measure.

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, I, Lech Lecha 7 explains Abraham’s refusal to benefit from Sodom as a clarification of his rescue of Lot. The good destined to emerge from Lot through Ruth and Naamah was mixed with the evil of Ammon and Moab. Abraham first removed personal benefit, allowing the purpose of his act to be clarified. This discipline accompanies the same verse, Psalms 119:126, cited here: a claim to higher purpose does not itself establish purity of motive.

p: [קב] מִי שֶׁמִּתְנַהֵג אֲפִילּוּ בְּכָל דִּבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת וְצָרְכֵי גּוּפָנִיִּים בִּקְדוּשָׁה, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשָׂיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וּמַכְנִיס בָּהֶם עַבְדוּת וּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בֵּיצָה טז.) בְּהִלֵּל וְשַׁמַּאי – זֶהוּ נִקְרָא "חָסִיד",

One who conducts himself with holiness even in all permitted mundane matters and bodily necessities—meaning all his deeds are for the sake of Heaven, infusing into them servitude and the will of the Blessed Name in the manner of Hillel and Shammai (Beitzah 16a)—is termed a "chasid,"
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁלָּאו דַּוְקָא מְדַקְדֵּק עַל פִּי שׁוּרַת הַדִּין.
meaning he does not restrict himself strictly to the baseline letter of the law.
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ" – בִּשְׁנֵי יְצָרֶיךָ וְכוּלֵי,
And this is termed "with all your heart"—with both your inclinations (Berakhot 54a),
שֶׁצַּדִּיק הוּא הַכּוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ, אֲבָל זֶה מַכְנִיס קְדוּשָׁה גַּם בְּכָל חֶמְדּוֹת הַיֵּצֶר;
for a "tzadik" subdues his inclination, whereas this person introduces holiness even into the desires of the inclination;
וְאָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה נוֹתֵן קְדוּשָׁה בְּכָל מַה שֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה, וְזוֹכֶה לְהוֹצִיא קְדוּשָׁה הַרְבֵּה מִן הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע דַּיְיקָא;
and then the Blessed Name, measure for measure, instills holiness into all that he does, and he merits to extract vast holiness specifically out of the evil inclination;
וְאָז נִקְרָא "טוֹב מְאֹד", שֶׁהוּא יוֹתֵר מִטּוֹב סְתָם;
and then he is termed "very good," which is superior to ordinary good;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין אֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים וְכוּלֵי.
and regarding this it was said: "In the place where penitents stand, the wholly righteous cannot stand, etc." (Berakhot 34b).
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ תַּקָּלוֹת וּמִכְשׁוֹלִים, וְהוּא צָרִיךְ תְּשׁוּבָה וְכַפָּרָה עַל זֶה דְּנִקְרָא חֵטְא, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל.
And the Blessed Name orchestrates mishaps and obstacles for him, requiring repentance and atonement for what is deemed a sin, and through this he extracts the precious from the vile.
אֲבָל צַדִּיק שֶׁאֵין יוֹצֵא מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין, גַּם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְנַהֵג עִמּוֹ כֵּן, וְ"לֹא יְאֻנֶּה לַצַּדִּיק" דַּיְיקָא "כָּל אָוֶן".
But with a "tzadik" who never departs from strict law, the Blessed Name conducts Himself likewise, and "no iniquity shall befall the righteous" (Proverbs 12:21) specifically.
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קכז:) בְּמַעֲשֶׂה דְּרָאָה קֶרִי "אוֹתוֹ חָסִיד"
And therefore they stated in Shabbat 127b in the episode of the nocturnal emission: "that chasid"
[וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִּׁ"י, וּבְבִרְכַּת הַזֶּבַח בִּתְמוּרָה דִּיקְדֵּק לָמָּה פֵּירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י שָׁם וְלֹא בִּבְרָכוֹת;
and see Rashi there, and Birkat HaZevach on Temurah examined why Rashi explained it there and not in Berakhot;
אַךְ כַּוָּונַת רַשִּׁ"י לְהוֹדִיעַ מִי הָיָה, דְּאָדָם גָּדוֹל הוּא, כְּדֵי לְהָסִיר מָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה מִמִּי שֶׁאֵירַע לוֹ רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן],
but Rashi's intent was to identify who he was, being a great sage, to remove depression from anyone to whom this occurred, may the Merciful One preserve us,
וְלֹא בְּחִנָּם נִקְרָא שָׁם בְּשֵׁם "אוֹתוֹ חָסִיד"
and not in vain was he specifically named "that chasid"
[וְכֵן בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנִּקְרָא כֵּן יֵשׁ טַעַם בַּדָּבָר].
and likewise in every place where someone is so designated, there is an inner rationale.
וְגַם בְּעֵירוּבִין (יח:): אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן חָסִיד גָּדוֹל הָיָה וְכוּלֵי, בְּשִׁכְבַת זֶרַע דַּחֲזָא לְאוֹנְסוֹ.
And also in Eruvin 18b: "Adam the First was a great chasid, etc.," regarding emission experienced involuntarily.
דְּדַיְיקָא לְחָסִיד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין זֶה לְהוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל
For specifically to a "chasid" does the Blessed Name orchestrate this to extract the precious from the vile
[יָקָר אוֹתִיּוֹת קְרִי],
yakar (precious) shares the letters of keri (emission),
כִּידוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל כִּי הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּטִפֵּי קֶרִי הֵם יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלוֹת מֵהַיּוֹצְאִים מִזִּוּוּג,
as is known from the holy Ari that the souls from involuntary emissions are greater than those emerging from marital union,
וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ יוֹתֵר כָּעֵת:
and this is not the place to elaborate further at present.

p: [קד] בְּכָל אָדָם יֵשׁ פְּסֹלֶת בַּתּוֹלָדָה מֵעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ – עִרְבּוּבְיָא דְּטוֹב וָרָע,
Within every human being there exists congenital dross stemming from the counsel of the primordial Serpent—an entanglement of good and evil;
וּמִזֶּה הוּא מִקְרֵה לַיְלָה,
and from this arises nocturnal emission,
שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמַר: "לֹא תְאֻנֶּה אֵלֶיךָ רָעָה" (תְּהִלִּים צא, י),
concerning which Scripture promises: "There shall no evil befall you" (Psalms 91:10),
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קג.): חֲלוֹמוֹת רָעִים וְהִרְהוּרִים רָעִים,
which our Sages of blessed memory expounded in Sanhedrin 103a as referring to distressing dreams and unchaste thoughts,
הַיְינוּ כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כ:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְנִשְׁמַרְתָּ מִכֹּל דָּבָר רָע" – שֶׁלֹּא וְכוּלֵי,

which aligns with the teaching of our Sages (Avodah Zarah 20b) on the verse "And you shall keep yourself from every evil thing" (Deuteronomy 23:10)—that one should not indulge in thoughts by day, etc.,
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "חֲלוֹמוֹת רָעִים", דְּמוֹצִיא זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה נִקְרָא "רַע" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּנִדָּה (יג:).
and this is designated as "evil dreams," since emitting seed in vain is termed "evil," as written in Niddah 13b.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר: "וְנֶגַע לֹא יִקְרַב בְּאָהֳלֶךָ",
And following this Scripture states: "neither shall any plague come near your tent,"
וְדָרְשׁוּ שָׁם: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בֵּן אוֹ תַלְמִיד וְכוּלֵי,
which they expounded there: that you shall have neither a son nor a disciple who publicly spoils his dish like Jesus the Nazarene;
שֶׁמִּי שֶׁלֹּא יְאֻנֶּה וְכוּלֵי, צָרִיךְ רַחֲמִים בָּזֶה שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא הַפְּסֹלֶת בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה.
for one who is spared from physical emission requires divine mercy so that the internal dross does not emerge instead through wayward offspring or disciples.
וְאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (יז:): "וְלֹא כֶאֱלִישָׁע שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ וְכוּלֵי",
And they stated in Berakhot 17b: "and not like Elisha, from whom emerged Gehazi, etc.";
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי אֱלִישָׁע לֹא רָאָה קֶרִי מִיָּמָיו כִּדְאִיתָא שָׁם (י:),
that is, because Elisha never experienced a seminal emission in his life, as brought there (Berakhot 10b),
וְעַל כֵּן בֵּרְכוֹ אָבִיו, שֶׁבָּזֶה אֵין מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה;
and therefore his father blessed him, for in this respect his spiritual "bed" was not complete;
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה, וְלֹא רָאָה קֶרִי, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק "רֵאשִׁית אוֹנִי" (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה).

whereas our father Jacob, peace be upon him, had a bed that was entirely whole, and yet he never experienced a seminal emission, as our Sages expounded on the verse "the first-fruits of my strength" (Bereishit Rabbah 98:4).
אֲבָל נִקְיוֹנוֹ הָיָה עַל יְדֵי גָּלוּת וְיִסּוּרִים,
But Jacob's purging of dross was accomplished through exile and tribulations;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "כִּי מַלְאָכָיו יְצַוֶּה לָּךְ וְגוֹמֵר",
and concerning this Scripture says: "For He will give His angels charge over you, etc." (Psalms 91:11),
וְהַסִּיּוּם: "כִּי יָדַע שְׁמִי" (שָׁם, יד)
and the psalm concludes: "because he has known My Name" (ibid. 91:14)—
הַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁנִּקְרָא שֵׁם ה',
which refers to words of Torah, which are termed the Name of Hashem;
בְּפֶרֶק מִי שֶׁמֵּתוּ (בְּרָכוֹת כא.) יָלֵיף בִּרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה לְפָנֶיהָ מִקְּרָא דְּ"שֵׁם ה'", עַיֵּין שָׁם,
as in the chapter Mi SheMeito (Berakhot 21a), where the blessing over Torah study is derived from the verse "When I proclaim the Name of Hashem" (Deuteronomy 32:3), see there,
כִּי כֻּלָּהּ שְׁמוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
for the entire Torah consists of mystical Names of the Holy One, blessed be He;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הָעֵצָה לְגָלוּת וְיִסּוּרִין: "הֱוֵי גוֹלֶה לִמְקוֹם תּוֹרָה" (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד),
and this is the spiritual counsel for exile and suffering: "Exile yourself to a place of Torah" (Avot 4:14);
וְהַתּוֹרָה נִקְרָא "מוּסַר הַשְׂכֵּל",
and the Torah is called "the discipline of wisdom,"
שֶׁהַמִּצְווֹת גַּם כֵּן נִקְרָא "עוֹל" בִּבְרָכוֹת (יז.) דּוּגְמַת יִסּוּרִין, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
for the commandments are likewise termed a "yoke" in Berakhot 17a, functioning like refining tribulations, see there.
וְכֵן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זָכָה וְנִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ "יִשְׂרָאֵל",
And thus our father Jacob, peace be upon him, merited and his name was called "Israel,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק אֵלּוּ מְצִיאוֹת, דְּשֵׁם יַעֲקֹב שׁוֹרֶשׁ לְעַם הָאָרֶץ וְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם:
as written at the end of the chapter Elu Metziot (Bava Metzia 33b), that the name "Jacob" is the root for simple folk, whereas the name "Israel" is the root for a Torah scholar.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Vayeshev 1:1: ““Yaakov dwelt in the land where his father had sojourned … These are the generations of Yaakov: Yosef.” In these verses he is mentioned twice by the name Yaakov, and afterward twice by the name Israel: “Israel loved Yosef,” and “Israel said to Yosef: Are not your brothers shepherding in Shechem?” The matter is that the name Yaakov is applied to ordinary people, while the name Israel indicates Torah scholars, as they said: “Declare to My people their transgression”—these are Torah scholars; “and to the house of Yaakov their sins”—these are the unlearned.”

p: עִנְיַן הַמִּקְרֶה רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן פְּעָמִים הוּא לְהַצָּלָה מִמָּוֶת כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּעֵת חָלְיוֹ,
The phenomenon of nocturnal emission, may the Merciful One preserve us, is at times for rescue from death when it occurs during the time of one's illness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בִּבְרָכוֹת (נז, ב) מִקְּרָא דְּ"יִרְאֶה זֶרַע יַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים".
as brought in Berakhot (57b) from the verse: 'He shall see seed, he shall prolong days' (Isaiah 53:10).
וְכֵן בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
And likewise on the Day of Atonement,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא שִׁילְהֵי יוֹמָא,
as brought at the end of tractate Yoma (88a),
שֶׁהוּא זְמַן גְּמַר דִּין דְּחַיִּים וָמָוֶת לַבֵּינוֹנִים,
for it is the time of the final seal of judgment concerning life and death for the intermediate individuals (beinonim),
וְהוּא כְּעִנְיַן מִקְצָת נֶפֶשׁ כְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ.
and it is akin to the concept that 'a portion of a life is accounted as the whole life.'

paragraphs.text: Yoma 88a:11: “It was taught in Rabbi Yishmael’s school: A person who experiences a seminal emission on Yom Kippur should be concerned throughout the entire year. If he lives out the year, he is assured a place in the World to Come. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: You can see this from the fact that the whole world is hungry, while he is satisfied. When Rav Dimi arrived, he said: Such a person will live long and have many children and grandchildren.”

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 16b:12: “Rabbi Kruspedai said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Three books are opened on Rosh Hashanah: one of the completely wicked, one of the completely righteous, and one of those in between. The completely righteous are written and sealed immediately for life; the completely wicked are written and sealed immediately for death. Those in between remain suspended from Rosh Hashanah until Yom Kippur: if they merit, they are written for life; if they do not merit, they are written for death.”

paragraphs.text: Kohelet Rabbah 7:27:1: ““One by one, to find an account”: Rabbi Yitzchak said: Ordinarily, a person stumbles in a transgression for which he is liable to death at the hands of Heaven. Through what is atonement made for him? His ox dies, his hen is lost, his flask breaks, or he stumbles and injures his little finger, from which a drop of blood comes out. A part of the life is like the whole life, as it is said, “One by one, to find an account”: one offsets another, and the account is brought to its full reckoning. How exact is the reckoning? Rabbi Pinchas said: Down to one.”

p: וּפְעָמִים הוּא לִמְחִילַת עֲווֹנוֹת, כִּדְאִיתָא (יוֹמָא פח, א) בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁהוּא זְמַנּוֹ.
And at times it serves for the forgiveness of sins, as brought in Yoma (88a) regarding Yom Kippur, which is its appointed season.
וּפְעָמִים לְהַבְטִיחוֹ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, כִּדְאִיתָא שָׁם גַּם כֵּן,
And at times it is to assure him of the World to Come, as also brought there,
דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים הוּא עָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי כַּנּוֹדָע.
for the Day of Atonement is of the aspect of the World to Come, as is known.
וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים עִקָּרוֹ לְכַפָּרַת פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
And the essence of Yom Kippur is for the atonement of the blemish of the covenant,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בְּיוֹמָא (סז:) לְכַפֵּר עַל מַעֲשֵׂה עוּזָּא וַעֲזָאֵל,
as brought in Yoma (67b) that the scapegoat comes to atone for the deeds of Uzza and Azael,
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם): "מֻבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא",
and this is why they stated (there): 'he is assured that he is a son of the World to Come,'
וּבֶן עוֹלָם הַבָּא נִקְרָא צַדִּיק בַּמִּשְׁנָה דְּרֵישׁ חֵלֶק,
and a possessor of the World to Come is termed righteous (tzaddik) in the Mishnah at the beginning of Chelek (Sanhedrin 90a),
וְהַיְינוּ שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית.
which signifies one who guards the covenant.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 15:50 links Yom Kippur with understanding in the heart and the World to Come. It reads the designation of all Israel as righteous as a revelation of the covenantal holiness at their deepest root, including those who have damaged the covenant. This explains the siman’s association of the day, future life, and covenant. It does not displace the repeated qualification that these meanings apply at times, or the instruction to remain concerned throughout the year.

לְפִי שֶׁהַמַּעֲשֶׂה לִכְאוֹרָה בַּהֲפֶךְ,
because the event superficially appears to be the complete opposite,

And at times it is a sign for success in words of Torah,

sections.en: Stumbling in Torah and Reaching Deeper Understanding

p: [קו] "אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְשַׁל" (גִּטִּין מג.),
"A person does not master words of Torah unless he has stumbled in them" (Gittin 43a),
וְהַמַּכְשֵׁלָה דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מְבִיאָה לִידֵי קֶרִי רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן,
and an intellectual stumbling in words of Torah brings about nocturnal emission, may the Merciful One preserve us,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל פָּסוּק "כִּי מִן הַמַּיִם מְשִׁיתִהוּ", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת ע"ו מֵעִנְיַן דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל,
as I wrote elsewhere on the verse "because I drew him out of the water" (Exodus 2:10), and as I wrote above in Section 76 regarding the Generation of the Flood,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת יד.): "וְשָׂבֵעַ יָלִין בַּל יִפָּקֶד רָע" – הַמַּשְׂבִּיעַ עַצְמוֹ מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי, וּמִינַּהּ לְהֵיפֶךְ.
and as written in Berakhot 14a: "'and he that has it shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil'—whoever sates himself with words of Torah, etc.," and infer the opposite from it.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ עַל יְדֵי זֶה "חֵפֶץ ה' בְּיָדוֹ יִצְלָח", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל, וְעוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
And afterward through this, "the purpose of Hashem shall prosper in his hand" (Isaiah 53:10), as I wrote above, and he masters words of Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר מֵעִנְיַן יוֹסֵף שֵׁידָא,
as I wrote elsewhere regarding the episode of the demon Yosef (Pesachim 110a),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי דַּעֲווֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוּ זְכִיּוֹת,
and as I wrote that willful sins are transformed into merits,
וּמִמַּיִם הַזֵּידוֹנִים נֶהְפַּךְ לְמֵי הַדַּעַת, וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ הָעֲשׁוּקָה נִכְנְסָה לִקְדוּשָׁה וְנַעֲשָׂה מִמֶּנּוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה;
and from the raging waters it is transformed into waters of divine knowledge, and the oppressed soul enters into holiness and becomes words of Torah;
כִּידוּעַ שֶׁנַּפְשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הֵם עַצְמָן דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְהִתְחַדְּשׁוּת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא הוֹלָדַת נְפָשׁוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת.
for it is known that the souls of Israel are themselves words of Torah, and the innovation of words of Torah is the birth of holy souls.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קכז:): שָׁנָה לְתַלְמִידָיו – הוּא מַה שֶּׁנִּתְחַדֵּשׁ לוֹ דַּיְיקָא אַחַר שֶׁטָּבַל מִקּוֹדֶם, שֶׁהוּא הַתְּשׁוּבָה וְהַתִּיקּוּן.

And therefore they stated in Shabbat 127b: "he taught his disciples"—this was what was specifically revealed to him anew after he had first immersed in a ritual bath, which is repentance and rectification.
וְנִרְאֶה שֶׁזֶּה עַצְמוֹ הָיָה מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב אַחַר כָּךְ מֵעִנְיַן לָדוּן לְכַף זְכוּת, אֲפִילּוּ בְּאֹפֶן זֶה שֶׁהַמַּעֲשֶׂה לִכְאוֹרָה מוֹרֶה בְּבֵירוּר לְחוֹב, וְלֹא יָדַע זֶה מִקּוֹדֶם,

And it appears that this itself was what is related there afterward regarding judging favorably, even in a case where the outward action seemingly points clearly to guilt, and he did not know this beforehand,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם בְּתַלְמִיד שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּדוּק וְדִבְּרָה תּוֹרָה לָשׁוֹן נְקִיָּה, הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה חָשׁוּד אֶצְלוֹ עַל זְנוּת;
as stated there regarding "a student who was not vetted," where the Torah employed clean language, meaning that he was suspected by him of licentiousness;
וּמִדְּאָמַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּדוּק מַשְׁמָע דְּבֶאֱמֶת כָּשֵׁר הָיָה, רַק שֶׁהוּא לֹא דָּנוֹ לְכַף זְכוּת, וְהָיָה הַמִּשְׁפָּט עֲבוּר זֶה רְאִיַּת הַקֶּרִי.
and from the phrasing "not vetted," it implies that in truth he was worthy, only that the master had not judged him favorably, and the resulting judgment for this was the nocturnal emission.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵירְעוֹ מִפְּנֵי טֹרַח הַדֶּרֶךְ שֶׁהָיָה דְּבַר מִצְוָה, וַהֲרֵי "שׁוֹמֵר מִצְוָה לֹא יֵדַע דָּבָר רָע", וְזֶה נִקְרָא "רָע" כַּנּוֹדָע.

Nonetheless, it occurred to him on account of the toil of the journey which was for a mitzvah; and behold, "he who keeps a commandment shall know no evil thing" (Ecclesiastes 8:5), and this is termed "evil," as is known.
רַק שֶׁכָּל דָּבָר נִידּוֹן עַל שֵׁם סוֹפוֹ, וְאָז נִקְרָא "טוֹב מְאֹד";
Rather, every matter is judged according to its ultimate outcome, and then it is termed "very good";
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהָיָה כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּעֲמוֹד עַל יְדֵי זֶה עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, זָכָה לָזֶה רַק עַל יְדֵי טֹרַח אוֹתוֹ דֶּרֶךְ לְפִדְיוֹן שְׁבוּיִים,
and since it occurred so that through it he would master words of Torah, he merited this solely through the toil of that journey for the redemption of captives,
דְּאוֹתָהּ רִיבָה הִתְנַהֲגָה בְּדַרְכֵי גוֹיִם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן סוֹף פֶּרֶק ח,
for that maiden conducted herself in the ways of gentiles, as written in Avot DeRabbi Natan (end of chapter 8),
וְהוּא מִדַּת חֲסִידוּת לְבַקֵּשׁ זְכוּת גַּם לָרְשָׁעִים,
and it is a measure of pious devotion (chasidut) to seek merits even for the wicked,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קי.): שְׁבָקֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לַחֲסִידוּתֵיהּ, מַאי חֲסִידוּתֵיהּ וְכוּלֵי עַיֵּין שָׁם.
as written in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 110a): "Rabbi Akiva abandoned his chasidut; what was his chasidut? etc.", see there.
וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא בְּאוֹתוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה "חָסִיד אֶחָד"
And therefore he was called in that narrative "a certain chasid"
[וְיְעוּיַּן מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת ק"ב],
and examine what I wrote above in Section 102,
שֶׁזֶּה לִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין וְאֵין רוֹאֶה לַעֵינַיִם, כִּי גַּם בְּכָל רַע גָּנוּז טוֹב.
for this goes beyond the strict letter of the law and does not look merely to outward appearances, since within every evil goodness is concealed.
וּלְכָךְ זָכָה אָז לַעֲמוֹד עַל דָּבָר זֶה שֶׁל תּוֹרָה לָדוּן לְכַף זְכוּת, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן גְּנִיזַת הַטּוֹב בְּמַעֲשֶׂה הָרָע לָעַיִן,
And therefore he merited then to master this principle of Torah—to judge favorably—which likewise represents the concealment of good within a deed that appears evil to the eye;
וְהִזְמִין לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹתוֹ מִכְשׁוֹל
and the Blessed Name orchestrated for him that very stumbling
[שֶׁהוּא לֵידַת נֶפֶשׁ בְּלֹא רְצוֹנוֹ וְדַעְתּוֹ, וְכֵן עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כְּמִי שֶׁעוֹמֵד מְזוּמָן עַל אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר בְּלִי דַעְתּוֹ וְהִשְׁתַּדְלוּתוֹ;
which is the birth of a soul without his conscious will and knowledge; and likewise "mastering words of Torah" means standing prepared upon that matter without his prior knowledge or effort;
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁחִדֵּשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, הוֹצִיא הַנֶּפֶשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל]
and through innovating the words of Torah afterward, he elevated that soul, as I wrote above
לַעֲמוֹד מִתּוֹכוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה:
in order to master words of Torah through it.

paragraphs.text: Rashi on Gittin 43a:15:2: ““And this stumbling block is under your hand”: He began his exposition in this way. Scripture says, “And this stumbling block is under your hand,” concerning the people of Jerusalem, among whom Torah had ceased. They would ask their fellows, “You have a garment; be our chief, and this stumbling block shall be under your hand.” That is: matters concealed like a garment belong to you, for you are knowledgeable in them; tell us, and become our chief. “And this stumbling block”—words of Torah whose truth a person does not grasp until he stumbles over them by issuing an erroneous ruling, is put to shame, and then pays attention and understands—are under your hand. I too stumbled in my ruling, and I retract it.”

: ““And this stumbling block is under your hand”: He began his exposition in this way. Scripture says, “And this stumbling block is under your hand,” concerning the people of Jerusalem, among whom Torah had ceased. They would ask their fellows, “You have a garment; be our chief, and this stumbling block shall be under your hand.” That is: matters concealed like a garment belong to you, for you are knowledgeable in them; tell us, and become our chief. “And this stumbling block”—words of Torah whose truth a person does not grasp until he stumbles over them by issuing an erroneous ruling, is put to shame, and then pays attention and understands—are under your hand.
