for through wasted seed comes the retribution of the Deluge, as written in Niddah 13b,
וּמְקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן דּוּגְמַת מַבּוּל כְּרֶגַע וְתֵיכֶף יוֹצֵא,
and by immersing he accepts upon himself a semblance of the Flood for an instant and immediately emerges;
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר: "לֹא אֹסִף וְגוֹמֵר, כִּי יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו",
for the Blessed Name declared: "I will not again curse the ground... for the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth" (Genesis 8:21),
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר עוֹד טֶרֶם יֵדַע הַנַּעַר וְכוּלֵי, וּבְלֹא דַעְתּוֹ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִתְגַּבֵּר, וְכֵן בִּשְׁנָתוֹ
meaning before the youth knows, etc., and without his conscious awareness the evil inclination surges, and so too in his sleep
זֶה נִקְרָא בְּלֹא דַעְתּוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "גַּם בְּלֹא דַעַת נֶפֶשׁ לֹא טוֹב",
which is called 'without his knowledge,' as written: 'Also, that the soul be without knowledge is not good' (Proverbs 19:2),
וּמָצִינוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קמט:): אֵין "לֹא טוֹב" אֶלָּא רָע, וְזֶה נִקְרָא רָע.
and we find in Shabbat 149b: 'not good' means evil, and this is termed evil.
וְאָמְרוּ בְּסוֹטָה (ג.): אֵין אָדָם עוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְנַס בּוֹ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת,
And they said in Sotah 3a: A person does not commit a transgression unless a spirit of folly enters him,
וְהַיְינוּ אֵל אַחֵר שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קג עַמּוּד א): אִסְתָּרַס וְלָא עָבִיד פֵּירִין,
which is the 'other god' of whom the Zohar states (Part II, 103a): it is castrated and produces no fruit,
וּפֵירֵשׁ הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ דַּעַת כַּנּוֹדָע.
and the holy Ari explained that it lacks Da'at (conscious divine awareness), as is known.
וּלְכָךְ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא סוֹד הַדַּעַת תִּיקּוּנוֹ,
And therefore Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who embodies the mystical secret of Da'at, is its rectification,
[וְרָצָה לְתַקֵּן זֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת צ"ו, וּ"מִן הַמַּיִם מְשִׁיתִהוּ" הוּא בְּסוֹד הַמִּקְוֶוה].
and he sought to rectify this as I wrote above in Section 96, and 'because I drew him out of the water' corresponds to the mystery of the mikveh.
וְהִנֵּה הוּקְשׁוּ אֹהָלִים לִנְחָלִים בִּבְרָכוֹת (טז.), לְכָךְ גַּם דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא מֵי הַדַּעַת מוֹעִיל כְּמוֹ כֵן.
And behold, tents of Torah were compared to flowing streams in Berakhot 16a; therefore words of Torah, which are the waters of Da'at, avail likewise.
וְצָרִיךְ לָזֶה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בִּדְחִילוּ,
And for this, one requires words of Torah studied with reverence (b'dchilu),
שֶׁזֶּה הוּא הֵיפֶךְ, דְּאֵימָה וְיִרְאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרָכוֹת (כב עַמּוּד א),
which is the exact opposite of complacency—characterized by dread and awe as written in Berakhot 22a,
וְהוּא דּוּגְמַת שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קח:) בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל: בְּרוֹתְחִין קִלְקְלוּ, בְּרוֹתְחִין נִידּוֹנוּ.
and this mirrors what they said in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 108a) regarding the Generation of the Flood: through boiling passion they corrupted, and in boiling waters they were judged.
וּלְכָךְ עֶזְרָא תִּקֵּן טְבִילָה לְבַעֲלֵי קְרָיִין כְּדֵי לַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה בְּאֵימָה כִּדְאִיתָא שָׁם,
And therefore Ezra instituted ritual immersion for those who experience seminal emission so that they engage in Torah with awe, as brought there,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיְּתַקֵּן עַצְמוֹ קוֹדֶם, וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (עב:): תּוֹרָה בְּטָהֳרָה,
meaning that one must purify himself first, along the lines of Yoma 72b: Torah studied in purity,
וְאָמְרִינַן עֲלַהּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (כט:): הָא לַן וְהָא לְהוּ.
and we said concerning this in Kiddushin 29b: this applies to us (in Babylonia) and that applies to them (in the Land of Israel).
וּכְשֶׁהִתְחִילָה תּוֹרָה בְּבָבֶל, בִּטְּלוּהוּ לִטְבִילוּתָא,
And when Torah study flourished in Babylonia, they nullified Ezra's decree of immersion,
דְּזֶה מִקְרֵי רֵחַיִם בְּצַוָּארוֹ שָׁם בְּקִדּוּשִׁין, וּבִטּוּל תּוֹרָה שָׁם בִּבְרָכוֹת,
for this was termed a millstone around the neck in Kiddushin, and neglect of Torah in Berakhot;
וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד, שֶׁזֶּה עִנְיַן תַּלְמוּד בַּבְלִי,
and all is one, for this is the unique nature of the Babylonian Talmud,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּקְרָא "בַּמַּחֲשַׁכִּים" בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כד.),
even though it is described as "in dark places" in Sanhedrin 24a,
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמוֹעֵד קָטָן (כה.) שֶׁבָּבֶל גָּרְמָה לוֹ לְעִנְיַן הֶאָרַת גִּלּוּי שְׁכִינָה,
which aligns with Moed Katan 25a that Babylonia was deficient regarding the open revelation of the Shechinah;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ שָׁם בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (שָׁם): מַאי "בָּבֶל"? בְּלוּלָה וְכוּלֵי,
nonetheless they stated in Sanhedrin: what is the meaning of Babel? Mingled with Scripture, Mishnah, and Talmud,
כִּי עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא רִבּוּי תּוֹרָה, וְהַכֹּל לְטוֹב, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ עוֹד:
for through this deep analytical dialectic Torah study increased, and everything is for the good, and this is not the place to elaborate further.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 15:42 explains immersion through the awe required for Torah study. It explicitly rejects attributing waking frivolity to supremely holy people when discussing an involuntary event during sleep. Its concern is the remaining bodily pleasure and impurity, and the resulting need to become ready for attachment to Torah. It presents immersion or nine kav of water within that account of purification, preserving the distinction between an involuntary state and a chosen offense.

This preserves the condition governing the promise of light after failure.

p: [קח] הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר נֹחַ (סב עַמּוּד א) דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה,
Emitting seed in vain, the Zohar states in Parashat Noach (62a), is a sin for which ordinary repentance does not avail;
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי טִפֵּי זֶרַע נִמְשָׁךְ מֵהַמּוֹחַ, וּפָגַם בְּטִפֵּי מוֹחוֹ.
and that is because drops of seminal fluid are drawn from the brain, and he blemished the spiritual drops of his intellect.
וְהַתְּשׁוּבָה הוּא בַּלֵּב כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּלְבָבוֹ יָבִין וְשָׁב",
And standard repentance resides in the heart, as it is written: "and his heart understand, and he return and be healed" (Isaiah 6:10),
וּלְכָךְ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְתַקֵּן עַל יָדָהּ הַחָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִמֶּנָּה.
and therefore it is impossible through the heart to rectify Wisdom (Chokhmah), which transcends it.
רַק צָרִיךְ תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא נוֹבְלוֹת חָכְמָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה יז),
Rather, one requires Torah study, which is the unripe fruit of Supernal Wisdom, as written in Bereishit Rabbah (17:5),
וְהִיא גַּם כֵּן בַּמּוֹחַ
and Torah likewise resides in the brain
[וְנִקְרָא "יֵשׁ" כַּנּוֹדָע, בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא "קֶרִי", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בָּזֶה].
and wisdom is called Yesh (substance), which shares the numerical value of keri (310), and as I wrote elsewhere on this.
לֵב נִשְׁבָּר – לִהְיוֹת מַמָּשׁ כְּאַיִן, שֶׁהוּא בַּכֶּתֶר כַּנּוֹדָע שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה עוֹד,
A broken heart means becoming literal nothingness (Ayin), which reaches into Keter (the Crown) that transcends even Chokhmah,
וְזֶה מוֹעִיל,
and this is effective;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "פְּנֵי ה' בְּעֹשֵׂי רָע", הוּא עָוֹן זֶה שֶׁנִּקְרָא כֵּן, "לְהַכְרִית מֵאֶרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר",
and as written: "The face of Hashem is against those who do evil"—which is this sin so designated—"to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth" (Psalms 34:17),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ", שֶׁיְּרֻשַּׁת הָאָרֶץ הוּא רַק לַצַּדִּיק דְּהַיְינוּ שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית.

as written: "Your people also shall be all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever" (Isaiah 60:21), showing that inheritance of the land belongs solely to the righteous, meaning the guardian of the Covenant.
וְאָמַר: "צָעֲקוּ וְגוֹמֵר" – תְּפִלָּה הוּא עֵצָה נֶגֶד לְהַכְרִית מֵאֶרֶץ
And Scripture states: "They cried, and Hashem heard" (Psalms 34:18)—prayer is the remedy against being cut off from the earth

[שֶׁהַתְּפִלָּה שָׁרְשָׁהּ בַּמַּלְכוּת שֶׁהִיא אֶרֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, וּפְגָמוֹ הִגִּיעַ לָהּ כְּעִנְיַן "ה' צִלְּךָ", מַמָּשׁ דּוּגְמַת הַצֵּל עוֹשֶׂה מַה שֶּׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה אִם לְטוֹב אִם לְהֵיפֶךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם];

for prayer is rooted in Malchut, the Supernal Land, and his spiritual blemish reached there, in the spirit of "Hashem is your shadow," where like a shadow Above reflects whatever man does below, whether for good or for the opposite, Heaven forbid;
אֲבָל לִהְיוֹת קָרוֹב לַה', הָעֵצָה – שְׁבִירוּת לֵב: "וְאֶת דַּכְּאֵי רוּחַ וְגוֹמֵר".
but to be genuinely close to Hashem, the remedy is brokenness of heart: "and saves such as are of a contrite spirit" (Psalms 34:19).
וְכֵן נֶאֱמַר בַּמִּזְמוֹר כַּאֲשֶׁר בָּא אֶל בַּת שֶׁבַע, שֶׁנִּתְקַן עַל קִלְקוּל הַבְּרִית
And likewise it is stated in the psalm composed when Nathan came to him after he had gone in to Bathsheba, which was composed to rectify the violation of the Covenant
[שֶׁהוּא בַּתּוֹלָדָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי יֵצֶר וְגוֹמֵר מִנְּעֻרָיו", לְכָךְ בִּקֵּשׁ "לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא", וּבְרִיאָה הוּא חֲדָשָׁה עַתָּה תִצְמַח יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן]:

which is congenital from birth, as written: "for the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth," which is why David pleaded: "Create in me a clean heart," where creation is an entirely new emergence ex nihilo:
"כִּי לֹא תַחְפֹּץ זֶבַח וְגוֹמֵר"
"For You desire not sacrifice, etc." (Psalms 51:18)
[הַיְינוּ תְּשׁוּבָה, כְּעִנְיַן "כָּל הַזּוֹבֵחַ יִצְרוֹ וּמִתְוַדֶּה וְכוּלֵי" (סַנְהֶדְרִין מג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב)],
which refers to standard repentance, as in: "Whoever slaughters his inclination and confesses, etc." (Sanhedrin 43b),
"זִבְחֵי אֱלֹהִים – רוּחַ נִשְׁבָּרָה, לֵב נִשְׁבָּר וְנִדְכֶּה אֱלֹהִים לֹא תִבְזֶה":
"The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise" (Psalms 51:19).

Concerning him it is written, “Your iniquity is stained before Me,” and it is written, “For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil will not dwell with You”—except through abundant repentance. And it is written, “Er, Yehudah’s firstborn, was evil in the eyes of Hashem, and Hashem put him to death.” This has already been explained.”

p: [קט] וּבְעִקְּבֵי מָשִׁיחַ מִתְגַּבֵּר מְאֹד עָוֹן זֶה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה כִּי כִּמְעַט אֵין אָדָם בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁנִּיצּוֹל.
And in the footsteps of the Messiah, this sin intensifies exceedingly, and as written in Sefer Reishit Chokhmah that virtually no person in his generation was spared from it.

כִּי כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁיָּצְאוּ עַד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נוֹטְעוּ בְּזַרְעוֹ אַחַר כָּךְ, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְבָמוֹת סג.) עַל פָּסוּק "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כָּל גּוֹיֵי הָאָרֶץ" – לְשׁוֹן הַבְרָכָה

For all souls that emerged prior to our father Abraham, peace be upon him, were subsequently replanted into his seed, as our Sages expounded (Yevamot 63a) on the verse "and in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed (venivrekhu)"—an expression of grafting (havrakhah)
[וְזֶה נֶאֱמַר לְטַעַם עַל הַהוֹדָעָה מִסְּדוֹם שֶׁגַּם הֵם נִתְבָּרְכוּ בוֹ וְהָיוּ צְרִיכִים הֲכָנָה יְתֵירָה לְשֶׁיְּתוּקְנוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ יוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם.

and this was stated as the rationale for informing Abraham regarding the destruction of Sodom, for they too were grafted through him and required intense preparation to be rectified, as the Ari wrote that they were the generation of the Exodus.
וְנוֹדַע דְּרָשַׁת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כג) עַל פָּסוּק "גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי".
And the rabbinic exposition (Vayikra Rabbah 23) on the verse "a nation from the midst of a nation" is well known.
וְגַם יָדוּעַ דְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה בַּעֲבוּר אַבְרָהָם, לְכָךְ הוּא הִתְפַּלֵּל עֲלֵיהֶם, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְקְנוּ בֶּעָתִיד].
And it is also known that the Egyptian exile occurred on account of Abraham; therefore he prayed for them, and through this they were rectified in the future.
וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא "אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם" – אַב מַמָּשׁ לְכָל הַגּוֹיִם.
And therefore he was called "the father of a multitude of nations"—a literal father to all nations.

וְהַיְינוּ כִּי ב' אֲלָפִים הוּא סִבּוּב שָׁלֵם בַּבְּרִיאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: בְּבֵי"ת נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה דְּתוֹרָה קָדְמָה ב' אֲלָפִים שָׁנָה לָעוֹלָם.

That is, because two thousand years constitute a complete cosmic cycle in Creation, as written: with the letter Beit (equaling two) the world was created, and as I wrote elsewhere on the rabbinic dictum that the Torah preceded the world by two thousand years.
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צז.): ב' אֲלָפִים תֹּהוּ וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁבְּכָל חֵלֶק הָיוּ כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הָרְאוּיוֹת לָצֵאת:
And therefore our Sages said (Sanhedrin 97a): two thousand years of Desolation, two thousand of Torah, etc., wherein in each epoch all the souls destined to emerge came forth:
דְּתֹהוּ – עַד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם;
Desolation—extending until our father Abraham, peace be upon him;
וּדְתוֹרָה – בְּזַרְעוֹ עַד מָשִׁיחַ, שֶׁיִּכְלוּ כָּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת שֶׁבַּגּוּף כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּיבָמוֹת (סב.);
and Torah—among his seed until the Messiah, until all souls in the Heavenly reservoir (Guf) are exhausted, as written in Yevamot 62a;
וְיִהְיֶה פַּעַם שְׁלִישִׁית בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ הַמַּתְחִיל בִּב' אֲלָפִים הַשְּׁלִישִׁיִּים.
and it will recur a third time in ultimate perfection in the generation of the Messiah, which commences in the third epoch of two thousand years.
וְהִנֵּה ג' דּוֹרוֹת שֶׁקָּדְמוּ לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מָנוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And behold, the three corrupt generations that preceded our father Abraham were enumerated in chapter Chelek as having no share in the World to Come,
וְהַיְינוּ לְתוֹקֶף הָרַע שֶׁנִּתְגַּבֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם, וְזֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה כַּאֲשֶׁר יְתוּקְנוּ הֵם גַּם כֵּן בְּתוֹקֶף גָּדוֹל.
and that was due to the overwhelming power of evil that overpowered them; and corresponding to this, when they are rectified, it unfolds likewise with tremendous power.
וּסְדוֹם הֵם דּוֹר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
And Sodom corresponds to the generation of the Exodus from Egypt, as noted above;
וְדוֹר הַפְלָגָה הֵם דּוֹר עוֹלֵי גוֹלָה גַּם כֵּן מֵאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר, וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ד.) שֶׁהָיוּ גַּם כֵּן רְאוּיִים לְנֵס כְּבִיאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה;

and the Generation of the Dispersion corresponds to the generation that returned from the Babylonian Exile, who also came from the land of Shinar, concerning whom our Sages stated (Berakhot 4a) that they were worthy of an overt miracle like the first entry into the Land;
וְדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל הֵם דּוֹר מָשִׁיחַ, בַּעֲלֵי בִּיאָה שְׁלִישִׁית, וּלְכָךְ מִתְגַּבֵּר עָוֹן דִּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל בְּיוֹתֵר
and the Generation of the Flood corresponds to the generation of the Messiah, the bearers of the third arrival, which is why the sin of the Generation of the Flood surges with supreme intensity
[וְג' אֵלּוּ הֵם גַּם כֵּן נֶגֶד כְּלַל ג' סִדְרֵי ב' אֲלָפִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ]:
and these three generations also correspond to the overarching three epochs of two thousand years mentioned above, and this is not the place to lengthen.

paragraphs.text: Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Ner HaMitzvot 2:28: “The world and the body are material and destined to cease, including heaven and earth, as our Sages said in Bereshit Rabbah, section 42. But “year”—that is, the order of times—has no grasp in physical matter. Therefore Bereshit Rabbah says that an order of times existed before this. Likewise, as it says in Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 8, Torah preceded the world by two thousand years; this is an order of times. As soon as spiritual beings were created, time was created, for it is spiritual like them. It separately distinguishes standing in judgment: the first opinion says the Flood generation does not stand but Sodom does; Rabbi Nechemyah excludes both. sections.en: The Divine Source and Rectification of All Offspring

p: [קי] כָּל תּוֹלְדוֹת הָאָדָם הוּא מִן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
All offspring of a person derive from the Blessed Name
[שֶׁעַל כֵּן אָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ תַּעֲנִית (ב.) דְּמַפְתֵּחַ שֶׁל עֲקָרוּת רַק בְּיָדוֹ],
which is why they stated at the beginning of Ta'anit 2a that the key of barrenness is in His hand alone,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "מִמֶּנִּי פֶּרְיְךָ נִמְצָא" (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, ט);
as it is written: "From Me is your fruit found" (Hosea 14:9);
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אֵל אַחֵר "אִסְתָּרַס וְלָא עָבִיד פֵּירִין" כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר, וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (מ.): עֲבֵירָה אֵין לָהּ פֵּירוֹת.
in contrast to the 'other god' who is castrated and produces no fruit, as brought in the Zohar, and likewise in Kiddushin 40a: a sin bears no lasting fruit.

וְהִנֵּה גַּם רוּחִין וְשֵׁדִין וְלִילִין שֶׁנּוֹלָדִים מֵהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה, הֵם נִקְרָאִים תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, נד עַמּוּד ב) עַל פָּסוּק "נִגְעֵי בְנֵי אָדָם".

And behold, even the spirits, demons, and night-spirits born of wasted seed are called his offspring, as written in the Zohar (Part I, 54b) on the verse "the stripes of the children of men" (II Samuel 7:14).
וְיָדוּעַ: "מִפִּי עֶלְיוֹן לֹא תֵצֵא הָרָעוֹת" (אֵיכָה ג, לח), וְנֶאֱמַר: "לֹא יְגֻרְךָ רָע" (תְּהִלִּים ה, ה), וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּמַה שֶּׁנִּקְרָא "רָע" יִהְיֶה מִמֶּנּוּ.

And it is known: "Out of the mouth of the Most High proceeds not evil" (Lamentations 3:38), and it is stated: "evil shall not dwell with You" (Psalms 5:5), so it is impossible that that which is termed evil should originate directly from Him.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
And concerning this it is said: "I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalms 23:4),
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת דְּהַיְינוּ גֵּיהִנָּם,
and even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, which is Gehenna,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּעֵירוּבִין (יח:) וּבְסוֹטָה (ד:) דְּעַל פְּגַם הַבְּרִית לֹא יִנָּקֶה מִדִּינָהּ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם.
and as written in Eruvin 18b and Sotah 4b that for a blemish of the Covenant one is not absolved from the judgment of Gehenna.
עַל זֶה אָמַר: "כִּי בָאֵשׁ ה' נִשְׁפָּט" (יְשַׁעְיָה סו, טז),
Concerning this Scripture states: "For by fire will Hashem enter into judgment" (Isaiah 66:16),
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב, מִזְמוֹר א; בַּדְּפוּס: מז, א): תֵּרֵד כָּל אוּמָּה וֵאלֹהֶיהָ וְכוּלֵי, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר הַנּוֹתֵן לָהּ כֹּחַ לַעֲשׂוֹת חַיִל.
and our Sages expounded (Shocher Tov, Psalm 1; cited in the base edition as 47a): every nation and its deity shall descend, etc., meaning that which granted it the strength to wield power.
וְעָלֵינוּ נֶאֱמַר: "כִּי הוּא הַנֹּתֵן לְךָ כֹּחַ" (דְּבָרִים ח, יח), וְנֶאֱמַר: "כִּי גַם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ" (יְשַׁעְיָה כו, יב).
And concerning us it is said: "for it is He that gives you power" (Deuteronomy 8:18), and: "for You also have wrought all our works in us" (Isaiah 26:12).
זֶהוּ "אַתָּה עִמָּדִי" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי שָׁם),
This is "You are with me,"
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הַגֵּיהִנָּם שֶׁהוּא שֶׁל אֵשׁ, דְּהַיְינוּ מַדְרֵגַת הַיִּרְאָה,
and through this, Gehenna which is of fire—representing the level of fear/awe—
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּחֲגִיגָה (יג:): נְהַר דִּינוּר מִזֵּיעָתָן שֶׁל חַיּוֹת יוֹרֵד עַל רֹאשׁ רְשָׁעִים בְּגֵיהִנָּם.
as written in Chagigah 13b: the river of fire (nehar dinur) issuing from the sweat of the holy Chayot descends upon the heads of the wicked in Gehenna.
וְאִית יִרְאָה רָעָה שֶׁהִיא רְצוּעָה לְאַלְקָאָה בִישַׁיָּא;
And there is an evil, morbid fear which acts as a scourge to lash the wicked;
וְעַל יְדֵי "כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי" נִתְהַפֵּךְ לְיִרְאַת ה' וְיִרְאַת הָרוֹמְמוּת הַמְּבִיאָה אַדְּרַבָּה לְשִׂמְחָה,
and through "for You are with me" it is transformed into the fear of Hashem and awe of His exalted majesty which leads, on the contrary, to holy joy,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְגִילוּ בִּרְעָדָה" (תְּהִלִּים ב, יא);
as written in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 3) and: "and rejoice with trembling" (Psalms 2:11);
וְאָז כְּבָר נִיתְקַן וְקִבֵּל עָנְשׁוֹ בָּזֶה, כִּי זֶה מֵסִיר הַיִּרְאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרָכוֹת (כב.).
and then he has already been rectified and has received his retribution through this, for this removes the debilitating fear, as written in Berakhot 22a.
וְכֵן הַיִּרְאָה מֵסִיר עָוֹן זֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "יְרָא אֶת ה' וְסוּר מֵרָע" (מִשְׁלֵי ג, ז),
And likewise holy fear eliminates this sin, as written: "Fear Hashem, and depart from evil" (Proverbs 3:7),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק ג דִּנְדָרִים (כ.) עַל פָּסוּק "וּבַעֲבוּר תִּהְיֶה יִרְאָתוֹ עַל פְּנֵיכֶם לְבִלְתִּי תֶחֱטָאוּ":
and as written in the third chapter of Nedarim 20a on the verse: "and that His fear may be before your faces, that you sin not" (Exodus 20:17).

paragraphs.text: Maharal, Chiddushei Aggadot, Kiddushin 40a (vol. II, p. 141): “Fruit is what necessarily follows and proceeds from an existing thing, just as fruit comes from a tree. A transgression, which has no existence in its own right, cannot be said to produce fruit—unless the transgression itself produces fruit, as with desecrating the Name and similar cases in which others learn from the sinner and he has disciples who are his fruit. This is certainly a transgression that produces fruit, and this transgression does have fruit. A mitzvah, however, has fruit, for the mitzvah’s exalted rank and level are in the World to Come, and this world is the fruit of the World to Come. Therefore a mitzvah has fruit, whereas a transgression does not.”

sections.en: Extracting the Precious in the Footsteps of Mashiach

p: [קיא] בְּעִקְּבָתָא דִּמְשִׁיחָא הָעִיקָּר הוּא רַק לְהוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל,
In the footsteps of the Messiah, the central task is exclusively to extract the precious from the vile (Jeremiah 15:19),
וְרַק בִּמְקוֹם יֵצֶר הָרָע וְתִגְבֹּורֶת עֲווֹנוֹת מִשָּׁם יִקָּחֲךָ דַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה,
and specifically from the place of the evil inclination and the raging surge of sins will He take you, expressly through repentance,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (צח.): בֶּן דָּוִד בָּא בְּדוֹר שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ חַיָּיב.
as written in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 98a): the Son of David comes in a generation that is entirely guilty.
וְנֶפֶשׁ כָּזֶה הוּא מֵחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ,
And such a soul belongs to the spiritual allotment of the Messiah,
וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נִקְרָא שֶׁהֵקִים עוֹלָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה.
and likewise King David, peace be upon him, is described as having established the yoke of repentance (Moed Katan 16b).
כִּידוּעַ דִּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל "רַגְלֶיהָ יֹרְדוֹת וְכוּלֵי" רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן;
For as is known, concerning the Congregation of Israel in exile it is written: "Her feet go down to death, etc." (Proverbs 5:5), may the Merciful One preserve us;
וּבְעִקְבֵי מָשִׁיחַ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִן הָרַגְלִין, וְשָׁם תִּגְבֹּורֶת הָרָע וְהַיֵּצֶר.
and in the footsteps of the Messiah, souls originate from the feet (raglin), where the surge of evil and passion is greatest.
וּלְכָךְ דּוֹר שֶׁל נְפָשׁוֹת כָּאֵלּוּ דַּיְיקָא יִזְכּוּ לְמָשִׁיחַ,
And therefore, precisely a generation comprised of such souls will merit the Messiah,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט): "טוֹב מְאֹד" – זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע.
as in the rabbinic dictum (Bereishit Rabbah 9): "'Very good'—this is the evil inclination."
וְכֵן מָשִׁיחַ עַצְמוֹ נוֹלַד מִמָּקוֹם כָּזֶה,
And so the Messiah himself was born out of such a lineage,
כִּידוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם וַיֵּרָא עַל בְּנוֹת לוֹט וְלוֹט, שֶׁהֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, וּמִשָּׁם נִצְמַח שׁוֹרֶשׁ בֶּן דָּוִד.
as is known from Midrash HaNe'elam (Vayeira) regarding Lot and his daughters, who represent the root of the power of passion, and from there sprouted the root of the Son of David.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אָז: שֶׁיִּתְהַפֵּךְ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרַע לְטוֹב, שֶׁזֶּה שְׁחִיטַת הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (נב.).

That is, because this represents the ultimate perfection that will unfold then: that the very root of evil will be transformed into good, which is the slaughter of the evil inclination described in Sukkah 52a.
וְהוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁבַּגּוּף, וְהַיּוֹתֵר סָמוּךְ לָרַע בְּכָל מִינֵי תֹּקֶף.
And he is the final soul in the reservoir of the Guf, and the one closest to evil in all manner of fierce intensity.
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַדּוֹרוֹת הוֹלְכִים וּמִתְקַטְּנִים,
And in this physical world the generations steadily diminish in stature;
אֲבָל אָז כְּשֶׁיְּתוּקַּן, יִהְיֶה בְּטוֹב "סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה",
but then, when rectified, it will become good according to "the end of action is conceived in the initial thought,"
בְּסוֹד הַחַיּוֹת: "רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב כְּמַרְאֵה הַבָּזָק",
in the mystical secret of the holy Chayot: "running and returning like the appearance of a flash of lightning" (Ezekiel 1:14),
שֶׁמִּמָּקוֹם שֶׁפּוֹסֵק, מִשָּׁם חוֹזֵר וּמַתְחִיל לְהָאִיר,
so that from the very place where it ceases, from there it returns and begins to radiate,
וְנַעֲשָׂה זֶה רֹאשׁ, וְנִתְהַפְּכוּ תַּחְתּוֹנִים לְמַעְלָה,
and this lowest point becomes the head, and the lower elements are inverted to the top,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים נ.): "עוֹלָם הָפוּךְ רָאִיתִי":
as our Sages expounded (Pesachim 50a): "I saw an inverted world—the upper below and the lower above."

paragraphs.text: Sichat Shedim 1:6 describes final repair as a return of created powers to their source. It connects Adam’s accepted repentance with Shabbat and argues that evil is not allowed absolute completion: creation contains a mixture and a possible benefit, culminating in future rectification. This explains the lowest point becoming the start of ascent. Both passages concern the completion of repair, and the present siman explicitly requires repentance.

This is the fuller explanation of the wording invoked here; the transformation occurs through return, not through distance alone.

sections.en: Parents and Children in Desire and Repentance

p: [קיב] תַּאֲוַת הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁל הָאָדָם הוּא מִתֹּקֶף הַתַּאֲוָה שֶׁל אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ בְּעֵת הֶרְיוֹנוֹ,
A person's passionate lust derives from the intensity of the desire of his father and mother at the time of his conception,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בַּמִּזְמוֹר כַּאֲשֶׁר בָּא וְכוּלֵי: "הֵן בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים נא, ז),
as King David, peace be upon him, expressed in the psalm composed when Nathan came to him: "Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity, etc." (Psalms 51:7),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם וַיֵּרָא (קיב עַמּוּד א) שֶׁהַמְּקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמוֹ בִּשְׁעַת תַּשְׁמִישׁ לָא מִסְתָּפוּ בָּנָיו מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
and as written in Midrash HaNe'elam (Vayeira 112a) that whoever sanctifies himself at the time of marital intimacy, his children do not fear the evil inclination.
וּלְכָךְ בַּת כֹּהֵן שֶׁזִּנְתָה – "אֶת אָבִיהָ הִיא מְחַלֶּלֶת" (וַיִּקְרָא כא, ט), וַאֲפִילּוּ הוּא בְּגַן עֵדֶן דָּנִין אוֹתוֹ עַל דָּבָר זֶה.
And therefore, regarding a priest's daughter who commits adultery Scripture states: "she profanes her father" (Leviticus 21:9), and even if he is in Gan Eden, he is judged for this matter.
וּלְכָךְ נִרְאָה לְיוֹסֵף דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו שֶׁלֹּא יֶחֱטָא.
And therefore the image of his father appeared to Joseph so that he would not sin (Sotah 36b).
וּכְשֶׁהָאָב קִבֵּל עָנְשׁוֹ וְנִתְקַן שָׁם, אָז הַבֵּן מִתְעוֹרֵר בִּתְשׁוּבָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
And when the father has received his retribution and is rectified there, then the son is awakened to repentance in this world;
וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ: עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבַת הַבֵּן וְתִיקּוּנוֹ לְיִצְרָא דַּעֲבֵירָה, מַנִּיחִים לְאָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ בְּגַן עֵדֶן.
and likewise conversely: through the son's repentance and his conquering of the impulse to sin, relief is granted to his father and mother in Gan Eden.
וּלְכָךְ בְּעֵת הַמִּילָה שֶׁהוּא תִּיקּוּן הַבְּרִית וְהַתַּאֲוָה, אוֹמְרִים: "יִשְׂמַח אָבִיךָ וְאִמֶּךָ וְגוֹמֵר" (מִשְׁלֵי כג, כה).
And therefore at the circumcision ceremony, which is the rectification of the Covenant and passion, we recite: "Let your father and your mother be glad, etc." (Proverbs 23:25).
וְזֶה בִּכְלַל "הָאָב זוֹכֶה לִבְנוֹ בְּחָכְמָה",
And this falls under "a father endows his son with wisdom" (Eduyot 2:9),
כִּי אֵין אָדָם עוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְנַס בּוֹ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת:
for a person does not commit a transgression unless a spirit of folly enters him (Sotah 3a).

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 14:5: “Rabbi Acha said: Even if he were the most pious of the pious, it is impossible that he should not have some aspect of sin. David said before the Holy One, blessed be He: “Master of the worlds, did my father Jesse intend to bring me into being? Did he not intend his own pleasure? Know that this is so: after they have fulfilled their needs, this one turns his face one way and that one turns her face the other way, while You gather every drop that is there.” This is what David said, “For my father and mother abandoned me, but the Lord gathered me in,” and “In sin my mother conceived me.””

Rav Tzadok develops the passage into his account of transmitted desire and the shared work of repair; the existing Beit Yaakov note retains the distinction between an inherited condition and a deliberate present action.

sections.en: Precious Souls and the Fruit of the Righteous

p: [קיג] "פְּרִי צַדִּיק" הוּא "עֵץ חַיִּים" (מִשְׁלֵי יא, ל),
"The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life" (Proverbs 11:30),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (פה.) גַּבֵּי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, אַף שֶׁהָיָה נִרְאֶה לֹא כֵן.
as written in Bava Metzia 85a regarding the son of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, even though initially he appeared quite the opposite.
דִּבְוַדַּאי הַצַּדִּיק מוֹלִיד נְפָשׁוֹת יְקָרוֹת
For certainly the righteous person engenders precious souls
[וְעֵץ חַיִּים הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד עִם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת].
and the 'tree of life' is Torah, which is one with these holy souls.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל: דְּרוּחִין וְשֵׁדִין וְלִילִין שֶׁהוֹלִיד אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן הָיוּ דּוֹר שִׁעְבּוּד מִצְרַיִם.
And along these lines is likewise what the holy Ari wrote: that the spirits and demons generated by Adam the First became the generation subjugated in Egypt.
וְכֵן י' טִפִּין שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִיּוֹסֵף הֵם עֲשָׂרָה הֲרוּגֵי מְלוּכָה.
And likewise the ten drops that issued from Joseph became the Ten Martyrs of the Kingdom.
רַק שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לָזֶה "וְלֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת חָכָם" (מִשְׁלֵי יא, ל), דִּבְחָכְמָה אִתְבְּרִירוּ וְלוֹקְחָם מִן הָרָע.
Only that for this is required "and he that wins souls is wise" (Proverbs 11:30), for through wisdom they are refined and extracted from evil.
וְלִפְעָמִים הוּא עַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם בַּדּוֹר, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל מִפֶּרֶק הַפּוֹעֲלִים בִּבְנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
And sometimes this is achieved through a specific Torah scholar in the generation, as mentioned above from chapter HaPo'alim regarding the son of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.
וְלִפְעָמִים הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ, שֶׁנִּקְרָא גַּם כֵּן לוֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת בְּמִשְׁפָּט בְּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן לְאָבֵל.
And sometimes it is accomplished by the Holy One Himself, Who is likewise termed "He Who takes souls in judgment" in the Grace after Meals for mourners.
וְעַל יְדֵי מִיתַת הָאָב שֶׁנִּקְרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לוֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת, הוּא גַּם כֵּן לוֹקֵחַ נֶפֶשׁ בְּנוֹ
And through the father's death, wherein the Blessed Name is termed the Taker of souls, He also gathers the soul of his son
[וְכֵן נְפָשׁוֹת הָעֲשׁוּקוֹת רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן]
and likewise the oppressed, captive souls, may the Merciful One preserve us
וְעוֹשֶׂה מִמֶּנָּה עֵץ חַיִּים
and transforms it into a tree of life
[וְלִפְעָמִים הוּא עַל אוֹתוֹ דֶּרֶךְ דִּבְגְמָרָא שָׁם דְּקָרוּ לֵיהּ "רַבִּי",
and sometimes it occurs in the manner described in the Gemara there, where they addressed him prematurely as "Rabbi,"
וְנוֹתֵן בְּלֵב בְּנֵי אָדָם לְהַסְמִיכוֹ בְּרַבִּי וּלְהַגְדִּילוֹ, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְגַּדֵּל אַחַר כָּךְ בֶּאֱמֶת.
inspiring people's hearts to ordain him as Rabbi and honor him, whereby he subsequently becomes genuinely great.
וְאָז גַּם "רַבִּי" שֶׁקָּרְאוּ לוֹ אָז, וַדַּאי לֹא לַשָּׁוְא הָיָה,
And then, even the title "Rabbi" they applied to him back then was certainly not in vain;
כִּי כְּשֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה הָאֱמֶת, אָז נִרְאֶה כִּי גַּם תְּחִלָּה הָיָה כֵן רַק שֶׁהָיָה בְּהֶעְלֵם,
for when the truth is revealed, it becomes evident that even initially it was so, only that it lay in deep concealment,
כִּי "מֵאַרְיָא בִּישָׁא גִּירָא טָבָא לָא נָפֵיק".
for 'from an evil lion a good arrow does not issue.'
וְתֵדַע, דְּאָמְרוּ שָׁם: "לֹא שֶׁזֶּה גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה וְכוּלֵי",
And you may know this, for they said there: "Not that this one is greater than that one, etc.,"
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה רוֹעֶה זוֹנוֹת תְּחִלָּה,
and even though he was initially an associate of harlots,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא תִזָּכַרְנָה רִאשׁוֹנוֹת,
nonetheless his former deeds are not mentioned,
רַק הָיָה גַּם בִּתְחִלָּתוֹ טוֹב וְגָדוֹל כְּמוֹ בַּסּוֹף,
but he was inherently good and great in his beginning just as at his end,
וְעַל כֵּן נִזְכַּר זֶה בַּגְּמָרָא]:
and therefore was this recorded in the Gemara.

paragraphs.text: Sha'ar HaPesukim, Parashat Shemot 6: “It follows that all those demons and spirits created during the 130 years when Adam separated from Eve, as is known, were all exalted holy souls from the aspect of daat. They became mixed among the shells and required many reincarnations to refine and purify them until their impurity was removed. Therefore you find that the nation of Israel did not come into being until Jacob and afterward: most of the souls were mixed among the shells and were progressively refined, reincarnating from generation to generation. Their repair did not begin until Jacob, the chosen of the patriarchs, who repaired Adam. Then the repair of his children—the aforementioned souls—also began, and they continued to be refined in the Egyptian exile until Israel left Egypt.”

sections.en: Redeeming Captive Souls Through Torah Study

p: [קיד] מִי שֶׁהוּא תַּלְמִיד חָכָם, הוּא לוֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת וּמְלַקֵּט נִיצוֹצוֹת מִנְּפָשׁוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת שֶׁנִּתְפַּזְּרוּ בְּעִמְקֵי תְּהוֹם רַבָּה.
Whoever is a Torah scholar gathers souls and collects holy sparks from sacred souls that have been scattered into the depths of the great abyss.
עַל יְדֵי לִמּוּד תּוֹרָתוֹ, כָּל דִּבּוּר שֶׁל תּוֹרָה מוֹצִיא אוֹתָם הַשַּׁיָּיכִים לוֹ,
Through his Torah study, every spoken word of Torah extracts those souls affiliated with him,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְלֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת חָכָם" (מִשְׁלֵי יא, ל).
as it is written: "and he that wins souls is wise" (Proverbs 11:30).
וְגַם נַפְשׁוֹ עַצְמוֹ,
And he also extracts his own soul,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פְּתִיחַת אֵיכָה): "הַמָּאוֹר שֶׁבָּהּ מַחֲזִירוֹ לְמוּטָב".
as written (Midrash Rabbah, introduction to Eichah): "the illumination within it returns him to good."
אֲבָל בָּזֶה יֵשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת, שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים כְּשֶׁהִיא בְּעֹמֶק רַע רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁנֶּחְבְּשָׁה וְנִשְׁקְעָה שָׁם,
However, in this there are gradations, for sometimes when a soul is in the depth of evil, may the Merciful One preserve us, so sunken and imprisoned there,
שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: "אֵין חָבוּשׁ מַתִּיר עַצְמוֹ" (בְּרָכוֹת ה:),
concerning which they said: "A prisoner cannot free himself from prison" (Berakhot 5b),
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "וְלָרָשָׁע אָמַר אֱלֹהִים מַה לְּךָ לְסַפֵּר חֻקָּי",
and regarding this it was stated: "And unto the wicked God says: What right have you to recount My statutes?" (Psalms 50:16);
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא עב:): לֹא זָכָה – נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ וְכוּלֵי,
and likewise they said (Yoma 72b): if he did not merit, it becomes a deadly potion to him,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לוֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת וּמַכְנִיסָם גַּם כֵּן בְּעֹמֶק רַע רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן.
such that through his words of Torah he gathers souls and drags them likewise into the depth of evil, may the Merciful One preserve us.
אַף דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם לַסּוֹף כְּשֶׁיְּתַקֵּן הוּא מַרְוִיחַ, דְּעוֹלֶה וְעוֹלִים עִמּוֹ;
Even though ultimately when he rectifies he gains, for he ascends and they ascend with him;
אַךְ לְפִי שָׁעָה נֶאֱמַר עַל זֶה: "וּפֹשְׁעִים יִכָּשְׁלוּ בָם" (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, י) דַּיְיקָא, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָרַע מִתְגַּבֵּר.
yet for the immediate present it is proclaimed: "and transgressors shall stumble in them" (Hosea 14:10), whereby through this evil is temporarily intensified.
רַק לִפְעָמִים גַּם לָזֶה יוֹעִיל תּוֹרָתוֹ, כְּשֶׁמַּצִּיל עַל יְדֵי כֵן אֵיזֶה נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא בַּחַיִּים,
However, sometimes even for this his Torah avails, when he thereby saves some soul that is alive in this world,
וְאוֹתוֹ נֶפֶשׁ מִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ וְיוּכַל לְהַצִּילוֹ,
and that soul overcomes its inclination and is empowered to save him,
וּכְמַעֲשֶׂה דְּתַלְמִיד אֶחָד בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ זוּטָא (סוֹף פֶּרֶק כב) שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהַצִּיל עַצְמוֹ בְּתוֹרָתוֹ, רַק הִצִּיל נֶפֶשׁ הָאִשָּׁה
as in the episode of a certain disciple in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta (end of chapter 22) who could not save himself through his own Torah, yet saved the soul of the woman
[שֶׁהָיְתָה גַּם כֵּן נֶפֶשׁ גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁהָיְתָה יְכוֹלָה לְהָבִין כְּשֶׁרָאֲתָה אוֹתוֹ לוֹמֵד שֶׁהוּא כְּמַלְאָךְ,
who was likewise a lofty soul, capable of discerning when she saw him learning that he was like an angel,
וּמִסְּתָמָא הָאֱמֶת כֵּן מִדְּנִזְכַּר בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֱלִיָּהוּ, אִם כֵּן יָדְעָה בְּטוּבָן שֶׁל מַלְאָכִים]
and presumably that was the truth since it was recorded in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu, showing she was versed in the nature of angels
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִיא הִצִּילַתּוּ.
and afterward she saved him.
וְעִמְקֵי רַע נִקְרָא רַע בְּתַאֲווֹת רָעוֹת, וְכָל סֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵי מָלֵא מִזֶּה, וְנֶאֱמַר: "שׁוּחָה עֲמֻקָּה זוֹנָה" (מִשְׁלֵי כג, כז).
And the "depths of evil" denotes the immersion in wicked lusts, with which the Book of Proverbs is replete, as stated: "For a harlot is a deep pit" (Proverbs 23:27).
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין (יט.): אֲפִילּוּ דּוֹמֶה לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁקִּבֵּל תּוֹרָה מֵהַר סִינַי, לֹא יִנָּקֶה מִדִּינָהּ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם;
And therefore they stated in Eruvin 19a: even if one resembles Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who received the Torah from Mount Sinai, he will not be cleared from the judgment of Gehenna;
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לְהַתִּיר עַצְמוֹ מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִים עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָתוֹ,
meaning that he cannot liberate himself from prison through his own Torah,
אֲבָל יָכוֹל עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים הַבָּאִים מִגִּירָא דִילֵיהּ.
but he can be freed through others who originate as arrows from his quiver.
וְכֵן אַחַר שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ "וְלָרָשָׁע וְגוֹמֵר", נִיצּוֹל עַל יְדֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר שֶׁלָּמַד תּוֹרָה מִמֶּנּוּ, וְהוּא תִּיקֵּן וְהִצִּיל נַפְשׁוֹ מִדִּינָהּ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם:

And thus Elisha ben Avuyah (Acher), after it was said to him "and unto the wicked God says, etc.," was saved through Rabbi Meir who studied Torah from him, who rectified and delivered his soul from the judgment of Gehenna (Chagigah 15b).

paragraphs.text: Or HaChaim on Leviticus 7:37:2 distinguishes two kinds of recovery through Torah: holy sparks that fell in the world of chaos, and souls taken captive through Adam’s sin. Torah returns the sparks to their source and breaks the power holding the souls. Its account of both kinds of recovery parallels Rav Tzadok’s description of the souls released through a scholar’s words of Torah.

paragraphs.text: Ramchal expressly excludes mockery and deliberate distortion from this restorative account: the person must at least study seriously, as one would approach another discipline. This preserves both the present impediment and the possibility of gradual repair.

The present siman nevertheless leaves open eventual repair.

sections.en: Truth and Personal Motives in Torah Innovation

p: [קטו] כְּשֶׁמְּחַדֵּשׁ דָּבָר בַּתּוֹרָה, צָרִיךְ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה מִצַּד שׁוּם נְגִיעָה בַּלֵּב שֶׁרוֹצֶה כָּךְ, אוֹ לְהִתְפָּאֲרוּת, אוֹ לַחְלוֹק עַל דִּבְרֵי זוּלָתוֹ וְכַיּוֹצֵא,

When a person innovates an insight in the Torah, it must not stem from any personal bias in the heart that desires it to be so, nor for self-aggrandizement, nor to dispute the words of another, or the like;
רַק מִצַּד הַתְּשׁוּקָה לֵידַע הָאֱמֶת,
but solely from the pure yearning to know the Truth.
וְאָז אֲפִילּוּ טוֹעֶה נִקְרָא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְדִבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים,
And then, even if he errs, it is termed words of Torah and the words of the living God,
שֶׁהֲרֵי נִזְכַּר בַּתַּלְמוּד דִּבְרֵי הַטּוֹעִים וְשֶׁנִּדְחוּ מֵהֲלָכָה, שֶׁגַּם הַהֲוָא אָמֵינָא הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,

for behold, the Talmud explicitly records the words of those who erred and opinions that were rejected from practical halakhah, showing that even the initial hypothesis (hava amina) is words of Torah;
שֶׁכָּךְ יִסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: מוּשְׂכָּל רִאשׁוֹן וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַגָּעָה לָאֱמֶת, וְגַם הַמּוּשְׂכָּל רִאשׁוֹן הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְדִבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים.

for thus the Blessed Name established the process: first an initial conception, and only subsequently arriving at the truth; and that initial conception is likewise from the Blessed Name and constitutes the words of the living God.
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הַנְּגִיעָה, אָז אֵינוֹ נִקְרָא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּלָל,
But when it stems from personal bias, then it is not termed words of Torah at all;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיָרָבְעָם: "הַחֹדֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר בָּדָא מִלִּבּוֹ" (מְלָכִים א יב, לג),
as written concerning Jeroboam: "the month which he had devised of his own heart" (I Kings 12:33),
וּבְוַדַּאי הוּא דָּרַשׁ לָהֶם אֵיזֶה דְּרָשׁ וְלִמּוּד שֶׁחַג הָאָסִיף הוּא בְּחֶשְׁוָן,
and certainly he expounded to them some textual exegesis and derivation that the Harvest Festival falls in Marcheshvan;
רַק לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה מִצַּד הַנְּגִיעָה לַעֲשׂוֹת נֶגֶד בֵּית דִּין שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, נִקְרָא "אֲשֶׁר בָּדָא מִלִּבּוֹ", וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר בָּזֶה "אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים".

yet because it stemmed from personal bias to undermine the Sanhedrin in Jerusalem, it was branded "which he had devised of his own heart," and concerning this it was not said: "both these and those are the words of the living God."
וְכֵן דּוֹאֵג עָשָׂה הַכֹּל עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה בְּדַעְתּוֹ, כִּי רֹאשׁ הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין הָיָה,
And likewise Doeg acted completely in accordance with the Torah in his own mind, for he was the head of the Sanhedrin,
וְהוּא הוֹרָה "עַמּוֹנִי – וְאֲפִילּוּ עַמּוֹנִית" עַל פִּי הֲלָכָה שֶׁבְּדַעְתּוֹ, שֶׁהֲרֵי אִשְׁתִּיקוּ נֶגְדּוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יְבָמוֹת עז.),
and he ruled: "'an Ammonite'—even a female Ammonite" based on the halakhah as he construed it, seeing that the scholars initially fell silent before him (Yevamot 77a),
וּמִמֵּילָא אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דָּוִד מֶלֶךְ וְהוּא מִפְּסוּלֵי קָהָל, וְדָנוֹ לְמוֹרֵד בַּמַּלְכוּת, וְכֵן לַאֲחִימֶלֶךְ.
and consequently it was impossible for David to be king, being disqualified from the congregation, and so he judged David as a rebel against the monarchy, and likewise Ahimelech.
וְשָׁאוּל, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה סָבוּר גַּם כֵּן כֵּן, הוּא הָיָה בְּטָעוּת וְנִקְרָא בֶּאֱמֶת בְּחִיר ה'.
And Saul, even though he likewise held this view, was merely in honest error, and was in truth titled the chosen one of Hashem.
אֲבָל דּוֹאֵג, דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֵלּוּ נָבְעוּ מִלִּבּוֹ מִצַּד הַקִּנְאָה, וְאִלּוּלֵי נְגִיעָה זוֹ לֹא הָיָה טוֹעֶה.
But with Doeg, these words of Torah welled up from his heart out of jealousy, and were it not for this personal bias, he would not have made this error.
בְּאֹפֶן זֶה נַעֲשִׂים דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה סַם הַמָּוֶת רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן, שֶׁנֶּאֶבְדוּ מִן הָעוֹלָם,
In this manner, words of Torah become a potion of death, may the Merciful One preserve us, causing one to be lost from the world,
כִּי אֵין זֶה נִקְרָא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בֶּאֱמֶת כְּלָל, רַק לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן
for this is not truly termed words of Torah at all, but only so to outward appearance
[וְאֵין בְּכֹחַ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כָּאֵלּוּ לְהוֹצִיא נְפָשׁוֹת כְּלָל, כְּעִנְיַן "אֵל אַחֵר אִסְתָּרַס וְלָא עָבִיד פֵּירִין".
and such words of Torah have no power to extract and redeem holy souls at all, in the manner of 'the other god is castrated and bears no fruit.'
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (חֲגִיגָה טו:) וּבְפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו:): מִי זוּטַר וְכוּלֵי, אֶלָּא רַחֲמָנָא לִבָּא בָּעֵי,
And this aligns with Chagigah 15b and Sanhedrin 106b: 'Is this a small matter, etc.? Rather, the Merciful One desires the heart.'
וּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁהַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ יִהְיֶה מְחֻבֶּרֶת עִם הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב יַחַד, וְהַחָכְמָה יִהְיֶה יוֹצֵאת מִן הַלֵּב,
Which means that the wisdom in the brain must be bound together with the understanding in the heart, wisdom emerging directly from the heart,
וְזֶה עַל יְדֵי הַדַּעַת הַמְּחַבֵּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה,
and this occurs through Da'at (awareness) which unites Chokhmah and Binah;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אֵל אַחֵר אֵין בּוֹ דַּעַת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת ק"ז,
whereas the 'other god' lacks Da'at as I wrote above in Section 107,

p: [קטז] עַל יְדֵי הַטָּעֻיּוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁטּוֹעֶה וְאַחַר כָּךְ עוֹמֵד עַל הָאֱמֶת, שֶׁזֶּה קָרָא יְשַׁעְיָה "מַכְשֵׁלָה" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּחֲגִיגָה (יד.) דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,

Through errors occurring in words of Torah wherein one stumbles and subsequently masters the truth—which Isaiah designated as a "ruin/obstacle" (makhshelah, Isaiah 3:6), explained in Chagigah 14a as referring to words of Torah—
עַל יְדֵי זֶה לוֹקֵחַ אוֹתָם נְפָשׁוֹת דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה שֶׁבָּאִים מִצַּד יֵצֶר הָרָע שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ יְשַׁעְיָה "מִכְשׁוֹל" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֻכָּה (נב.),
one gathers those captive souls generated by emitting seed in vain that stem from the evil inclination, which Isaiah titled a "stumbling block" (mikhshol, Isaiah 57:14; Sukkah 52a),
וְהוּא בְּפָרָשַׁת "הַצַּדִּיק אָבָד" שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ עַל עָוֹן זֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת מ"ה.
located in the passage "The righteous perishes" which is expounded upon this very sin, as I wrote above in Section 45.
וּמִכְשׁוֹל הַיְינוּ "לִפְנֵי עִוֵּר" בְּאֵין רוֹאֶה, וְכֵן זֶה בַּחֲלוֹם לַיְלָה
And a stumbling block means "before the blind" where none sees, and likewise this emission occurs in the nocturnal slumber of the night

[וּ"מִדֶּרֶךְ עַמִּי", וְ"דֶרֶךְ" בְּכָל מָקוֹם רוֹמֵז עַל "דֶּרֶךְ גֶּבֶר בְּעַלְמָה", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרָכוֹת (יא.) "מִבְּלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ", וְכֵן עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ קִדּוּשִׁין].
and 'out of the way of My people,' where 'way' everywhere alludes to 'the way of a man with a maid' (Proverbs 30:19), as in Berakhot 11a, and likewise to words of Torah, as at the start of Kiddushin.
וּבְוַדַּאי אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹבֵר עַל לָאו דְּ"לִפְנֵי עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשֹׁל"
And certainly the Blessed Name does not violate the prohibition "you shall not put a stumbling block before the blind"

[וְעַיֵּין בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (כט.) פְּלוּגְתָּא אִי נִתְקָל פּוֹשֵׁעַ, וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר בֵּאַרְנוּ דְּכָל אֶחָד דִּבֵּר כְּפִי שָׁרְשׁוֹ, רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְשִׁיטָתוֹ בְּגִטִּין נב. וְהוֹרָיוֹת יג: דְּדִבְרֵי חֲלוֹמוֹת לֹא מַעֲלִין וְלֹא מוֹרִידִין, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ],

and see Bava Kamma 29a regarding the dispute whether one who trips is negligent, which we explained elsewhere as reflecting each sage's soul-root, Rabbi Meir following his view in Gittin 52a and Horayot 13b that dreams are meaningless, and this is not the place to lengthen,
רַק הוּא כְּדֵי לַעֲמוֹד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְהוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל.
but rather it occurs so that one subsequently masters words of Torah to extract the precious from the vile.
וְאָז דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִקְרָא "מַכְשֵׁלָה" – נוּקְבָא לְגַבֵּי "מִכְשׁוֹל" דְּכַר, וּמְקַבֶּלֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ הָעֲשׁוּקָה הַהוּא שֶׁהוּא הַמִּכְשׁוֹל, וּמוֹצִיאָתוֹ לָאוֹר וְלִקְדוּשָׁה,

And then words of Torah are called a makhshelah (feminine noun) relative to the masculine mikhshol, receiving that oppressed captive soul which was the stumbling block and delivering it into light and holiness,
שֶׁגַּם בָּהּ נֶאֱרַע מַכְשֵׁלָה וְהַעֲמָדָה עַל הָאֱמֶת אַחַר כָּךְ דַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה, כִּי אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד וְכוּלֵי בְּעִנְיָן אַחֵר, עַל יְדֵי זֶה הֶעֱלָה הַמִּכְשׁוֹל.

for in the Torah study there likewise occurred an initial stumbling and an arrival at the truth specifically through it—since a person does not master Torah in any other way—and through this he elevates the stumbling block.
וְדַיְיקָא יְשַׁעְיָה קְרָאוֹ כֵן וְנִתְנַבֵּא "הָרִימוּ מִכְשׁוֹל וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁהוּא עָמַד עַל זֶה,
And specifically Isaiah termed it thus and prophesied "take up the stumbling block, etc.," for he grasped this deeply,
כַּנּוֹדָע דִּבְרִית הַלָּשׁוֹן וּבְרִית הַמָּעוֹר מְכֻוָּונוֹת, דִּלְכָךְ בַּתּוֹרָה מְתַקְּנִים חֵטְא הַמָּעוֹר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת צ"ז וְק"ז;
as is known that the Covenant of the Tongue and the Covenant of Circumcision run parallel, which is why through Torah one rectifies the sin of the organ, as I wrote above in Sections 97 and 107;
וְכֵן לְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם: "פִּיו הִכְשִׁילוֹ",
and so is the common idiom of our Sages: "his mouth caused him to stumble,"
וּבְגִטִּין (נז.): אַכְשְׁלֵיהּ פּוּמֵיהּ לְבַר דְּרוֹמָא,
and in Gittin 57a: his mouth caused Bar Droma to stumble,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה מֵזִיד קְרָאוּהוּ
even though he spoke deliberately, they called it
[וְכֵן בְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה, הוּא מְהַרְהֵר וְרוֹצֶה שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא לִידֵי הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה],
and likewise with wasted seed, a person struggles in thought and desires not to incur it,
"מִכְשׁוֹל", כִּי הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּמֵה' מַעֲנֵה לָשׁוֹן" (מִשְׁלֵי טז, א), וּמִזְדַּמֵּן לוֹ בַּפֶּה מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לְדַבֵּר כְּלָל כַּנּוֹדָע בְּכָל מָקוֹם.

“a stumbling block,” because it is from the Blessed Name, as written: "and the answer of the tongue is from Hashem" (Proverbs 16:1), bringing to his lips what he never intended to articulate, as known in multiple sources.
וּבָזֶה נִכְשַׁל יְשַׁעְיָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי אִישׁ טְמֵא שְׂפָתַיִם אָנֹכִי" (יְשַׁעְיָה ו, ה),
And in this Isaiah stumbled, as it is written: "because I am a man of unclean lips" (Isaiah 6:5),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּיבָמוֹת (מט:): כִּי מְטָא לַהֲדֵי פּוּמָא וְכוּלֵי, בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁדִּבֵּר רַע עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and as written in Yevamot 49b: when the saw reached his mouth he perished, because he spoke critically of the children of Israel;
וְנַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם עֶצֶם הַתּוֹרָה, נִמְצָא הוּא טָעוּת בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
and the souls of Israel are the very essence of the Torah, so that speaking against them constituted an error in words of Torah.
וְאָמְנָם בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לֹא נִכְשַׁל רַק לְשָׁעָה, שֶׁהֲרֵי מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְבְּעוּ דְּבָרָיו בַּסֵּפֶר וְהֵם דִּבְרֵי נְבוּאָה מִפִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
However, in truth, Heaven forbid that he stumbled permanently, but only for an instant, for his words were nonetheless established in the canon as prophetic words from the mouth of the Blessed Name;
רַק טָעוּת לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן, לְכָךְ הָיָה עָנְשׁוֹ עַל יְדֵי מְנַשֶּׁה שֶׁטָּעַן נֶגְדּוֹ שֶׁנִּכְשַׁל בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת לֹא נִכְשַׁל:

it was merely a seeming error to outward appearance, which is why his punishment came through Manasseh who alleged against him that he contradicted the Torah of Moses (Yevamot 49b), even though in truth he had not stumbled.

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52a: ‘Isaiah called it a ‘stumbling block,’ as it is said: ‘Build up, build up; clear a way; remove the stumbling block from My people’s path.’ Ezekiel called it a ‘stone,’ as it is said: ‘I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.’ Joel called it the ‘northern one’—tzefoni—as it is said: ‘I will remove the northern one far from you.’ The Sages taught: ‘I will remove the northern one far from you’ refers to the evil inclination, which lies hidden—tzafun—in a person’s heart.’

: ““When you sit in your house”—excluding one occupied with a mitzvah; “when you walk on the way”—excluding a bridegroom. From here they said: One who marries a virgin is exempt, and one who marries a widow is obligated.”

paragraphs.text: Rashi on Gittin 43a:15:2: ““And this stumbling block”: That is, he began his discourse with the verse, “And this stumbling block shall be under your hand,” concerning the people of Jerusalem, from whom Torah had ceased. They would ask their fellows: “You have a garment; be our leader, and let this stumbling block be under your hand”—meaning: matters concealed like a garment are yours, for you are expert in them; tell them to us and become our leader. “This stumbling block” means words of Torah, whose truth a person does not grasp until he errs in them by giving an incorrect ruling and is put to shame, whereupon he applies his mind and understands. These are “under your hand.” I too have erred in my ruling and retract it.”

sections.en: Purity from Desire and Vigilance Against Anger

p: [קיז] כָּל מִי שֶׁנָּקִי מֵחֲטָאֵי הַתַּאֲוָה, צָרִיךְ שְׁמִירָה יְתֵירָה בְּעִנְיְנֵי כַּעַס וּרְצִיחָה שֶׁהוּא עָלוּל לָהֶם,
Whoever is pristine and free from sins of passion requires extraordinary vigilance regarding anger and bloodshed to which he is susceptible;
וְכִידוּעַ דְּ"לֹא תִרְצַח" וְ"לֹא תִנְאָף" הֵם שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים, וְהֵם יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל בָּרָע
for as is known, "You shall not murder" and "You shall not commit adultery" are two opposites, representing the right and left sides within evil
[וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל יָרָבְעָם בֶּן נְבָט שֶׁנִּקְרָא אֶפְרָתִי – דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה קֶרִי מִיָּמָיו, וְשֵׁם אִמּוֹ צְרוּעָה – הַיְסוֹד שֶׁלּוֹ כַּעַס].

and as I heard regarding Jeroboam son of Nebat who was called an Ephraimite (Efrati)—meaning he never experienced a nocturnal emission in his days, while his mother's name was Tzeruah (afflicted with tzara'at), showing his flaw lay in anger.
וְכָל זַרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף הֵם שׁוֹמְרֵי הַבְּרִית כַּנּוֹדָע, וּרְצִיחָה שְׁכִיחָה שָׁם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמַכּוֹת (י.): בְּגִלְעָד שְׁכִיחֵי רוֹצְחִים, בִּשְׁכֶם שְׁכִיחָא רוֹצְחִים.

And all the seed of Joseph are guardians of the Covenant as is known, and murder was prevalent in their territories, as written in Makkot 10a: in Gilead murderers were common, in Shechem murderers were common.
וּבְבָבָא מְצִיעָא (פד.) שֶׁסִּפְּרוּ מִשּׁוּפְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וְיָדוּעַ שׁוּפְרֵיהּ וְיוֹפִי הַתֹּאַר בְּכָל מָקוֹם הוּא עַל שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת צ"ו,
And in Bava Metzia 84a they recounted the exquisite beauty of Rabbi Yochanan, and it is known that beauty of form everywhere denotes guardianship of the Covenant as I wrote above in Section 96,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נֶאֱמַר עָלָיו דְּאָתֵי מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף,
and immediately thereafter it is stated of him that he descended from the seed of Joseph;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָעִנְיָן שֶׁאֵירַע לוֹ מֵרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
and following this comes the painful episode that occurred between him and Reish Lakish

[כְּמִנְהַג רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּגְּמָרָא בְּכָל מָקוֹם, מִתּוֹךְ שִׁבְחוֹ וּבִמְקוֹם גְּדוּלָּתוֹ שָׁם אַתָּה מוֹצֵא גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁנִּרְאֶה קְצָת הֵיפֶךְ, כִּי תוֹרָה הִיא וְלִלְמוֹד צָרִיךְ, וּכְמוֹ כֵן גַּם בַּתַּנַּ"ךְ],

as is the custom of our Sages throughout the Talmud, out of a sage's praise and in the very place of his greatness you find that which appears somewhat opposite, for it is Torah and we must study it, and likewise throughout Scripture,
שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד הָרִתְחָא דְּרַבָּנָן שֶׁהָיְתָה גּוֹבֶרֶת בּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לִמְחוֹל.
which arose from the righteous scholarly indignation (ritcha de-rabbanan) surging within him, such that he refused to forgive.

וְגַם גּוּף הַהַעֲנָשָׁה שֶׁהָיָה רָגִיל בָּהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (קיז.) עִם רַב כַּהֲנָא, דָּבָר זֶה הוּא גַּם כֵּן לְמִי שֶׁהוּא בַּטֶּבַע כֵּן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשִׁילְהֵי שַׁבָּת (קנו.): מָר נַמֵּי עָנֵישׁ וְקָטֵיל.

And the severe penal power that Rabbi Yochanan wielded, as recorded in Bava Kamma 117a with Rav Kahana, belongs naturally to one of such temperament, as stated at the end of Shabbat 156a: "The master also punishes and slays."
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּרִתְחָא דְּרַבָּנָן הוּא טָב בְּכָל סִטְרִין כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קפב עַמּוּד ב) וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּתַעֲנִית (ד.) דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מְרַתְּחָא לֵיהּ,
And although scholarly indignation is praiseworthy from all angles as written in Zohar II:182b, and in Ta'anit 4a that it is the fiery Torah that boils within him,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּפִי הַנִּרְאֶה דְּשָׁם לֹא הִצְלִיחַ רִתְחֵיהּ, וּמַאי סְלֵיק בֵּיהּ.
nonetheless it is evident that in that instance his wrath did not succeed, and consider what tragic end came of it!
וּלְפִי שֶׁקָּרָא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ "לִסְטָאָה", דְּהַיְינוּ רוֹצֵחַ, וּלְפִי שֶׁאָסוּר לְהַזְכִּיר לְבַעַל תְּשׁוּבָה מַעֲשָׂיו הָרִאשׁוֹנִים,
And because he called Reish Lakish a "bandit"—which denotes a killer—and because it is forbidden to remind a penitent of his past deeds (Bava Metzia 58b),
לְכָךְ הוּא גַּם כֵּן נִזְדַּמֵּן לוֹ עִנְיָן כָּזֶה עַצְמוֹ עַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁחֲבֵירוֹ נֶעֱנַשׁ עַל יָדוֹ, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא מִזֶּה הַגְּרָם מִיתָה לְעַצְמוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁגָּרַם לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
therefore he too was met with this exact dynamic: through his colleague being punished on his account, he thereby caused his own death, just as he had caused the death of Reish Lakish

[וְנִרְאֶה מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָצָה לִמְחוֹל, כִּי הִרְגִּישׁ שֶׁקָּרַב קִצּוֹ וְחָשַׁב דְּנִדְחֶה מִפְּנֵי גַּבְרָא, וּבְוַדַּאי רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ יִמְלוֹךְ תַּחְתָּיו, וְסָבַר חַיָּיו קוֹדְמִין, וּבָזֶה אֵין צָרִיךְ לִמְחוֹל כִּדְאַשְׁכְּחַן בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּיוֹמָא פז:,

and it appears that the reason he refused to forgive was that he sensed his end approaching, suspecting he was being pushed aside in favor of another, since Reish Lakish would certainly preside in his place, and he held that his own life took precedence, in which case one is not obligated to forgive, as we find with Rabbi Chanina in Yoma 87b;

וְהוּא חִשֵּׁב זֶה לְהַצָּלַת חַיָּיו, אֲבָל "נוֹרָא עֲלִילָה עַל בְּנֵי אָדָם" חָשַׁב לוֹ זֶה לִקְצָת חֵטְא, וְאַדְּרַבָּה זֶה גָּרַם לוֹ הַהֵיפוּךְ, וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פְּדָת מָלַךְ תַּחְתָּיו]:

and he intended this for the preservation of his own life, yet He Who is 'awesome in deed toward the children of men' accounted this as a slight flaw, and on the contrary it caused the opposite, and Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat reigned in his stead.

sections.en: The Power of a Torah Scholar's Everyday Speech

p: [קיח] מִי שֶׁהוּא תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ שִׂיחַת חוּלִין שֶׁלּוֹ צְרִיכָה לִמּוּד כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה כא:),
One who is a Torah scholar whose very casual conversation requires study (Sukkah 21b),
אָז יֵשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ גַּם בְּשִׂיחַת חוּלִין לְתַקֵּן נְפָשׁוֹת, שֶׁהוּא מַמָּשׁ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
possesses the power through mundane conversation to rectify souls, for it is literally Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין נד:) שֶׁכָּל שִׂיחָתָן תּוֹרָה;
as our Sages stated (Eruvin 54a) that all of their conversation is Torah;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁתִּמְצָא בַּתּוֹרָה כַּמָּה סִפּוּרֵי מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת, וְכֵן בַּתַּלְמוּד כַּמָּה דְּבָרִים נִרְאִים כְּסִפּוּרֵי חוֹל, וְהֵם תּוֹרָה מַמָּשׁ כְּכָל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
and just as you find in the Torah numerous historical narratives, and in the Talmud many passages appearing as secular accounts which are in truth actual Torah like all sacred words.
וְכָל הַגָּדוֹל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ, שִׂיחַת חוּלִין שֶׁלּוֹ גְּדוֹלָה מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ,
And whoever is greater than his fellow, his casual conversation is greater than the formal Torah study of his peer,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס): יָפָה שִׂיחָתָן שֶׁל עַבְדֵי אָבוֹת מִתּוֹרָתָן שֶׁל בָּנִים
as written in Bereishit Rabbah 60:8: "More beautiful is the casual speech of the servants of the Patriarchs than the Torah of their children"

[וְלֹא הָיְתָה מַעֲלַת אֱלִיעֶזֶר רַק מַעֲלַת אַבְרָהָם, לְכָךְ קְרָאוֹ עַבְדֵי אָבוֹת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יוֹמָא כח:): דַּמֶּשֶׂק – דּוֹלֶה וּמַשְׁקֶה מִתּוֹרַת רַבּוֹ, כִּי מַה שֶּׁקָּנָה עֶבֶד קָנָה רַבּוֹ, וְכָל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ הַכֹּל נִקְרָא תּוֹרַת רַבּוֹ].

and this was not Eliezer's independent virtue but Abraham's, which is why they were termed 'servants of the Patriarchs,' and in Yoma 28b: Dammasek—he draws and gives drink from the Torah of his master, for what a servant acquires his master acquires, and all Torah he possessed was termed his master's Torah.
וְאָמְרוּ זֶה בְּסֻכָּה (שָׁם) בְּשִׂיחַת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּסֻכָּתוֹ,
And they stated this in Sukkah 21b concerning the conversation of Rabban Gamliel in his sukkah;
וְנִרְאֶה מִזֶּה דִּבְסֻכָּה, עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהֵם בְּצִלָּא דִּמְהֵימְנוּתָא, זוֹכִים לִהְיוֹת כֵּן;
and it appears from this that in the sukkah, because they dwell in the Shade of Faith, they merit this elevation;
וְשָׁם קְרָאוּ לְשִׂיחַת חוּלִין "עָלֵהוּ", וּמָצִינוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק.): "וְעָלֵהוּ לִתְרוּפָה" – לְהַתִּיר פֶּה עֲקָרוֹת,
and there they compared casual conversation to the leaves of the tree ("its leaf does not wither"), and we find in Sanhedrin 100a: "'and its leaf for healing'—to open the mouth of the barren,"
דְּהַיְינוּ הוֹלָדַת נְפָשׁוֹת חֲדָשׁוֹת הוּא עַל יְדֵי חִדּוּשֵׁי תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּשִׂיחַת חוּלִין שֶׁלָּהֶם;
meaning the begetting of new souls occurs through the Torah novelties embedded within their casual conversations;

וְכֵן לְהַתִּיר פֶּה אִלְּמִים הוּא גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "מַרְפֵּא לָשׁוֹן – עֵץ חַיִּים" (מִשְׁלֵי טו, ד), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה דְּבָרִים רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה א:
and likewise to open the mouth of the mute is achieved through words of Torah, as written: "A soothing tongue is a tree of life" (Proverbs 15:4), and in Devarim Rabbah 1:1.

paragraphs.text: Divrei Soferim 36:1 explains that sustained immersion of thought in Torah can shape even spontaneous conversation. It connects the depth and demanding labor of Talmud with the principle that a person is where his thought is attached. Conversation here means an utterance made without deliberate preparation; its Torah character arises from the person’s inward immersion rather than from its outward subject alone.

Rabbi Yehudah said: We used to sleep beneath a bed in the presence of the elders, and they said nothing to us. sections.en: The Enduring Power of Torah Narratives

p: [קיט] כָּל הַסִּפּוּרִים שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה וּבַגְּמָרָא מִדְּבָרִים מוּפְלָאִים שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ, שָׁם עַצְמוֹ יֵשׁ הַכֹּחַ לַעֲשִׂיָּה הַהוּא,
All the narratives in the Torah and the Talmud recounting wondrous miracles performed contain within themselves the active power to execute that deed,
כִּי כָּל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה חַיִּים וְקַיָּימִים וְשָׁם יֵשׁ הַחַיּוּת לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר,
for all words of Torah are alive and enduring, and within them resides the vital energy for that specific occurrence;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתִּיקּוּנִים סוֹף תִּיקּוּן נ"ה: כִּי מִפָּסוּק "וְהַמִּכְתָּב מִכְתַּב אֱלֹהִים הוּא" יָצָא שֵׁם הַכּוֹתֵב,
as written in Tikkunei Zohar (end of Tikkun 55): from the verse "and the writing was the writing of God" (Exodus 32:16) issues the mystical Name that causes writing to appear;
וּמִפָּסוּק "ה' אֱלֹהִים נָתַן לִי לְשׁוֹן לִמּוּדִים וְגוֹמֵר" – שֵׁם הַדּוֹרֵשׁ.
and from the verse "The Lord God has given me the tongue of the learned, etc." (Isaiah 50:4) issues the Name of the preacher.
וּבְסֵפֶר עֲבוֹדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל פָּרָשַׁת חַיֵּי מִפָּסוּק "וָאָבֹא הַיּוֹם אֶל הָעָיִן", שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י: הַיּוֹם יָצָאתִי וְהַיּוֹם בָּאתִי, יוֹצֵא שֵׁם לִקְפִיצַת הָאָרֶץ.

And in Sefer Avodat Yisrael (Parashat Chayei Sarah): from the verse "And I came this day unto the fountain" (Genesis 24:42), where Rashi explains: today I departed and today I arrived, issues the Name for miraculous contraction of the road (kefitzat haderekh).
וְכֵן יָדוּעַ מִפָּסוּק שֶׁל הַכָּאַת סַנְוֵרִים יוֹצֵא שֵׁם לִפְעוֹל כֵּן.
And likewise it is known that from the verse of smiting with blindness (Genesis 19:11) issues a Name to effect the same.
וּבְדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ה:): "יְהַב לֵיהּ יְדָא וְאוֹקְמֵיהּ", דְּרָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת יְ'הַב לֵ'יהּ יְ'דָא הוּא שֵׁם הַפּוֹעֵל כֵּן.
And in the words of our Sages (Berakhot 5b): "He gave him his hand and raised him up," the initial letters of Yehav Lei Yada
(י-ל-י)
form a Name that performs this healing.
וְכֵן הַרְבֵּה בְּסֵפֶר שִׁמּוּשׁ תְּהִלִּים וּשְׁאָרֵי, כִּי כָּל שֵׁם הוּא כְּמוֹ מַפְתֵּחַ לְאוֹתוֹ חֶדֶר.
And likewise many examples in Sefer Shimush Tehillim and others, for every holy Name is like a key to that specific chamber.
וְהָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁפָּעַל אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר, הוּא שֶׁמָּצָא וְעָמַד עַל אוֹתוֹ מַפְתֵּחַ וּמְסָרוֹ לָרַבִּים שֶׁנָּהַג בּוֹ טוֹבַת עַיִן,
And the first master who achieved that miracle was the one who discovered that key and transmitted it to the public with a generous eye,
וְהֵם גְּנִיזִין בַּתּוֹרָה וּבִלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים, שֶׁכָּל חֶמְדִּין טָבִין גְּנִיזִין שָׁם.
and they are concealed within the Torah and the language of the Sages, wherein all precious treasures are hidden.
וְ"אִם רֵיק הוּא – מִכֶּם", לָמָּה? שֶׁאֵין אַתֶּם יְגֵיעִים וְכוּלֵי
And "if it is empty—it is from you" (Yerushalmi Peah 1:1); why? Because you do not exert yourselves
[וְכָל שֵׁמוֹת הָאֲמוּרִים לְעִנְיַן לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּמַעֲשֶׂה הוּא מִצַּד עוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה, אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הָעִיקָּר הָרְמִיזוֹת בּוֹ בַּעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ וְלֵב כַּנּוֹדָע]:
and all Names mentioned regarding physical actions belong to the World of Action, but in truth the essential allusions pertain to interior service in the mind and heart, as is known.

paragraphs.text: Sha'ar Maamarei Razal, Berakhot 5b: “I have already informed you, concerning “The ox knows its owner,” that by the name Y-L-Y, the second name of the seventy-twofold name, Moshe our teacher raised Yosef’s coffin; its reason was explained there. This name also has the property of raising a sick person from his illness. It is therefore alluded to in the initial letters of “He gave him his hand,” whose initials are Y-L-Y, and thereby “he raised him.” Therefore he should say to the sick person, “Give me your hand.” The sick person then gives his hand, and the person raising him says, “He gave him his hand and raised him,” intending the name indicated by these initial letters.”

paragraphs.text: Sha’arei Orah, Introduction 8–10: Rabbi Yosef Gikatilla compares the divine names to keys for the different matters a person needs. Their use depends on learning their meaning through Torah, recognizing God’s greatness, revering Him, and seeking attachment to Him. He emphasizes knowing the divine name, rather than merely pronouncing it, as the basis of answered prayer. This gives context to Rav Tzadok’s closing emphasis on service of the mind and heart.

paragraphs.text: Nedarim 38a:4-6: “Rabbi Yosi son of Rabbi Chanina said: Torah was given only to Moshe and his descendants, as it is said, “Write for yourself” and “Carve for yourself”: just as the discarded stone is yours, so the writing is yours. Moshe acted generously with it and gave it to Israel. Of him Scripture says, “One with a generous eye shall be blessed.” Rav Chisda objected: “Hashem commanded me at that time to teach you”! He commanded me, and I taught you. “See, I have taught you statutes and laws as Hashem my God commanded me”! He commanded me, and I taught you. “Now write this song for yourselves”! That concerns the song alone. But it says, “So that this song may be a witness for Me among the children of Israel”! Rather, the statement concerns analytical reasoning alone.”

p: [קכ] מִי שֶׁמְּזַכֶּה לְחַיָּיבַיָּא, אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יִדְבַּק בּוֹ מְאוּמָה.
One who brings merit to the guilty cannot avoid having some slight trace cling to him.
וְכִידוּעַ הַמָּשָׁל עַל זֶה מִמִּי שֶׁגּוֹרֵף בִּיבִין
And known is the parable of one who cleans out sewers
[וּבָזֶה יוּבַן צַחוּת לְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וָאֵרָא): נוֹחַ הָיָה לִשְׁלֹמֹה לִהְיוֹת גּוֹרֵף בִּיבִין וְכוּלֵי, [עַיֵּין שָׁם בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
and through this one understands the phrasing in Shemot Rabbah (beginning of Va'era): "Better had it been for Solomon to clean sewers, etc.,"
אֲבָל בַּגְּמָרָא דְּשַׁבָּת נ"ו עַמּוּד ב' אִיתָא שַׁמָּשׁ לְדָבָר אַחֵר, וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],
though in Shabbat 56b it reads: an attendant to swine, which is all one,
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא לֹא רָצָה לְהוֹכִיחָן וְלִהְיוֹת גּוֹרֵף בִּיבִין שֶׁלֹּא יִדְבַּק בּוֹ מְאוּמָה,
meaning that Solomon did not wish to rebuke them and clean out sewers lest anything cling to him;
וּבֶאֱמֶת כָּל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדוֹ לִמְחוֹת וְכוּלֵי, וְנִדְבַּק בּוֹ הַכֹּל].
but in truth, whoever has the power to protest and does not, bears the guilt, and all clung to him.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא לִרְאִיַּת קֶרִי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת (קכז:) בְּאוֹתוֹ חָסִיד מִפְּנֵי טֹרַח הַדֶּרֶךְ לִפְדּוֹת אוֹתָהּ רִיבָה,
And through this he came to experience a nocturnal emission, as written in Shabbat 127b regarding that pious man who toiled on the road to redeem that captive maiden,
דְּאִיתָא בְּאָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן (פֶּרֶק ח) שֶׁהִטְבִּיל לָרִיבָה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָכְלָה אִיסּוּרִים, וְהָיָה מְזַכֶּה לְחַיָּיבַיָּא;
for it is stated in Avot DeRabbi Natan (chapter 8) that he immersed the maiden because she had eaten forbidden foods, thus bringing merit to the guilty;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אֱלִישָׁע, שֶׁאָמְרוּ עָלָיו סַנְהֶדְרִין (קז:) שֶׁהָיָה מַדְחֶה בִּשְׁתֵּי יָדַיִם, נֶאֱמַר עָלָיו בִּבְרָכוֹת (י:) שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה קֶרִי מִיָּמָיו.
unlike Elisha, concerning whom they said in Sanhedrin 107b that he pushed away Gehazi with both hands, regarding whom it is stated in Berakhot 10b that he never saw a seminal emission in his days.
וְאָמְרוּ שָׁם בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין דְּאֵין לִהְיוֹת כֶּאֱלִישָׁע, רַק הַקֵּירוּב יוֹתֵר בְּחֹזֶק מִן הַדִּחוּי, שֶׁהוּא בַּיָּמִין.
And they said there in Sanhedrin that one should not act like Elisha, but drawing near must be stronger than pushing away, operating with the right hand.
וְאָמְרוּ תֵּיכֶף אַחַר כָּךְ שָׁם דְּגַם הַיֵּצֶר כֵּן יִהְיֶה: שְׂמֹאל דּוֹחָה וְיָמִין מְקָרֶבֶת,
And immediately afterward they said there that with the inclination it should be likewise: the left pushes away and the right draws close,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בֶּאֱלִישָׁע הָיָה גַּם יָמִין דּוֹחָה.
whereas with Elisha the right pushed away as well.
וְאַף שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ט): "טוֹב מְאֹד" – זֶה יֵצֶר הָרָע,
And even though they said in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 9): "'Very good'—this is the evil inclination,"
יָדוּעַ דְּהַכֹּל לְפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא אָדָם, וְיֵשׁ מִדָּתוֹ לְאַכְפַּיָּא וְלִהְיוֹת דּוֹחֶה לְגַמְרֵי, וְיֵשׁ מִדָּתוֹ לְאַהְפָּכָא:

it is known that all depends on each person's unique spiritual path: there is one whose task is to suppress (le-akpaya) and reject completely, and there is one whose task is to transform (le-ahpakha).

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 57:1: “As long as the community of Israel is whole—that is, their intention in joining with the nations is solely for the sake of Heaven, to bring out the holy sparks within them, so that the thighs remain joined to the body—then although “the wicked watches for the righteous,” “Hashem will not abandon him into his hand.” Yet it is indeed said, “Because you joined with Achazyahu…” Although his intention at the outset was for the sake of Heaven, one who deals with something filthy becomes soiled, like someone who cleans sewers, whose body cannot avoid becoming dirty with mud and excrement. This requires great vigilance and strength, so as not to allow any filth to adhere to him, and not everyone merits it.”

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 6:1: “Of Shlomo, who contemplated nullifying a letter of Torah, what is written? “The words of Agur son of Yakeh”: he gathered words of Torah and then cast them up. “The utterance of the man to Itiel”: this command of the Holy One, blessed be He, “He shall not multiply wives,” was given only because “his heart shall not turn away.” “To Itiel”: he said, “God is with me, and I am able.” What is written of him? “When Shlomo grew old, his wives turned his heart.” Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said: It would have been better for Shlomo to clean sewers than to have this verse written about him. Therefore Shlomo said of himself, “I turned to consider wisdom and knowledge, madness and folly.” Shlomo said: What I thought was being wiser than the words of Torah, imagining that I understood Torah’s reasoning—that understanding and that knowledge were madness and folly.”

paragraphs.text: Avot DeRabbi Natan 8:8 recounts two pious men’s efforts to ransom a captive girl; one was imprisoned during the effort and later released with her. After she spent the night beside him fully clothed, he requested ritual baths for himself and for her. His companions attributed his immersion to an involuntary emission after the hardship of imprisonment, and hers to purification after eating and drinking among her captors. He confirmed their favorable judgment. These details explain Rav Tzadok’s reference to helping the captive and to her immersion; the subsequent stories about the righteous men’s animals concern a different point.

These details explain Rav Tzadok’s reference to helping the captive and to her immersion; the subsequent stories about the righteous men’s animals concern a different point.

p: [קכא] בְּכָל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ לֹא נִזְכַּר בְּפֵירוּשׁ עָוֹן דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה, רַק נִזְכַּר שֶׁנֶּעֶנְשׁוּ דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל וְעֵר וְאוֹנָן

Throughout the entire Torah the sin of emitting seed in vain is not explicitly stated as a direct commandment, but it is merely recorded that the Generation of the Flood, and Er and Onan, were punished for it
(וְיָדוּעַ דְּעֵר הוּא נִיצוֹץ מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁיָּרַד פַּעַם רִאשׁוֹן לָעוֹלָם וּבָא לְתַקֵּן עָוֹן דְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל, עַיֵּין מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת ק"ט וְקי"א),
(and it is known that Er was a spark of the Messiah who descended for the first time into the world to rectify the sin of the Generation of the Flood; see what I wrote above in Sections 109 and 111),

כִּי לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לִכְתּוֹב הָאִיסּוּר בְּפֵירוּשׁ, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִסַּד בְּטֶבַע הָעוֹלָם שֶׁיֶּאֱרַע זֶה גַּם כֵּן לָאָדָם בְּאֹנֶס, וְיִהְיֶה צְעָקָה גְּדוֹלָה: עַל מֶה עָשָׂה ה' כָּכָה לָנוּ לְהַכְשִׁילֵנוּ.

for it was impossible to write the prohibition explicitly, seeing that the Blessed Name established in the nature of the world that this also occurs to a person involuntarily, which would have prompted an outcry: "Why has Hashem done this to us to cause us to stumble?"
רַק הִנִּיחָה תּוֹרָה דָּבָר זֶה לִלְמוֹד דָּבָר זֶה מִמִּצְוֹת בְּנֵי נֹחַ דְּ"וְדָבַק בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ", כְּמוֹ דְּמִיעֲטֵיהּ אֵשֶׁת חֲבֵירוֹ, הָכָא נַמֵּי כָּל שֶׁלֹּא בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ.

Rather, the Torah left this to be derived from the Noahide commandment "and he shall cleave unto his wife" (Genesis 2:24): just as this excludes the wife of his fellow, so too it excludes any discharge not within his wife.

וְכָל מִצְווֹת בְּנֵי נֹחַ הוּא מִכְּלַל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ שֶׁקָּדְמוּ לַתּוֹרָה, וְכֵן דָּבָר זֶה גַּם כֵּן מִדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, דְּיֵשׁ לֵידַע מֵעַצְמוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן, וְכָל הַבַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים אֵין עוֹשִׂים כֵּן וְאֵין לָצֵאת מִיִּשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם

And all Noahide laws are part of natural decency (derekh eretz) that preceded the Torah, and likewise this matter is part of derekh eretz, for one should understand intuitively that it violates decency to act thus, as no animals act thus, and one should not depart from the civilized order
[וּבָזֶה יוּבַן מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק מִי שֶׁמֵּתוּ (בְּרָכוֹת כב.) דְּבַעַל קֶרִי שׁוֹנֶה בְּהִלְכוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ].
and through this one understands Berakhot 22a, that one who experienced an emission may study the laws of derekh eretz, and this is not the place to elaborate.
וְהִנֵּה דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ קָדְמָה לַתּוֹרָה, וּבְתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק א נִקְרָא דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ "דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים" עַיֵּין שָׁם
And behold, derekh eretz preceded the Torah, and in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 1) derekh eretz is called "the way to the Tree of Life," see there
[וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא "פְּרִי צַדִּיק" דַּיְיקָא "עֵץ חַיִּים"],
and therefore the fruit of the righteous specifically is titled a 'tree of life',
וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ אֶל הַתּוֹרָה:
and one who lacks derekh eretz cannot attain the Torah.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 10:12 explains Er’s birth as the first appearance of Mashiach’s light in the world, attributing the underlying teaching to the Ari. Though Er died and Mashiach’s eventual lineage did not descend from Bat Shua, that first disclosure had already occurred. Rav Tzadok connects the evil that overcame Er with the generation of the Flood, which could have received Torah had it merited to do so. This is Rav Tzadok’s exposition of the Ari’s teaching; the note does not independently identify the original passage in the Ari’s writings.

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, Simchat Torah 39:2, reads the encounter between Rabbi Yannai and his unlearned guest as a demand to recognize the Torah point within every Jewish soul. The guest’s decent conduct expressed an inheritance he could not yet articulate through learning; Rabbi Yannai should have discerned that inward source and regretted insulting him. On this reading, derekh eretz prepares a person for Torah while already expressing a connection to it. This complements Rav Tzadok’s description of the path to the tree of life.
