sections.en: Repentance and the Reach of Atonement

p: [קכב] קַיְימָא לַן בְּשַׁבָּת (עא.) שֶׁהַחַטָּאת הַבָּא לְכַפֵּר הַחֵטְא גּוֹרֵר אוֹתוֹ חֵטְא גַּם פַּעַם אַחֵר שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם.
We establish in Shabbat 71a that a sin-offering brought to atone for a sin drags along and atones for that same sin performed another time, see there.
וְנִלְמַד גַּם כֵּן מִזֶּה בִּתְשׁוּבָה, שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְכַפָּרָה נִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ גַּם פְּעָמִים אֲחֵרִים שֶׁעָשָׂה דָּבָר זֶה, כִּי חֵטְא גּוֹרֵר חֵטְא.
And we likewise learn from this regarding repentance: when one merits atonement, other instances in which he committed that same act are also forgiven, for one sin drags along another.
וְשָׁם אִיתָא בְּלֹא יוֹדֵעַ דְּחַיָּיב אָשָׁם תָּלוּי, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְכַּפֵּר בְּחַטָּאת עַל זֶה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן (פֶּרֶק ל),

And there it is stated that if he does not know, he is liable for a provisional guilt-offering (asham talui), meaning he cannot attain atonement through a sin-offering, as in Avot DeRabbi Natan (chapter 30);

וְנִזְכַּר הָעִנְיָן גַּם כֵּן בְּתַלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת, כִּי הֶחְמִירָה תּוֹרָה בְּסָפֵק דְּאָשָׁם תָּלוּי חָמִיר מֵחַטָּאת, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתַלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה הַטַּעַם: כִּי הַיְּדִיעָה שֶׁנּוֹדַע לוֹ מְכַפֶּרֶת מִקְצָת מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא מִתְחָרֵט, עַיֵּין שָׁם.

and this concept is also cited by Talmidei Rabbeinu Yonah in the first chapter of Berakhot, for the Torah was more stringent regarding doubt—an asham talui being more demanding than a chatat—the reason being that the definite knowledge of the sin provides partial atonement because through it he experiences genuine remorse, see there.
וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכֵי בִּגְרִירָה נִתְכַּפְּרָה, וְהוּא הַדִּין לְכָל כַּפָּרַת חֲטָאִים בִּתְשׁוּבָה.
And even so, through the principle of dragging (grirah) it is atoned, and the same applies to all atonement of sins through repentance.

וּלְכָךְ הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, ריט עַמּוּד ב), אִם שָׁב עַל עֲוֹן קֶרִי וּמִתְכַּפֵּר וּמוֹצִיא אוֹתָן טִפִּין הָעֲשׁוּקִים, מִמֵּילָא בִּגְרִירָה מוֹצִיא גַּם כֵּן טִפֵּי דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה בְּהָקִיץ.

Therefore, regarding emitting seed in vain where ordinary repentance does not avail (Zohar I:219b): if one repents over an involuntary emission and is forgiven, extracting those oppressed captive sparks, automatically by dragging he likewise redeems the drops emitted willfully while awake.
וְעַל כָּךְ גַּם כֵּן יִסַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עִנְיַן הַקֶּרִי בַּטֶּבַע, כִּי הוּא "חֹשֵׁב מַחֲשָׁבוֹת לְבִלְתִּי יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח" (שְׁמוּאֵל ב יד, יד), וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יְתוּקַּן;

And for this reason too the Blessed Name established the phenomenon of nocturnal emission in nature, for "He devises means that the banished not be cast out from Him" (II Samuel 14:14), and through this it is rectified;
וּמִי שֶׁחָטָא בְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה, הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ גַּם כֵּן מִקְרִים כְּדֵי לָשׁוּב עֲלֵיהֶם
and for one who sinned through wasting seed, the Blessed Name orchestrates nocturnal occurrences so that he may repent over them

[וְזֶה סוֹד גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (יוֹמָא פו:): עָבַר וְשָׁנָה הֻתְּרָה לוֹ, סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ? אֶלָּא וְכוּלֵי. וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁשָּׁב עַל הַהֶיתֵּרִים דְּאַחַר כָּךְ, מִמֵּילָא נִתְכַּפְּרוּ הָרִאשׁוֹנִים, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ],

and this is also the secret of Yoma 86b: 'If one transgressed and repeated it, it became permitted to him—could you think so? Rather, it seems to him as permitted'; and through repenting over those later instances that appeared permitted, the earlier willful ones are automatically forgiven, and this is not the place to lengthen.
וְאַף מִי שֶׁלֹּא חָטָא בְּזָדוֹן בְּהָקִיץ, הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַזְמִין לוֹ בְּאֹנֶס גָּמוּר לְתַקֵּן אוֹתוֹ הַבָּא עַל יְדֵי הִרְהוּר בַּיּוֹם,
And even for one who never sinned willfully while awake, the Holy One brings upon him an entirely involuntary occurrence in order to rectify any stray unchaste thought by day,
וְכֵן לְתַקֵּן אֲחֵרִים הַחוֹטְאִים, דִּיחִיד שֶׁשָּׁב מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ וּלְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם):
and likewise to rectify other sinners, for when a single individual repents, forgiveness is granted to him and to the entire world (Yoma 86b).

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 21:1, describes the scapegoat as a communal asham talui: protection while a matter remains unknown, pending fuller clarification and atonement. Its remaining alive until the service of the other goat was completed expresses the continuing possibility of drawing actions into divine service and transforming sins into merits. Only what could no longer be clarified in that way was sent away. This is a parallel account of repair under uncertainty, distinct from Rav Tzadok’s particular inference that one act of atonement can draw another with it.

sections.en: Toiling in Torah as a Path to Atonement

p: [קכג] וְעַל יְדֵי לִמּוּד תּוֹרָה בִּיגִיעָה נִתְקָן עָוֹן דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה,
And through the study of Torah with diligent, exhausting toil, the sin of emitting seed in vain is rectified,
כִּי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּנִדָּה (יג.) דְּחַיָּיב מִיתָה;
for our Sages of blessed memory stated in Niddah 13a that one who does so is liable to the death penalty;
וּבְוַדַּאי כָּל דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים לְרַחֵם עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת וּלְהַמְשִׁיךְ טוֹבָה וְחַיִּים לָעוֹלָם.
and certainly all words of the Sages are intended to arouse mercy upon created beings and to draw down goodness and life unto the world.
וְכַוָּנָתָם בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁאָמְרוּ חִיּוּב עוֹנֶשׁ עַל הָאָדָם, הַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּעוֹנֶשׁ זֶה מִתְכַּפֵּר,
And their underlying intent in any place where they articulated a liability of punishment upon a person is that through this very punishment he attains atonement,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (מז:) בְּחַיָּיבֵי מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין דְּמִיתָתָם כַּפָּרָתָם;
as written in Sanhedrin 47b regarding those liable to court-imposed capital execution, that their death constitutes their atonement;
כִּי רָאוּ שֶׁקָּשֶׁה לִמְצוֹא כַּפָּרָה [וּכְמוֹ בְּעָוֹן זֶה רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן],
for the Sages recognized that it was exceedingly difficult to find atonement as with this sin, may the Merciful One preserve us,
וּמָצְאוּ לוֹ מִקְרָא מִן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁמְּחַיֵּיב עוֹנֶשׁ כָּךְ,
and they discovered for it a scriptural verse from the Torah mandating such a penalty,
וּמִמֵּילָא עַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁבְּעוֹנֶשׁ זֶה מִתְכַּפֵּר, כִּי אִם לֹא כֵן לָמָּה יֵעָנֵשׁ,
and consequently perforce through this punishment he is atoned, for were it not so, why should he be punished?
כַּנּוֹדָע שֶׁהָעוֹנֶשׁ הוּא כְּדֵי לְהִתְכַּפֵּר.
seeing that retribution exists entirely in order to achieve spiritual purification and atonement.

וּלְכָךְ פְּעָמִים נִגְזַר עַל הָאָדָם בִּשְׁבִיל הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ בָּנִים וְכַיּוֹצֵא, שֶׁהוּא מֵאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים שֶׁנִּקְרָא מִיתָה בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ה.).

And therefore it is sometimes decreed upon a person on account of wasted seed that he have no children, or the like, which is one of the four conditions termed "death" in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (5a).

וְעַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁמֵּמִית עַצְמוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן מִיתָה כִּדְרָשַׁת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת סג:) עַל פָּסוּק "אָדָם כִּי יָמוּת בְּאֹהֶל",

And through words of Torah, wherein a person slays himself over words of Torah—which is likewise termed death, as our Sages expounded (Berakhot 63b) on the verse "when a man dies in a tent" (Numbers 19:14)—
וְאָז נִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ בָּזֶה גַּם כֵּן דּוּגְמַת מִיתָה
he is thereby atoned through this form of spiritual death
[וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (תָּמִיד לב.): מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה אָדָם וְיִחְיֶה? יָמִית עַצְמוֹ].
and therefore they stated in Tamid 32a: "What shall a man do to live? Let him slay himself".
וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִקְרָא "עֵץ הַחַיִּים" כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (רֵישׁ סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה),
And words of Torah are designated as the "Tree of Life," as our Sages stated (beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah),
וּמִיתָה נִקְרָא "דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אָנֹכִי הֹלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ כָּל הָאָרֶץ" (מְלָכִים א ב, ב);
and physical death is termed the "way of the earth" (derekh eretz), as written: "I go the way of all the earth" (I Kings 2:2);
וּלְכָךְ מִיתָה הוּא דֶּרֶךְ לְהַגִּיעַ לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם, שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ הוּא דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת קכ"א.
and therefore death serves as the path to attain eternal life, for derekh eretz is the path leading unto the Tree of Life, as I wrote above in Section 121.
וְכֵן מִי שֶׁמֵּמִית עַצְמוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, זֶהוּ הַדֶּרֶךְ לְעֵץ הַחַיִּים דְּהַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וּמְתַקֵּן בָּזֶה מַה שֶּׁפָּגַם בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
And likewise, one who slays himself over words of Torah follows the path to the Tree of Life—namely Torah—and rectifies through this that which he blemished in the realm of derekh eretz
[וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ב): טוֹב תּוֹרָה עִם דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
and our Sages stated (Avot 2:2): "Excellent is Torah study combined with derekh eretz,"
וּבִבְרָכוֹת (לה:): הַנְהֵג בָּהֶן מִנְהַג דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ וְכוּלֵי, וְאִם לָאו אֵין מִתְקַיֵּים;
and in Berakhot 35b: "Conduct yourself with them in the manner of derekh eretz, etc., for if not, it will not endure";
אַךְ הָעֵצָה עַל זֶה: לְהָמִית עַצְמוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
yet the sublime counsel for this is to slay oneself over words of Torah.
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא נָהַג בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ בִּפְרִישׁוּת מִן הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁגַּם כֵּן נִקְרָא דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, did not conduct himself according to standard derekh eretz regarding marital intimacy, which is likewise termed derekh eretz,
וּלְכָךְ דִּבְּרוּ עָלָיו לָשׁוֹן הָרָע עַל זֶה שֶׁחֲשָׁבוּהוּ לִמְבַטֵּל מִצְוָה, כֵּיוָן דְּאִשְׁתּוֹ לֹא מָחֲלָה;
and therefore Aaron and Miriam spoke against him on this account, considering him to have neglected a mitzvah since his wife had not explicitly waived her marital rights;
וּבְוַדַּאי כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה, יֵשׁ מַמָּשׁ בְּדִבּוּרָם גַּם כֵּן.
and certainly, since it was recorded in the Torah, their words contained some substance as well.
אֶלָּא שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם נֶעֶנְשׁוּ וְנֶאֱמַר: "אֲשֶׁר נוֹאַלְנוּ וַאֲשֶׁר חָטָאנוּ", דְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הִסְכִּים עַל יָדוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שַׁבָּת פז.),

However, they were nonetheless punished, Aaron declaring: "wherein we have done foolishly, and wherein we have sinned" (Numbers 12:11), because the Holy One, blessed be He, retroactively consented with Moses's choice (Shabbat 87a),
וְהוּא כְּעֵין עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ דְּהִיא גְּדוֹלָה גַּם כֵּן.
and it functioned like a transgression performed purely for Heaven's sake (aveirah lishmah), which is likewise immensely great.
וְחָשֵׁיב שָׁם שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים, וְדִמָּה זֶה לִשְׁבִירַת לוּחוֹת דְּהוּא גַּם כֵּן עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ.
And the Talmud enumerates there three things Moses did on his own initiative, comparing his marital separation to the breaking of the Tablets, which was likewise an aveirah lishmah.
וְלִפְעָמִים עַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל גַּם כֵּן לְתַקֵּן, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "רְאֵה חַיִּים עִם אִשָּׁה", וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ]:
And sometimes through this one can likewise rectify, as written: "Enjoy life with the wife whom you love" (Ecclesiastes 9:9), and this is not the place to elaborate.

paragraphs.text: Rashi on Makkot 14b:16:1 explains that a positive command prescribed as the remedy for a prior violation can take the place of lashes. He describes that command as both its penalty and its repair. His qualification is essential: a positive command that can be fulfilled before the violation does not become such a remedy merely because it is performed afterward. Rav Tzadok’s broader account of punishment as purification is illustrated here by a particular legal category, not by a rule that any later good deed cancels a penalty.

This supplies the positive mechanism of the siman’s image: the exertion of study becomes the path to renewed life and purity.

sections.en: Procreation and the Rectification of the Covenant

p: [קכד] אִיסּוּר דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה הוּא בִּכְלַל מִצְוָה דִּפְרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה,
The prohibition against emitting seed in vain is subsumed within the positive commandment of procreation (peru u'revu),
כַּנִּרְאֶה מִדִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹסָפוֹת סַנְהֶדְרִין (נט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּחִדּוּשַׁי;
as is evident from the words of Tosafot in Sanhedrin 59b and as I wrote in my novellae;
וְלָכֵן עַל יְדֵי מִצְוַת פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה בְּכַוָּנָה הָרְאוּיָה לְשֵׁם ה', יוּכַל גַּם כֵּן לְתַקֵּן מַה שֶּׁחָטָא בְּאִיסּוּר זֶה וְלִקְלוֹט אוֹתָן טִפִּין לִקְדוּשָׁה,

and therefore through the mitzvah of procreation fulfilled with holy intention for the sake of Hashem, one can likewise rectify that wherein he sinned regarding this prohibition, drawing those captive drops back into holiness,
כִּי כָּל לָאו הַבָּא מִכְּלַל עֲשֵׂה – הָעֲשֵׂה הוּא תִּיקּוּן הַלָּאו.
for in every negative prohibition derived implicitly from a positive commandment, the positive performance serves as the rectification of the prohibition.
וְגַם בְּלָאו הָכִי אָמְרוּ בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה כא): כִּי בָּאֵבֶר שֶׁעָשָׂה בּוֹ חֲבִילוֹת עֲבֵירוֹת – יַעֲשֶׂה בּוֹ חֲבִילוֹת שֶׁל מִצְווֹת, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
And even without this, they stated in Vayikra Rabbah (21:5): with the very limb wherewith one performed bundles of transgressions, let him perform bundles of mitzvot, see there;
וְכֵן כָּאן, בְּאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר חֲבִילוֹת מִצְווֹת הַיְינוּ פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה וּמִצְוַת עוֹנָה
and so here, with that same physical organ the "bundles of mitzvot" are procreation and marital intimacy
[וּמִיהוּ יֵשׁ לוֹמַר נַמֵּי "יָשַׁב וְלֹא עָבַר עֲבֵירָה" כִּדְרַב חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפָּא שֶׁנִּזְדַּמְּנָה לְיָדוֹ, מִקְרֵי גַּם כֵּן מִצְוָה כִּדְאִיתָא בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (לט:)].

though one may also say that passive restraint—"he sat and did not commit a sin" when an opportunity presented itself, like Rav Chanina bar Pappa—is likewise credited as a mitzvah, as brought in Kiddushin 39b.
וְאֵין רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר חֲבִילוֹת בְּרִבּוּי בְּמַעֲשֶׂה,
And "bundles" does not mean excessive physical frequency,
דְּעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (כב.): שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מְצוּיִין וְכוּלֵי, וְאָמְרוּ בְּאָבוֹת: "אַל תַּרְבֶּה שִׂיחָה" כַּנּוֹדָע;

for regarding this they taught in Berakhot 22a: so that Torah scholars should not be constantly engaged in marital intimacy like roosters, and in Avot: "Do not converse excessively with a woman," as is known;
רַק אֵין רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר בְּכַמּוּת אֶלָּא בְּאֵיכוּת, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּקְדוּשָׁה וּבְטָהֳרָה,
rather "bundles" refers not to quantity but to spiritual quality: that it be conducted in profound holiness and purity,
דִּבְלָאו הָכִי מִקְרֵי בְּעִילַת זְנוּת וּכִבְהֵמוֹת כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים.
for otherwise it is considered an act of licentiousness and animalistic behavior, as stated repeatedly in the Zohar.
רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בִּקְדוּשָׁה כְּפִי אֶפְשָׁרוּת הָאָדָם
Only when it is carried out in holiness according to human capacity

[דְּאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא בִּטְרוּנְיָא, וַהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "בֶּעָווֹן מָלֵא" – דַּאֲפִילּוּ חָסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים וְכוּלֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ)],

for the Holy One does not act tyrannically, and our Sages noted: "in total iniquity"—meaning even the most pious of the pious cannot entirely avoid some subtle base element (Midrash Rabbah, Tazria 14:5),
אָז "ה' צִלְּךָ", גַּם כֵּן דּוּגְמָתוֹ שׁוֹפֵעַ לָאָרֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה
then "Hashem is your shadow" (Psalms 121:5): a corresponding holy influx is poured out unto the Supernal Earth (Malchut),
אֲשֶׁר הָיְתָה חֲרֵיבָה וִיבֵשָׁה עַל יְדֵי חֲטָאָיו כַּנּוֹדָע כִּדְאִיתָא בַּתִּיקּוּנִים, וְנִתְקַן הַכֹּל.
which had been made barren and parched through his past sins, as brought in the Tikkunim, and everything is healed.
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁיּוֹרְדִים טִפֵּי גְּשָׁמִים מִלְּמַעְלָה עַל הָאָרֶץ, הִיא נוֹתֶנֶת יְבוּלָהּ,
And through the descent of supernal rain-drops from Above upon the Earth, she yields her produce,
שֶׁהִיא רוּחַ קְדוּשָׁה בְּלֵב הָאָדָם תַּחַת רוּחַ הַטֻּמְאָה שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ מִקּוֹדֶם,
which is a spirit of holiness within the human heart replacing the spirit of impurity that resided there previously,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּאוֹתוֹ מִזְמוֹר: "וְרוּחַ קָדְשְׁךָ אַל תִּקַּח מִמֶּנִּי, הָשִׁיבָה לִּי וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים נא, יג–יד):
as King David, peace be upon him, pleaded in that psalm: "and take not Your holy spirit from me; restore unto me the joy of Your salvation, etc." (Psalms 51:13–14).

sections.en: Charity and the Redemption of Captive Souls

p: [קכה] צְדָקָה לַעֲנִיִּים גַּם כֵּן מוֹעִיל לְתַקֵּן עָוֹן הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה,
Giving charity to the poor is likewise effective to rectify the sin of wasted seed,

וּבִכְלָל לְכָל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה חַיָּיב מִיתָה מוֹעִיל צְדָקָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב דְּ"תַּצִּיל מִמָּוֶת" (מִשְׁלֵי י, ב), וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא (יא.).
and generally for anything regarding which our Sages said one is liable to death, charity avails, as written: "and righteousness delivers from death" (Proverbs 10:2; Bava Batra 11a).

וּלְעָוֹן זֶה בְּיִחוּד, דְּעַל יְדֵי שֶׁמְּחַיֶּה נְפָשׁוֹת, וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שָׁם: כָּל הַמְּקַיֵּים נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל כְּאִלּוּ קִיֵּים עוֹלָם מָלֵא, וּבִכְלַל הָעוֹלָם גַּם כֵּן אוֹתָם נְפָשׁוֹת עֲשׁוּקוֹת – מְחַיִּים מַמָּשׁ.

And for this sin in particular: because through sustaining living souls—our Sages stating there that whoever preserves a single Jewish soul is as though he preserved an entire world—he literally sustains from death the entire universe, including those captive, oppressed souls.
וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְעָנִי הָגוּן, דִּבְלָאו הָכִי אֵין מוֹעִיל,
Provided that the charity is given to a worthy, upright poor person, for otherwise it does not avail,
דְּהוּא קְצָת מֵעֵין דּוּגְמָא דְּחֶטְאוֹ שֶׁמַּשְׁפִּיעַ חַיִּים לְמִי שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי,
as giving to an unworthy recipient somewhat mirrors the nature of his original sin, channeling life unto that which is undeserving;

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיִרְמְיָה שֶׁקִּלֵּל לְאַנְשֵׁי עֲנָתוֹת: "וְיִהְיוּ מֻכְשָׁלִים לְפָנֶיךָ, בְּעֵת אַפְּךָ עֲשֵׂה בָהֶם" (יִרְמְיָה יח, כג) – הַכְשִׁילֵם בִּבְנֵי אָדָם שֶׁאֵינָם מְהֻגָּנִים, כִּדְאִיתָא סוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּבָבָא קַמָּא (טז:).

and as written concerning Jeremiah who cursed the men of Anathoth: "and let them be overthrown before You; deal with them in the time of Your anger" (Jeremiah 18:23)—cause them to stumble through unworthy recipients, as brought in Bava Kamma 16b.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי הֵם הֶחֱטִיאוּ לְיִרְמְיָה בְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה כַּנּוֹדָע, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּאֶבֶן הָעֵזֶר סִימָן א בְּחֶלְקַת מְחוֹקֵק סָעִיף קָטָן ו)
That is, because they forced Jeremiah into a situation resulting in wasted seed, as noted in Even HaEzer 1:6 in Chelkat Mechokek
[וְאוּלַי זֶה גַּם כֵּן בִּכְלַל "כִּי כָרוּ שׁוּחָה וְגוֹמֵר", עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּבָבָא קַמָּא.
and perhaps this is likewise allured to in "for they have digged a pit to take me," see Bava Kamma there.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָשַׁב מַחֲשָׁבוֹת לְבִלְתִּי יִהְיֶה לְבַטָּלָה, וְנוֹלַד מִזֶּה בֶּן סִירָא כִּדְאִיתָא שָׁם,
However, the Blessed Name devised means that it not be in vain, and from that conception was born Ben Sira, as brought there;
וּלְכָךְ בֶּן סִירָא הָיָה כָּלוּל טוֹב וָרָע כִּדְאִיתָא בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין ק:) דְּהוּא מִסְּפָרִים חִיצוֹנִים, וּמִילְּתָא מַעֲלָיוּתָא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ דָּרְשִׁינַן עַיֵּין שָׁם,
and therefore Ben Sira embodied an intermingling of good and evil, being enumerated in Sanhedrin 100b among external apocryphal books, yet whose sublime teachings we cite and expound, see there,
וְכֵן בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (צב:) קְרָאוּהוּ "כְּתוּבִים",
and in Bava Kamma 92b they even referred to his proverbs as "Scriptures,"
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הָיְתָה נֶפֶשׁ יְקָרָה, רַק דְּיָצְאָה לַחִיצוֹנִים וּמִשָּׁם נִלְקְחָה, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],
for in truth his soul was immensely precious, only that it emerged through the external realm and was rescued from there, and this is not the place to elaborate,
וְקִלְּלָם שֶׁיִּכָּשְׁלוּ מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה, דְּלֹא רָצָה לְקַלְּלָם שֶׁיִּכָּשְׁלוּ בְּחֶטְאוֹ, דְּזֶה גּוֹרֵם רָעָה לַכֹּל כַּנּוֹדָע בַּזֹּהַר, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בָּזֶה.

and Jeremiah cursed them that they stumble measure for measure, refusing to curse them to stumble in actual wasted seed, which inflicts universal spiritual damage throughout creation as known in the Zohar, unlike stumbling in unworthy charity.

רַק מִי שֶׁשָּׁב כָּרָאוּי וּמְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם שֶׁיְּתוּקַּן חֶטְאוֹ מִכֹּל וָכֹל, אָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ כָּרָאוּי:
only one who repents properly and pleads for Heavenly mercy that his sin be utterly rectified, does the Blessed Name providential arrange for him truly worthy recipients.

paragraphs.text: Moed LeKol Chai 28, rectification 43, quoting Maaseh HaTzedakah 121a, describes giving charity privately to those who labor in Torah: forty small coins for a wealthy giver, and at least four for a poor giver. The giver travels through the city’s four directions, beginning in the southeast, as physical capacity allows, intending to gather dispersed sparks into holiness. The four directions recall Israel’s exiles; the concealed giving is compared to a mikveh of forty seah. The source presents this practice as a rectification of the covenant’s blemish for that week without additional fasts. Its amounts depend on means, and its exertion on capacity.

paragraphs.text: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Chayei Sarah 5:2, observes that charity gives another person strength whose eventual use remains hidden: it may serve God’s will or be used wrongly. Since the giver cannot fully clarify the outcome, he should pray to encounter a worthy recipient and complete the mitzvah properly. This parallels the siman’s appeal to divine help in directing charity, while retaining the obligation to act despite uncertainty.

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 11a:2: “It was taught: They said of Binyamin the Righteous that he was in charge of a charity fund. Once, during years of drought, a woman came before him and said to him: ‘Rabbi, provide for me!’ He said to her: ‘By the Temple service, the charity fund has nothing!’ She said to him: ‘Rabbi, if you do not provide for me, a woman and her seven sons will die!’ He arose and provided for her from his own funds. Some time later he became ill and was near death. The ministering angels said before the Holy One, blessed be He: ‘Master of the universe, You said: Whoever sustains a single life from Israel is as though he had sustained an entire world. Should Binyamin the Righteous, who kept a woman and her seven sons alive, die after these few years?’ Immediately his sentence was torn up. It was taught: Twenty-two years were added to his life.”

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 10a:16–10b:2 distinguishes charity’s protection from an unusual death from its protection against Gehinnom. It associates the former with giving in which neither donor nor recipient knows the other’s identity. A communal charity fund can accomplish this, provided its administrator is trustworthy, like Rabbi Chananya ben Teradyon. This qualification remains part of the Gemara’s recommendation. The account of Binyamin the righteous in the preceding note supplies a separate example of charity saving life.

sections.en: Restoring the Soul by Bringing Others to Repentance

p: [קכו] מַאן דִּמְזַכֵּי לְחַיָּיבַיָּא מוֹעִיל גַּם כֵּן לְתַקֵּן זֶה,
Whoever brings merit to the guilty is likewise empowered to rectify this sin,

שֶׁהוּא נִקְרָא "לוֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת", וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק "וְאֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ בְחָרָן" (בְּרֵאשִׁית יב, ה) שֶׁהוּא כְּאִלּוּ עֲשָׂאָם, וְנֶפֶשׁ מֵשִׁיב אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ

for he is titled "he that wins souls" (Proverbs 11:30), as our Sages expounded on the verse "and the souls that they had gotten in Haran" (Genesis 12:5), that it is as though he created them, and soul restores soul
[וּמֵעָוֹן דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה, כְּשֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ מִזְּדוֹנוֹת זְכִיּוֹת וְאוֹתָם נְפָשׁוֹת נִלְקָחִים לִקְדוּשָׁה, מוֹסִיף שֶׁפַע גָּדוֹל,
and regarding the sin of wasted seed, when willful sins are converted into merits and those souls are redeemed into holiness, vast divine influx is added,
וְנִמְצָא דְּהָיָה מְזַכֶּה לְחַיָּיבַיָּא בָּזֶה, וְחֶטְאוֹ מַמָּשׁ מֵעֵין דּוּגְמָא דְּתִיקּוּנוֹ,
and it turns out that he brought merit to the guilty through this, his sin mirroring the very pattern of his rectification,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין ע.): בַּדָּבָר שֶׁקִּלְקְלוּ בּוֹ נִתְקָנוּ;
and concerning this they said (Sanhedrin 70a): in the very matter wherein they corrupted are they rectified;
וְעַיֵּין לְעֵיל אוֹת ק"כ דְּעַל זֶה מַגִּיעַ עוֹנֶשׁ זֶה, וּבְוַדַּאי אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְגַלְגֵּל חוֹבָה עַל יְדֵי זַכַּאי רַק זְכוּת,
and see above Section 120 that on this account this penalty arrives, and certainly the Blessed Name brings about liability through the guilty and merit through the meritorious,
רַק הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת כְּעִנְיַן "שְׂכַר מִצְוָה – מִצְוָה", דְּגַם בָּזֶה הוּא מְזַכֶּה לְחַיָּיבַיָּא עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה.
rather it is truly in the manner of "the reward of a mitzvah is a mitzvah," wherein through repentance he brings merit to the guilty.
וּדְכַוָּותֵיהּ עַל יְדֵי מַכְשֵׁלָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה בָּא קֶרִי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת ק"ו, וְעַל יָדוֹ הַתִּיקּוּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת קט"ז].
And parallel to this, through a stumbling in Torah study nocturnal emission occurs as I wrote above in Section 106, and through it comes rectification as I wrote above in Section 116.
וְלָכֵן אָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּאוֹתוֹ מִזְמוֹר: "אֲלַמְּדָה פֹשְׁעִים דְּרָכֶיךָ וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים נא, טו),
And therefore King David, peace be upon him, proclaimed in that psalm: "I will teach transgressors Your ways, etc." (Psalms 51:15),
רַק הִקְדִּים: "הָשִׁיבָה לִּי שְׂשׂוֹן יִשְׁעֶךָ",
only he preceded with: "Restore unto me the joy of Your salvation,"
כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְחַיָּיב לְזַכּוֹת אֶת הַחַיָּיב, וְאָמְרוּ: "יָבוֹא טָהוֹר וִיכַפֵּר עַל הַטָּהוֹר", וְאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת לב.): "מְגַלְגְּלִין זְכוּת עַל יְדֵי זַכַּאי".

for it is impossible for a debtor to absolve another debtor, and they taught: "let the pure come and atone for the pure" (Yoma 43b), and: "merit is brought about through the meritorious" (Shabbat 32a).
רַק צָרִיךְ מִקּוֹדֶם תְּשׁוּבָה וְרַחֲמִים שֶׁיָּשִׁיב לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוּחַ קְדוּשָׁה שֶׁבְּנֶפֶשׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי,
Rather, one first requires repentance and mercy so that the Blessed Name restores to him the holy spirit intrinsic to the Jewish soul,
וְאָז אַחַר כָּךְ, לְתַקֵּן הַקּוֹדֵם וּלְהוֹצִיא נְפָשׁוֹת עֲשׁוּקוֹת, יוּכַל עַל יְדֵי זֶה דַּ"אֲלַמְּדָה וְגוֹמֵר"
and then afterward, to rectify the past and redeem captive souls, he is empowered through "I will teach transgressors Your ways, etc."
[וּפְעָמִים אוֹתָן חַיָּיבַיָּא הֵם אוֹתָם נְפָשׁוֹת עַצְמָן, וּלְכָךְ נִזְדַּמְּנוּ לְיָדוֹ דַּיְיקָא לְתַקְּנָם.
and sometimes those very sinners are those captive souls themselves, which is why they were orchestrated into his hands specifically so that he rectify them.
וְעַיֵּין רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כָּל הַיָּד: הַמְשַׂחֲקִין בַּתִּינוֹקוֹת וּמְקַבְּלֵי גֵּרִים, זֶה בָּא מִזֶּה, כִּי הֵם גַּם כֵּן אוֹתָם נְפָשׁוֹת כַּיָּדוּעַ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ]:

And examine Niddah 13b regarding those who delay the Messiah through playing with children and receiving converts, the one stemming from the other, for they are likewise those very souls as is known, and this is not the place to elaborate.

This further opportunity is a fruit of the first mitzvah in this world; it does not exhaust the enduring reward reserved for the World to Come. Rav Tzadok uses this conception of one mitzvah enabling another to describe the further opportunity to restore souls.

paragraphs.text: Tosafot on Yevamot 109b:3:1, citing Ri, limits the criticism of accepting converts to persuading people to convert or receiving them precipitately. Those who earnestly seek conversion must be accepted. Tosafot cites the consequences of rejecting Timna, as well as the acceptance of Rachav, Naamah, and Rut. Hillel’s acceptance of converts who initially imposed conditions is explained by his recognition that they would ultimately become sincere. The warning cited in the siman therefore does not reject sincere converts.

sections.en: Awareness of Hashem as a Sign of Repentance

p: [קכז] סִימָן לִתְשׁוּבָה גְּמוּרָה וְשֶׁנִּתְקַבְּלָה תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ עַל עָוֹן זֶה דְּהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה וּבִכְלָל קִלְקוּל הַבְּרִית, הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר נִפְתְּחוּ לְפָנָיו מַרְאוֹת הָאֱלֹהִים;
A definitive sign of complete repentance and that his repentance over this sin of wasted seed and blemishes of the Covenant has been accepted, is when the visions of God open before him;
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁרוֹאֶה וּמַכִּיר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִכְחוֹ, שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה נִקְרָא אֵצֶל דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם "רוּחַ קָדְשְׁךָ" וּ"שְׂשׂוֹן יִשְׁעֶךָ";
meaning that he perceives and recognizes that the Blessed Name is directly before him, which King David, peace be upon him, titled "Your holy spirit" and "the joy of Your salvation";
כִּי אָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּרָא עַל פָּסוּק "מִבְּשָׂרִי אֶחֱזֶה אֱלוֹהַּ" (אִיּוֹב יט, כו), דִּלִשְׁמִירַת בְּרִית בָּשָׂר תֵּיכֶף מַגִּיעַ מַחֲזֶה: "וַיֵּרָא וְגוֹמֵר".

for they stated in Bereishit Rabbah (beginning of Parashat Vayeira) on the verse "from my flesh shall I see God" (Job 19:26), that for guarding the covenant of the flesh there immediately follows divine vision: "And Hashem appeared unto him, etc." (Genesis 18:1).
וְהִנֵּה בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה, אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר חַיֵּי שָׂרָה (קכט סוֹף עַמּוּד א) דִּבְשַׁעְתָּא חֲדָא בְּרִגְעָא חֲדָא זוֹכֶה לְכָל הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת
And behold, regarding a penitent (ba'al teshuvah), the Zohar states (Chayei Sarah 129a end) that in one hour, in a single instant, he merits to ascend to all spiritual rungs
[וְשָׁמַעְתִּי בְּשֵׁם הָרַב רַבִּי בּוּנִם זַ"ל כִּי דָּבָר זֶה מִיגִיעַת רַשְׁבִּ"י עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם],
and I heard in the name of Rabbi Bunim, of blessed memory, that this achievement was unlocked through the spiritual toil of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him,
וְדָבָר זֶה עִיקָּרוֹ עַל בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה מֵעָוֹן קִלְקוּל הַבְּרִית כִּדְאִיתָא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (יז.) עַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דּוֹרְדְּיָא;
and this concept applies primarily to a penitent repenting from the sin of blemishing the Covenant, as brought in Avodah Zarah 17a concerning Rabbi Elazar ben Dordaya;
וּבְלָאו הָכִי סְתָם תְּשׁוּבָה בְּעָוֹן זֶה כִּדְמַשְׁמָע בְּפֶרֶק יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים (יוֹמָא פו:): הֵיכִי דָּמֵי בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה? מַחֲוֵי וְכוּלֵי בְּאוֹתָהּ אִשָּׁה.
and even generally, standard repentance is framed around this sin, as implied in Yoma 86b: "Who is a true penitent? One to whom the same woman presents herself in the same situation, etc."
וּכְשֶׁמְּתַקֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה הָרְאוּיָה
And when one rectifies through proper repentance

[שֶׁהוּא שֶׁלְּעוֹלָם לֹא יַחֲזוֹר לְדָבָר זֶה אֲפִילּוּ יַעֲבוֹר עָלָיו מָה, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיָּעִיד עָלָיו יוֹצֵר בְּרֵאשִׁית עַל כָּךְ כִּלְשׁוֹן הָרַמְבַּ"ם בְּהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁהִגִּיעַ תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ לְכָךְ],
which means that he will never return to this act no matter what befalls him, such that the Creator of the universe can testify concerning him as formulated by Maimonides in Hilkhot Teshuvah,
אָז תֵּיכֶף מַגִּיעַ לוֹ הָרְאִיָּה הָרְאוּיָה לְשׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
then there immediately reaches him the divine vision appropriate to the guardian of the Covenant as noted above

[וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דּוֹרְדְּיָא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שָׁם שֶׁמֵּת תֵּיכֶף, הָא אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק לד) עַל פָּסוּק "כִּי לֹא יִרְאַנִי וְגוֹמֵר": הָא בִּשְׁעַת מִיתָתוֹ רוֹאֶה,

and regarding Rabbi Elazar ben Dordaya in Avodah Zarah who died immediately, our Sages stated (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 34) on the verse "for man shall not see Me and live" (Exodus 33:20): behold, at the hour of his death he sees,
וְהִיא הָרְאִיָּה שֶׁזָּכָה לָהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת כִּי הָיָה מְחוּיָּב מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין,
which was the divine vision he merited, and afterward he died because he was liable to court-imposed capital punishment,
וְדִין אַרְבַּע מִיתוֹת לֹא בָּטְלוּ, כִּי מִמִּיתַת בֵּית דִּין לָא מַהֲנֵי כֹּפֶר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "לֹא תִקְחוּ כֹפֶר וְגוֹמֵר",
and the dynamic of the four capital penalties was never abolished, seeing that for court execution no ransom avails, as written: "You shall take no ransom, etc.",
וְאֵין שׁוּם פִּדְיוֹן וְתִיקּוּן מוֹעִיל מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לְמִיתָה בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם.
and no monetary redemption or ritual substitution avails, unlike death at the hands of Heaven.
וְאָמְנָם חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה הִמְצִיאוּ כַּמָּה עֵצוֹת וְהַצָּלוֹת גַּם לְהַמִּיתַת בֵּית דִּין, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ.
Truly, our Sages devised numerous spiritual counsels and deliverances even for court execution, which is not to be elaborated here.
וְאָמְרוּ שָׁם: בָּכָה רַבִּי: יֵשׁ קוֹנֶה וְכוּלֵי,
And they said there: Rebbe wept and said: "There is one who acquires his world in a single hour, etc.",
כִּי אָמְרוּ: "יָפָה שָׁעָה אַחַת בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים וְכוּלֵי",
for they taught: "Better is one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than all the life of the World to Come,"
וְגַם זֶה הוּא לְעוֹנֶשׁ מַה שֶּׁקָּנָה עוֹלָמוֹ בְּשָׁעָה אַחַת וְהֻוצְרַךְ תֵּיכֶף לֵילֵךְ לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא, גַּם זֶה מִכְּלַל עוֹנְשָׁיו]:
and that he acquired his world in one hour and was compelled to depart immediately to the World to Come was likewise part of his punishment, depriving him of further years of Torah and mitzvot.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Vayera 1:3, distinguishes Avraham’s earlier revelations for particular prophetic messages from the appearance after circumcision. Previously the revelation ended with the message, as Genesis 17:22 records. After circumcision, his body had become continually ready to house the Shekhinah, so the appearance was not limited to a particular communication. This explains why circumcision marks a new kind of revelation even though Avraham had already received prophecy, and illuminates the siman’s description of recognizing Hashem before oneself.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Chayei Sara 16:121: “Fortunate are the masters of repentance, for in one hour, in one day, in one moment, they draw near to the Holy One, blessed be He. This is not so even for the completely righteous, who draw near to the Holy One, blessed be He, over many years. Avraham did not enter those supernal days until he was old, as has been said. So too David, of whom it is written, “King David was old, advanced in days.” But the master of repentance immediately enters and cleaves to the Holy One, blessed be He.”

sections.en: Atonement Even for a Transgression with Holy Intent

p: [קכח] כְּשֶׁאָדָם עוֹשֶׂה עֲבֵירָה כְּעִנְיַן "עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים קיט, קכו) וּ"בְּכָל דְּרָכֶיךָ דָעֵהוּ" (מִשְׁלֵי ג, ו), מִכָּל מָקוֹם צָרִיךְ כַּפָּרָה עַל הָעֲבֵירָה שֶׁעָשָׂה,

When a person commits a transgression under the principle of "It is time to work for Hashem; they have made void Your Torah" (Psalms 119:126) or "In all your ways acknowledge Him" (Proverbs 3:6), he nonetheless requires atonement for the transgression he committed,
וּכְאוֹתָהּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת לא:): דְּמִתְעַנִּין תַּעֲנִית חֲלוֹם בְּשַׁבָּת וְצָרִיךְ לְמֵיתַב תַּעֲנִיתָא לְתַעֲנִיתֵיהּ;
as in that which they taught (Berakhot 31b): one who observes a dream fast on Shabbat must sit in a subsequent fast to atone for having fasted on Shabbat;
וְכֵן בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כו:): סָבְרִי מִצְוָה קָעָבְדִי, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם צְרִיכָה כַּפָּרָה;
and likewise in Sanhedrin 26b: they reasoned they were performing a mitzvah, yet it nonetheless required atonement;
וְכֵן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּשְׁבִירַת הַלּוּחוֹת, וְגָרַם עַל יְדֵי זֶה שִׁכְחַת הַתּוֹרָה כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין נד.): אִלְמָלֵא וְכוּלֵי,
and so with Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, regarding the breaking of the Tablets, which caused the forgetfulness of Torah (Eruvin 54a): "Had not the first tablets been broken, etc.,"
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִסְכִּים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל יָדוֹ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִקְרֵי עֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ,
even though the Holy One consented with his action, it was nonetheless titled an aveirah lishmah,

וּלְכָךְ סָבַל גַּם הוּא כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת וָאֶתְחַנַּן) שֶׁנִּיטְּלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ מָסוֹרוֹת הַחָכְמָה וְהָיָה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ יוֹשֵׁב וְדוֹרֵשׁ וְכוּלֵי.
and therefore he too suffered, as our Sages stated (Midrash Tanchuma, end of Va'etchanan) that the traditions of wisdom were sealed from him and Joshua sat and expounded in his presence.
וְכֵן אֶסְתֵּר, דְּנִיטְּלָה מִמֶּנּוּ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ כְּשֶׁהִגִּיעָה לְבֵית הַצְּלָמִים (מְגִילָּה טו:), הוּא לְעוֹנֶשׁ אַעֲבֵירָה אַף עַל גַּב דְּמִצְוָה רַבָּה קָעָבְדָא

And likewise Esther, from whom the Holy Spirit departed when she reached the chamber of idols (Megillah 15b), which occurred as punishment for entering, even though she was performing a momentous mitzvah
[וְזֶה סוֹד שֶׁאָמְרָה: שֶׁמָּא בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁקְּרָאתִיו "כֶּלֶב", וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ].
and this is the mystical secret of why she asked: perhaps it is because I called him a 'dog', and this is not the place to elaborate.
וּלְכָךְ בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה, אַף דִּזְדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוּ זְכִיּוֹת, מִכָּל מָקוֹם צָרִיךְ סִגּוּפִים וְתַעֲנִיּוֹת לְכַפָּרָה, מִשּׁוּם דְּעַל כָּל פָּנִים לֹא עֲדִיפֵי מֵעֲבֵירָה לִשְׁמָהּ.

And therefore a penitent, even though willful transgressions are transformed into merits, nonetheless requires self-afflictions and fasts for atonement, since at the very least his past sins are no superior to an aveirah lishmah.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (נ.): כָּל הָאוֹמֵר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וַתְּרָן וְכוּלֵי,
And concerning this they said in Bava Kamma 50a: "Whoever says that the Holy One is indulgent, let his life be yielded,"
דְּעַל כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁעָשָׂה מִיָּמָיו נִפְרָעִים בְּעוֹנֶשׁ הַקָּצוּב וְרָאוּי לְכָךְ;
for regarding every deed a person ever committed, payment is exacted through the designated punishment fitting for it;

אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָזֶה עֵצוֹת רַבּוֹת בְּרַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יז:) בִּגְזַר דִּין דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בִּירִידַת גְּשָׁמִים: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיוּ וְכוּלֵי.

save that there exist many mitigating counsels through Heavenly mercy, along the lines of what our Sages taught (Rosh Hashanah 17b) regarding the decree of rainfall on Rosh Hashanah: behold, if they were initially sentenced to scarce rain, etc.
וְכֵן כָּאן, לִפְעָמִים נוֹתֵן לוֹ הַיִּסּוּרִין בְּאוֹתוֹ עֵת שֶׁהוּא טוֹבָה לוֹ,
And so here: sometimes He sends the afflictions at a time when it turns out to his benefit,
וְגַם יֵשׁ חִלּוּפִין בִּדְבָרִים הַדּוֹמִים זֶה לָזֶה, וְעַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְתַכְלִית יִסּוּרִין שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּעֵרָכִין (טז:).

and there are substitutions made through analogous tribulations, down to the minimal definition of suffering stated in Arachin 16b (such as reaching into one's pocket for a coin and pulling out the wrong denomination).
וְגַם פְּעָמִים הוּא שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּאָבוֹת (ג, טז) דְּנִפְרָעִין שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ
And sometimes retribution is exacted unconsciously, as written in Avot (3:16) that payment is collected without his awareness
[וְכָל שֶׁלֹּא בְּהַרְגָּשָׁתוֹ מִשּׁוּם עוֹנֶשׁ מִקְרֵי שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ, שֶׁפְּעָמִים אָדָם שָׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ וּמְדַמֶּה שֶׁטּוֹב לוֹ מְאֹד וַאֲחֵרִים מְבִינִים שֶׁאֵין טוֹב].
and whenever he does not feel it as a punitive blow, it is termed 'without his knowledge,' for sometimes a man rejoices in his lot imagining all is wonderful, while others perceive his misfortune.
וְגַם עַל יְדֵי הַמְּרִירוּת בִּתְשׁוּבָתוֹ – זֶה מַמָּשׁ עוֹנְשֵׁי גֵיהִנָּם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר:
And likewise, through the bitter remorse experienced in his repentance—that is literally the retribution of Gehenna, as I wrote elsewhere.

paragraphs.text: Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Berakhot 7, reads the command to know Hashem even in a matter of transgression as an instruction not to despair after sin. Citing the Zohar’s account of divine patience and the Midrash’s comparison of repentance to an ever-open sea, it insists that return remains possible. This complements the siman’s demand for repair after even a spiritually motivated transgression: the path back is open, while responsibility for the act remains.

p: [קכט] מִיָּד שֶׁאָדָם רוֹצֶה לָשׁוּב, הֲרֵי הוּא "בָּא לִטָּהֵר", וְהַמִּשְׁפָּט לְסַיֵּיעַ אוֹתוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹמָא (לח:);
The moment a person desires to repent, behold he is "coming to purify himself," and the heavenly rule is to assist him, as written in Yoma 38b;
וּכְשֶׁמְּסַיְּיעִין, אָז מִמֵּילָא נִיתּוֹסַף בּוֹ רוּחַ טָהֳרָה וְהוּא מוֹסִיף לָבוֹא לִטָּהֵר,
and when they assist him, there is automatically added within him a spirit of purity, prompting him to strive further to purify himself;
וְאָז חוֹזֵר הַסִּיּוּעַ מִלְּמַעְלָה בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת, וּמִמֵּילָא מוֹסִיף לְמַטָּה לָבוֹא לִטָּהֵר,
and then assistance from Above returns with even greater intensity, leading him below to strive further to purify himself;
וְכָךְ חוֹזֵר חָלִילָה, עַד שֶׁמִּפֶּתַח כְּחֻדָּהּ שֶׁל מַחַט נַעֲשָׂה כְּפִתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב).
and so it cycles repeatedly, until from an opening as narrow as the eye of a needle it expands into the portal of the Temple Hall (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2).
וּמֵאַיִן בָּא שֶׁפְּעָמִים אָדָם רוֹצֶה לָשׁוּב וְאֵין נִגְמָר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִין חֲרָטוֹת רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן?
Whence then comes it that sometimes a person desires to repent yet it never comes to fruition, in the manner of: "transgressors in Israel are full of regrets," may the Merciful One preserve us?
הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם בְּזֹהַר חָדָשׁ סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית, כִּי בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָדָם רוֹצֶה לָשׁוּב, אָז הוּא הַקִּטְרוּג הַגָּדוֹל מִיֵּצֶר;
This is as written in Midrash HaNe'elam in Zohar Chadash (end of Bereishit), for at the very moment a person desires to repent, then arises the fiercest accusation from the evil inclination;
וּלְכָךְ זְמַן הַקִּטְרוּג בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה [שֶׁנִּקְרָא "בְּהִמָּצְאוֹ" וְעֵת רָצוֹן], עַיֵּין שָׁם.
which is why the time of accusation peaks on Rosh Hashanah which is called "while He may be found" and an acceptable time, see there.
וּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר בְּקִטְרוּג – הַיְינוּ אִם מַגִּיעוֹ עַל פִּי מִשְׁפָּט לְסַיְּיעוֹ, בְּטַעֲנוֹת שׁוֹנוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ.
And by "accusation" it means challenging whether according to strict justice he is deserving of divine assistance, through various claims the accuser levels.
וּלְכָךְ צָרִיךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם בְּעֵת שֶׁבָּא לִיטָּהֵר עַל הַסִּיּוּעַ.
Therefore, when coming to purify oneself, one must intensely plead for Heavenly mercy to receive that assistance.
וְהָעֵצָה נֶגְדּוֹ הוּא הַשִּׂמְחָה וְהַבְּטִיחוּת בַּלֵּב, שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרוֹב רַחֲמָיו וַחֲסָדָיו יְקַבְּלוֹ בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה לְפָנָיו;

And the spiritual remedy against this obstacle is heartfelt joy and steadfast confidence that certainly the Blessed Name in His abundant mercy and kindness will accept him in complete repentance before Him;
וְתוֹכוֹ רָצוּף הַמְּרִירוּת הַגָּדוֹל עַל חֶטְאוֹ,
while his interior is simultaneously lined with profound bitterness over his sin,
שֶׁזֶּה מַמָּשׁ דּוּגְמַת תַּשְׁרַ"ת שֶׁעוֹשִׂין בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כַּיָּדוּעַ,
which is an exact reflection of the Tashrat shofar order performed on Rosh Hashanah:
דְּהַתְּקִיעוֹת הֵם לְשִׂמְחָה, וּשְׁבָרִים-תְּרוּעָה הַיְינוּ גְּנוֹחֵי גָּנַח וִילּוֹלֵי יִילֵיל כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה,
for the clear blasts (tekiah) denote joy, while the broken sobs (shevarim-teruah) denote groaning and wailing,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְעַרְבֵּב הַשָּׂטָן.
and through this integration the Satan is confounded.
וּלְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר: "מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד בְּבוֹא אֵלָיו נָתָן וְגוֹמֵר" (תְּהִלִּים נא, א–ב),
And therefore it is stated: "A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came unto him, etc." (Psalms 51:1–2),
שֶׁהוּא הַפְּשׁוּטָה שֶׁלְּפָנֶיהָ בְּשִׂמְחָה וְזִמְרָה, בָּטוּחַ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יַעֲנֶנּוּ
which opens with a mizmor (song), functioning as the simple straight blast (peshutah) that precedes, in joy and song, confident that the Blessed Name will answer him
וּבְכָל מִזְמוֹר שֶׁל בַּקָּשָׁה שֶׁבִּתְהִלִּים, סוֹפוֹ לְעוֹלָם בִּישׁוּעָה וְנֶחָמָה כְּעִנְיַן פְּשׁוּטָה לְאַחֲרֶיהָ.
and in every supplication psalm in the Psalter, its conclusion is invariably in salvation and consolation, like the simple blast that follows.
וְגַם כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה, אָז מַשִּׂיג תֵּיכֶף בְּשַׁעְתָּא חֲדָא בְּרִגְעָא חֲדָא הָאוֹר וְהַגִּלּוּי, וְזֶהוּ הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁלְּאַחֲרֶיהָ,
And also because in true repentance, one immediately attains in one hour, in a single instant, supernal light and revelation, which is the joy that follows,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "בְּדִמְעָתִי עַרְשִׂי וְגוֹמֵר", וְתֵיכֶף אַחַר כָּךְ: "כִּי שָׁמַע ה' קוֹל בִּכְיִי וְגוֹמֵר", וְכֵן בְּכָל מָקוֹם.
as in: "I water my couch with my tears, etc." (Psalms 6:7), followed immediately by: "for Hashem has heard the voice of my weeping, etc." (ibid. 6:9), and so throughout.
וְשֶׁלְּפָנֶיהָ הוּא כְּעִנְיַן "טֶרֶם יִקְרָאוּ וַאֲנִי אֶעֱנֶה",
And that which precedes reflects "before they call, I will answer" (Isaiah 65:24);
וּבְוַדַּאי כְּשֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹנֶה, הוּא בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת, וּמַרְגִּישׁ תֵּיכֶף לֵב הָאָדָם גַּם קוֹדֶם הַקְּרִיאָה קְצָת שִׂמְחָה וּבְטִיחוּת.
and certainly when the Holy One answers, it reverberates through all worlds, and the human heart immediately senses even before calling a measure of joy and confidence.
וּכְשֶׁהָאָדָם מִתְאַמֵּץ לְבָבוֹ לִהְיוֹת כֵּן, אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ כֵן מֵעַצְמוֹ עַל יְדֵי הָעֲנִיָּה דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
And when a person braces his heart to cultivate this trust, even if it does not arise spontaneously through Hashem's response,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל יְדֵי פְּעֻלַּת לִבּוֹ עוֹשֶׂה רֹשֶׁם לְמַעְלָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כֵּן, כְּעִנְיַן "ה' צִלְּךָ" כַּנּוֹדָע:
nonetheless through the deliberate stirrings of his heart he creates an impression Above to make it so, in the manner of "Hashem is your shadow," as is known.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 38b: ‘Reish Lakish said: What is the meaning of ‘If it concerns scoffers, He scoffs, but to the humble He gives favor’? When someone comes to become impure, an opening is made for him; when someone comes to become pure, he is helped. The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: It is like a man selling naphtha and balsam. When a customer comes to measure out naphtha, the seller tells him: ‘Measure it for yourself.’ When a customer comes to measure out balsam, he tells him: ‘Wait for me until I measure it with you, so that both you and I will be perfumed.’’

paragraphs.text: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 5:6, describes divine help given gradually, in a measure its recipients can bear. Each gift leads them to recognize the Giver and turn to Him again; the new help can even precede their request. God nevertheless credits the resulting attainment to their prayer and effort. This parallels Rav Tzadok’s ascending movement in which assistance awakens a further desire for purification and a further request for help.

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Part I; Likkutei Amarim 11:6: “There is a person in whom evil predominates more strongly, and all three garments of evil are clothed in him, causing him to commit more serious transgressions and at more frequent intervals. Yet in between he regrets them, and thoughts of repentance arise from the good within his soul, which grows somewhat stronger in the interval. But it does not gain enough strength to overcome the evil so that he abandons his sins entirely and becomes one who “confesses and forsakes.” Concerning this our Sages said, “The wicked are full of regrets.” These are most of the wicked, who still have an element of good within their souls.”

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Iggeret HaTeshuvah 11:1–2, joins humility and remorse with joy and firm trust in God’s readiness to forgive. Its example is the Amidah: immediately after asking forgiveness, one confidently blesses God as abundantly forgiving, without the doubt that would ordinarily prevent a questionable blessing. The passage also states that renewed sin delays redemption. Trust in forgiveness thus accompanies sincere return; it does not remove the need to cease sinning.

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Resisei Layla explains why the broken cry is surrounded by notes of joy: they awaken the Father's kindness and compassion toward His children. The comparison develops the siman's instruction to hold both confidence and inward bitterness together. Joy here concerns the relation that makes return possible, while the broken sound still gives expression to the work of repentance.

sections.en: Free Choice and the Soul's Hidden Root

p: [קל] אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַבְּחִירָה נְתוּנָה לָאָדָם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין אָדָם יָכוֹל לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ וְעִיקָּרוֹ,
Even though free choice is granted unto man, nonetheless a person cannot alter his essential root and core;
וּכְאוֹתָהּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (מד.): "אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא – יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא", מִשּׁוּם דְּהוּא מִשָּׁרְשָׁא וְגִזְעָא קַדִּישָׁא;
as in that which they stated in Sanhedrin 44a: "Even though he sinned, he remains Israel," because he derives from a holy root and stock;
וְכֵן אִיתָא בִּבְרָכוֹת (כט.): טָבָא לָא הָוֵי בִּישָׁא, אִם לֹא בְּרַע מֵעִיקָּרוֹ;
and so it is stated in Berakhot 29a: one who is fundamentally good does not turn bad, unless he was corrupt from his very root;
וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּחֲגִיגָה (טו:): טִינָא הָיְתָה בְּלִבָּם;
and in Chagigah 15b: there was muddy slime in their hearts from the start;
וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ: בִּישָׁא לָא הָוֵי טָבָא,
and likewise conversely: one fundamentally evil does not become good;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא רָצוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה לְגַלּוֹת זֶה הַגְּמִירָא בְּפֵירוּשׁ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם גִּלּוּהוּ בְּסוֹד בְּכָל מָקוֹם לַמְּבִינִים,
and although our Sages did not wish to disclose this tradition explicitly, they revealed it in esoteric allusions in many places for the discerning,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת מח.): בּוּצִינָא מִקַּטְפֵיהּ יְדִיעַ.
and concerning this they said (Berakhot 48a): a pumpkin is known from its very blossom.
רַק הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַזֶּה נֶעְלָם מִכָּל הַבְּרוּאִים
Only that this primordial root is concealed from all created beings
[דְּזֶהוּ בְּסוֹד הַיְדִיעָה וְהַבְּחִירָה שֶׁנִּתְקַשּׁוּ הַקַּדְמוֹנִים],
which touches upon the mystery of divine Foreknowledge and human Free Choice with which the early masters struggled,
כִּי לִבָּא לְפוּמָא לָא גַּלְיָא.
for the heart does not reveal its secrets to the mouth.
וּלְכָךְ מָצִינוּ גַּם כֵּן חֲטָאִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And therefore we also find transgressors concerning whom our Sages stated that they have no share in the World to Come;
וְ"אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא" הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָעִיקָּר חָסֵר מִן הַסֵּפֶר וְשָׁרְשׁוֹ רַע
and having no portion in the World to Come means that the foundation is lacking from the ledger and his root was evil
[וּלְכָךְ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְנַשֶּׁה אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, לֹא הוֹעִילָה לוֹ תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ, כִּי מֵאַחַר דְּעִיקָּרוֹ בִּישָׁא,
and therefore according to the opinion that Manasseh has no portion in the World to Come, his repentance was not accepted because his essential root was corrupt,
וְלָכֵן אָמַר אִידָךְ דִּמְרַפֶּה יְדֵי בַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה, וְלָכֵן לֹא גִּלּוּ זֶה רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּפֵירוּשׁ,
which is why the opposing sage challenged that this weakens the hands of penitents, and why our Sages did not disclose this openly;
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין זֶה רִפּוּי כְּלָל, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ],
yet in truth it is no discouragement at all, and this is not the place to lengthen,
וְהוּא נַעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי פְּעֻלָּתוֹ וּבְחִירָתוֹ לְרַע;
which becomes manifest through his active deeds and choices for evil;
וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ: עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים יָכוֹל לְהִתְקָרֵב, וַאֲפִילּוּ עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה הֲרֵי הוּא כְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ג.),
and likewise conversely: through repentance and good deeds one can draw near, and even a gentile who engages in Torah study is comparable to the High Priest (Avodah Zarah 3a),
וְכָל הַתּוֹרָה מָלֵא מִזֶּה, וְנֶאֱמַר: "לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא וְגוֹמֵר", וּבְרִיאָה הוּא יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן,
and the entire Torah is replete with this, and it is stated: "Create in me a clean heart, etc." (Psalms 51:12), where creation is something from nothing,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמֵּאַחַר שֶׁזֶּה בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, מוֹעִיל רַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם
meaning that since this is in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, Heavenly mercy is efficacious
[וּלִכְשֶׁיִּזְכֶּה בְּרַחֲמִים אוֹ לְהֵיפֶךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אָז יִהְיֶה בֶּאֱמֶת לְמַפְרֵעַ שָׁרְשׁוֹ כָּךְ,
and when he merits through mercy, or the reverse, Heaven forbid, then in ultimate retroactive truth his root becomes defined as such,
וְאֵין שִׁינּוּי בַּיְדִיעָה, כִּי יְדִיעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵין נוֹפֵל תַּחַת הַזְּמַן דְּעָבָר וְעָתִיד, רַק אָנוּ תַּחַת הַזְּמַן, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ בֵּיאוּרוֹ].
and there is no alteration in Foreknowledge, for the knowledge of the Blessed Name does not fall under time of past and future, only we are under time, and this is not the place to explain it.
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ (יַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי יְחֶזְקֵאל שנח): שָׁאֲלוּ לַחָכְמָה וְכוּלֵי, לַתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי, לַנְּבוּאָה וְכוּלֵי, וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָמַר: יַעֲשׂוּ תְּשׁוּבָה;
And therefore they taught (Yalkut Shimoni, Ezekiel 358): they asked Wisdom, Torah, and Prophecy what the sinner's fate should be, and the Holy One alone responded: "Let them repent";
אֲבָל מִצַּד כֻּלָּם בִּישָׁא לָא הָוֵי טָבָא.
for from the perspective of all of them, what is corrupt cannot become good.
וְזֶה הָיָה טַעֲנַת הָעָם בִּיחֶזְקֵאל בְּפָרָשַׁת "וּבְשׁוּב צַדִּיק וְגוֹמֵר וּבְשׁוּב רָשָׁע וְגוֹמֵר": "וַאֲמַרְתֶּם לֹא יִתָּכֵן דֶּרֶךְ ה'" (יְחֶזְקֵאל יח, כה);

And this was the objection of the people in Ezekiel in the passage "When the righteous turns away, etc., and when the wicked turns away, etc.": "Yet you say: The way of the Lord is not equal" (Ezekiel 18:25);
וּבְוַדַּאי דַּעַת שׁוֹטִים לֹא נִזְכַּר בַּכָּתוּב, רַק הֵם אַטָּבָא וּבִישָׁא מֵעִיקָּרוֹ אָמְרוּ, וְהֵם חָשְׁבוּ שֶׁגַּם הֵם מְבִינִים;

and certainly a foolish argument would not be memorialized in Scripture, but they were arguing based on the principle of what is fundamentally good or evil from its root, imagining that they understood this;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר לָהֶם: "דַּרְכֵיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁאַתֶּם אֵין יוֹדְעִים כְּלָל בָּזֶה;
and concerning this the prophet answered: "are not your ways unequal?", meaning that you do not understand this at all;
וּכְשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְקַבְּלוֹ, אָז מִתְגַּלֶּה לְמַפְרֵעַ דְּעִיקָּרוֹ כָּךְ:
and when the Blessed Name accepts him, it is revealed retroactively that such was his true root from the beginning.

paragraphs.text: Mishneh Torah, Repentance 5:5, states the difficulty of reconciling divine foreknowledge with human choice. Rambam explains that God and His knowledge are one, so human beings cannot comprehend how He knows events. Yet he affirms without doubt that people choose their own deeds and are accountable for them; God does not compel those choices. These are the two conclusions relevant here. Rav Tzadok’s further account of divine knowledge beyond time is his own exposition.

paragraphs.text: Reaching the higher root through return

rich.text: Reaching the higher root through return

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 19:1, insists that the soul’s higher bond cannot be reached without repentance and service. Its parable, attributed to the author’s grandfather, is of a wealthy traveler who cannot reach the riches at home without food for the journey. Likewise, retrospective clarification at the level untouched by sin depends on surrendering one’s understanding to God’s will. The higher root therefore does not dispense with the path of chosen return emphasized in this siman.

paragraphs.text: A new heart and humility toward converts

rich.text: A new heart and humility toward converts

paragraphs.text: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 4:9, contrasts Shammai’s strictness with Hillel’s humility in receiving converts. Humility measures one’s own deficiency against God’s greatness and leaves no place for contempt toward the newcomer. Just as God can make vinegar burn, He can create a new heart. The passage also connects Avraham’s humility with his being father of converts, giving a practical expression to the siman’s teaching that a person’s root is hidden from human judgment.

sections.en: Israel's Enduring Root in the Source of Life

p: [קלא] שׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִמְּקוֹר הַחַיִּים,
The root of the souls of all Israel is derived directly from the Source of Life,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא" (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ.)
as it is written: "All Israel have a portion in the World to Come" (Sanhedrin 90a)
[וַאֲפִילּוּ אוֹתָם שֶׁמָּנוּ שָׁם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם תִּיקּוּן עַל יְדֵי דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קד:)].
and even those from Israel enumerated there as excluded possess rectification according to the interpreters of esoteric traces, see Sanhedrin 104b.
וְדָבָר זֶה נִתְגַּלָּה לָרִאשׁוֹנָה בְּבֵיאוּר גָּמוּר עַל יְדֵי בִּלְעָם, שֶׁכָּל פָּרָשָׁתוֹ הוּא עַל עִנְיַן מַעֲלָה זוֹ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל:
And this principle was first revealed with absolute clarity through Balaam, whose entire biblical narrative centers on this supreme virtue of Israel:
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ יַגְדִּילוּ חֲטָאִים זוֹ עַל זוֹ, אֵין אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִיתֶּקֶת מֵהֶם כִּמְלֹא נִימָא
that even if their sins multiply and pile one upon another, the love of the Blessed Name is never severed from them by even a hairsbreadth
[וְהוּא הָיָה מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק דְּאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
and Balaam stood as the absolute antithesis of this, as written in chapter Chelek that he has no portion in the World to Come;
וְעִם כָּל מַעֲלָתוֹ שֶׁהָיָה נְבִיא אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם וְדוּגְמַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
and despite all his virtue as prophet of the gentiles mirroring Moses our teacher, peace be upon him,
וַאֲפִילּוּ יוֹסִיף מַעֲלוֹת זֶה עַל גַּבֵּי זֶה, וְכֵן אָמַר: "אֶת שִׁבְעַת הַמִּזְבְּחֹת עָרַכְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר" בַּעֲבוֹדָה
and even if he piled virtues one upon another, professing in worship: 'I have prepared the seven altars, etc.'—
אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם וְאַחֲרִיתוֹ עֲדֵי אֹבֵד.
it amounts to nothing, and his end is unto destruction.
וְדַיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי הַהֵיפֶךְ מִתְגַּלֶּה מַעֲלָה זוֹ, כְּעִנְיַן: אֵין שְׁבָחָהּ שֶׁל מַטְרוֹנִיתָא וְכוּלֵי (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת עֵקֶב)].
And precisely through the opposite is this virtue revealed, in the spirit of: 'The praise of the matron is not recognized, etc.' (Midrash Rabbah, Eikev).
וּקְרָאוּהוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בִּדְבָרִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א): "מַחֲלִיק לָשׁוֹן", שֶׁהֶחֱלִיק וְכוּלֵי וְנָפְלוּ עַל יָדוֹ;
And our Sages of blessed memory called him (Devarim Rabbah 1) a "flatterer" who smoothed his tongue, causing them to stumble through his seductive words;
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין קה:): מִבִּרְכָתוֹ אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ מַה הָיָה בְּלִבּוֹ, וְנֶאֱמַר: "וַיַּהֲפֹךְ ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְּךָ אֶת הַקְּלָלָה לִבְרָכָה";
and so they said (Sanhedrin 105b): "From his blessing you may discern what was in his heart," as it is written: "and Hashem your God turned the curse into a blessing for you" (Deuteronomy 23:6);
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, סג עַמּוּד ב) שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְהַכְנִיס עַיִן הָרָע.
and our Sages stated in the Zohar (Part III, 63b) that he sought to cast an evil eye upon them.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי יָדַע שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַמַּעֲשִׂים יוּכַל לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת גַּם הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
That is, because he knew that through practical deeds even the spiritual root can potentially be altered,
וְהוּא לֹא הוֹדִיעָם זֶה, רַק הֶחֱלִיק לָשׁוֹן כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּבְטְחוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה וְיֶחֶטְאוּ וְיִשְׁתַּנֶּה הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
yet he did not inform them of this, but flattered them with smooth speech so that they would become complacent, sin, and thereby have their root altered;
וְזֶה שֶׁהָיָה בְּלִבּוֹ: שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ
and this is what was hidden in his heart: that they should become the absolute opposite
[וְגַם כִּי כָּל הַשָּׂגוֹת אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מֵעוֹלָם הַבָּא הוּא דּוּגְמַת מַשִּׂיג בַּחֲלוֹם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּשׁוּב ה' וְגוֹמֵר",
and also because all of a person's perceptions in this world of the World to Come resemble a dream, as written: 'When Hashem brings back, etc., we were like dreamers,'
וְהָעוֹלָם הַבָּא נִקְרָא שׁוֹרֶשׁ וְיָכוֹל לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
and the World to Come is termed 'root' and can be altered as noted above;
וְאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נה.): חֶלְמָא טָבָא חֶדְוָותֵיהּ מִסְתַּיֵּיהּ, וְכָל יָמָיו שֶׁל דָּוִד לֹא רָאָה חֲלוֹם טוֹב,
and they said (Berakhot 55b): 'For a good dream, the joy it brings suffices,' and throughout David's days he never saw a good dream,
וּלְכָךְ בִּקֵּשׁ הוּא דִּיהֵא חֶדְוָותֵיהּ מִסְתַּיֵּיהּ,
which is why he prayed that the joy itself suffice,
וּלְכָךְ מַזְכִּירִים בַּהֲטָבַת חֲלוֹם הֲפוֹךְ קִלְלַת בִּלְעָם]
and why in the prayer for transforming bad dreams we mention the inversion of Balaam's curse –
וְהַיְינוּ עַיִן הָרָע וּמַחֲלִיק.
and this was his evil eye and flattery.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָפַךְ, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן: שֶׁגַּם שֶׁיֶּחֶטְאוּ לֹא יִשְׁתַּנֶּה הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ כְּלָל;
And the Blessed Name inverted it, ensuring that in ultimate truth it remains thus: even when they sin, their essential root is never altered at all;
וּלְכָךְ נִקְבְּעוּ דְּבָרָיו בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן.
and therefore his words were canonized within the Torah, because this is absolute divine truth.
וְנִמְצָא נֶהֶפְכוּ דְּבָרָיו לִבְרָכָה מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַכֹּל בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן.
And it turns out that his words were converted into blessing, since everything is in truth so
[וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא הָיָה אָדָם שֶׁיָּדַע אֲמִיתַּת דָּבָר זֶה כָּמוֹהוּ,
and concerning King Solomon, peace be upon him, no man knew the truth of this like him,
וּלְכָךְ בָּטַח לַעֲבוֹר עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה עַל פִּי דַעְתּוֹ,
and therefore he relied upon it to transgress biblical restrictions based on his own reasoning,
וּלְכָךְ בִּקְשׁוּ לְדוּנוֹ לְאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא אֲבָל לֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדָם,
leading the Sages to seek to exclude him from the World to Come, yet they could not,
וְלָכֵן נִיתַּן בִּלְעָם תְּמוּרָתוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר]:
and therefore Balaam was substituted in his stead, as I wrote elsewhere.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Achrei Mot 20:124-21:130: ‘There is a person through whom curses are destined to be fulfilled: wherever he directs his gaze, he brings curses, blight, and terror. Such was Balaam, who was called ‘evil-eyed’: he was suited to every evil and was not suited to good. Even when he blessed, his blessing was no blessing and did not endure. When he cursed, however, his curse against anyone was fulfilled, even in a single moment. Therefore it is written: ‘Open of eye’ (Numbers 24:3). Wherever his eye held sway became cursed. Come and see what is written: ‘He turned his face toward the wilderness’ (Numbers 24:1), so that he might arouse from that side the power ruling there, and it would bring an accusation against Israel. What is written of the priests? ‘One with a good eye shall be blessed’ (Proverbs 22:9), for he is suited to this, and blessing rests in his gaze. Therefore we learned: A person should turn aside even from a hundred roads rather than encounter someone who has an evil eye.’

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Masei 11:3, explains Bilaam’s flattery as encouraging Israel to rely on the claim that God would ultimately clarify all their deeds for the good. This made sin appear harmless and contributed to their fall at Shittim. Rav Tzadok expressly distinguishes retrospective transformation through repentance out of love from choosing sin in anticipation of that result. The person who plans to sin and then repent is not granted assistance to repent. The eventual clarification therefore supplies no advance permission.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 104b:13–14 recounts an attempt to add one more king to the list of those excluded from the World to Come. Rashi identifies him as Shlomo and the pleading image of his father as David. Fire and a heavenly voice protested, recalling Shlomo’s priority in building God’s house; a further voice challenged the assembly’s authority to determine divine recompense. The attempted inclusion and its rejection are in the Gemara. The claim that Bilaam stands in Shlomo’s place is Rav Tzadok’s interpretation, not an explicit statement there.

p: [קלב] בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָעִיקָּר הוּא טָהֳרַת הַלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: רַחֲמָנָא לִבָּא בָּעֵי.
In this world, the primary foundation is the purity of the heart, as stated: the Merciful One desires the heart.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי שָׁם מִשְׁכַּן הַיֵּצֶר וְשָׁם הוּא הַיְגִיעָה.
And that is because there lies the dwelling place of the evil inclination, and there unfolds the spiritual labor.
אֲבָל הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁהוּא הַנִּיחָא, שָׁם הָעִיקָּר הוּא בַּחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ,
But in the World to Come, which is the realm of tranquil rest, the primary foundation is in the wisdom residing within the mind,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי בְּיָהּ ה' צוּר עוֹלָמִים" (יְשַׁעְיָה כו, ד) – בְּיוֹ"ד נִבְרָא עוֹלָם הַבָּא וּבְהֵ"א עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
as it is written: "for in Yah Hashem is an everlasting rock" (Isaiah 26:4)—with the letter Yud the World to Come was created, and with the letter Hei this world was created (Menachot 29b).
וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁהַיּוֹ"ד רוֹמֵז לַחָכְמָה, וְהַהֵ"א לַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב
And it is known that the Yud alludes to Chokhmah (Wisdom), and the Hei to Binah (Understanding) in the heart
[וְאָמְרוּ: הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כִּפְרוֹזְדּוֹר, וּמִי שֶׁלֹּא הִתְקִין עַצְמוֹ בּוֹ אֵין יָכוֹל לִכְנוֹס לִטְרַקְלִין,
and they said: 'This world is like an antechamber, and he who does not prepare himself in it cannot enter the banquet hall' (Avot 4:16),
הוּא כְּאוֹתָהּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת לא:): מָשָׁל לְמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדוֹ מַפְתְּחוֹת הַפְּנִימִיּוֹת וְהַחִיצוֹנוֹת לֹא מָסְרוּ לוֹ, בְּהֵי עָיֵיל?
matching Shabbat 31b: 'a parable of one who holds the inner keys while the outer keys were not delivered to him—how can he enter?';
עַיֵּין יוֹמָא (עב:) שֶׁלָּמְדוּ זֶה מִפָּסוּק "וְלֵב אָיִן"].
see Yoma 72b where they derived this from 'and he has no heart'.
וּלְכָךְ שַׁבָּת, שֶׁהוּא מֵעֵין הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת נז:),
Therefore Shabbat, which is a foretaste of the World to Come (Berakhot 57b):
מִי שֶׁזָּכָה לִטְעוֹם מִפְּרִי מַעֲשָׂיו זוֹכֶה לְהַשִּׂיג אָז חָכְמָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
whoever has merited to taste from the fruit of his labors merits to apprehend then divine wisdom from the Blessed Name, reflecting the World to Come.
וּבַלֵּב יֵשׁ שׁוֹרֶשׁ רַע כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו", רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר מִשָּׁרְשׁוֹ, וְהַיְינוּ בַּעֲוֹן דְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל,

And within the heart there exists an inclination toward evil, as written: "for the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth" (Genesis 8:21)—meaning from his very root, identified with the sin of the Generation of the Flood;
וּלְכָךְ אֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה לָזֶה, דִּלְשׁוֹרֶשׁ רַע אֵין מוֹעִיל, דְּבִישָׁא לָא הָוֵי טָבָא.
and therefore ordinary repentance does not avail for this, for against a corrupted root it is ineffective, since what is inherently evil does not become good.
וְהַיְינוּ תְּשׁוּבָה תַּתָּאָה;
This applies to lower repentance (teshuvah tata'ah);
רַק צָרִיךְ תְּשׁוּבָה עִלָּאָה מֵעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי הַמִּתְעוֹרֵר מִן הַחָכְמָה, שֶׁהוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ לַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
rather, one requires higher repentance (teshuvah ila'ah) drawn from the World to Come, awakened from Chokhmah, which is the root of roots,
וְשָׁם אֵין רַע כְּלָל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַתָּ בִּי טְהוֹרָה",
and there no evil exists whatsoever within Israel, as written: "the soul which You gave within me is pure,"
כִּי גַּם הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ רַע שָׁרְשׁוֹ "טוֹב מְאֹד" כַּנּוֹדָע
for even the root of evil has its ultimate supernal root in "very good," as is known
[וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין קח:) בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל שֶׁהִטְעִימָן מֵעֵין הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, הַיְינוּ כְּדֵי לְתַקְּנָם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הוֹעִיל]:
and therefore they stated in Sanhedrin 108a that He gave the Generation of the Flood a taste of the World to Come in order to rectify them, though it did not avail.

paragraphs.text: The heart’s preparation for lasting wisdom

rich.text: The heart’s preparation for lasting wisdom

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 11:8, calls Torah eternal life but also affirms the necessary time for prayer. Prayer and fear of Heaven prepare a person to receive that enduring life, like preparation in an entrance hall before entering the banquet hall. This parallels the siman’s outer-key image: intellectual attainment does not replace the heart’s work of preparing to enter.

paragraphs.text: Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:19–21, explicitly rejects an absolute denial of repentance for wasting seed. It explains the severe Zoharic language as excluding reliance on lower repentance alone: the blemish reaches both Yesod, termed Tzaddik, and the Shekhinah. Crying out to God can overcome judgment and lead to higher repentance. The conclusion is that this repentance is difficult and must reach a deeper level, not that repair is unavailable. This distinction underlies Rav Tzadok’s discussion of reaching the root.

paragraphs.text: Tomer Devorah 4:1–2 describes repentance through Binah as returning harsh judgments to their sweet root. It explicitly includes the evil part of a person in that repair, rather than limiting repentance’s benefit to the already holy part. Kayin is its example: his origin does not prevent him from ascending through the good rooted above. This provides a parallel account of reaching a deeper root, while the source’s own explanation names Binah.

sections.en: Yearning for Torah That Enters the Heart

p: [קלג] הַתּוֹרָה הִיא פּוֹעֶלֶת בְּלֵב הָאָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: הַמָּאוֹר שֶׁבָּהּ מַחֲזִירוֹ לְמוּטָב, וְעַל שֵׁם כָּךְ נִקְרָא תּוֹרָה.
The Torah operates directly upon the heart of man, as written: the illumination within it returns him to good (Midrash Eichah), and for this reason it is termed Torah (instruction).
אֲבָל יֵשׁ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהֵם מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (קו:) עַל דּוֹאֵג,
But there are words of Torah which remain merely from the lips outward, as written in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 106b) concerning Doeg,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "לָמָּה זֶּה מְחִיר בְּיַד כְּסִיל לִקְנוֹת חָכְמָה וְלֶב אָיִן" (מִשְׁלֵי יז, טז),
and regarding this Scripture states: "Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?" (Proverbs 17:16),

וְזֶה נִקְרָא "פִּטְטַיָּא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא", דְּגַם כֵּן טָבִין לְהָבִיא הָאָדָם לִידֵי תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ וְכוּלֵי [כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת נ"ט], אִם אֵין הַחֵטְא גּוֹרֵם כִּבְדוֹאֵג.

and this is called "idle chatter of the Torah," which is nonetheless good to bring a person to authentic Torah, since from not for its own sake one comes to its own sake (as I wrote above in Section 59), provided sin does not intervene as with Doeg.
אֲבָל הָעִיקָּר הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁנִּכְנָס לַלֵּב;
However, the ultimate core consists of words of Torah that penetrate the heart;
וְאֵיזֶה נִכְנָס לַלֵּב? כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא צָמֵא וּמִשְׁתּוֹקֵק מְאֹד,
and which words penetrate the heart? When a person is deeply thirsty and intensely yearns,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וָאֹכְלָה וַתְּהִי בְפִי כִּדְבַשׁ לְמָתוֹק" (יְחֶזְקֵאל ג, ג), שֶׁהוּא כְּעִנְיַן: "וְתוֹרָתְךָ בְּתוֹךְ מֵעָי" (תְּהִלִּים מ, ט), פֵּירוּשׁ נִבְלָעָה בְּכָל הָאֵבָרִים.

matching: "and I ate it, and it was in my mouth as honey for sweetness" (Ezekiel 3:3), which is as: "and Your Torah is within my inward parts" (Psalms 40:9), meaning absorbed throughout all the limbs.
וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ זוּטָא (פֶּרֶק יד): אֵין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִבְלָעִים בְּלֵב הָאָדָם אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁהוּא עָיֵיף לָהֶם.
And so it is stated in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta (chapter 14): words of Torah are not absorbed into the heart of man unless he is weary for them.
וְהָעֲיֵיפוּת וְהַצִּמָּאוֹן הוּא מִצַּד הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁמַּרְגִּישׁ שֶׁחָסֵר בַּדָּבָר וְשֶׁצָּרִיךְ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְהַשְׁלִימוֹ.
And weariness and thirst emerge from the perception of lack, feeling deficient in a matter and recognizing that words of Torah are needed to complete him.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת לא.): אִי יִרְאַת ה' הִיא אוֹצָרוֹ – אִין, וְאִי לָא – לָא;
And concerning this they said (Shabbat 31a): "If the fear of Hashem is his storehouse, yes; and if not, no";
פֵּירוּשׁ, הַיִּרְאָה הוּא הַרְגָּשַׁת הַחִסָּרוֹן, שֶׁמִּזֶּה יַגִּיעַ הַיִּרְאָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "עֵקֶב עֲנָוָה יִרְאַת ה'" (מִשְׁלֵי כב, ד), וְהִיא הָאוֹצָר לְקַבֵּל בָּהּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.

for fear is the awareness of deficiency from which true awe arrives, as written: "The reward of humility is the fear of Hashem" (Proverbs 22:4), and this humility serves as the treasury to receive words of Torah.
וְהַצִּמָּאוֹן הוּא בַּלֵּב מִצַּד הַיֵּצֶר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם (תּוֹלְדוֹת קלח עַמּוּד א) דְּאִלְמָלֵא יֵצֶר הָרָע חֶדְוָותָא דִּשְׁמַעְתָּא לָא לֶהֱוֵי.
And thirst resides in the heart from the side of the inclination, as written in Midrash HaNe'elam (Toldot 138a) that were it not for the evil inclination, the joy of legal learning would not exist.

וּכְשֶׁמִּתְמַלֵּא עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ שֶׁנִּבְלָעִין בַּלֵּב, אָז הוּא תִּיקּוּן חַטֹּאת יִצְרָא דַּעֲבֵירָה, שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים:

And when the heart is replenished through words of Torah originating in the mind and absorbed into the heart, that constitutes the rectification for the sins of the inclination to transgress, achieved through Torah as I wrote above many times.

paragraphs.text: Tiferet Yosef, Ki Tavo 6, attributes to the author’s grandfather an interpretation of the heart as inwardness. The fool who can purchase wisdom but lacks a heart is satisfied with its outward garment rather than seeking the divine utterance within. By contrast, Israel’s proper aim even in worldly enjoyment is to gain strength for God’s service. This illuminates Rav Tzadok’s account of thirst: possession of the outer form does not yet satisfy the learner’s desire for Torah to enter the heart.

paragraphs.text: Or HaChaim on Leviticus 18:2:8 interprets Psalm 40:9 as the transformation of desire itself. David’s heart came to long for God’s will, beyond merely restraining a contrary appetite. His Torah study then felt like nourishment filling his inward parts. This is a parallel explanation of the verse’s image of inwardly absorbed Torah and of the heart’s changed longing.

paragraphs.text: Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta 14:1 places fear of Heaven and good deeds at the beginning and end of learning. Against excessive eating, drinking, and sleep, it presents Torah as the bread and wine for which one must exert oneself. Its conclusion is that Torah is absorbed in the heart of one who is weary for it. Rav Tzadok interprets that weariness as thirst arising from a felt deficiency; the source itself supplies the setting of fear of Heaven and sustained effort.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 31a:11: “Rava said: When a person is brought in for judgment, he is asked: ‘Did you conduct business honestly? Did you set fixed times for Torah study? Did you engage in procreation? Did you look forward to salvation? Did you reason deeply in wisdom? Did you understand one thing from another?’ Even so, if fear of Hashem is his storehouse, then yes; if not, then no. This is like a man who told his agent: ‘Take a kor of wheat up to the upper story for me.’ He went and took it up. The man asked him: ‘Did you mix a kav of homton, preservative earth, into it for me?’ He answered: ‘No.’ The man said: ‘It would have been better had you not taken it up.’”
