paragraphs.text: Explanation: Sod Yesharim explains the same question, ‘Who can bring pure from impure—is it not One?’ Its point is the disclosure of purity within the very garment that previously seemed impure, rather than merely replacing that garment. This develops why Rav Tzadok links the paradox to divine unity and why Bilaam's view of the outward act alone misses the source of its holiness.

paragraphs.text: The remaining trace of the serpent

rich.text: The remaining trace of the serpent

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Lech Lecha 9:8, explains that even the most pious person can retain some self-enjoyment inherited from the serpent’s counsel. Yishai, who died only through that counsel, is its example. The final removal of this root belongs to Mashiach ben David. This parallel distinguishes an inherited mixture from deliberate impurity and explains how holiness remains possible in bodily life while its fullest repair is still to come.

sections.en: The Spread of Torah and Its Inward Possession

p: [קמח] יֵשׁ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁזּוֹכֶה דִּשְׁמַעְתָּתֵיהּ מִבַּדְּרִין בְּעָלְמָא, וְיֵשׁ שֶׁאֵין זוֹכֶה לְכָךְ,
There is a Torah scholar who merits that his teachings are widely disseminated throughout the world, and there is one who does not merit this,
וְאֵין זֶה רְאָיָה שֶׁזֶּה גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה,
and this disparity is no proof that the former is greater than the latter,
שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים יֵשׁ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה יְקָרִים בְּפִי מִי שֶׁהוּא.
for sometimes precious words of Torah are placed in the mouth of anyone.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָנוּ רוֹאִים בְּבִלְעָם שֶׁאָמַר פָּרָשָׁה שְׁלֵימָה בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
Just as we see concerning Balaam, who uttered an entire section in the Written Torah

[וּלְיוֹדְעֵי חֵ"ן, כִּי גַּם כָּל הַדִּבּוּרִים מִפַּרְעֹה וַאֲבִימֶלֶךְ וְעֵשָׂו שֶׁנִּזְכַּר בַּתּוֹרָה, הֲרֵי הֵם דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מַמָּשׁ, וְהָיָה זֶה אֶצְלָם, וְעַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּרָם נִתְגַּלָּה לָנוּ].

and to the initiates of esoteric wisdom, all the utterances of Pharaoh, Abimelech, and Esau recorded in the Torah are actual words of Torah, which were latent within them and through their speech were revealed to us.

וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו:) עַל דּוֹאֵג, דְּמִתְּחִלָּה בִּקֵּשׁ דָּוִד עָלָיו שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא לְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי, וְאַחַר כָּךְ דְּלָא לֵימְרוּ שְׁמַעְתָּא בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ;

And so it is stated in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 106b) regarding Doeg, that initially David prayed concerning him that he not enter the World to Come, and subsequently that they not cite teachings in the house of study in his name;
הֲרֵי דְּאֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ שְׁמַעְתָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ, אַף עַל פִּי דְּאֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
which proves that it is possible for a halakhic teaching to be cited in a person's name even though he has no portion in the World to Come.
וְכֵן בְּאַחֵר, מִתְּחִלָּה בְּחַיֵּי רַבִּי מֵאִיר אָמְרוּ שֶׁהָיָה מִשְׁפָּטוֹ דְּלָא לֵיתֵי לְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי, וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכֵי אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר שְׁמוּעוֹת מִמֶּנּוּ,

And likewise with Acher (Elisha ben Avuyah): initially during the lifetime of Rabbi Meir they declared that his judgment was not to enter the World to Come, yet even so Rabbi Meir transmitted teachings from him,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַקַּדְמוֹנִים דִּבְכָל מָקוֹם "אֲחֵרִים" הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁלָּמַד מֵאַחֵר.
and as the early authorities wrote, wherever the Talmud cites "Acheirim say," it refers to what Rabbi Meir learned from Acher.

וְכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ עֲדַיִן הָיָה בְּגֵיהִנָּם עַד זְמַן רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כִּדְאִיתָא בַּחֲגִיגָה (טו:), וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכֵי רַבִּי שֶׁסִּידֵּר הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת קָבַע שְׁמוּעָה בִּשְׁמוֹ בְּאָבוֹת (פֶּרֶק ד, כ), לְפִי שֶׁשְּׁמוּעוֹתָיו הֵם תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת וְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מַמָּשׁ.

And likewise afterward Acher still remained in Gehenna until the days of Rabbi Yochanan as brought in Chagigah 15b, and even so, Rebbe who redacted the Mishnayot canonized a teaching in his name in Avot (4:20), because his teachings are Torah of truth and authentic words of Torah.
אֲבָל צָרִיךְ רַחֲמִים גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁיִּהְיוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִבְלָעִים בְּלִבּוֹ, וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא כָּךְ כְּמוֹ הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג וּמוֹצִיא מִפִּיו.
But a person requires vast divine mercy so that words of Torah be absorbed into his heart, and that he himself embody that reality just like the words of Torah he grasps and expresses with his mouth.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (שָׁם) בְּתוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל דּוֹאֵג "מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ", פֵּירוּשׁ וְאֵין נִבְלָע בַּלֵּב לִהְיוֹת כָּךְ;
And as written in chapter Chelek (ibid.) concerning the Torah of Doeg which was "from the lip outward," meaning it was not absorbed into the heart to become integrated as his character;
וְכִדְאִיתָא הָתָם: רְבוּתָא לְמִיבְעֵי בָּעֲיָא וְכוּלֵי, אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּא בָּעֵי.
and as stated there: Is it such a great feat to raise conceptual queries, etc.? Rather, the Holy One desires the heart.
פֵּירוּשׁ, הַבְּעָיוֹת הֵם סְפֵקוֹת בַּעֲבוֹדַת ה' וּמִצְווֹתָיו, וְאִם הֵם כָּךְ בַּלֵּב – אָז הוּא רְבוּתָא, וְלֹא בַּפֶּה:

The explanation is: queries represent analytical doubts in the service of Hashem and His commandments, and if they resonate with genuine longing in the heart—then it is a great virtue, and not when merely formulated with the mouth.

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 15b:6–10 asks how Rabbi Meir could learn from Acher when Torah should be sought from a teacher of exemplary character. Its resolution distinguishes a mature student capable of separating the teaching from the teacher’s errors from an immature student. Rabbi Meir is compared to one who eats a date and discards its pit. The following nut analogy says that a scholar’s Torah need not be spoiled by his misconduct. Both images must be read with the qualification about the student’s discernment.

paragraphs.text: Pirkei Avot 4:20: ‘Elisha ben Avuyah says: What is someone who learns as a child like? Ink written on fresh paper. What is someone who learns in old age like? Ink written on paper that has been erased. Rabbi Yosei bar Yehudah of Kfar HaBavli says: What is someone who learns from the young like? Someone who eats unripe grapes and drinks wine straight from the press. What is someone who learns from the old like? Someone who eats ripe grapes and drinks aged wine. Rabbi says: Do not look at the jar, but at what is inside it. There is a new jar filled with old wine, and an old jar that does not contain even new wine.’

sections.en: Becoming What One Understands Through Torah

p: [קמט] שְׁלֵימוּת הָאָדָם הוּא כְּשֶׁיִּהְיֶה כָּךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא מַשִּׂיג הַשְּׁלֵימוּת שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת.
A person's true spiritual perfection is reached when he actually embodies the perfection that he intellectually grasps ought to be.

וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא מַשִּׂיג וְהַהַנְהָגָה הַתּוֹרִיִּית אֵיךְ שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם הַשָּׁלֵם לְהַשִּׂיג, זֶה הוּא שְׁלֵימוּתוֹ: מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהַשִּׂיג וְצָרִיךְ לְהַשִּׂיגוֹ.

That is, all the words of Torah that he perceives and the Torah conduct which a perfected person can comprehend—this defines his personal perfection: what is possible for him to grasp and what he is destined to attain.
כִּי הַשָּׂגַת הָאָדָם וְחָכְמָתוֹ הוּא עֶצֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתוֹ וְחַיּוּתוֹ,
For a person's comprehension and wisdom constitute the essential root of his soul and vitality,
וְכָל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת נח.) שֶׁאֵין בְּנֵי אָדָם דּוֹמִין זֶה לָזֶה בְּפַרְצוּפֵיהֶן;
and each individual possesses an independent soul-root, as our Sages stated (Berakhot 58a) that no two people are identical in their facial appearance;

וְהַפַּרְצוּף הוּא מֵעִיד עַל פְּנִימִיּוּת הַלֵּב כַּנּוֹדָע, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (יִתְרוֹ ע עַמּוּד א) מֵחָכְמַת הַפַּרְצוּף, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "חָכְמַת אָדָם תָּאִיר פָּנָיו" (קֹהֶלֶת ח, א),

and the facial visage bears witness to the interior of the heart as is known, and as written in the Zohar (Yitro 70a) concerning the physiognomy of the face, and as stated: "A man's wisdom makes his face to shine" (Ecclesiastes 8:1),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁפְּנִימִיּוּת הַלֵּב וְכֵן עֹמֶק חָכְמַת כָּל אֶחָד מִשְׁתַּנֶּה זֶה מִזֶּה.
meaning that the interior of the heart and the depth of wisdom of each person differ one from another.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה נב) עַל פָּסוּק "הֹלֵךְ הָאָדָם אֶל בֵּית עוֹלָמוֹ" (קֹהֶלֶת יב, ה), שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ עוֹלָם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ;

And therefore they expounded (Shemot Rabbah 52) on the verse "man goes to his long home (beit olamo, the home of his world)" (Ecclesiastes 12:5), that every person possesses an entire world of his own;
וְהוּא הַנִּקְרָא אֶצְלָם בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר (שַׁבָּת קנב.): כָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ מָדוֹר לְפִי כְּבוֹדוֹ,
and this is what they termed elsewhere (Shabbat 152a): each person has a dwelling according to his honor,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (רֵישׁ תִּיקּוּן סט) דְּעוֹלָם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר עוֹלָם קָטָן שֶׁלּוֹ.
and as written in the Tikkunim (beginning of Tikkun 69) that "his own world" denotes his individual microcosm.
וּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד כּוֹלֵל כָּל כֹּחוֹת הָעוֹלָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, כו),
That is, each person encompasses all the cosmic forces of the universe, as written: "in Our image, after Our likeness" (Genesis 1:26),
וּכְשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לִשְׁלֵימוּתוֹ, זֶה נִקְרָא בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה "קוֹנֶה עוֹלָמוֹ", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (יז.): יֵשׁ קוֹנֶה עוֹלָמוֹ וְכוּלֵי,

and when he reaches his ultimate fulfillment, this is termed in the language of our Sages "acquiring his world," as written in Avodah Zarah 17a: "There is one who acquires his world in a single hour, etc.,"
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעוֹלָם שֶׁלּוֹ הוּא אֶצְלוֹ בְּקִנְיָן.
meaning that his personal world is possessed by him as an enduring acquisition.
כִּי יֵשׁ שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג וְאֵינוֹ כָּךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג, וְאָז הַשָּׂגָתוֹ רַק בִּרְאִיָּה לְבַד.
For there is one who perceives lofty ideals yet does not embody what he perceives, and then his perception remains merely in external sight.
וְזֶהוּ הַתְחָלַת כְּנִיסַת הָאָדָם לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּרוֹקֵחַ: אֵין חֹזֶק כַּחֲסִידוּת בִּתְחִלָּתוֹ, אֲבָל הוּא רַק בִּרְאִיָּה;
And this marks the initial entry of a person into words of Torah, as written in the Rokeach: there is no fervor like pious devotion at its outset, yet it exists only in vision;
וְצָרִיךְ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לִהְיוֹת כָּךְ בְּקִנְיָן וְנִבְלָע בַּלֵּב כָּל מַה שֶּׁמַּשִּׂיג, וְאָז נִקְרָא "קוֹנֶה עוֹלָמוֹ".

and one requires long exertion until he reaches the state where it becomes an internalized acquisition and all that he perceives is absorbed into his heart, and then he is termed "one who acquires his world."
וְאָז הוּא עֵת הַפְּטִירָה כִּלְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שָׁם,
And that corresponds to the hour of passing, matching the idiom of the Gemara in Avodah Zarah there,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עוֹד מַה לְּהִשְׁתַּדֵּל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא הַפְּרוֹזְדּוֹר וְעוֹלַם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְהַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, וְהוּא לֹא יוּכַל לְהַגִּיעַ יוֹתֵר מֵעוֹלָמוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ.
meaning that he has nothing left to labor for in this world—which is the antechamber and the realm of action and exertion—since he cannot surpass his own personal universe.
וּלְכָךְ בְּעֵת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, שֶׁאָז הָיָה הַבְלָעַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּקִנְיָן [אַחַר שֶׁקָּדְמָה הָרְאִיָּה בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף: "רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה וְכוּלֵי"] כַּנּוֹדָע,

And therefore at the Giving of the Torah, when the absorption of words of Torah occurred as an absolute acquisition following the preliminary vision at the Red Sea where 'a maidservant saw, etc.' as is known,
אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת פח:): שֶׁיָּצְתָה נִשְׁמָתָם וְהוֹרִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא טַל שֶׁל תְּחִיָּה,
our Sages stated (Shabbat 88b): their souls departed and the Holy One, blessed be He, brought down the dew of resurrection,
וּכְאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק לד) עַל פָּסוּק "לֹא יִרְאַנִי הָאָדָם וָחָי" (שְׁמוֹת לג, כ) – שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת מִיתָתוֹ רוֹאֶה.
and as they taught (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 34) on the verse "man shall not see Me and live" (Exodus 33:20)—at the hour of his death he sees.
וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְתַכְלִית הַקִּנְיָן זוֹכֶה לִרְאִיָּה שֵׁנִית כִּי חוֹזֵר לַהַתְחָלָה, וּמִיָּד מִסְתַּלֵּק לְעוֹלָם מְחוּדָּשׁ, וְהוּא עוֹלָם הַבָּא:

That is, when one reaches the ultimate culmination of acquisition, he merits a second vision because he returns to the beginning, and immediately departs to a renewed world, which is the World to Come.

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: כִּי הַשָּׂגַת הָאָדָם וְחָכְמָתוֹ הוּא עֶצֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמָתוֹ וְחַיּוּתוֹ,
footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: For a person's comprehension and wisdom constitute the essential root of his soul and vitality,

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Parshat Shekalim 1:2, explains that each Jewish soul contains a distinctive point of divine wisdom, even when its bearer does not recognize it. That point is the root of the person’s vitality and a quality not duplicated in others. The difference in faces reflects this difference in inward understanding. The passage thus joins individuality of soul, wisdom, and appearance without limiting the hidden wisdom to those already conscious of it.

p: [קנ] כְּשֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְרוֹמֵם אֵיזֶה דָּבָר טוֹב בָּעוֹלָם, אָז מִמֵּילָא אוֹתוֹ דַּרְגָּא בְּסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא מִשְׁתַּפֵּל;
When the Holy One, blessed be He, exalts a particular good quality in the world, that corresponding rung in the Other Side (Sitra Achra) automatically sinks low;
וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ: כְּשֶׁרוֹאֶה אֵיזֶה דָּבָר רַע בְּתַכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת, יֵדַע כִּי אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר בִּקְדוּשָׁה הוּא בְּתַכְלִית הָרוֹמְמוּת.
and likewise conversely: when one sees a particular evil matter at the absolute depth of degradation, let him know that that very attribute in holiness stands at the pinnacle of exaltation.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי לִי כָל בְּכוֹר בְּיוֹם הַכֹּתִי כָל בְּכוֹר בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם" (בַּמִּדְבָּר ג, יג).
As it is written: "for all the firstborn are Mine; on the day that I smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt I hallowed unto Me all the firstborn in Israel" (Numbers 3:13).
וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְכָל קַרְנֵי רְשָׁעִים אֲגַדֵּעַ, תְּרוֹמַמְנָה קַרְנוֹת צַדִּיק" (תְּהִלִּים עה, יא) – בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר שֶׁזֶּה נִגְדָּע, זֶה נִתְרוֹמֵם;

And it is stated: "All the horns of the wicked also will I cut off; but the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up" (Psalms 75:11)—in the exact matter wherein the former is severed, the latter is exalted;

וְנֶאֱמַר: "אִמָּלְאָה הָחֳרָבָה" (יְחֶזְקֵאל כו, ב), וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה ו.): קֵיסָרִי וִירוּשָׁלַיִם וְכוּלֵי, פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם בְּמַדְרֵגָה אַחַת בְּמַלְכוּת.

and it is stated: "I shall be replenished, now that she is laid waste" (Ezekiel 26:2), which our Sages expounded (Megillah 6a): Caesarea and Jerusalem, if one is full the other is desolate, meaning that both occupy one identical level in the realm of sovereignty.
וְכָל אוּמָּה יֵשׁ לָהּ כֹּחַ מַה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: אָפְיָהּ שֶׁל אוּמָּה זוֹ וְכוּלֵי;
And each nation possesses a distinct spiritual faculty, as noted regarding the distinct character of each nation;

וּלְכָךְ יִרְמְיָה קוֹנֵן עַל אָבְדַן אֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "לִבִּי לְמוֹאָב וְגוֹמֵר" (יִרְמְיָה מח, לו), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּבַמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת בָּלָק כ, א),
and therefore Jeremiah lamented over the destruction of gentile nations, as written: "My heart for Moab …" (Jeremiah 48:36), and in Bemidbar Rabbah (beginning of Parashat Balak 20:1),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּאָבְדַן אוֹתָהּ אוּמָּה נִתְבַּטֵּל אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְעֵיל אוֹת מ"ז, עַיֵּין שָׁם).
meaning that with the destruction of that nation that spiritual power was abolished (as explained above in Section 47, see there).
וּבְכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן טוֹב כַּיָּדוּעַ, וְאָז נִתְרוֹמֵם אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ הַטּוֹב.
And within every trait there also resides good as is known, and then that corresponding power of good is exalted.
וּכְמוֹ בְּאָבְדַן סְדוֹם שֶׁהָיוּ אַבִּירֵי לֵב הָרְחוֹקִים מִצְּדָקָה, נִתְבַּשֵּׂר לֵידַת יִצְחָק שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן גִּבּוֹר הַלֵּב כַּנּוֹדָע.
And as with the destruction of Sodom who were stout-hearted and far from charity, the birth of Isaac was announced, who was likewise a mighty warrior of the heart in holiness as is known.
וְכֵן בְּאָבְדַן מִצְרַיִם הָיָה הֲכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, כִּידוּעַ מֵחָכְמַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהָיְתָה מֻפְלֶגֶת;
And so the downfall of Egypt was the preparation for the Giving of the Torah, as is known from the wisdom of Egypt which was extraordinarily vast;

וּלְכָךְ יְחֶזְקֵאל שֶׁנְּבוּאָתוֹ חָכְמָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרָכוֹת (נז:): יְצַפֶּה לְחָכְמָה, אָמַר כַּמָּה פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת עַל חוּרְבַּן מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה תְּרוֹמַמְנָה קַרְנוֹת חָכְמַת הָאֱמֶת.

and therefore Ezekiel whose prophecy was wisdom—as written in Berakhot 57b: one who sees Ezekiel should anticipate wisdom—uttered several prophecies concerning the destruction of Egypt, through which the horns of authentic wisdom were lifted up.
וְכֵן אָמַר כַּמָּה פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת עַל צוֹר שֶׁגַּם כֵּן הָיְתָה מְפוֹאָרָה בְּחָכְמָה כַּנּוֹדָע, רַק צוֹר הָיְתָה מֻפְלֶגֶת בְּחָכְמוֹת שִׂכְלִיּוֹת מִפְּעֻלּוֹת בְּנֵי אָדָם
And likewise he uttered several passages concerning Tyre which was also celebrated for wisdom as is known, only that Tyre was distinguished in intellectual philosophies emerging from human actions

[צוֹר לְשׁוֹן צַיָּיר וְצָר צוּרָה; וּמָלֵא וָא"ו שֶׁהוּא אוֹת אֱמֶת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (רֵישׁ וַיִּקְרָא יא עַמּוּד ב), לְפִי שֶׁנִּתְעַסְּקוּ בְּבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְהָיָה לִפְעֻלָּתָם אֲחִיזָה בְּחַיֵּי עוֹלָם.

Tyre (Tzor) shares the root of tzayyar (artisan) and shaping a form; and it is spelled fully with a Vav which is the letter of truth as written in Zohar III:11b, because they participated in the building of the Temple and their actions had a hold in eternal life.
אֲבָל "צָר" חָסֵר [לְשׁוֹן צַר וְצוֹרֵר] בְּמַלְכוּת רְבִיעִית הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה סא),
However, 'Tzar' spelled deficiently without a Vav alludes to an adversary, referring to the Fourth Kingdom (Rome) as in Bereishit Rabbah 61 end,

הַיְינוּ לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהֶם "וְהַיָּדַיִם יְדֵי עֵשָׂו" שֶׁגַּם כֵּן כֹּחָם בִּפְעֻלַּת יָדָם וְנֶחְסְרָה הַוָּא"ו, וְעַיֵּין בְּלִקּוּטֵי תּוֹרָה מֵהָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֶּחְסַר אוֹת מֵהַשֵּׁם יוֹרֶה עַל הַטֻּמְאָה]

meaning because it is said of them 'the hands are the hands of Esau' whose power is in their hands, lacking the Vav; and see Likkutei Torah of the Ari that wherever a letter is missing from a name it indicates impurity,
וְהוּא דּוּגְמַת חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and this served as the counterpart to the wisdom of the Oral Torah

[שֶׁאָז הָיְתָה הַתְחָלָתָהּ, וּלְכָךְ אָבְדַן צוֹר הָיָה בְּיוֹתֵר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְשָׂכָר לֹא הָיָה וְגוֹמֵר" (יְחֶזְקֵאל כט, יח), שֶׁנֶּאֱבַד גַּם כָּל שְׁלָלָהּ, וְהַיְינוּ כְּפִי תֹּקֶף הָרוֹמְמוּת הָרְאוּיָה לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּהַתְחָלָתָהּ.

which was then in its initial emergence; therefore the destruction of Tyre was so severe, as written: 'yet had he no wages, etc.' (Ezekiel 29:18), its spoil being lost, matching the intensity of exaltation due to the Oral Torah at its dawn.
וְקִבֵּל נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר שְׂכַר עֲבוֹדָתוֹ מִצּוֹר בְּמִצְרַיִם, כִּי מִשָּׁם נִצְמַח].
And Nebuchadnezzar received the wages of his labor against Tyre in Egypt, for from there it sprouted.
וְחָכְמַת מִצְרַיִם הוּא בִּכְשָׁפִים, שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַטֶּבַע וְהַשֵּׂכֶל, דּוּגְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, שֶׁהָיוּ הֵם דּוּגְמָתָם בְּזֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה:
And the wisdom of Egypt lay in sorcery, which transcends nature and human intellect, serving as the pagan counterpart to the Written Torah, which stood one facing the other.

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar Rabbah 20:1: “See the difference between the prophets of Israel and the prophets of the nations: the prophets of Israel warn Israel against transgressions, as it is said, “And you, son of man, I have appointed as a watchman.” But the prophet who arose from the nations opened a breach to destroy people from the world. paragraphs.text: The prophet’s lament and remaining good

rich.text: The prophet’s lament and remaining good

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, The Seventh Day of Pesach 10:1, explains lament over another nation’s fall through the loss of the particular field of spiritual service associated with its opposing inclination. Egypt supplies a further qualification: despite its devastation, some good remains to be gathered into holiness from a distance. The passage connects this with Egypt’s future gift to Mashiach, accepted because it had hosted Israel. Thus the disappearance of an opposing power can involve both loss and a later gathering of good.

sections.en: Spiritual Descent as Preparation for Great Ascent

p: [קנא] עִתּוֹת הַיְּרִידָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם חֵשֶׁק לְתוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה – זֶהוּ הֲכָנָה לַעֲלִיָּה גְּדוֹלָה,
Periods of spiritual descent which a person experiences, wherein he feels no desire for Torah study and divine service, are the preparation for a great ascent.
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי הַצְּעָקָה שֶׁצּוֹעֵק כְּשֶׁמִּתְבּוֹנֵן עַל דְּרָכָיו וְרוֹאֶה שִׁפְלוּתוֹ וִירִידָתוֹ.
And that is achieved through the heartfelt outcry he raises when he contemplates his ways and beholds his lowliness and descent.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַיִּסְעוּ מֵרְפִידִים וַיָּבֹאוּ מִדְבַּר סִינַי" (שְׁמוֹת יט, ב), וְיָדוּעַ דְּרָשַׁת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קו.) עַל "רְפִידִים" – שֶׁרָפוּ יְדֵיהֶם מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה;

As it is written: "And they departed from Rephidim, and came to the wilderness of Sinai" (Exodus 19:2), and known is the exposition of our Sages (Sanhedrin 106a) on Rephidim—that they slackened their hands from words of Torah;
וְזֶה הָיָה הֲכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַחִיזּוּק יָדַיִם בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
and this very slackening was the preparation for the Giving of the Torah, which is the ultimate strengthening of hands in words of Torah.

וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְהַנְּשִׂאִם הֵבִיאוּ אֵת אַבְנֵי הַשֹּׁהַם" (שָׁם לה, כז), וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יב, טז): "נְשִׂאִם" חָסֵר, לְפִי שֶׁנִּתְעַצְּלוּ וְכוּלֵי;

And it is stated: "And the rulers (nesi'im) brought onyx stones" (Exodus 35:27), where our Sages expounded (Bemidbar Rabbah 12:16): nesi'im is spelled deficiently without a Yud because they were sluggish in bringing their gifts;
וּבַגְּמָרָא (יוֹמָא עה.): נְשִׂיאִים מַמָּשׁ וְכוּלֵי.
and in the Gemara (Yoma 75a): literal clouds (nesi'im) brought them.
פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הָעַצְלוּת, וְצָעֲקוּ לַה', זָכוּ לְכָךְ שֶׁהַנְּשִׂיאִים מַמָּשׁ – הֵם הָעֲנָנִים – הֵבִיאוּ לָהֶם אַבְנֵי הַשֹּׁהַם;
The meaning is that through their realization of sluggishness, and their crying out to Hashem, they merited that the literal nesi'im—the clouds—brought them the onyx stones;
מִסְּתָמָא לְכָל נָשִׂיא הִמְצִיא אֶבְנוֹ, וְזֶה דָּבָר יָקָר יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הַנְּדָבוֹת, וְאִלּוּ הֵבִיאוּ נִדְבָתָם מִקּוֹדֶם לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם זֶה עֲדַיִן.

presumably providing each prince with his own designated tribal stone, which was far more precious than all other donations, whereas had they brought their gifts at the outset they would not yet have possessed this miraculous elevation.
וְהַמָּשָׁל בִּנְשִׂיאִים – שֶׁהוּא חֹשֶׁךְ עַל פְּנֵי הָעוֹלָם, וּמִמֶּנָּה הָאוֹרָה יֵצֵא לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם.
And the parable of the clouds (nesi'im) is that they bring darkness over the face of the world, yet from that darkness rain and light issue forth unto all mankind.
וְכֵן שָׁמַעְתִּי עַל פָּסוּק: "הַמְכַסֶּה שָׁמַיִם בְּעָבִים", וְאַחַר כָּךְ עַל יְדֵי זֶה "הַמֵּכִין לָאָרֶץ מָטָר" (תְּהִלִּים קמז, ח).
And so I heard expounded on the verse: "Who covers the heaven with clouds," and immediately through this, "Who prepares rain for the earth" (Psalms 147:8).
וְכֵן עָשׂוּ הֵם: מִתְּחִלָּה הָעַצְלוּת הוּא הַחֹשֶׁךְ:
And so it occurred with them: initially the sluggishness constituted the dark cloud.

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 16:5 describes the weakness between successive spiritual levels as a descent that can become preparation for ascent. Rephidim followed the sea and preceded the greater revelation at Sinai. When a person recognizes the lapse and immediately renews effort, the descent may be only momentary; a greater coming ascent may involve a stronger challenge. This is an account of overcoming a lapse, not a recommendation to seek one.

paragraphs.text: Leaving weakness begins the ascent

rich.text: Leaving weakness begins the ascent

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Yitro 10:1, identifies the turning point from Rephidim to Sinai as setting the heart to seek God’s will. That small opening draws assistance from above and makes possible the self-effacement needed to receive Torah. The constructive movement begins with leaving the weakness, which clarifies the present siman’s requirement of crying out and turning toward Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Returning to Torah repairs the failure

rich.text: Returning to Torah repairs the failure

paragraphs.text: Tiferet Yosef, Shavuot 4, reads the journey from Rephidim to Sinai as showing that earlier failures can be repaired through Torah. It connects this with teachings that become understood through first stumbling over them. Read with Rav Tzadok’s requirement of renewed prayer, the parallel locates repair in the ensuing return and reception of Torah, not in weakness by itself.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 14:1: “Even during the day there are sometimes clouds that obstruct the light without making it dark. They are beneficial, because one who looks at the sun damages his eyesight, and they also prevent the intensity of the heat that sometimes harms a person, as we find concerning Nadav and Avihu. Their principal benefit is also as I heard explained concerning the verse, “Who covers the heavens with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth”: through this He brings a fresh drop into the body that causes growth. Yet rain itself is beneficial only at its proper time. Sometimes the cloud is harmful, when the full heat is needed—at the completion of the harvest, which is the completion of action, called harvesting, as stated at the end of the first chapter of Bava Kamma, as I explained elsewhere.”

sections.en: Fear and Wisdom as Paths to Divine Closeness

p: [קנב] כְּפִי הִתְרַחֲקוּת הָאָדָם מִן הָרַע, וְהַיְינוּ מִכָּל חֲמוּדוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וּתְשׁוּקוֹת דִּלְגַרְמֵיהּ, כָּךְ הוּא מִתְקָרֵב לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמַשִּׂיג אוֹרוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
In proportion to a person's distancing of himself from evil—meaning from all worldly delights and self-centered desires—so does he draw near unto the Blessed Name and attain His divine illumination,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ... וְהָאֵר פָּנֶיךָ" (תְּהִלִּים פ, ד).
as it is written: "Restore us... and cause Your face to shine" (Psalms 80:4).
וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ: כְּפִי הַשָּׂגָתוֹ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כָּךְ מִתְרַחֵק מֵעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אָנֹכִי" וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ".
And likewise conversely: in proportion to his spiritual perception of the Blessed Name, so does he withdraw from worldly pursuits, as in "I am Hashem your God" and "You shall have no other gods."
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: אִם אֵין יִרְאָה אֵין חָכְמָה, אִם אֵין חָכְמָה אֵין יִרְאָה (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ג, יז).
And concerning this they taught: "If there is no fear, there is no wisdom; if there is no wisdom, there is no fear" (Avot 3:17).
חָכְמָה הוּא הַשָּׂגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְיִרְאָה הוּא מִן הַחֵטְא, וְהָא בְּלָא הָא לָא סַגִּי.
Wisdom is the perception of the Blessed Name, while fear is dread of sin, and neither can function without the other.
וְיִרְאָה נִקְרָא "אוֹצָר" וּכְלִי קִבּוּל, שֶׁהַלֵּב מִתְפַּנֶּה מִכָּל מִינֵי תְּשׁוּקוֹת וַחֲמוּדוֹת, וּמִמֵּילָא הוּא כְּלִי פָּנוּי לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
And fear is termed a "treasury" and a receptive vessel, wherein the heart empties itself of all base longings and lusts, automatically becoming a cleared vessel to receive words of Torah,
וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: יָצָא דָּבָר שֶׁל לֵיצָנוּת – נִכְנַס דָּבָר שֶׁל תּוֹרָה, יָצָא דָּבָר שֶׁל תּוֹרָה – נִכְנַס שֶׁל לֵיצָנוּת.
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded: when levity departs, words of Torah enter; when words of Torah depart, levity enters.
כִּי כְּשֶׁהַלֵּב פָּנוּי מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, מִמֵּילָא הוּא מוּכָן לְקַבֵּל כָּל מִינֵי תַּאֲווֹת, כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה פָּנוּי לְגַמְרֵי.
For when the heart is vacant of words of Torah, it is automatically primed to absorb every worldly lust, since it is impossible for the human heart to remain completely empty.
וּלְכָךְ הֵם שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּיַחַד וְאֵין הָאֶחָד קוֹדֵם לַחֲבֵירוֹ רַק בְּרֶגַע כְּמֵימְרֵיהּ, אֲבָל תֵּיכֶף תָּכוּף לוֹ מַדְרֵגָה הָאַחֶרֶת.
Therefore both go hand-in-hand, neither preceding the other except for a split second, the alternate level following immediately in its wake.
וְהַמְפַנֶּה לִבּוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, תֵּיכֶף הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁרֶה אוֹרוֹ שָׁם;
And whoever clears his heart for the Blessed Name, the Blessed Name instantly causes His light to dwell there;
כִּי הַיִּרְאָה הִיא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹאֵל מִבְּנֵי אָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְעַתָּה... מָה [ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ שֹׁאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה]" (דְּבָרִים י, יב),
for fear is what the Blessed Name asks of mortal man, as it is written: "And now... what does Hashem your God ask of you but to fear" (Deuteronomy 10:12),
וְהַחָכְמָה מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁפִּיעַ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "יָהֵב חָכְמְתָא [לְחַכִּימִין]" (דָּנִיֵּאל ב, כא), וְנֶאֱמַר: "כִּי ה' יִתֵּן חָכְמָה וְגוֹמֵר" (מִשְׁלֵי ב, ו).
whereas wisdom is what the Blessed Name generously bestows, as it is written: "He gives wisdom unto the wise" (Daniel 2:21), and: "For Hashem gives wisdom, etc." (Proverbs 2:6).
וְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת מִקּוֹדֶם,
And an awakening from below must precede;
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב): "פִּתְחוּ לִי כְּחֻדָּהּ שֶׁל מַחַט", כִּי דַּי בְּכָל שֶׁהוּא יִרְאָה, וְאָז יֻשְׁפַּע בְּלִבּוֹ נֶגְדּוֹ כָּךְ חָכְמָה.

and regarding this our Sages expounded (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2): "Open for Me an opening like the eye of a needle"—for a minute fraction of fear is sufficient, and then a corresponding measure of wisdom will be poured into his heart.
וּמִמֵּילָא עַל יְדֵי הַחָכְמָה תָּבוֹא לוֹ עוֹד יִרְאָה, וְאָז תָּבוֹא עוֹד חָכְמָה, וְחוֹזֵר חָלִילָה עַד שֶׁיִּהְיוּ פְּתָחִים שֶׁיִּהְיוּ וְכוּלֵי.
And through that wisdom further fear will naturally arise within him, which in turn brings greater wisdom, cycling continuously until portals open wide.
וְאָמְרוּ קַדְמוֹנִים: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נֶקֶב מְפוּלָּשׁ מֵעֵבֶר לְעֵבֶר,
And the early masters stated: provided that this aperture penetrates entirely from side to side;
וּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִמַּעֲמַקֵּי לִבּוֹ הִתְעוֹרְרוּת גָּמוּר דַּעֲזִיבַת הַחֵטְא, וְלַעֲזוֹב כָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, אֲפִילּוּ רֶגַע אֶחָד דַּי:
meaning that from the innermost depths of his heart there must arise a sincere, total awakening to renounce sin and abandon all worldly attachments—and even for a single moment, it is sufficient.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 17:5, presents Yosef’s holiness—guarding the covenant and holding fast to fear of Heaven—as preparation for Yaakov’s level of truth. A heart filled with physical desires cannot receive that illumination. This gives a particular expression to the siman’s receptive vessel; Rav Tzadok then describes the continuing cycle in which fear opens the heart to wisdom and wisdom deepens fear.

paragraphs.text: Yisrael Kedoshim 6:4 reconciles apparently reversed images: fear is the outer key to Torah, yet Torah is also the gate into fear. The initial Torah inheritance already present in Israel permits entry into service; developed fear then enables fuller wisdom. The stages therefore prepare one another. This clarifies why the siman’s first opening does not exhaust either fear or wisdom.

p: [קנג] הָעָגְמַת נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם עַל עֲווֹנוֹתָיו הוּא תְּמוּרַת יִסּוּרִין, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (וַיַּקְהֵל ריב עַמּוּד א) מִמָּשִׁיחַ, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
The anguish of soul that a person endures over his iniquities substitutes for physical suffering, as written in the Zohar (Vayakhel 212a) regarding the Messiah, see there.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּנֶפֶשׁ מַנְהִיג הַדּוֹר הוּא הַכּוֹלֶלֶת כָּל נַפְשׁוֹת הַפְּרָטִיּוֹת שֶׁבַּדּוֹר.
And it is known that the soul of the leader of the generation encompasses all the individual souls within that generation.
וְנֶפֶשׁ מָשִׁיחַ הוּא כְּלַל נַפְשׁוֹת כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת אַחַר הַשְּׁלֵימוּת שֶׁל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
And the soul of the Messiah comprises the collective souls of all generations following the completion of their spiritual toil in this world
[כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָאָבוֹת כּוֹלְלִים נַפְשׁוֹת כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת בְּהַתְחָלָתָם וְשָׁרְשָׁם וּמְקוֹר מוֹצָאָם],
just as the Patriarchs encompass the souls of all generations at their inception, root, and origin;
וְנִמְצָא בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִי נְקֻדַּת הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ אֶל הַתַּכְלִית הָאֲמִיתִּי הוּא נְקֻדַּת מָשִׁיחַ,
and it turns out that within each individual soul, the focal point of its striving toward the ultimate Truth is the spark of the Messiah,
וּבְאוֹתוֹ נְקֻדָּה הוּא סוֹבֵל צַעַר עַל עֲווֹנוֹת, כְּטַעַם "מְדֻכָּא מֵעֲוֹנֹתֵינוּ" (יְשַׁעְיָה נג, ה), וּמֵקֵל בָּזֶה הָעֳנָשִׁים דְּיִסּוּרִין.
and within that point he bears grief over sins, tasting "crushed for our iniquities" (Isaiah 53:5), thereby lightening the retributions of bodily afflictions.

וְעַיֵּין שָׁם דִּמְקַבְּלָם בְּגַן עֵדֶן, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר עַל זֶה מִכֹּחַ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, עַיֵּין שָׁם (רי עַמּוּד א) דִּרְקִיעַ שֶׁעַל הַגַּן עֵדֶן נַעֲשֶׂה מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, עַיֵּין שָׁם,

And see there in the Zohar that he receives them in Gan Eden—meaning that he is awakened to this remorse through the power of Torah study, as stated there (210a) that the firmament above Gan Eden is formed from words of Torah—
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁרוֹאֶה חוֹמֶר הָעֲווֹנוֹת וְכַיּוֹצֵא.
for through Torah he perceives the profound gravity of sin.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַצַּעַר וְהָעָגְמַת נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בִּנְקֻדַּת הַלֵּב מֵעֲווֹנוֹתָיו, עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְעוֹרֵר תֹּקֶף נְקֻדַּת מָשִׁיחַ הַגְּנוּזָה בּוֹ וּמֵאִיר לוֹ.
And through the grief and anguish of soul he endures in the core of his heart over his sins, the power of the spark of the Messiah hidden within him is awakened and shines upon him.
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם (ריא עַמּוּד ב) דִּמְאוֹר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם בָּא לְגַן עֵדֶן,
And see there (211b) that fire from Gehenna reaches Gan Eden,
וְזֶהוּ הַסִּימָן עַל הָעָגְמַת נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁנִּתְקַבֵּל לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר בָּא עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְעוֹנֶג דְּהַיְינוּ גַּן עֵדֶן,
and this is the sign that the heartache was accepted before the Blessed One: when through it he arrives at holy delight (oneg), which is Gan Eden,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמֵּאִיר לוֹ מִנְּקֻדַּת מָשִׁיחַ דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר הַשְּׁלֵימוּת שֶׁבַּסּוֹף.
meaning that the messianic spark shines upon him, representing the final ultimate perfection.
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם דְּהַהוּא אֶשָּׁא נָחִית מִלְּעֵילָא, רַק כֵּיוָן דְּמָטֵי לְאַרְעָא לָא דַּקִּיק,
And see there that this fire descends from Above, yet when it reaches the earth it is no longer refined,
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא מִיִּרְאָה עִלָּאָה,
meaning that it originates from Supernal Awe (Yirah Ila'ah),
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֲגִיגָה יג:): נְהַר דִּינוּר מִזֵּיעָתָן שֶׁל חַיּוֹת מִתֹּקֶף הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁלָּהֶם, וְיוֹרֵד עַל רֹאשׁ רְשָׁעִים,
in line with what our Sages stated (Chagigah 13b): the river of fire (nehar dinur) issues from the sweat of the holy Chayot out of the intensity of their awe, descending upon the head of the wicked,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְלַבְּנִים, וְזוֹכִים יִרְאֵי שְׁמִי דַּיְיקָא לְשֶׁמֶשׁ צְדָקָה, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם:
through which they are refined and purged, and specifically those who fear My Name merit the sun of righteousness (Malachi 3:20), see there.

paragraphs.text: Remorse and the hidden root

rich.text: Remorse and the hidden root

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 7:13 distinguishes an expressed fault from the deeper root associated with the serpent’s counsel, hidden within the heart. Sorrow over sin and the reading of the red-heifer passage gradually bring awareness and repair of that root when its practical rite is unavailable. The passage relates this preparation to Pesach and resurrection. Its subject is remorse directed toward repentance and renewed life; distress alone is not presented as proof of completed repair.

sections.en: Faith in Hashem and in One's Own Soul

p: [קנד] כְּשֵׁם שֶׁצָּרִיךְ אָדָם לְהַאֲמִין בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כָּךְ צָרִיךְ אַחַר כָּךְ לְהַאֲמִין בְּעַצְמוֹ.
Just as a person is required to believe in the Blessed Name, so too must he subsequently believe in himself.
רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר, שֶׁיֵּשׁ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עֵסֶק עִמּוֹ, וְשֶׁאֵינֶנּוּ פּוֹעֵל בָּטֵל שֶׁבֵּין לַיְלָה וְכוּלֵי, וּכְחַיְתוֹ שָׂדֶה שֶׁלְּאַחַר מִיתָתָם נֶאֶבְדוּ וְאֵינָם.

That is to say, he must believe that the Blessed Name has purposeful dealings with him, and that he is not a pointless creature who sprang up overnight and perishes, or like wild beasts that after death vanish into nothingness.
רַק צָרִיךְ לְהַאֲמִין כִּי נַפְשׁוֹ מִמְּקוֹר הַחַיִּים יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְעַנֵּג וּמִשְׁתַּעֲשֵׁעַ בָּהּ כְּשֶׁעוֹשָׂה רְצוֹנוֹ.
Rather, he must believe that his soul stems from the Source of Life, blessed be His Name, and that the Blessed Name delights and revels in it when it fulfills His will.
וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ: "וַיַּאֲמִינוּ בַּה' וּבְמֹשֶׁה עַבְדּוֹ" (שְׁמוֹת יד, לא)
And this is the inner meaning of: "and they believed in Hashem, and in Moses His servant" (Exodus 14:31)—
פֵּירוּשׁ, "מֹשֶׁה" רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כְּלַל שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּדּוֹר הַהוּא, הֶאֱמִינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ בָּהֶם
"Moses" denotes the collective sum of the 600,000 souls of Israel in that generation; they believed that the Blessed Name desired them

[וּמִמֵּילָא גַּם כֵּן בְּמֹשֶׁה, אֲשֶׁר הוּא מַמָּשׁ הֵם, וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכא:) שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל נְזוּפִים לֹא נִתְיַיחֵד הַדִּבּוּר לְמֹשֶׁה.

and automatically they believed in Moses, who was essentially identical with them; as our Sages stated in Bava Batra 121b that all the years Israel were under censure in the wilderness, divine communication was not granted uniquely to Moses.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר, כִּי בְּכָל חֲטָאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל חָטָא גַּם כֵּן מֹשֶׁה שֶׁהוּא כְּלָלוּתָם:
And as I wrote elsewhere, in all sins committed by Israel Moses likewise stumbled in an aspect thereof, since he was their aggregate:

כְּמוֹ בָּעֵגֶל הָיָה חֵטְא מֹשֶׁה בִּשְׁבִירַת הַלּוּחוֹת, וּבֶאֱמֶת הוּא דָּבָר תָּמוּהַּ וְזָר מְאֹד אֲפִילּוּ לִקְרוֹעַ סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה בַּחֲמָתוֹ וּלְהַשְׁלִיכָהּ לָאָרֶץ מִכְּתַב יַד סוֹפֵר דְּעָלְמָא, כָּל שֶׁכֵּן הַלּוּחוֹת מִכְּתַב ה'.

as with the Golden Calf, Moses's counterpart was breaking the Tablets; and in truth it is an astonishing and bizarre thing even to tear a Torah scroll written by a simple scribe in one's anger and cast it to the ground, all the more so the Tablets inscribed by the hand of God!
וְהוּא מַמָּשׁ חֵטְא דְּעֵגֶל כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
And that was the precise parallel to the sin of the Calf, as I wrote elsewhere;
וּכְשֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ: "יִישַׁר כֹּחֲךָ שֶׁשִּׁבַּרְתָּ", יָדַע כִּי גַּם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כֵּן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ה.): "בּוֹאוּ וְנַחֲזִיק טוֹבָה לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ וְכוּלֵי".

and when God told him: "Congratulations that you broke them" (Shabbat 87a), he knew that this applied to the children of Israel as well, as in Avodah Zarah 5a: "Come and let us acknowledge the good of our forefathers, etc."
וּבְקִבְרוֹת הַתַּאֲוָה אָמַר: "הֲצֹאן וּבָקָר יִשָּׁחֵט [לָהֶם וּמָצָא לָהֶם]" (בַּמִּדְבָּר יא, כב), וְכֵן בְּמֵי מְרִיבָה;
And at Kivrot HaTa'avah he sinned when saying: "If flocks and herds be slain for them, will they suffice?" (Numbers 11:22), and so too at the Waters of Meribah;

It does not treat retrospective transformation as erasing every consequence of the original act.

sections.en: Ordinary Life and the Garments of Spiritual Honor

p: [קנה] הַכָּבוֹד שֶׁל הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא כְּפִי טָהֳרָתוֹ בְּדִבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת שֶׁלּוֹ, שֶׁהֵם הַלְּבוּשִׁין בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְדִבְרֵי הַמִּצְוָה,
A person's honor in this world corresponds to his purity in mundane, permitted pursuits, which serve in this world as the outer garments for holy commandments,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (בְּשַׁלַּח סא עַמּוּד א) דְּנֶצַח וָהוֹד לְבוּשֵׁי מַלְכָּא, וְהֵם תְּרֵין בַּדֵּי עֲרָבָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא וּבַתִּיקּוּנִים,
as written in the Zohar (Beshalach 61a) that Netzach and Hod are the garments of the King, representing the two willow branches (aravah),
שֶׁעֲלֵיהֶם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת אֱמוֹר: עֲרָבָה לֹא טַעַם וְלֹא רֵיחַ, כָּךְ וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
concerning which our Sages stated in Vayikra Rabbah (Emor 30:12): the willow has neither taste nor fragrance, so are those who have neither Torah nor good deeds, see there.
וְכֵן הִמְשִׁילוּ בְּחֻלִּין (צב.) עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים לְעַלְיָא וְאִתְכַּלְיָא, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And so in Chullin 92a they compared simple folk and Torah scholars to the protective grape leaves (alya) and the clusters of grapes (itkalya), see there.
וְכֵן יֵשׁ בִּפְעֻלַּת כָּל אֶחָד בְּעַצְמוֹ: פְּעֻלּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה הֵם מַעֲשֵׂה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם, וּפְעֻלּוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ נִקְרָא עַם הָאָרֶץ.
And so it is within the actions of each individual: spiritual Torah actions are the deeds of a scholar, while practical mundane endeavors are termed simple labor.
וְכֵן דָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה כא:) עַל "וְעָלֵהוּ לֹא יִבּוֹל" – אֲפִילּוּ שִׂיחַת חוּלִין וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁהֵם עַלְיָא לְאִתְכַּלְיָא דְּהַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
And so our Sages expounded (Sukkah 21b) on "and its leaf does not wither"—even the casual speech of scholars, which serves as the protective leaf for the cluster of Torah,
וְאִלְמָלֵא עַלְיָא וְכוּלֵי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרָכוֹת (לה:): הַנְהֵג בָּהֶן וְכוּלֵי, בְּמָטוּתָא מִינַּיְיכוּ וְכוּלֵי, וְהַרְבֵּה וְכוּלֵי וְלֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדוֹ, דְּאִלְמָלֵא וְכוּלֵי.

and were it not for the leaf, the cluster could not endure, as written in Berakhot 35b: "Conduct yourself with them in the way of the world... I beg of you, etc., many did as Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and did not succeed, because without the leaf, etc."
וְאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קיג.): מָאנֵי מְכַבְּדוּתָא, (וְשָׁם קמה:): וּבְלָא מָתָא תּוֹתְבָאי.
And they stated in Shabbat 113a: clothes are that which honor a person; and on 145b: when out of town, my clothes establish my name.
וְהַיְינוּ דִּלְאַחַר שֶׁנִּתְגָּרֵשׁ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן מִגַּן עֵדֶן שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹמוֹ, עָשׂוּ לוֹ מַלְבּוּשִׁים, וּכְפִיהֶם הוּא הַכָּבוֹד.
That is, after Adam the First was expelled from Gan Eden which was his native home, garments were made for him, and according to them honor is bestowed.
וְזֶהוּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁפְּעֻלּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת הוּא נִקְרָא גּוּף הָאָדָם וְהָרְשׁוּת הוּא מַלְבּוּשָׁיו;
And this applies to this world, wherein actions of Torah and mitzvot are termed the person's essential body, while permitted mundane acts are his outer garments;
אֲבָל בְּגַן עֵדֶן הַלְּבוּשׁ מִפְּעֻלַּת הַתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (וַיַּקְהֵל רי עַמּוּד א),
but in Gan Eden the soul's garment is woven from the deeds of Torah and mitzvot, as written in the Zohar (Vayakhel 210a),
וְהַיְינוּ דְּגוּף הָאָדָם שָׁם נִקְרָא רַק הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ וָלֵב
meaning that the "body" of the person there consists strictly of the thoughts and desires within mind and heart
[וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַגּוּף נִקְרָא גּוּף הָאָדָם וְהַלְּבוּשׁ הוּא הַמַּלְבּוּשׁ אֶת הַגּוּף, וּלְאַחַר מִיתָה אָז גּוּף הָאָדָם נִקְרָא הַנְּשָׁמָה וְהַגּוּף נִקְרָא רַק לְבוּשׁ.

and just as in this world the physical body is called the person's body and clothes are the garments worn over the body, after death the soul is termed the body and the physical form is merely a garment.
וְזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּרַשְׁבִּ"י בִּבְרָכוֹת שָׁם דְּלֵית לֵיהּ הַנְהֵג בָּהֶן מִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
And this was the lofty level of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in Berakhot who rejected engaging in mundane labor,
כִּי הוּא זָכָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַמָּשׁ לִהְיוֹת כְּמוֹ בְּגַן עֵדֶן, שֶׁהַגּוּף רַק לְבוּשׁ וְעַלְיָא לְאִתְכַּלְיָא, וְלֹא הַמִּדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
for in this physical world he merited to live as in Gan Eden, where the body itself serves as the garment and the leaf for the grape-cluster, instead of worldly occupation serving that role,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת (לג:) שֶׁהֶעֱנִישׁ לְהָעוֹסְקִים בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],
as written in Shabbat 33b that he struck down those who engaged in mundane plowing, and this is not the place to elaborate,
וְשָׁם הַכָּבוֹד כְּפִי הַפְּעֻלּוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ בְּתוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת.
and there in Gan Eden honor corresponds to his practical deeds in Torah and mitzvot.
וְעוֹד לְמַעְלָה הַלְּבוּשׁ כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר (שָׁם עַמּוּד ב) מִן הַכַּוָּנוֹת שֶׁבַּלֵּב וּרְצוֹנוֹת לְתוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
And higher still in the celestial realms, the garments are woven from the intentions of the heart and holy longings for Torah and mitzvot (Zohar ibid. 210b), see there;
וְשָׁם הַכָּבוֹד לְכָל אֶחָד כְּפִי כַּוָּנָתוֹ הַטּוֹבָה, וַעֲדַיִן נִקְרָא "בְּלָא מָתָא".
and there honor is bestowed according to his pure intention, yet even this is still termed being "away from home."
אֲבָל "בְּמָתָא" – זֶה יִהְיֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁהוּא שְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל (כַּנּוֹדָע בַּזֹּהַר):
But being "at home" will unfold in the World to Come, which is the Jubilee Year (as known in the Zohar):
"תָּשֻׁבוּ אִישׁ אֶל אֲחֻזָּתוֹ" (וַיִּקְרָא כה, יג), שָׁם יִהְיֶה שְׁמִי – הַשֵּׁם מוֹרֶה עַל הָעֶצֶם, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כְּפִי עֶצֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹר מַחְצַב הַנְּשָׁמוֹת.
"You shall return every man unto his possession" (Leviticus 25:13), where my name defines my essence, meaning according to the essential root of each soul in the primordial Quarry of Souls.
וְאָז יִהְיוּ עֲרוּמִּים כְּקוֹדֶם הַחֵטְא בְּלִי לְבוּשׁ,
And then they will be naked as before the primal sin without garments,
שֶׁהַלְּבוּשׁ נַעֲשָׂה רַק עַל יְדֵי יְדִיעָה דְּטוֹב וָרָע וְעַל יְדֵי הַבְּחִירָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָדָם, שֶׁהוּא הַטֹּרַח דְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת;
for garments were created solely through the knowledge of good and evil and through human choice and striving, which is the toil of Friday;
אֲבָל אָז יִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁאֵין מָקוֹם לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת כְּלָל:
but then it will be clarified that there is no room for human striving at all.

paragraphs.text: Leaves and fruit within one person

rich.text: Leaves and fruit within one person

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 12:1, applies the vine’s protective leaves and fruit within the individual: mitzvah action sustains the wisdom cultivated through Torah. The present siman instead places ordinary worldly work around Torah and mitzvot together, then changes the garment’s meaning at higher levels. The image is therefore relational. What serves as leaf or garment depends on the level being discussed, while its sustaining role remains essential.

paragraphs.text: Sichat Malakhei HaSharet 1:4 describes a mouth so formed by Torah that even unplanned speech expresses it, like the unfading leaf. Its comparison of a Levi with an angel depends on the direction of his thought and speech, not on being created without choice. This illuminates the siman’s account of permitted activity supporting and expressing the Torah within a person.

rich.text: Garments away from one’s own place

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, Hoshana Rabba 13:1, explains the saying about one’s name at home and clothing abroad through the vulnerability of being outside one’s own place. Outward distinctions and boundaries answer the opposition encountered there. Recognition that God is the world’s place provides a deeper security, since nothing lies outside His protection. This parallels the siman’s changing garments and its final image of returning home.

sections.en: Rectifying the Covenant Through Faith in Divine Providence

p: [קנו] תִּיקּוּן לְמִקְרֵה לַיְלָה
The rectification for nocturnal emission

[וְגַם בְּמֵזִיד נִקְרָא כֵּן בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב וּבְדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין (קו.) עַל פָּסוּק "וַתִּקְרֶאןָ" – רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ כֻּלָּם וְכוּלֵי]

and even when committed willfully it is termed thus in Scripture and Chazal; and in Sanhedrin 106a on "and they called the people" (Numbers 25:2), Rabbi Yehoshua states that they all experienced emissions
לְהַאֲמִין בֶּאֱמוּנָה שְׁלֵימָה שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם מִקְרֶה בָּעוֹלָם כְּלָל, וְכָל מַה שֶּׁיֶּאֱרַע לוֹ, יֵדַע שֶׁהַכֹּל בְּכַוָּנַת מְכַוֵּין יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ.

is to believe with complete faith that there is no such thing as chance (mikreh) in the world at all, and whatever occurs to him, let him know that it is entirely through the deliberate design of the Designer, blessed be His Name.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא בֶּאֱמֶת עִיקַּר הַכֹּל, וְכָל תַּרְיַ"ג מִצְווֹת הַתּוֹרָה הֵם רַק עֵיטִין לְהַגִּיעַ לִידִיעָה זוֹ שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
And this realization is truly the core of everything, and all 613 commandments of the Torah are merely counsels of advice to arrive at this awareness: that everything is from the Blessed Name.
וְכָל הָעֲבֵירוֹת נִקְרָא בַּתּוֹכָחָה "אִם תֵּלְכוּ עִמִּי קֶרִי" (וַיִּקְרָא כו, כא) – לְשׁוֹן מִקְרֶה, כִּי הָעֲבֵירוֹת הֵם יְצִיאָה מִן הַסֵּדֶר וְאֵין לָהֶם סֵדֶר

And all sins are designated in the Reproof as "if you walk with Me in happenstance (keri)" (Leviticus 26:21)—an expression of chance (mikreh), for sins appear as a departure from cosmic order, having no divine structure
[וּבְשׁוּב ה' וְגוֹמֵר "כְּחֹלְמִים", כְּמוֹ בַּחֲלוֹם אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה כַּמָּה מַעֲשִׂים וּכְשֶׁהֵקִיץ אֵין כְּלוּם, כָּךְ כָּל הָעֲבֵירוֹת אָז;
and when Hashem returns the captivity we shall be 'like dreamers,' for just as in a dream a man performs deeds that vanish upon awakening, so will all sins be seen then;
זוּלַת הַקֶּרִי שֶׁזֶּה גַּם כְּשֶׁהֵקִיץ יֵשׁ פְּעֻלָּה, וְכֵן כָּל הָעֲבֵירוֹת נִקְרָא כֵּן, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ],
save for nocturnal emission where even upon awakening a physical result remains, and likewise all sins are so termed, and this is not the place to elaborate,
וְכֵן כָּל הָעֳנָשִׁים נִקְרָא שָׁם "חֲמַת קֶרִי".
and likewise all the punishments are designated there as "the fury of happenstance (chamat keri)."
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁמַּאֲמִין שֶׁאֵין מִקְרֶה, מַמְתִּיק כָּל הַדִּינִים וּמְתַקֵּן כָּל הָעֲבֵירוֹת,
And by believing that there is no chance, he sweetens all strict judgments and rectifies all sins;
כִּי אִם כֵּן עַל כָּרְחֲךָ כֻּלָּם לֹא הָיוּ יוֹצְאִים מִן הַסֵּדֶר, וְהָיָה מְסוּדָּר כָּךְ וְלֹא בְּמִקְרֶה, וְאִם כֵּן אֵינוֹ עֲבֵירָה,
for if so, perforce none of them truly departed from divine order, but all was so orchestrated and not by chance, and if so, it was not an absolute rebellion,
וְעַל עָוֹן הַנִּזְכָּר הוּא תִּיקּוּן בְּיִחוּד:
and for this aforementioned sin of seminal emission it serves as a unique rectification.

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, On Book of Joshua 23, distinguishes God’s forgiving disclosure from the person’s acknowledgment of failure and dependence upon Him. The person must recognize sin and deficiency, including on renewed occasions of confession. Declaring on one’s own authority that there was no failure is itself a failure. This distinction accompanies Rav Tzadok’s retrospective account of providence: divine forgiveness does not replace the human work of recognizing and returning from sin.

paragraphs.text: See Tzidkat HaTzadik 40:1, which describes the illumination of repentance through the distinction between divine knowledge and human choice: both are true in their respective places. Its example is the scapegoat. An act that would be forbidden if undertaken independently becomes a mitzvah because God expressly commands it. The parallel explains retrospective transformation without erasing responsibility at the point of choice or making a person’s own declaration equivalent to a divine command.

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, Rosh Hashanah 18:2, describes a distorted form of Ashur’s belief that everything is in Heaven’s hands: using that assurance to pursue desire. The fault can lie at the root even when outward conduct appears unblemished. This provides a pointed qualification to the siman: recognition of providence in repentance must be distinguished from using it as encouragement to indulge.

sections.en: Perfect Covenant Guarding and the Promise of Life

p: [קנז] אִלּוּ הָיָה נִמְצָא אָדָם שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית כָּל יָמָיו בְּתַכְלִית שֶׁלֹּא נִתְכַּוֵּין מֵעוֹלָם בְּאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר לַהֲנָאָתוֹ, הָיָה חַי לְעוֹלָם,
Had there existed a person who guarded the Covenant throughout all his days to such perfection that he never once intended in that organ for personal pleasure, he would live forever,
וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כז): אִם יֹאמְרוּ לְךָ: אִלּוּ לֹא חָטָא אָדָם הָיָה חַי לְעוֹלָם? אֱמוֹר לָהֶם: הֲרֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ וְכוּלֵי.
as our Sages stated in Vayikra Rabbah (27:4): "If they say to you: Had Adam not sinned, would he have lived forever? Say to them: Behold, Elijah, etc."
וְאֵלִיָּהוּ נִקְרָא "מַלְאַךְ הַבְּרִית" כַּנּוֹדָע
And Elijah is designated the "Angel of the Covenant," as is known
[וּלְכָךְ אָמְרָה לוֹ אוֹתָהּ אִשָּׁה: בָּאתָ אֵלַי בִּתְשַׁמִּישׁ הַמִּטָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפִרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק לג;
and therefore that woman alleged to him: "You came to me in marital intimacy," as written in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 33;
וְיָדוּעַ כִּי כָּל שֶׁקֶר שֶׁאוֹמְרִים עַל אָדָם הוּא מַה שֶּׁאוֹתוֹ אָדָם מְיוּחָד לְטוֹבָה בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר,
and it is known that every falsehood spoken against a person targets the very matter in which that person is uniquely sublime for good,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְמֹשֶׁה: "וּמַדּוּעַ תִּתְנַשְּׂאוּ וְגוֹמֵר", וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה עָנָו וְגוֹמֵר".
as they accused Moses: "Why do you lift yourselves up, etc.," while Scripture testifies: "Now the man Moses was very humble, etc."
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יח): אוֹתוֹ תִּינוֹק – מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף;
And our Sages stated (Seder Eliyahu Rabbah 18): that child was Mashiach ben Yosef;
וְיָדוּעַ כִּי הוּא הַמְתַקֵּן אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר, דַּרְגָּא דְּיוֹסֵף,
and it is known that he is the one who rectifies that very trait, the rung of Joseph,
וּמִיתָתוֹ נִקְרָא: "וְהִבִּיטוּ אֵלַי אֵת אֲשֶׁר דָּקָרוּ" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֻכָּה (נב.),
and his death is referred to in: "and they shall look unto Me whom they have pierced" (Zechariah 12:10; Sukkah 52a);
וְחַד אָמַר: יֵצֶר הָרָע, וּשְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת, כִּי מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף דּוֹקֵר לְיֵצֶר הָרָע,
and one sage interprets this as the evil inclination, both being truth, for Mashiach ben Yosef pierces the evil inclination,
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין נְקִיִּים בָּזֶה, עַל יָדָם מַגִּיעַ מִיתָתוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
and because the people of Israel are not pristine in this realm, his death is brought about through them as I wrote elsewhere;
וְלָכֵן אָמְרָה: "מַדּוּעַ בָּאתָ... לְהַזְכִּיר אֶת עֲוֹנִי", וְהוּא הֶחֱיָהוּ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ].
and therefore she challenged: "Have you come to call my sin to remembrance?" (I Kings 17:18), and he revived him, and this is not the place to elaborate.
וְיִשַׁי מֵת בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ וְנִקְרָא "נָחָשׁ" בַּכָּתוּב (שְׁמוּאֵל ב יז, כה), רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁרַק דָּבָר זֶה הָיָה בּוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ,

And Jesse died solely through the counsel of the Serpent and was called "Nachash" (Serpent) in Scripture (II Samuel 17:25), meaning that only in this single trait was the root of the Serpent present in him,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עָלָיו (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ) עַל פָּסוּק "הֵן בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי",
as our Sages expounded concerning him (Midrash Rabbah, Tazria) on the verse "Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity" (Psalms 51:7);
וְנִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן בִּישַׁעְיָה: "מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ יֵצֵא צֶפַע וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה יד, כט) עַל מָשִׁיחַ.
and it is likewise said in Isaiah: "out of the serpent's root shall come forth a basilisk, etc." (Isaiah 14:29), referring to the Messiah.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּבֶן דָּוִד יִהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ זֶה, וְהוּא יִזְכֶּה לְחַיִּים דַּיְיקָא וְלֹא מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף,
That is, the Son of David will likewise issue from this lineage, yet he specifically will merit eternal life and not Mashiach ben Yosef,
כִּי רַק עַל יְדֵי תִּיקּוּן הַקִּלְקוּל יִהְיֶה הַחַיִּים, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תָּמִיד לב.): מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה אָדָם וְיִחְיֶה? יָמִית עַצְמוֹ.
for specifically through rectifying the damage will eternal life be attained, in the manner of: "What shall a man do to live? Let him slay himself" (Tamid 32a).
כִּידוּעַ דְּאִילָנָא דְּמוֹתָא נִקְרָא הָאָרֶץ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר בַּמִּדְבָּר קיט עַמּוּד א, בְּהַעֲלוֹתְךָ קנה עַמּוּד ב,
For as is known, the "Tree of Death" denotes the Supernal Earth (Malchut), as written in Zohar III:119a and 155b,
וְתִיקּוּנָהּ לְחַבְּרָהּ בְּבַעְלָהּ, עַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשֶׂה מֵאִילָנָא דְּמוֹתָא – אִילָנָא דְּחַיֵּי, וְלֹא בְּעִנְיָן אַחֵר.
and its rectification is to unite it with its Husband (Tiferet), through which the Tree of Death is transformed into the Tree of Life, and in no other way.
וְעַל יְדֵי קִלְקוּל הַבְּרִית מַגִּיעַ הַקִּלְקוּל בָּזֶה כַּנּוֹדָע בְּטַעַם "ה' צִלְּךָ",
And through blemishing the Covenant the rupture reaches this supernal union, as known regarding "Hashem is your shadow,"
וּלְכָךְ אֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה, הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אִם יְכֻפַּר הֶעָוֹן הַזֶּה לָכֶם עַד תְּמֻתוּן" (יְשַׁעְיָה כב, יד) בְּג' חִלּוּקֵי כַּפָּרָה שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל דּוֹרֵשׁ,

and therefore ordinary repentance does not avail, matching: "Surely this iniquity shall not be expiated by you till you die" (Isaiah 22:14) among the categories of atonement expounded by Rabbi Yishmael (Yoma 86a),
דִּשְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית נִקְרָא קִדּוּשׁ ה' בְּסוֹטָה (י:): יוֹסֵף שֶׁקִּדֵּשׁ שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וְכוּלֵי
for guarding the Covenant is termed sanctifying the Name of Hashem, as in Sotah 10b: "Joseph who sanctified the Name of Heaven, etc."
[כִּידוּעַ דְּשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם הוּא הֵ"א (שֶׁנִּיתּוֹסַף בְּיוֹסֵף) אַחֲרוֹנָה דְּשֵׁם שֶׁמּוֹסֵר עַצְמוֹ לָשֵׁם, שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּאֶרֶץ הַנִּזְכָּר],
for as is known, 'the Name of Heaven' is the final Hei of the Tetragrammaton added to Yehosef, wherein one surrenders himself unto that Name, which is the rung of the Supernal Earth,
וּבְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִדְרָשׁ מִכְּלַל הֵן – לָאו.
and in words of Torah, from the positive we infer the negative: violating it constitutes a desecration of the Name requiring death.
וְהָעֵצָה לָזֶה בַּזֹּהַר סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת בַּמִּדְבָּר (קכא עַמּוּד א): שֶׁיִּמְסוֹר נַפְשׁוֹ לְמִיתָה בְּלֹא רַמִיָּה, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
And the counsel for this is in the Zohar (end of Bemidbar 121a): that he surrender his soul unto death without deceit, see there.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַעֲנִית (ח:) מִקְּרָא דְּדָנִיֵּאל, דְּקַבָּלַת הַלֵּב בֶּאֱמֶת הָוֵי כְּמַעֲשֶׂה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לְחַיִּים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל

And that matches what is stated in Ta'anit 8b from the verse in Daniel, that the sincere acceptance of the heart is legally equivalent to action, and through this he merits eternal life as noted above
[אַךְ צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בֶּאֱמֶת, כִּי אִם יַחְשׁוֹב עַל יְדֵי זֶה לִזְכּוֹת בַּחַיִּים – אֵינוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת, וְאָז אַדְּרַבָּה סַכָּנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם בַּזֹּהַר.
yet it must be in total sincerity, for if he calculates through this to attain life, it is not genuine truth, and then on the contrary it invites mortal danger as written in the Zohar.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: אַל יִפְתַּח פִּיו לַשָּׂטָן, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפָרָשַׁת בְּהַעֲלֹתְךָ שָׁם גַּבֵּי מֹשֶׁה.
And that aligns with: 'A person should never open his mouth to the Satan,' and as written in Parashat Beha'alotekha regarding Moses.
וְהַיְינוּ לְפִי שֶׁשָּׁם מֹשֶׁה לֹא רָצָה בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן, שֶׁהֲרֵי בִּקֵּשׁ אַדְּרַבָּה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה טוֹבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ]:
For there Moses did not truly desire death, seeing that on the contrary he sought the welfare of Israel, and this is not the place to elaborate.

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 27:4 invokes Elijah’s continuing life as an example supporting the possibility that Adam could have lived forever had he not sinned. It then explains that future divine works already have partial precedents among the prophets. The Elijah comparison is the portion used here.

paragraphs.text: Radak on Malachi 3:1:4: ““The lord”—this is the King Messiah, and he is the angel of the covenant. Alternatively, “the angel of the covenant” refers to Elijah. Thus the aggadah says that Elijah was zealous for the covenant of circumcision, which the kingdom of Ephraim prevented them from observing, as it says: “I have been very zealous for the Lord, God of Israel, for the children of Israel have forsaken Your covenant.” He said to him: You were zealous at Shittim, and here you are zealous for circumcision. By your life, Israel will not perform circumcision without your seeing it with your own eyes. From this they established a seat of honor for Elijah, who is called the angel of the covenant, as it says: “The angel of the covenant whom you desire—behold, he comes, says the Lord of hosts.””

paragraphs.text: Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 33:3 records the bereaved widow’s accusation against Elijah and expressly presents it as false. In his prayer, Elijah attributes her words to grief and asks that the boy’s soul be restored, both to vindicate the truth and to demonstrate resurrection. God answers him, and he returns the living child to her. The false accusation is therefore part of the Midrash’s narrative, not a statement that the alleged act occurred.

paragraphs.text: Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 18:6 discusses Elijah’s descent and the objection that his request for the widow’s first portion appeared priestly. His answer identifies the child as a son of Joseph and speaks of his own descent to Babylonia before the coming of the son of David. Rav Tzadok reads this sequence messianically. The cited wording itself says son of Joseph; that distinction should be kept visible when following the interpretation here.

paragraphs.text: The two messianic roles and renewed life

rich.text: The two messianic roles and renewed life

paragraphs.text: Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 2:4, explains that Yosef’s holy power of opposing Esav belongs to the period when destructive forces remain. When death is abolished, that opposing power must also cease. Mashiach ben David then revives Mashiach ben Yosef as a renewed being, without the earlier rivalry. Israel’s effort to remove the serpent’s counsel indirectly brings about this transition. The passage thus connects, rather than merely equates, the deaths of Mashiach ben Yosef and the evil inclination.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 11:7: “Since Hashem's name was sanctified through King David's consequences and the greatness of his repentance, that act is truly considered a sanctification of Hashem, rather than a desecration. Nevertheless, he does not need death to complete the cleansing; on the contrary, through this he merits enduring life. In every passage of Torah one infers the affirmative from the negative: if desecration of the Name requires death for atonement, the good measure is greater, and sanctification of Hashem gives life.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Takanat HaShavin explains the positive counterpart of the siman's atonement language. Through David's repentance and its consequences, the Name is sanctified; the former desecration becomes part of that sanctification. The source therefore speaks of gaining enduring life. This clarifies why Rav Tzadok locates the life of the Davidic repair in transformed failure rather than in an untouched outward record alone.

sections.en: Surrendering One's Life in Thought and Beginning Anew

p: [קנח] עַל יְדֵי מְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ לְמִיתָה בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת גָּמוּר, שֶׁמַּסְכִּים בְּלִבּוֹ אִם רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְטוֹב לוֹ יוֹתֵר לָמוּת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, הוּא רוֹצֶה כָּךְ בְּרָצוֹן טוֹב – הוּא נִיצוֹל מִגְּזֵירַת מִיתָה רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן.

Through the surrender of one's soul unto death in his thought in absolute truth—wholeheartedly consenting that if it is the will of the Blessed Name and better for him to die, Heaven forbid, he desires it with goodwill—he is delivered from the decree of death, may the Merciful One preserve us.

כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל, שֶׁמַּחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ וְקַבָּלָתוֹ עַל עַצְמוֹ כְּמַעֲשֶׂה, וְהוּא אַחַר כָּךְ כְּאִלּוּ בָּא בְּגִלְגּוּל שֵׁנִי לְזֶה הָעוֹלָם, וְהוּא יֵדַע מַה שֶּׁקִּלְקֵל בְּגִלְגּוּלוֹ הָרִאשׁוֹן וְיָכוֹל לְתַקְּנוֹ בְּגִלְגּוּל זֶה.

As I wrote above, his thought and heartfelt acceptance are accounted as action, and subsequently he is as though he returned in a second reincarnation (gilgul) into this world, knowing what he corrupted in his first lifetime and empowered to rectify it in this reincarnation.
וְאֵין לְךָ שׁוּם עֲבֵירָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תִּיקּוּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה, כִּי הַמִּיתָה מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל הַכֹּל.
And you have no sin in the world that does not find rectification through this, for death atones for everything.
וְלָכֵן מִזְמוֹר דְּ"אֵלֶיךָ ה' נַפְשִׁי אֶשָּׂא" (תְּהִלִּים כה, א) מְסַיֵּים בִּנְפִילַת אַפַּיִם: "וְהוּא יִפְדֶּה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִכֹּל עֲוֹנֹתָיו" (שָׁם קל, ח)

And therefore the recitation of the psalm "Unto You, Hashem, do I lift up my soul" (Psalms 25:1) in the Tachanun supplication concludes with the added verse: "and He shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities" (Psalms 130:8)
[וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה דִּמְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ לְמִיתָה, הַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא כְּלֹא נֶחְשָׁב בְּעֵינֵי עַצְמוֹ, עַל יְדֵי זֶה דָּבוּק בְּאוֹתָהּ מַדְרֵגָה שֶׁנִּקְרָא "הוּא" כַּנּוֹדָע].
and through this surrender unto death, viewing himself as absolute nothingness, he cleaves unto that supreme level termed 'Hu' (He), as is known.
וּלְכָךְ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, הַגֶּבֶר שֶׁהֵקִים עוֹלָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, אָמַר דָּבָר זֶה.
And therefore King David, peace be upon him, the man who established the yoke of repentance, articulated this.

כִּי רָאשֵׁי הַיְצָרִים הֵם שְׁנַיִם: דַּעֲבֵירָה וּדְעַבוֹדָה זָרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹמָא (סט:) וּבְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה, וּמִשְּׁנֵיהֶם מִי שֶׁפּוֹרֵשׁ מֵת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (יז.);
For the foremost inclinations are two: that of unchastity and that of idolatry (Yoma 69b; Shir HaShirim Rabbah), and from both of them one who separates dies, as written in Avodah Zarah 17a;
וְזָכָה דָּוִד לְ"אֵלֶיךָ ה' וְגוֹמֵר", פִּדְיוֹן עַל הַמִּיתָה, וְ"חַיִּים שָׁאַל מִמְּךָ נָתַתָּה לּוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים כא, ה).
and David merited "Unto You, Hashem, etc.," achieving redemption from death: "He asked life of You, You gave it to him" (Psalms 21:5).
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי שְׁנֵי הַיְצָרִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים הֵם שְׁנֵי קְצוֹת שֶׁהֵם הָפְכִיִּים זֶה לָזֶה כַּנּוֹדָע, וְיוֹסֵף עָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן דַּעֲבֵירָה וְלֹא דָּוִד.
That is, because these two inclinations are two polar extremes opposing one another, and Joseph withstood the trial of unchastity while David did not.
וְהִנֵּה הַמִּשְׁפָּט מֵת בְּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף, וּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד הוּא לְהֵיפֶךְ;
And behold, the judgment of death befalls Mashiach ben Yosef, while Mashiach ben David experiences the reverse;

רַק דְּמִיּוֹסֵף יָצָא יָרָבְעָם שֶׁהוּא יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְדָבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם לְתַקֵּן רַק עַל יְדֵי בִּיטּוּלוֹ מִן הָעוֹלָם לְגַמְרֵי עַל יְדֵי אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה בְּטַעֲנַת "לָא הוּא וְלָא אַגְרֵיהּ".

only that from Joseph issued Jeroboam who personified the inclination for idolatry, which was impossible for human effort to rectify except through its complete eradication by the Men of the Great Assembly claiming: "Neither it do we desire, nor its reward" (Yoma 69b).
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יִצְרָא דַּעֲבֵירָה צָרִיךְ בָּעוֹלָם כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם, וּלְכָךְ אֵין מַגִּיעַ הַמִּיתָה, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ.
In contrast, the inclination for unchastity is necessary for the world's survival, which is why actual death is not mandated, and this is not the place to elaborate.

וּלְכָךְ זָכָה דָּוִד לְדַרְגָּא דִּמְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ לְמִיתָה בַּחַיִּים, שֶׁהוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי בִּיטּוּל יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶצְלוֹ לְגַמְרֵי, שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם כֹּחַ זוּלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמוֹסֵר עַצְמוֹ כֻּלּוֹ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְהַאֲרִיךְ עוֹד

And therefore David merited the level of surrendering his soul unto death during physical life, achieved solely through utterly nullifying the inclination for idolatry within himself, recognizing no power other than Hashem and surrendering himself entirely to the Blessed Name
[וּפִינְחָס זֶה אֵלִיָּהוּ מַלְאַךְ הַבְּרִית, וּבָא מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף שֶׁפִּטְפֵּט בְּיִצְרוֹ;
and Phinehas is Elijah the Angel of the Covenant, descending from the seed of Joseph who curbed his inclination;
רַק שְׁבָטִים בִּזּוּהוּ: מִזַּרְעָא דְּיִתְרוֹ שֶׁפִּטֵּם וְכוּלֵי – יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
yet the tribes degraded him: descending from Jethro who fattened calves for idols—the inclination for idolatry as noted above;
רַק הוּא מָסַר נַפְשׁוֹ לְמִיתָה בְּזִמְרִי, שֶׁאִלְמָלֵי נֶהֱפַךְ זִמְרִי וַהֲרָגוֹ וְכוּלֵי כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין פב.),
yet he surrendered his life unto death against Zimri, for had Zimri turned and slain him, etc. (Sanhedrin 82a),
וְלָכֵן זָכָה לִבְרִית שָׁלוֹם בְּאֵלִיָּהוּ דְּחַי לְעוֹלָם]:
and therefore he merited the Covenant of Peace in Elijah who lives forever.

paragraphs.text: Life renewed through a hidden bond

rich.text: Life renewed through a hidden bond

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, Shabbat Chol HaMoed Sukkot 33:1, compares repentance with the inward surrender of nefilat apayim and God’s restoration of life through a path hidden even from angels. An angel cannot perceive the continuity of the sinner’s connection to God; God Himself can reveal that continuity through repentance. This explains Moshe’s resistance to governance by an angel after the sin and gives context to the siman’s image of beginning life anew with knowledge of what needs repair.

rich.text: Sod Yesharim, Shabbat Chol HaMoed Sukkot 33:1

, compares repentance with the inward surrender of nefilat apayim and God’s restoration of life through a path hidden even from angels. An angel cannot perceive the continuity of the sinner’s connection to God; God Himself can reveal that continuity through repentance. This explains Moshe’s resistance to governance by an angel after the sin and gives context to the siman’s image of beginning life anew with knowledge of what needs repair.

paragraphs.text: Sichat Malakhei HaSharet, From Yerushalmi 16, explains that overcoming the impulse to idolatry had been a setting for open recognition of the Shekhinah. When the Great Assembly abolished that impulse, the corresponding open prophecy and revelation receded as well. Esther marks the transition from the open miracles recorded in Scripture to concealed miracles. This gives content to their renunciation of both the impulse and its reward, and distinguishes its history from that of bodily desire.

: ““My covenant of peace”—peace from the angel of death, as in “He makes peace in His heights,” for destruction occurs only through the opposition of contrary forces. This was indeed fulfilled in Phinehas, who lived far longer than the other men of his generation, until he served in the sanctuary at Shiloh at the time of the concubine at Gibeah. That was undoubtedly after the deaths of Joshua and the elders who outlived Joshua. All the more so if he was still living in Jephthah’s time, when Jephthah wrote to the Ammonite king that Israel had dwelt in Heshbon and its towns for three hundred years; our Sages related that Phinehas then refused to go to Jephthah to release his vow. And all the more according to the opinion that Elijah is Phinehas, who is still alive and enduring.”

paragraphs.text: Context: Sforno interprets the covenant of peace as protection from the opposing forces that cause mortality. His explanation includes both Phinehas’s exceptional longevity and the opinion identifying him with Elijah.

sections.en: One Soul's Repentance and the Awakening of Others

p: [קנט] יָחִיד שֶׁשָּׁב מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ וּלְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא פו:);
If a single individual repents, forgiveness is granted to him and to the entire world, as our Sages stated (Yoma 86b);
וְאֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר מְחִילָה? רַק שֶׁמְּעוֹרֵר בְּלִבָּם גַּם כֵּן הִרְהוּרֵי תְשׁוּבָה.
and how is such universal forgiveness possible? It is because he awakens in the hearts of others thoughts of repentance as well.
וְלֹא כָּל הָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת עַצְמוֹ יָחִיד בָּזֶה עוֹשֶׂה, כִּי לֹא הָיָה עֲדַיִן;
And not everyone who wishes to make himself that unique individual can do so, for such a figure has not yet arisen;
רַק מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד הוּא יִהְיֶה כֵּן, כִּי צָרִיךְ שֶׁתִּהְיֶה נַפְשׁוֹ כּוֹלֶלֶת מִכָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת,
only the Messiah son of David will be thus, for his soul must encompass all souls,
כִּי בְּלָאו הָכִי אֵין הִרְהוּרֵי תְשׁוּבָתוֹ יְכוֹלִים לְהוֹלִיד הִרְהוּרֵי תְשׁוּבָה בְּמִי שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְנַפְשׁוֹ.
since otherwise the stirrings of his repentance cannot generate repentance in those who have no affinity to his soul.
וְצָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הַהִרְהוּרֵי תְשׁוּבָה כּוֹלְלִים כָּל חֶלְקֵי נַפְשׁוֹ.
And those thoughts of repentance must encompass all facets of his soul.
כִּי מִי שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ, אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ לוֹ כָּל מִינֵי כֹּחוֹת שֶׁל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ,
For whoever encompasses the entire world contains within himself all the varied powers found in the entire world,
וְאִם שָׁב רַק בְּכֹחַ אֶחָד לְבַד, אֵין מְעוֹרֵר תְּשׁוּבָה רַק לְמִי שֶׁנִּתְלִים בְּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ.
and if he repents only within one single faculty, he awakens repentance only in those attached to that faculty.
כְּמוֹ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן כּוֹלֵל כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת, שֶׁהֲרֵי הוּא רֶגֶל ד' שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה, וְהֵקִים עוֹלָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה רַק בַּעֲוֹן תַּאֲוָה לְבַד.

Like King David, peace be upon him, who likewise encompassed all souls, being the fourth leg of the divine Chariot, yet who established the yoke of repentance specifically regarding the sin of passion alone.
וְלָכֵן יָרָבְעָם שֶׁהָיָה נָקִי בָּזֶה
And therefore Jeroboam, who was pristine in this regard

[כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁנִּקְרָא אֶפְרָתִי, שֶׁפֵּירוּשׁ שֵׁם זֶה: מִי שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה קֶרִי מִיָּמָיו, וְלָכֵן מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי אֲחִיָּה הַשִּׁילֹנִי שֶׁזֶּהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּשִׁילֹה יֵשׁ לוֹ יַחַס עִם שֵׁבֶט אֶפְרָיִם],

as I heard that he was called Efrati, meaning one who never experienced nocturnal emission, which is why he found favor in the eyes of Ahijah the Shilonite, Shiloh being connected to the tribe of Ephraim,
לֹא שָׁב וְנֶחְלַק עַל מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד.
did not repent, and rebelled against the Davidic monarchy.
וְזוּלַת הָאָבוֹת וְדָוִד לֹא הָיָה מִי שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ
And apart from the Patriarchs and David, there was no one who encompassed the entire world
[כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כּוֹלֵל רַק הַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁדּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר כֻּלּוֹ דּוֹר דֵּעָה וְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים].
for Moses our teacher encompasses solely Torah scholars, except that the Generation of the Wilderness was entirely a generation of knowledge and scholars.
וּשְׁאָר יְחִידִים שֶׁשָּׁבִים יֵשׁ לָהֶם יְכוֹלֶת לְהָשִׁיב רַק הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַתְּלוּיִים בָּהֶם [וּבְאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ שֶׁשָּׁבִים],
And other individuals who repent are empowered to awaken only those souls dependent upon them, and within that specific faculty in which they repent,
כְּאוֹתוֹ תַלְמִיד בִּמְנָחוֹת (מד.) שֶׁעַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ עוֹרֵר גַּם כֵּן הִרְהוּר תְּשׁוּבָה בְּאוֹתָהּ אִשָּׁה שֶׁהָיְתָה שַׁיָּיכֶת לוֹ, שֶׁהֲרֵי נַעֲשֵׂית אַחַר כָּךְ אִשְׁתּוֹ.
like that student in Menachot 44a whose repentance awakened a stirring of repentance in that woman who was soul-tied to him, becoming subsequently his wife.
וּמִי שֶׁמְּחוּיָּב מִיתָה בַּחֲטָאָיו, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְעוֹרְרוֹ בִּתְשׁוּבָה עַד שֶׁיִּמְסוֹר נַפְשׁוֹ לְמִיתָה גַּם כֵּן, שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַדְרֵגַת תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ, וְאָז יוּכַל לְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ תְּשׁוּבָה.

And one who is liable to death for his sins cannot be awakened to repentance until the tzadik surrenders his own life unto death as well, which matches his level of repentance, and only then can he stir repentance within him.
וּלְכָךְ פִּינְחָס עָצַר הַמַּגֵּפָה
Therefore Phinehas halted the plague
[שֶׁהוּא עוֹנֶשׁ הַמַּגִּיעַ לִזְנוּת – אַנְדְּרָלָמוּסְיָא, רַק שֶׁשָּׁבוּ]
which is the retribution visiting unchastity—indiscriminate destruction, save that they repented
עַל יְדֵי מְסִירַת נַפְשׁוֹ לְמִיתָה, וְעוֹרְרָם שֶׁשָּׁבוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גַּבֵּי מִלְחֶמֶת מִדְיָן.
through surrendering his life unto death, awakening them to repent as recorded concerning the war with Midian.
וְכֵן בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה סה) בְּעוּבָדָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה, שֶׁרַק כְּשֶׁהוֹלִיכוּהוּ לַצְּלָב, אָז עוֹרֵר בִּתְשׁוּבָה לְבֶן אֲחוֹתוֹ.
And so in Bereishit Rabbah (end of Parashah 65) regarding Rabbi Yose ben Yoezer of Tzreidah, that only when they led him to the gallows did he awaken his nephew Yakum to repentance.
וְכֵן מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן נָפְלוּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶם בְּעֵת מַחֲלוֹקֶת קֹרַח, שֶׁרָאוּ שֶׁנִּגְזַר עֲלֵיהֶם מִיתָה וּמָסְרוּ נַפְשָׁם לְמִיתָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר, וּכְדֵי לְהַעֲלוֹתָם בִּתְשׁוּבָה;

And so Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces during the rebellion of Korah, seeing death decreed upon them and surrendering their lives unto death, as written in the Zohar, in order to elevate them in repentance;
וְלֹא הוֹעִיל, לְפִי שֶׁהֵם נֶחְלְקוּ עָלָיו וְהִפְרִידוּ עַצְמָם מֵחִבּוּרָם בְּנַפְשׁוֹ, וּלְכָךְ לֹא פָּעַל הִתְעוֹרְרוּתוֹ בְּלִבָּם,
yet it did not avail because they rebelled against him and severed themselves from connection with his soul, so his spiritual awakening could not operate within their hearts,
כִּי בְּמִדָּה שֶׁאָדָם מוֹדֵד מוֹדְדִין לוֹ, וּבְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁרוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ מוֹלִיכִין אוֹתוֹ:
for with the measure a man metes out is it measured unto him, and in the way one desires to go, along that path they lead him.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 7:1: “Because all the souls together constitute one complete stature—the stature of Adam, within whom the souls of all his descendants were included, as the Midrash explains the verse “Where were you when I founded the earth”—even someone who returns to God with all his heart cannot rectify himself completely as long as all Israel have not returned as he has, so that the entire stature is rectified. As long as a single spark of that stature has not been fully rectified, its deficiency causes a deficiency in the whole stature.”
