paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Deuteronomy, Shoftim 15: “We find that Ahijah the Shilonite anointed Jeroboam as king because Ahijah came from Shiloh, from Joseph’s tribe. Of Jeroboam too it is written, “an Ephratite,” for he was very refined and careful concerning “You shall not commit adultery,” which is Joseph’s inheritance. This was not found in Judah: of Solomon it is written, “He married,” and so forth, while of King David it is written, “The son of an Ephratite man.” Therefore Ahijah was very pleased to anoint him. Afterward, when Jeroboam sinned with the two golden calves, Ahijah prayed to God concerning this error. God then showed him that his love had been directed only toward Abijah son of Jeroboam, in whom something good was found.”

paragraphs.text: Divrei Soferim 10:2: “The Ari’s teaching concerning the statement in Shabbat and elsewhere, “Moses, you have spoken well,” is known: every Sage of the generation is called Moses. The straightforward meaning is that he is like Moses our teacher in his generation and stands in his place. The Zohar in Ekev states that Moses our teacher shines in every generation. paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 6:2, reads the response to Rabbi Yosei ben Yoezer’s words and Yosef Meshita’s return as disclosures of a heart still bound to holiness beneath earlier betrayal. The other person’s own will becomes active, rather than forgiveness being transferred mechanically. This develops the awakening described in the siman, whose stated limits remain the connection between particular souls and faculties; universal completion belongs to Mashiach.

sections.en: The Soul's Influence on Those Within Its Care

p: [קס] הָאָדָם נַפְשׁוֹ כּוֹלֶלֶת מִכָּל נַפְשׁוֹת מְשָׁרְתָיו וְהַנִּכְנָעִים תַּחְתָּיו,
A person's soul encompasses the souls of all his servants and those subordinate to him,
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ: "מֹשֵׁל מַקְשִׁיב עַל דְּבַר שָׁקֶר, כָּל מְשָׁרְתָיו רְשָׁעִים" (מִשְׁלֵי כט, יב), וְאָמְרוּ בְּחֻלִּין (ד:): הָא עַל דְּבַר אֱמֶת וְכוּלֵי.
which is why Scripture states: "If a ruler hearkens to falsehood, all his servants are wicked" (Proverbs 29:12), from which Chullin 4b infers: but if he hearkens to truth, his servants are righteous.

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה עֹבַדְיָה גַּם כֵּן מִמְּשָׁרְתֵי אַחְאָב, לְפִי שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קב:): אַחְאָב וַתְּרָן בְּמָמוֹנוֹ הָיָה, וּלְכָךְ עֹבַדְיָה עַל הַבַּיִת, שֶׁבָּזֶה הָיָה כִּשְׁרוֹנוֹ.
Nonetheless Obadiah was among the stewards of Ahab, because Sanhedrin 102b states: Ahab was generous with his money, and therefore Obadiah presided over his household, where his financial virtue lay.
וּמִצַּד הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ בְּוַתְּרָנוּת הָיָה עֹבַדְיָה.
And from the element of good within Ahab's generosity stemmed his connection to Obadiah.
וְכֵן כָּל אֶחָד שֶׁמּוּרְכָּב מִטּוֹב וָרָע, כֵּן מְשָׁרְתָיו: וְהַטּוֹב הוּא מְמוּנֶּה עַל הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ, וְכֵן לְהֵיפֶךְ.
And so with every person composed of good and evil, so are his attendants: the good is appointed over his good traits, and the evil over his bad.
וְכֵן כָּל הַחֲפָצִים, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר הַמַּאֲכָלִים שֶׁל הָאָדָם, הוּא מֵהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כֹּחַ נַפְשׁוֹ וְחַיּוּתוֹ בָּהֶם, וּמִזֶּה הוּא חַיּוּתָם כַּיָּדוּעַ.

And so with all possessions, and it goes without saying a person's food, which derive from the extension of his soul-power and vitality within them, from which they receive their vitality as is known.
וּמִמָּקוֹם שֶׁהוּא טוֹב, כָּךְ כָּל כֵּלָיו הַמִּתְפַּשְּׁטִים מֵאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ, וְכֵן הַמַּאֲכָלִים שֶׁמֵּאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ יֵשׁ בָּהֶם קְדוּשָּׁה גְּדוֹלָה.
And from whatever source within him is good, so are all his utensils extending from that power, and likewise the food deriving from that power contains immense holiness.
וְזֶה טַעַם גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "עַל כֵּן לֹא יֹאכְלוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לב, לג), שֶׁמֵּאַחַר שֶׁהַמַּלְאָךְ יָכֹל לוֹ שָׁם, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דְּיֵשׁ שָׁם חִסָּרוֹן בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ

And this is the inner reason of the sciatic nerve (gid hanasheh), concerning which it is said: "Therefore the children of Israel eat not, etc." (Genesis 32:33), for since the angel could prevail against Jacob there, infer that there existed a deficiency in the spiritual root
[וְהַיְינוּ בַּתַּאֲוָה דְּשָׁם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: אֲפִילּוּ חָסִיד וְכוּלֵי],
namely in the bodily desire situated there, as I wrote elsewhere on the rabbinic dictum: 'even the most pious, etc.';

וּלְכָךְ אֵין לֶאֱכוֹל גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה, דִּמְקוֹם חַיּוּתוֹ מִגִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה דְּאָדָם, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (מד עַמּוּד ב): נֶפֶשׁ מְשִׁיב אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ, כִּי יֵשׁ שָׁם חַיּוּת מֵאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר.

and therefore one must not eat the sciatic nerve, for the food's vitality would nourish the sciatic nerve of the human body, in line with Berakhot 44b: soul restores soul, drawing vitality into that organ.
[וְטַעַם דָּם – כִּי "הַדָּם הוּא הַנָּפֶשׁ" (דְּבָרִים יב, כג), שֶׁעִיקַּר חֵטְא בַּנֶּפֶשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "נֶפֶשׁ כִּי תֶחֱטָא" (וַיִּקְרָא ה, א) כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
And the prohibition of blood is because 'the blood is the life' (Deuteronomy 12:23), the root of sin lying in the animal soul, as in 'if a soul sins' (Leviticus 5:1).

וְכֵן עִיקַּר הַחֵטְא כְּעִנְיַן "שָׁמַנְתָּ עָבִיתָ וְגוֹמֵר" (דְּבָרִים לב, טו), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "יָצָא מֵחֵלֶב עֵינֵמוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים עג, ז) וּבְכָל מָקוֹם, וְלָכֵן אָסוּר חֵלֶב, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ]:

And likewise the essence of sin arises from indulgence, as in 'you grew fat, thick, etc.,' and 'their eyes stand out with fatness,' which is why forbidden animal fat (chelev) is prohibited, and this is not the place to elaborate.

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Vayishlach 10:1, explains the righteous person’s care for property through its source in God’s gift: because he takes nothing belonging to others, he recognizes his possessions as connected with the root of his life. This illuminates the present account of possessions extending a person’s faculties. The siman itself distinguishes good and bad within a mixed person, so the relation does not make every possession or use of it holy automatically.

paragraphs.text: Ramban on Leviticus 4:2:1: ““When a soul sins inadvertently”: Because thought belongs to the soul, and it is the soul that errs, “soul” is mentioned here. Therefore the soul that sins inadvertently brings an offering, so that it may merit drawing near to the God who gave it. For this reason too, “soul” is mentioned.”

p: [קסא] כְּשֶׁאָדָם מִתְיַסֵּר בְּאֵיזֶה אֵבֶר אוֹ בְּאֵיזֶה כֹּחַ מִכֹּחוֹתָיו
When a person experiences suffering in a particular limb or in a specific faculty among his spiritual powers
כִּי ע' כֹּחוֹת בַּנֶּפֶשׁ נֶגֶד ע' אֻמּוֹת בָּרָע כַּיָּדוּעַ],
for there are seventy faculties in the soul corresponding to seventy nations in evil, as is known,
מִסְּתָמָא בּוֹ חָטָא,
presumably through it he sinned;
וּמִיָּד שֶׁלָּקָה, הֲרֵי הוּא כְּאָחִיךָ, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַכּוֹת כג.)
and the moment he is afflicted with lashes, behold he is restored as your brother, as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Makkot 23a)
וַאֲפִילּוּ רַק כְּפָתוּהוּ וְכוּלֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמַכּוֹת (שָׁם),
and even if they merely bound him to be lashed, etc., as written in Makkot there,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קכא:) בְּנָחָשׁ שֶׁהָיָה רוֹדֵף אַחֲרָיו, כִּי בָּזֶה יָצָא יְדֵי עוֹנְשׁוֹ וְיִסּוּרִין שֶׁלּוֹ בַּפַּחַד שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁיִּשְּׁכֶנּוּ;
and as in Shabbat 121b regarding a snake that was pursuing a person, for through that alone he fulfilled his punishment and suffering via the mortal terror that it would bite him;
וְכֵן הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת דְּמִן הַשָּׁמַיִם נִזְדַּמְּנוּ וְכוּלֵי כִּדְאִיתָא הָתָם,
and so it was in truth that from Heaven it was orchestrated, as brought there,
רַק שֶׁחָסוּ עָלָיו וּפְדָאוּהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַפַּחַד, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נה.): חֶלְמָא בִּישָׁא וְכוּלֵי,
only that they showed compassion upon him and redeemed him through that terror, along the lines of Berakhot 55b regarding a distressing dream whose anguish suffices,
כִּי כְּשֶׁשָּׁב בֶּאֱמֶת, אָז כָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא כְּחוֹלְמִים;
for when one truly repents, all worldly experiences become like dreamers;
וְאָז אוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר וְכֹחַ מְתוּקָּן, וְנֶפֶשׁ מֵשִׁיב אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ, שֶׁאוֹתוֹ אֵבֶר יֵשׁ בּוֹ תִּיקּוּן, אֶלָּא שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהוֹסִיף וּלְחַזְּקוֹ.
and then that limb and faculty are spiritually rectified, and soul restores soul, seeing that within that limb rectification now resides, only that one must further strengthen and fortify it.
וְאָז "בִּמְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם לֹא עַמִּי אַתֶּם יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם בְּנֵי אֵל חָי]" (הוֹשֵׁעַ ב, א) – דַּיְיקָא בְּאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם הוּא מַמָּשׁ לְהֵיפֶךְ:

And then "in the place where it was said unto them: 'You are not My people,' there it shall be said unto them: 'You are the children of the living God'" (Hosea 2:1)—specifically in that exact spot is it transformed into the literal opposite.

rich.text: Yosef turns fear toward his own repair

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 20:4, applies the snake-and-scorpion passage to Yosef in the pit. Their presence prompts him to examine his reports about his brothers: the snake is linked with the covenant and appetite, and the scorpion with bloodshed and the cruelty of eating a limb from a living animal. Recognizing that he too required clarification, Yosef repents. The parallel gives a concrete account of fear leading to repair of the corresponding faculties.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 15:86 places Hosea 2:1 within the dispute in Kiddushin 36a. Rabbi Yehudah links Israel’s designation as children to their conduct; Rabbi Meir maintains it even when conduct is deficient. Rav Tzadok cites Responsa Rashba I, 124 and 212, in support of Rabbi Meir’s view, and points to Israel’s designation as God’s firstborn before the Exodus. The siman’s reversal can thus disclose an enduring bond rather than create an unrelated identity.

paragraphs.text: The cry that remains in concealment

rich.text: The cry that remains in concealment

paragraphs.text: Tiferet Yosef, Bamidbar 1, teaches that even when a person perceives no connection to God, a path of return remains. Concern for Heaven’s honor can itself become the cry that opens that path: the person asks how God’s great name will be revealed through Israel’s service. This parallels the siman’s conclusion that the very place of apparent rejection becomes the place where renewed sonship is disclosed.

p: מִכָּל עֲבֵירָה נַעֲשָׂה מַלְאָךְ רַע כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה,
From every transgression an evil angel is formed, as our Sages of blessed memory taught,
זֶהוּ לְטוֹבָה לִבְנֵי אָדָם,
and this is actually for the benefit of human beings;
שֶׁהַמַּלְאָךְ הוּא חַיּוּת רוּחָנִי, וְהוּא מַכִּיר בַּאֲמִתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְחָפֵץ שֶׁיִּתְהַפֵּךְ לְטוֹב,
for the angel is spiritual vitality, and it recognizes the truth of Hashem, blessed be He, and yearns to be transformed into good,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְעוֹרֵר הָאָדָם לִתְשׁוּבָה.
and through this the person is aroused to repentance.

p: שֶׁהִרְהוּרֵי תְשׁוּבָה הוּא כְּשֶׁנִּזְכַּר כְּאִילּוּ הַחֵטְא וַעֲבֵירָה שֶׁעָשָׂה עוֹמֶדֶת לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו וּמִתְמַרְמֵר עָלֶיהָ,
For reflections of repentance occur when one remembers, as though the sin and transgression he committed stands directly before his eyes, and he feels bitter contrition over it;
וְהוּא הַמַּלְאָךְ שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה עַל יָדוֹ
and this is the very angel created through him
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ב, ב): "רָאָה וַיַּתֵּר גּוֹיִם" – שֶׁהִתִּיר לָהֶם, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוֹלְכִים לַאֲבַדּוֹן],

and therefore they taught (Avodah Zarah 2b): ''He saw and released (vayater) the nations'—that He permitted them the seven Noahide laws, and through this they head toward destruction'—meaning because no accusing angels were created to stir them to repentance,
וְאֵין לְךָ עֲבֵירָה שֶׁל אָדָם שֶׁלֹּא הִרְהֵר עָלֶיהָ בִּתְשׁוּבָה,
and there is no transgression committed by a man of Israel over which he did not reflect with repentance,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: "פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְלֵאִים חֲרָטוֹת",
as our Sages of blessed memory said: 'The sinners of Israel are full of remorses,'
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הָעֲבֵירָה עַצְמָהּ.
and this remorse is generated through the agency of the transgression itself.

paragraphs.text: Tzidkat HaTzadik 241:1: “A person’s commandments and good deeds—and certainly words of Torah—bring good thoughts into his heart; transgressions bring the opposite, as our Sages say, “One commandment draws another, and a transgression, and so forth.” The meaning of this drawing is that an angel is created from every commandment: that is, a spiritual power. As the Zohar states, no deed or speech of a person, good or evil, is lost. Through this good angel, which belongs to him, was born of his action, and dwells near him—for the angel is spiritual, like human thought—a thought falls into his heart to perform other commandments.”

p: וְעַל יְדֵי הוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה מַרְבֶּה מַזִּיקִים רַחֲמָנָא לִיצְלַן יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הָעֲבֵירוֹת כַּיָּדוּעַ מִזֹּהַר,
And through the sin of nocturnal emission/wasting seed, a person multiplies harmful spirits, may the Merciful One preserve us, more than through all other transgressions, as is known from the Zohar;
לְכָךְ גַּם כֵּן הִרְהוּרֵי תְשׁוּבָה שֶׁנּוֹפְלִים בְּלִבּוֹ הֵם הַרְבֵּה.
therefore, the reflections of repentance that fall into his heart are likewise very numerous.
וְכָל עִיקַּר עִנְיַן הָעֲבֵירוֹת הוּא רַק לְעוֹרֵר הָאָדָם לִתְשׁוּבָה עַל יְדֵי זֶה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל,
And the fundamental underlying reason for the existence of transgressions is solely to awaken a person to repentance through them, as mentioned above;
כִּי יֵשׁ אִימָּא עִילָּאָה וְאִימָּא תַּתָּאָה,
for there exist Imma Ila'ah (Supernal Mother - Binah/Repentance) and Imma Tata'ah (Lower Mother - Malchut/Prayer),
הַיְינוּ תְּשׁוּבָה וּתְפִלָּה,
namely Repentance and Prayer,
שֶׁעַל יָדָם הוּא הַכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵיךְ הוּא שׁוֹכֵן בְּקִרְבּוֹ,
through which one attains recognition of Hashem, blessed be He, how He dwells within him;
וּתְפִלָּה הִתְעוֹרְרוּתָהּ עַל יְדֵי מִצְווֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים,
and prayer's awakening occurs through mitzvot and good deeds,
וּתְשׁוּבָה עַל יְדֵי עֲבֵירָה.
whereas repentance is awakened specifically through transgression.
אֲבָל תּוֹרָה הוּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא עַצְמוֹ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ.
However, Torah is the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself, and this is not the place to elaborate.

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 7:12–16, distinguishes the quantity of harmful forces from the way vitality is bound within them. Vitality lost through wasted seed can rise through proper repentance and focused bedtime Shema. In forbidden relations it is more deeply bound, requiring repentance from great love that transforms sins into merits. If a mamzer has been conceived, the passage says that this vitality is already embodied in a living person and cannot be retrieved in that manner, even through such repentance. The limitation concerns the recovery of vitality, not whether the sinner can repent. This preserves the distinctions behind the siman’s comparison of harmful spiritual forces.

However, the ultimate perfection of Malchut, which consists of the absolute recognition of human lack and deficiency,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא לִתְשׁוּבָה שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִכָּל ז' יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן,

and its culmination will be: 'Then all shall recognize the power of Your sovereignty.'

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 15:79 distinguishes the disappearance of sins from the disappearance of sinners. Israel’s root remains attached to God even when conduct produces the appearance of rejection. Hoshea is therefore directed to seek mercy for the people rather than assume that another nation can replace them. The reversal from rejection to sonship reveals the enduring root once sin is removed. This explains what the rope image preserves through injury and division, while directing repair toward the removal of wrongdoing.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 50:2 develops the rope image: one end is bound above to Yaakov’s image, while the lower end includes even the lowest sinners. An individual’s repentance draws others upward, each according to the strength of that influence and the recipient’s level. Rav Tzadok distinguishes this shared awakening from the separate dispute between Rabbi and the Sages over complete Yom Kippur atonement for those who do not repent. The collective effect is therefore not identical with unconditional complete atonement.

paragraphs.text: Each individual retains a distinct task

rich.text: Each individual retains a distinct task

paragraphs.text: Tiferet Yosef, Bamidbar 2, reads Hosea’s numberless multitude alongside the significance of each counted person. God assigns each soul a particular service that another cannot perform in its place, as an expression of His desire to benefit creation. From God’s own side nothing is lacking, and all particulars are included in His unity. This complements the siman’s division of the common rope: unity and an individual’s irreplaceable work coexist.

paragraphs.text: Machshavot Charutz 15:9: “For they said in Avodah Zarah 5a: “Had Israel not sinned, we would not have come into the world”; the conclusion is, “as though we had not come into the world.” That is, all Jewish souls are rooted in the Torah, and as the Oral Torah is renewed in the hearts of Israel’s sages in each generation, so are the souls renewed in each generation. Had our ancestors merited that everything be revealed to all Israel within the Written Torah, so that they all grasped every renewal of the future generations, there would have been no place for the renewal of souls. Although souls would still have emerged into actuality in the world, it would have been “as though we had not come,” because everything would already have been included in the ancestors, openly actualized for all, with nothing new.”

And therefore, even in the section of admonition and in other passages dealing with sins, the term 'Vehayah' is employed, which always denotes joy,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה מב),
as our Sages of blessed memory expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 42:3),
כִּי צֵירוּף "וְהָיָה" הַבָּנִים קוֹדְמִים לָאָבוֹת, כַּיָּדוּעַ,
for in the letter-permutation of 'Vehayah'
(ו-ה-י-ה),
the children (Vav-Hei) precede the parents (Yud-Hei), as is known,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל מְנַצְּחִים לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם,
meaning that Israel triumphs over their Father in Heaven,
וְזֶהוּ שִׂמְחָה בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת.
and that constitutes joy across all worlds.
וְכֵן עַל יְדֵי הָעֲבֵירוֹת כִּבְיָכוֹל "נִצְּחוּנִי בָּנַי" לַעֲבוֹר עַל רְצוֹנִי,
And so through transgressions, as it were, 'My children have defeated Me' (Bava Metzia 59b) in transgressing My explicit will,
כְּשֶׁיִּגָּלֶה לֶעָתִיד זֶה שֶׁהַכֹּל לְטוֹבָה,
when it is unveiled in the ultimate future that all was for the good;
וְאֵין מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ עוֹד.
and there is no room to elaborate further.

sections.en: The Hidden Greatness of the Penitent

p: [קסד] בְּדַעַת בְּנֵי אָדָם אֵין הַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה כְּמוֹ הַצַּדִּיק גָּמוּר,
In human perception, a penitent (ba'al teshuvah) is not equal to a wholly righteous person (tzadik gamur),
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הַחֲטָאִים שֶׁעָשָׂה כְּבָר חֲשׁוּבִים כִּזְכִיּוֹת,
and it goes without saying that the sins he committed previously would not be considered as merits,
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמַּאֲמִין בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוּ כִּזְכִיּוֹת,
even though one believes in the words of our Sages that willful sins become like merits (Yoma 86b),
וְגַם אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת לד:): "בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵי"
and they also said (Berakhot 34b): "In the place where penitents stand, the wholly righteous cannot stand"
וּמַאן דִּפְלִיג, הַיְינוּ בְּעִנְיַן הַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבִיאִים, דְּמָר יָלֵיף מִקְּרָא דִּ"לָרָחוֹק וְלַקָּרוֹב" שֶׁהוּא בַּנְּבִיאִים, וּלְדַעְתּוֹ אֵינוֹ כֵן מִצַּד הַנְּבוּאָה.

and the one who disputes this does so regarding the comprehension of the prophets, where one master derives from the verse 'to him that is far off and to him that is near' (Isaiah 57:19) which is among the prophets, and in his view it is not so from the side of prophecy.
דְּצַדִּיק גָּמוּר – "עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה", שֶׁזֶּהוּ רַק מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
For concerning the wholly righteous it is said 'no eye has seen' (Isaiah 64:3), which is exclusively from the side of the Blessed Name.
אֲבָל תְּשׁוּבָה שַׁיָּיכוּת לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, רַק הוּא כְּטַעַם: לֹא זָז מֵחַבְּבָהּ עַד שֶׁקְּרָאָהּ אִמִּי, שֶׁגְּדוֹלָה מִמֶּנּוּ, וְעוֹד דְּבָרִים בְּגוֹ, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ.

But repentance belongs to the Congregation of Israel, which mirrors: He did not cease cherishing her until He called her His mother, which is greater, and there are deeper matters within this, and this is not the place to elaborate.
וְהַיְינוּ לְפִי שֶׁהַתְּשׁוּבָה נִקְרָא עָלְמָא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא, וְאֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה לִבְנֵי אָדָם הַיְקָרוּת וְהַיּוֹפִי שֶׁבָּהּ.
And this is because repentance is termed the Concealed World (alma de-itkasya), and its inner preciousness and beauty are not visible to ordinary human beings.
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל, נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ: "כִּי שְׂנוּאָה לֵאָה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, לא), וְעַיֵּין בַּזֹּהַר הַטַּעַם.
And of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who is the root of all Israel, it is stated: "that Leah was hated" (Genesis 29:31), and see the Zohar for the inner reason.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכג.) שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים: הַגְּדוֹלָה לַגָּדוֹל וְכוּלֵי,
That is, as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Bava Batra 123a) that people would say: the elder daughter is for the elder son, etc.;
הַיְינוּ לְפִי הַנִּגְלֶה שַׁיָּיכֶת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְחֵלֶק עֵשָׂו, וְהָיְתָה בּוֹכָה – זֶהוּ סוֹד הַתְּשׁוּבָה.
meaning according to outward appearance she seemed linked, Heaven forbid, to the portion of Esau, and she wept—and this weeping is the mystical secret of repentance.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן רָחֵל: "יְפַת תֹּאַר וִיפַת מַרְאֶה", שֶׁהַכֹּל אוֹמְרִים: הַקְּטַנָּה לַקָּטָן, כִּי בְּעָלְמָא דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא יֵשׁ בָּהּ יֹפִי מַעֲשִׂים.

In contrast, Rachel was "beautiful of form and fair to look upon," where all said: the younger daughter is for the younger son, for in the Revealed World (alma de-itgalya) she possessed manifest beauty of deeds.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, עִיקַּר תּוֹלָדוֹת מִשֶּׁל לֵאָה, שֶׁעִיקַּר הַהוֹלָדָה, הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּנְפָשׁוֹת לִרְצוֹן ה', הַכֹּל עַל יְדֵי מַדְרֵגַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה.

Nevertheless, the primary offspring issued from Leah, for the essence of true spiritual generation—innovating words of Torah and birthing holy souls for the will of Hashem—is entirely through the spiritual rung of repentance.

וּבֶאֱמֶת הִיא אִמּוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (זוּטָא פֶּרֶק ה) דְּאֵין לְךָ מִדָּה טוֹבָה וְדָבָר טוֹב בָּא לִבְנֵי אָדָם אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי עֲנִיּוּת – פֵּירוּשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
And in truth she is his mother, as written in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta (chapter 5) that no worthy trait or good thing comes to human beings except through poverty—meaning poverty in words of Torah,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּגִטִּין (מג.) עַל פָּסוּק "וְהַמַּכְשֵׁלָה וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁאֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד וְכוּלֵי,
as our Sages taught in Gittin 43a on the verse "and let this ruin be under your hand" (Isaiah 3:6), that a person does not master Torah unless he has stumbled in it,
וְעַל יְדֵי הָעֲבֵירָה וְהַתְּשׁוּבָה נוֹלָד הַחַיּוּת אַחַר כָּךְ.
and through the sin and the subsequent repentance, authentic spiritual vitality is born afterward.
אַךְ סָנֵי בַּר נָשׁ עֶרְיַין דְּאִמֵּיהּ, וּמִטֶּבַע הָאָדָם שֶׁשּׂוֹנֵא הַתְּשׁוּבָה עַל הָרַע;
However, a person naturally disdains his mother's nakedness, and by nature man dislikes repenting over evil;
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקָּר שֶׁהֶעֱמִידוֹ עַל מַה שֶּׁהוּא, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין חָפֵץ לִדְבַּק בָּזֶה.
and even though this repentance is the very foundation that established him as what he is, he nevertheless has no desire to cleave to it.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין אִשָּׁה אֶלָּא לְבָנִים, וְהַתּוֹלָדוֹת רַק מִלֵּאָה
But in truth, a wife is chosen primarily for children, and the true progeny derived from Leah
וְגָרַם עַד "וַתְּקַנֵּא רָחֵל וְגוֹמֵר", לְפִי שֶׁזֶּה עִיקָּר.
and this reality led to "And Rachel envied her sister" (Genesis 30:1), because this fruitfulness was paramount.
וְכָל כָּךְ כֹּחַ הַקִּנְאָה שֶׁהוֹעִיל, שֶׁאָז עָמְדָה לֵאָה מִלֶּדֶת, דִּפְסוּק "וַתְּקַנֵּא וְגוֹמֵר" נֶאֱמַר שָׁם עַיֵּין שָׁם,
And so potent was the force of this envy that Leah ceased bearing, for the passage of 'And Rachel envied' was recorded there, see there,
וְלֹא יָלְדָה עַד שֶׁאָמַר לָהּ רָחֵל: "לָכֵן יִשְׁכַּב וְגוֹמֵר", וְסִילְּקָה קִנְאָתָהּ.
and she did not bear again until Rachel told her: 'Therefore he shall lie with you tonight,' and removed her envy.

וְכֵן דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהֵקִים עוֹלָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, נֶאֱמַר: "וְסָרָה קִנְאַת אֶפְרַיִם וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה יא, יג) – זַרְעָא דְּרָחֵל, וְהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּצַדִּיק כַּיָּדוּעַ,

And likewise King David, peace be upon him, who established the yoke of repentance, concerning him it is said: 'The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, etc.' (Isaiah 11:13)—Ephraim representing the seed of Rachel and the rung of the tzadik as is known,
וְהוֹעִיל לַחֲלוֹק מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד, שֶׁזֶּה חִסָּרוֹן בְּעֶצֶם מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד לְפִי שָׁעָה, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ:
which had the effect of dividing the Davidic monarchy, an essential temporary blemish in the kingdom of the House of David, and this is not the place to lengthen.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86b:3: “Reish Lakish said: Great is repentance, for a person’s deliberate sins become like inadvertent sins, as it is said, ‘Return, Israel, to Hashem your God, for you have stumbled through your iniquity.’ Iniquity is deliberate wrongdoing, yet the verse calls it stumbling. Is that so? But Reish Lakish also said: Great is repentance, for deliberate sins become like merits, as it is said, ‘When a wicked person turns from his wickedness and practices justice and righteousness, through them he shall live.’ There is no contradiction: repentance out of love makes the sins into merits; repentance out of fear makes them into inadvertent sins.”

paragraphs.text: Yisrael Kedoshim 7:2 distinguishes the height reached through repentance from God’s primary desire for righteous conduct. By raising holy sparks from low places and turning darkness into light, a penitent can attain exceptional closeness in a moment. Nevertheless, Torah was given to guide the person created upright, and the Midrash’s preference for light means that righteous conduct remains God’s principal desire. The penitent’s eventual elevation does not make sin an aim.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 7:3 interprets the daughter–sister–mother parable through the development of Malchut from a point into the complete feminine stature. The Congregation of Israel is the final level capable of clothing itself in this physical world, where the Divine Presence is to dwell. Yet that final fulfillment was the original purpose of creation: the end of the deed was first in thought. When Israel reaches completion, the last recipient is therefore called mother, the source of the unfolding that was directed toward her from its beginning. This is the mystical reversal assumed in the present siman.

paragraphs.text: Takanat HaShavin 6:7 distinguishes the public claim that the elder daughter belonged with the elder son from Leah’s inward rejection of Esav’s deeds. Rachel’s children oppose Esav as good opposes evil; Leah’s distinction lies in the heart’s repudiation of the root of those deeds, even when outward appearance suggests resemblance. Rav Tzadok relates this inward refusal to Judah’s rejection of idolatry. The parallel explains hidden spiritual fruitfulness without treating visible failure itself as a virtue.

sections.en: The Unique Stature and Ascent of Each Soul

p: [קסה] הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל כָּל אֶחָד מַדְרֵגָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
The souls of Israel each constitute an independent, unique spiritual level,
כִּי אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹשֶׂה שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים שָׁוִים מַמָּשׁ, דְּאִם כֵּן מַה צֹּרֶךְ לִשְׁנַיִם
for the Blessed Name never makes two things completely identical, since if so, what need would there be for two?
וְעוֹד בְּרוּחָנִיִּים, בַּמֶּה יִתְחַלֵּק אֶחָד מִשְּׁנַיִם אִם לֹא בְּחִלּוּק מַדְרֵגָה?
Moreover, in spiritual entities, through what could one be distinguished from another if not through a difference in level?
וְכָל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת קוֹמָה אַחַת שְׁלֵימָה, וְכֵן כָּל נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִית קוֹמָה שְׁלֵימָה,
And all souls together form one complete cosmic stature, and likewise each individual soul is itself a complete stature;
נִמְצָא יֵשׁ לְכָל נֶפֶשׁ לַעֲלוֹת בְּמַדְרֵגוֹת כְּמִסְפַּר הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
consequently, every soul must ascend through levels corresponding to the total number of the souls of Israel.
וְעִיקַּר הַיְגִיעָה לְהַגִּיעַ עַד מַדְרֵגַת עַצְמוֹ,
And the primary toil is to reach the rung of oneself,
דְּהַיְינוּ מִמֶּנּוּ מִמְּקוֹם נַפְשׁוֹ בַּקּוֹמָה הַכְּלָלִית] וּלְמַטָּה, מִסּוֹף הַכֹּל עַד מַדְרֵגָה שֶׁלּוֹ.
meaning from where he stands the station of his soul within the collective stature downward, from the very lowest point up to his own inherent level.
אֲבָל מִמֶּנּוּ וּלְמַעְלָה, שֶׁכְּבָר יָצְאוּ נְפָשׁוֹת שְׁלֵימוֹת מִמַּדְרֵגוֹת הָהֵם
But from his level upward, where perfected souls from those higher rungs have already emerged into the world
כִּי הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת הוֹלְכִים מִמַּעְלָה לְמַטָּה, וְאָנוּ הַיּוֹם בְּעִקְּבוֹת מָשִׁיחַ מִן הָעִקְבִיִּים,
for the generational levels descend from above to below, and we today in the footsteps of the Messiah stem from the heels,
עִיקָּר בַּעֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁאָדָם דָּשׁ בַּעֲקֵבָיו וּשְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית, וְכֵן הַמִּצְווֹת וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לָצֵאת מִן הַהֶרְגֵּל,
where the primary struggle lies in sins a person treads upon with his heels and guarding the Covenant, as well as breaking habitual routine in mitzvot,
יֵשׁ לוֹ סַיַּעְתָּא גְּדוֹלָה מֵאוֹתָם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁכְּבָר יָצְאוּ,
he possesses immense Heavenly assistance from those souls who have already lived,
שֶׁכְּשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לַמַּדְרֵגָה שֶׁל כָּל אֶחָד בַּקּוֹמָה הַכְּלָלִית], הוּא בָּא וּמְסַיְּיעוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בְּסוֹד הָעִבּוּר.
for when he reaches the level of each soul in the collective stature, that soul comes and assists him, as I wrote elsewhere concerning the mystery of spiritual impregnation (ibbur).
כִּי אוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת שֶׁל מַדְרֵגָה זוֹ כְּבָר נִשְׁאַר בָּעוֹלָם
For that power of spiritual effort belonging to that level has already remained in the world
עַל יְדֵי הַהֶבְלָא דְּגַרְמֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר],
through the spiritual vapor of the bones, as I wrote elsewhere,
וְאֵין צָרִיךְ יְגִיעָה כָּל כָּךְ רַק עַד לוֹ
and one does not need such exhausting labor once he reaches his own level
וְזֶה סוֹד מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טו.): לֹא עָלָה עֶזְרָא מִבָּבֶל עַד שֶׁיִּחֵס עַצְמוֹ].
and this is the secret of Bava Batra 15a: Ezra did not ascend from Babylonia until he traced his lineage.
וְלָכֵן בְּדוֹרוֹת אֵלּוּ אֵין צָרִיךְ יְגִיעָה כָּל כָּךְ כִּבְדוֹרוֹת רִאשׁוֹנִים, וְנָקֵל לָבוֹא לְמַדְרֵגוֹת מִיָּד שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגַת עַצְמוֹ.
Therefore in these latter generations one does not require as much exertion as in the early generations, and it is easy to attain higher levels the moment he reaches his own inherent level.
אֲבָל לְעֻמַּת זֶה הָיָה מַעֲלַת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים שֶׁהָיוּ מִמָּקוֹם יוֹתֵר גָּבוֹהַּ,
However, corresponding to this was the great virtue of the early generations who stemmed from a much loftier place,
וְכָל כָּךְ מַכְבִּיד עָלֵינוּ הַיֵּצֶר אוֹתָהּ יְגִיעָה מוּעֶטֶת בְּדוֹרֵנוּ כְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הַמְּרֻבָּה שֶׁלָּהֶם:
and the evil inclination weighs down upon us regarding that small exertion in our generation just as heavily as it did upon their immense striving.

Head, body, and feet receive differently. The Congregation of Israel likewise forms one complete stature, with souls corresponding to its various organs; each apprehends according to its position. Thus a person is a complete individual stature while also occupying a particular place within the collective, the framework for the ascent described here.

paragraphs.text: Sha’ar HaGilgulim 15:2 describes redemption as the gathering of souls and sparks from the powers of impurity, extending from head to feet. The final gathering reaches the feet, but it depends on the deeds, prayers, and repentance of those below. Complete repentance could enable their release at once, whereas sin weakens that process. The image therefore includes human responsibility and does not describe an automatic completion without effort.

paragraphs.text: Freedom from habitual bondage

rich.text: Freedom from habitual bondage

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 26:5, calls an apparently inescapable habit a personal Egyptian bondage. Accepting Torah as higher than worldly constraints, and impressing it through speech and action, brings freedom until even bodily response follows it. The Yerushalmi’s account of the head bowing at Modim without conscious direction illustrates that settled response. This explains the work of leaving habit, while the siman’s account of help from earlier souls remains a distinct matter.

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 15:9–11, explains the difference between reviewing one hundred times and one hundred and one. In the customary system, the first hundred followed habit; the extra repetition broke beyond it and could outweigh the rest as active service. Like travel beyond a hired driver’s usual distance, it requires a different measure of exertion. The intermediate person masters habitual nature by awakening love of God through contemplation, or by arousing the hidden love already in the heart. The distinction concerns effort against one’s accustomed nature, not the number alone.

paragraphs.text: Sha’ar HaGilgulim 1:12–13 explains assistance through ibbur as the entry of enduring aspects of righteous souls into one seeking to serve God. The highest attained spirit remains bound in the bond of life at its fitting root, as do the higher soul levels; it does not leave that place. Earlier aspects that remained at lower levels can descend to assist another person. This distinction between the soul’s highest attainment and its enduring lower aspects is essential to the account of assistance here.

paragraphs.text: In Sha’ar HaGilgulim 38:154, Rabbi Chayim Vital asks the Ari how his soul could be esteemed so highly when his deeds seemed below those of earlier generations. The Ari answers that attainment must be weighed against the obstacles of one’s time: a small deed amid the greater strength of impurity can equal many great deeds in another generation. The comparison with Noah in his generations supports this contextual measure. It explains the siman’s final qualification that apparently smaller exertion can still involve a formidable struggle.

p: [קסו] כְּשֶׁהָאָדָם מְקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ עוֹל תּוֹרָה וְנִכְנָס תַּחַת עֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, צָרִיךְ קַבָּלָה בַּלֵּב וְהַסְכָּמָה גְּמוּרָה לַעֲזוֹב כָּל חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַמִּתְנַגְּדִים לִרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,

When a person accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah and enters under the service of the Blessed Name, he requires an internal acceptance in the heart and complete resolve to abandon all worldly desires that conflict with the will of the Blessed Name,
וְלֹא לֶאֱחוֹז בָּזֶה וְגַם מִזֶּה אַל יַנַּח יָדוֹ, שֶׁאָז זֶה וְזֶה לֹא עָלְתָה.
and not grasp onto this while also failing to withdraw his hand from that, for then neither the one nor the other will succeed.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (יוֹמָא עב:): לֹא זָכָה – נַעֲשֵׂית וְכוּלֵי, כִּי גַּם תּוֹרָה אֵין לוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יְבָמוֹת קט:).
And concerning this it was stated (Yoma 72b): if he does not merit, it becomes a deadly potion, for he does not truly possess Torah either (Yevamot 109b).
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּעֵשָׂו: "וַיִּשְׁמַע עֵשָׂו] כִּי רָעוֹת בְּנוֹת כְּנָעַן וְגוֹמֵר וַיֹּסֶף וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, ח–ט),
And just as was said regarding Esau: "And Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father... and he took Mahalath, etc." (Genesis 28:8–9),
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה סז): כּוֹב עַל כּוֹב, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
and our Sages expounded in Bereishit Rabbah (end of Parashah 67): adding misery upon misery, see there.

וְהַיְינוּ מֵאַחַר שֶׁלֹּא גֵּירַשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת, רַק כִּמְבַקֵּשׁ לָצֵאת יְדֵי יִצְחָק גַּם כֵּן וְלִקַּח גַּם שֶׁלֹּא מִבְּנוֹת כְּנַעַן, אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֶחֱזִיק גַּם הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת, לְכָךְ נֶהֶפְכָה לוֹ גַּם זֶה לְרֹעַ.

That is, since he did not divorce the first wives, but merely sought to satisfy Isaac by also taking a wife not from the daughters of Canaan while still retaining the former wives, this marriage likewise turned to wickedness for him.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נֶאֱמַר בַּתּוֹרָה "אָנֹכִי" קוֹדֵם לְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ",
Nevertheless, in the Torah "I am Hashem your God" precedes "You shall have no other gods,"
כִּי אֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַדַּאי מֵ"אָנֹכִי" יָבוֹא לְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" וְסוֹפוֹ לְרַחֵק;
for among the children of Israel, from "I am" one will certainly arrive at "You shall have no," and he will ultimately distance all evil;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (פְּסָחִים נ:): לְעוֹלָם יַעֲסוֹק וְכוּלֵי שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ וְכוּלֵי.
and as written in Pesachim 50b: a person should always engage in Torah even not for its own sake, for from not for its own sake he will come to its own sake.
וְהַתּוֹסָפוֹת הִקְשָׁה מַה שֶּׁמָּצִינוּ בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹסֵק שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ נוֹחַ לוֹ וְכוּלֵי, וְשֶׁנֶּהֶפְכָה וְכוּלֵי, וְלֹא זָכָה נַעֲשֵׂית וְכוּלֵי.

And Tosafot challenged this from what we find elsewhere, that whoever engages in Torah not for its own sake, it would have been better had he not been created, and it is overturned, and if he did not merit it becomes a potion of death.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת שְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת: וְכָל הָעוֹסֵק וְכוּלֵי, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ דְּשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ נוֹחַ וְכוּלֵי וְנַעֲשֵׂית וְכוּלֵי,
But in truth both are truth: whoever engages in Torah, even though he knows that studying not for its own sake invites severe warnings,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא מְקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ כָּל זֶה, כִּי חָשְׁקָה נַפְשׁוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה,
he nonetheless accepts all this upon himself because his soul passionately yearns for the Torah;
וּמַה יַּעֲשֶׂה אִם אֵין לִבּוֹ שָׁלֵם וּמְנוּקֶּה מִכָּל רַע וּפְנִיּוֹת וְחֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה עֲדַיִן?
and what shall he do if his heart is not yet completely whole and cleansed of all base motives and worldly desires?
בְּאַהֲבָתָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה יִשְׁגֶּה, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ הַסַּכָּנָה וְהָרָע שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ,
In the love of Torah let him be enraptured (Proverbs 5:19), even though he knows the spiritual danger involved;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲסוֹק וְכוּלֵי, וִיקַבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ כָּל זֶה, לְפִי שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ וְכוּלֵי, וְאָז יָשׁוּב הַכֹּל לְטוֹב:
nonetheless, let him always engage in Torah and accept all this upon himself, because from not for its own sake he will come to its own sake, and then everything will be transformed to good.

paragraphs.text: Imperfect motives and irreverent study

rich.text: Imperfect motives and irreverent study

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 6:2 distinguishes ordinary study for mixed motives from study that turns wisdom’s strength into levity, arrogance, and skill in wrongdoing. The latter attracts the severe warnings; ordinary shelo lishmah need not produce that irreverence. Study for Heaven’s sake instead increases fear and care in action. This provides a criterion for the present tension: beginning with an imperfect heart is joined to the willingness to let Torah change one’s conduct.

Another explanation: a thorn upon a thorn, an addition to an already full house.”

Its preceding favorable interpretation of Esav’s intention is retained, followed by Rabbi Elazar’s criticism that the earlier wives were not sent away. Rav Tzadok uses that criticism to explain why accepting Torah must be joined to abandoning incompatible desires.

paragraphs.text: An opening for subsequent purification

rich.text: An opening for subsequent purification

paragraphs.text: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Bo 5, asks why I am Hashem precedes the rejection of other gods, when turning from evil would ordinarily come first. In divine mercy, the initial encounter is given before complete purification, which no person could confidently claim. It opens the way for the heart’s subsequent clarification. This supports beginning Torah with mixed motives while intending to leave contrary desires; it does not support retaining them as Esav retained his earlier wives.

paragraphs.text: Tosafot on Pesachim 50b:5:1: ““Here it concerns those who act not for its own sake, in accordance with Rav Yehudah”: This is difficult, for Rav himself said in the second chapter of Berakhot that anyone who engages in Torah not for its own sake would have been better off not being created. Ri explains that there it concerns someone who studies to exalt himself, provoke others, and defeat his fellows in halakhic argument, without studying in order to practice. Here, however, it resembles the earlier case of one who is lowly yet rewarded: he does not work all week, nor on the eve of Shabbat. He intends no evil, but acts from laziness; even so, “Your kindness is great, up to the heavens.””

paragraphs.text: An imperfect beginning directed toward lishmah

rich.text: An imperfect beginning directed toward lishmah

paragraphs.text: Peri Tzadik, Toldot 10:1, relates the statement that one would have been better uncreated to the broader debate about human creation. Service like Yaakov’s, for God’s sake, fulfills creation’s purpose; study begun with mixed motives can lead there. Rav Tzadok uses this to resolve that particular severe expression, but expressly retains Tosafot’s distinction as necessary for other warnings. The eventual aim explains continued learning without dissolving all cautions about its motive and effect.

sections.en: Reverent Fear and the Purification of Torah Study

p: [קסז] בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מוּתָּר אָדָם לִפְחוֹד, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרָכוֹת (ס.);
Regarding words of Torah a person is permitted to feel fear, as our Sages of blessed memory stated in Berakhot 60a;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּפְחַד שֶׁמָּא הוּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם סַם הַמָּוֶת, וְעַל יְדֵי הַפַּחַד עַצְמוֹ מִתְמַתֵּק וְנַעֲשָׂה "מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ – לִשְׁמָהּ".
meaning that he should fear lest it become for him a potion of death, and through that very fear it is sweetened and transformed from "not for its own sake" into "for its own sake."
כִּי "הַאי מַאן דִּמְבַעִית – מַזָּלֵיהּ חָזֵי" (מְגִילָּה ג.),
For "one who is frightened, his guardian star (mazal) sees it" (Megillah 3a),
וְהוּא דּוּגְמַת חֲלוֹם דְּגַם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁמַּזָּלוֹ רוֹאֶה,
and this is analogous to a dream which also reflects what one's mazal sees,
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת נה.): חֶלְמָא בִּישָׁא – עֲצִיבוּתֵיהּ מִסְתַּיֵּיהּ, הַיְינוּ שֶׁבַּעֲצִיבוּת עַצְמוֹ דַּי.
and our Sages stated (Berakhot 55b): for a bad dream, the sorrow it causes suffices as its atonement.
וְכֵן בְּעִנְיַן תּוֹרָה: "שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם נַעֲשֵׂית וְכוּלֵי", וְדַי בָּזֶה מַה שֶּׁהוּא מְפַחֵד בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
And likewise regarding Torah: "if he did not merit, it becomes a potion of death," and it suffices that he experiences this reverent dread over words of Torah.
וּ"פִקּוּדֵי ה' יְשָׁרִים מְשַׂמְּחֵי לֵב" (תְּהִלִּים יט, ט), וְ"הַחָכְמָה תָּעֹז לֶחָכָם" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, יט), וְכֵן בִּשְׁאָר פְּסוּקִים שֶׁנּוֹתֶנֶת עֹז וְחֶדְוָה שֶׁהוּא הִפּוּךְ הַפַּחַד.

And "The statutes of Hashem are right, rejoicing the heart" (Psalms 19:9), and "Wisdom strengthens the wise" (Ecclesiastes 7:19), and so throughout verses testifying that Torah grants strength and joy, which is the antithesis of fear.
רַק רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אָמְרוּ: "לְעוֹלָם יַעֲסוֹק אָדָם שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ וְכוּלֵי",
However, our Sages stated: "A person should always engage in Torah not for its own sake, etc.,"
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי דָּבָר זֶה הוּא "לְעוֹלָם", פֵּירוּשׁ בִּתְמִידוּת;
and that is because this condition is "always"—meaning in continuous daily routine;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַלִּשְׁמָהּ אִי אֶפְשָׁר כְּלָל לִהְיוֹת בִּתְמִידוּת, דְּלִשְׁמָהּ הַיְינוּ דְּבֵיקוּת,
whereas pure study for its own sake cannot possibly be continuous, since lishmah denotes absolute meditative cleaving (devekut),
וְשִׁעוּרוֹ כְּעוֹנַת תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אַחַת בְּשַׁבָּת, שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לָבוֹא לִדְבֵיקוּת רַק בְּשַׁבָּת,
whose frequency is like the conjugal time of Torah scholars once a week, for one cannot reach such devekut except on Shabbat,
אוֹ הַטַּיָּילוֹן פֵּירוּשׁ הַמְטַיְּילִים בַּפַּרְדֵּ"ס הַיָּדוּעַ] אַחַת בַּיּוֹם לְכָל הַיּוֹתֵר.
or for spiritual wanderers meaning those strolling in the mystical Orchard once a day at most.

אֲבָל בִּתְמִידוּת הוּא שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, רַק שֶׁ"מִּתּוֹךְ וְכוּלֵי" – פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ הַלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ עַצְמוֹ, מִתּוֹכוֹ וּפְנִימִיּוּתוֹ, הוּא בָּא לִהְיוֹת אוֹתוֹ לִמּוּד עַצְמוֹ לִשְׁמָהּ;
But continuous study is technically not for its own sake, except that "from within it he comes to its own sake"—meaning from within the interior of that study itself it comes to be for its own sake;
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי הַפַּחַד דִּמְפַכְּחָא לֵיהּ, שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: "אִי יִרְאַת ה' אוֹצָרוֹ – אִין וְכוּלֵי",
and that is through the reverent fear that sobers him, concerning which they said: "If the fear of Hashem is his storehouse, yes, etc.,"
וְזֶהוּ "אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם מְפַחֵד תָּמִיד" (מִשְׁלֵי כח, יד) – פֵּירוּשׁ עַל עִסְקוֹ הַתְּמִידוּת,
and this is "Praiseworthy is the man that fears always" (Proverbs 28:14)—meaning regarding his continuous study,
דְּוַדַּאי לִפְרָקִים מַגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגַת הַדְּבֵיקוּת שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לִפְחוֹד כְּלָל.
for certainly at designated times he reaches the level of devekut where he does not need to fear at all.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ח.): "אַשְׁרֶיךָ" – בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דִּלְשׁוֹן אִישּׁוּר מַשְׁמָע מֵאֲחֵרִים מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לְשׁוֹן "וְטוֹב לָךְ",
And our Sages stated (Berakhot 8a): "praiseworthy are you" refers to this world, for praise (ashrekha) implies acclaim recognized by others unlike the phrase "and it shall be good with you",
וְזֶהוּ רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, דִּבְעוֹלָם הַבָּא כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ עוֹלָם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה נב).
and this applies only in this world, for in the World to Come each individual possesses a world of his own (Shemot Rabbah 52).
וּבֶאֱמֶת לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ כְּלָל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, וְכִדְאָמְרוּ בִּזְבָחִים (ב:): סְתָמָא לִשְׁמָן קָיְימָא.
And in truth, Torah does not fundamentally admit "not for its own sake," as they stated in Zevachim 2b: by default offerings stand for their own sake.
רַק דִּלַאֲחֵרִים יֵשׁ טַעֲנוֹת, כִּי עַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּרִים בַּתּוֹרָה נִתְגַּבֵּר כֹּחַ הַדִּבּוּר בָּעוֹלָם,
Only that other observers raise accusations, for through words of Torah the power of speech is energized in the world,
וּלְפִי שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם יֵשׁ דִּבּוּרִים דְּלָשׁוֹן הָרָע וְגַם כֵּן מִתְגַּבְּרִים, וְיוּכְלוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְדַבֵּר "חֵץ שָׁחוּט לְשׁוֹנָם" עָלָיו
and since in the world evil speech exists and also gains strength, people might speak "their tongue is a sharpened arrow" against him
שֶׁזֶּה עִנְיַן דָּוִד שֶׁהוּא סוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, הָיוּ דוֹרוֹ בַּעֲלֵי דִּלְטוֹרְיָא וְדִבְּרוּ לָשׁוֹן הָרָע עָלָיו],
which was the situation of David who embodies the Oral Torah, whose generation contained slanderers speaking evil against him,
וּלְזֶה הָעֵצָה – פַּחַד, שֶׁהוּא הַצִּמְצוּם, וּמִצְטַמְצְמִים כֹּחוֹתָיו וְאֵין מִתְפַּשְּׁטִים לַחוּץ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וְהָאִישּׁוּר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אָז:
and the remedy for this is holy fear, which constitutes constriction (tzimtzum), concentrating his faculties so they do not disperse outward, and then praise is affirmed in this world.

paragraphs.text: Awe distinguishes holy intensity from the inclination’s fire

rich.text: Awe distinguishes holy intensity from the inclination’s fire

paragraphs.text: The concern accompanying Torah study directs its energy against the yetzer hara rather than allowing that energy to become self-assertion.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 7:1: “The Gemara expounds “Why is there a price in the hand of a fool?” concerning those who engage in Torah but have no awe of Heaven. The anger of the sages is to stir against the evil inclination so that one will not be a fool. This comes through awe, Isaac’s fear, holy fire; its waste is Esau—anger, the evil inclination’s fire. This is according to the Geonim’s reading.”

rich.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok ·
Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 7:1

: “The Gemara expounds “Why is there a price in the hand of a fool?” concerning those who engage in Torah but have no awe of Heaven. The anger of the sages is to stir against the evil inclination so that one will not be a fool. This comes through awe, Isaac’s fear, holy fire; its waste is Esau—anger, the evil inclination’s fire. This is according to the Geonim’s reading.”

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Kislev distinguishes the fire of holy awe from its waste, anger, even while discussing the intensity of the sages. This sharpens the present siman’s explanation of why fear can sweeten learning that is not yet wholly lishmah. Awe governs the direction of the energy released by Torah and gathers it toward service. It is therefore compatible with Torah’s strength and joy, while checking the misuse of those powers that the siman fears.

sections.en: Transforming Fear into Joy Through Fear of Heaven

p: [קסח] הַפְּחָדִים שֶׁל הָאָדָם הוּא מִן הַחֲטָאִים, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ס.), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "פָּחֲדוּ בְצִיּוֹן חַטָּאִים" (יְשַׁעְיָה לג, יד);
A person's fears arise from sins, as our Sages stated in Berakhot 60a, and as written: "The sinners in Zion are afraid" (Isaiah 33:14);
וְהַפְּחָדִים הֵם מַמָּשׁ יִסּוּרֵי גֵיהִנָּם, עַיֵּין רַאֲבַ"ד עַל סֵפֶר יְצִירָה בְּעִנְיַן יִסּוּרֵי גֵיהִנָּם.
and fears are literally the afflictions of Gehenna, see the Ra'avad on Sefer Yetzirah regarding the afflictions of Gehenna.

וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא הַמְתָּקַת הַדִּינִים, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם ה. וְזֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, קנג סוֹף עַמּוּד א): מַה מֶּלַח מְמַתֶּקֶת הַבָּשָׂר, אַף יִסּוּרִין מְמַתְּקִין הָעֲווֹנוֹת.
And this experience constitutes the sweetening of judgments, as our Sages stated (ibid. 5a; Zohar III:153a): just as salt sweetens meat, so suffering sweetens sins.
וְהַחֲטָאִים וְהַדִּינִים וְהַיִּסּוּרִים הַכֹּל דָּבָר אֶחָד, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טז.): יוֹרֵד וּמַסִּית, עוֹלֶה וּמַקְטְרִיג, יוֹרֵד וְנוֹטֵל נְשָׁמָה.
And sins, strict judgments, and afflictions are all one single entity, as our Sages stated (Bava Batra 16a): he descends and incites, ascends and accuses, descends and takes the soul.
וַהֲרֵי אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה נ): אֵין מַלְאָךְ אֶחָד עוֹשֶׂה שְׁתֵּי שְׁלִיחוּת, הַיְינוּ דְּהַמַּלְאָךְ נִקְרָא כֹּחַ אוֹתוֹ דָּבָר
And behold, our Sages stated (Bereishit Rabbah 50): a single angel does not perform two missions, meaning that the angel is the specific metaphysical power of that thing
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמוֹרֶה נְבוּכִים, וְיַצִּיבָא מִילְּתָא גַּם מִטַּעַם חַכְמֵי הָאֱמֶת בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר],
and as written in the Moreh Nevukhim, and this is confirmed likewise by the Kabbalists as I wrote elsewhere,
וְכָל כֹּחַ וָכֹחַ מְיוּחָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
and every force is distinct in its own right.
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּזֶה הַכֹּל עִנְיָן אֶחָד: וּבְעוֹלַם הַכִּסֵּא שֶׁשָּׁם מֶלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא דִּין נִקְרָא "דִּינִים",
So perforce all of this is one unified dynamic: in the World of the Throne where the King sits upon the Throne of Judgment it is called "judgments,"
וּבְעוֹלַם הַמַּלְאָכִים נִקְרָא "חֲטָאִים", כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה א, ו): מַתִּישׁ כֹּחַ פַּמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה;
and in the World of Angels it is termed "sins," as our Sages stated (Midrash Rabbah, Eichah 1:6): it weakens the Heavenly Host;
וּלְמַטָּה – "יִסּוּרִים".
and down below in this world it is called "afflictions."
וְהַמְתָּקַת הַחֲטָאִים הוּא הַמְתָּקַת הַדִּינִים.
And sweetening sins is identical to sweetening judgments.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה, אָז נַעֲשֶׂה הַמְתָּקַת הַדִּינִים בְּשָׁרְשָׁם,
And through repentance, the sweetening of judgments occurs at their very root,
כִּי הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכֹּל בַּלֵּב, וְעִיקַּר תְּשׁוּבָה בַּלֵּב – זֶה נִקְרָא הַמְתָּקָה בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ.
for the root of all is in the heart, and the essence of repentance is in the heart—which is termed sweetening at the root.
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן הַפַּחַד בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה דְּשָׁרֵי, שֶׁמְּפַחֵד עַל מַה שֶּׁעָבַר עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
And this is likewise the permitted fear in words of Torah, where one fears having transgressed words of Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּעֶזְרָא שֶׁהָעָם רָעֲדוּ מְאֹד עַל הָעֲבֵירָה, וְלֹא שֶׁמְּפַחֵד מִפְּנֵי מִילֵּי דְּעָלְמָא – זֶהוּ "אַשְׁרֵי";
as written in Ezra (10:9) that the people trembled exceedingly over the transgression, and not that he fears worldly affairs—this is praiseworthy;
כִּי הוּא הַמְתָּקָה בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ, דְּאִתְהֲפֵיךְ מְרִירוּ לְמָתוֹק, שֶׁהַפַּחַד עַצְמוֹ שִׂמְחָה,
for it is a sweetening at the root, transforming bitterness into sweetness, where the fear itself becomes joy,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג): אֲנִי שָׂמַחְתִּי מִתּוֹךְ יִרְאָתִי;
as written in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 3): "I rejoiced out of my fear";
וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק בְּיִרְאַת ה', אֲבָל בִּשְׁאָר יְרָאוֹת רַק מֵבִיא לִידֵי שִׂמְחָה אַחַר כָּךְ:
and this is possible only within the fear of Hashem, whereas with other fears it merely brings to joy afterward.

paragraphs.text: Kometz HaMinchah 2:46:1 contrasts Avimelech’s melancholy fear with Yitzchak’s reverence born from love and directed by Torah. The relevant exchange is in Berakhot 60a: ordinary fearful anxiety is rebuked, while the praise of constant fear is explained as concern for words of Torah. That answer does not recast the student’s sinful fear as Torah study. The supplied reference to HaNizakin is inaccurate. This distinction clarifies why the siman’s praiseworthy fear turns a person toward God and can itself be joined to joy.

paragraphs.text: Ra'avad on Sefer Yetzirah, Introduction, The Fifty Gates of Understanding 2:3:1-2: “The heat of illness becomes material for the heat of elemental fire. When the soul departs from the sick person’s body, it reaches the element of fire through the imaginative faculty, which received its impression from the pain and heat of the illness. That elemental fire adheres to this soul, adding heat to its heat, until the fire descending from the river of fire reaches it and rests upon that fire. Further, the storm of Hashem—fury and whirling anguish—descends upon it, resting on the head of the wicked. The same applies to one who dies from cold: judgments and punishments from snow and hail attach to him, “for the day of battle and war.””

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 50:2 teaches that one angel does not perform two missions and two angels do not perform one mission. It explains the arrival of two angels at Sodom by distinguishing their tasks: Michael had delivered his tidings and departed, Gabriel came to overturn Sodom, and Raphael to rescue Lot. This distinct assignment of powers is the point used here; the Midrash’s subsequent explanations of why the visitors are called men or angels concern a separate question.

sections.en: Anticipating Distress with Prayer and Sweetening Its Root

p: [קסט] כַּאֲשֶׁר נוֹפֵל עַל אָדָם פַּחַד מֵאֵיזֶה דָבָר, אָז תֵּיכֶף יְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים לְהִנָּצֵל מִזֶּה,
When fear of something falls upon a person, let him immediately plead for mercy to be saved from it,
כִּי לְכָךְ עוֹרְרוּהוּ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם בְּפַחַד זֶה,
for this very purpose did Heaven awaken him through this fear,
כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד:): לְעוֹלָם יַקְדִּים אָדָם תְּפִלָּה לַצָּרָה;
as our Sages stated (Sanhedrin 44b): "A person should always anticipate distress with prayer";
וּמִנַּיִן יוֹדֵעַ קוֹדֶם מִן הַצָּרָה? רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְעוֹרֵר עַל יְדֵי הַפַּחַד.
and whence does he know beforehand of the distress? The Blessed Name awakens him through fear.
כִּי יֵשׁ דִּינָא קַשְׁיָא שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַמְתִּיק אַחַר צֵאתוֹ לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם, רַק צָרִיךְ לְהַמְתִּיקוֹ בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ בְּעוֹדוֹ בְּבֶטֶן אִמּוֹ.
For there exists harsh judgment (dina kashya) which cannot be sweetened after it emerges into the world, but must be sweetened at its root while still in its formative gestation.
דְּמַזָּל הוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ כַּיָּדוּעַ וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר, וּמַזָּלֵיהּ חָזֵי מַה שֶּׁהוּא בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲדַיִן וּמִיבְעִית.
For one's mazal is the root as is known, and his mazal perceives what is still in the root, and he becomes frightened.
וּבִתְפִלָּה מַמְתִּיק בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ עַד שֶׁיֵּצֵא אַחַר כָּךְ טוֹב
And through prayer he sweetens it at the root until it subsequently emerges as good
וְזֶה עִנְיַן יְמֵי אֱלוּל שֶׁהוּא ל' יוֹם לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, שׁוֹאֲלִין וְדוֹרְשִׁין בְּעִנְיָנוֹ, דְּל' יוֹם מִקּוֹדֶם הוּא זְמַן הַהֲכָנָה.
and this is the significance of the days of Elul, thirty days before Rosh Hashanah when we inquire into its themes, for thirty days prior is the period of preparation.
וְיָדוּעַ דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה נִקְרָא "הַיּוֹם הֲרַת עוֹלָם", שֶׁהוּא הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁעָלָה לִבְרוֹא בְּמִדַּת הַדִּין, דְּהַיְינוּ סוֹף מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהוּא עֵת קֵץ וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And it is known that Rosh Hashanah is called 'the day of the world's conception,' which represents the initial Thought to create with strict Judgment—meaning the ultimate end, the World to Come,
שֶׁאָז יִהְיֶה יִצְחָק רֹאשׁ הַהַנְהָגָה כַּנּוֹדָע, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כָּל מִינֵי טוֹבָה בְּדִין, זֶה הָיָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה.
when Isaac will head the governance, when all goodness will be awarded by strict justice, which was in Thought first.

וּלְהַמְתִּיק גַּם הַדִּינִים דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה בְּשָׁרְשָׁם, שֶׁהוּא עֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַנִּקְרָא מַזָּלָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר], מַקְדִּימִים בֶּאֱלוּל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל.
And to sweeten even the judgments of Thought at their root, the depth of Thought's inception termed mazala, we anticipate in Elul with prayer.
וּלְהַמְתִּיק שָׁם בְּעֹמֶק רֵאשִׁית אֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת אַף לְרֹשֶׁם רָע כְּלָל כַּיָּדוּעַ.
And sweetening there in the depth of inception leaves no room even for an impression of evil, as is known.
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה דְּחֹדֶשׁ אֱלוּל בְּיוֹ"ד, כִּידוּעַ דִּבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּמְנָחוֹת (כט:) עַל פָּסוּק "כִּי בְּיָהּ ה' וְגוֹמֵר": עוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּהֵ"א,
Therefore Sefer Yetzirah states that the month of Elul was created with the letter Yud, reflecting Menachot 29b: this world was created with Hei,
וּלְכָךְ חֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן שֶׁהוּא כְּפִי סוֹף הַבְּרִיאָה וּמַעֲשֵׂה עוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּהֵ"א, וְעוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּיוֹ"ד, וְהָיָה רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת כֵּן תִּשְׁרֵי.
so the month of Nisan which aligns with the physical world is with Hei, while the World to Come is with Yud, and so should Tishrei have been.

אֲבָל יָדוּעַ דְּהַזְּמַנִּים יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא דִּמְקַדְּשֵׁי לְהוּ, וְהֵם קִדְּשׁוּ לֶאֱלוּל בִּקְדוּשָּׁה זוֹ כִּי רָצוּ לְהַמְתִּיק בְּשָׁרְשָׁן, וּלְכָךְ אֱלוּל בְּיוֹ"ד, וְהוּא עַל שֵׁם הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה כַּנּוֹדָע.
But Israel sanctifies the seasons, and they sanctified Elul with this holiness to sweeten at the root; thus Elul is associated with Yud, signifying Thought.
וְל' יוֹם קוֹדֶם הַיְינוּ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה לַחְשׁוֹב זוֹ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה, שֶׁהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה דְּבוּקָה בְּשָׁרְשָׁהּ:
And thirty days prior represents thinking this thought, where thought cleaves to its primordial root.

paragraphs.text: Explanation: Mei HaShiloach describes Yosef's cry intensifying immediately before his deliverance, and explains that Hashem places such a cry in the heart so the gift may become the fruit of the person's own work. This supplies a concrete counterpart to the siman's call to turn an awakening into prayer before the matter fully emerges. The comparison concerns the sequence of awakening and response; it does not replace the siman's distinct explanation of Elul.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 11:1 describes distress as an awakening to prayer, citing the Midrash’s parable of a king desiring to hear a woman’s voice and the patriarchs’ childlessness. The instruction to pray before trouble means awakening that voice oneself before a crisis must do so. Through prayer, worldly concerns are raised toward their divine source. This parallels the siman’s first response to fear before it develops the account of Elul and judgment at the root.

paragraphs.text: Resisei Layla 43:1 distinguishes the soul’s mazal from astrological constellations. The mazal called an advocating angel concerns divine judgment and the soul’s merit, but its root cannot be only an angel produced by completed mitzvot, since even a newborn possesses it. Rav Tzadok traces it to the soul hewn from the Throne of Glory, above the angelic world and inclusive of lower worlds. This explains why the present siman speaks of the person’s root perceiving what has not yet appeared below.

paragraphs.text: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Shofar 5, interprets the Rosh Hashanah phrase about the world’s conception by distinguishing conception in Tishrei from birth in Nisan. The two opinions about creation thus concern different stages. Tishrei is linked with reishit, beginning; Nisan with the miracle needed for emergence, as the Exodus is depicted as birth. The passage qualifies that the Rosh Hashanah formulation concerns the human being, whereas the world’s creation begins on the twenty-fifth of Elul. These distinctions support the siman’s language of thought, gestation, and preparation.

sections.en: Fear as an Awakening to Prayer and Blessing

p: [קע] כְּשֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רוֹצֶה לְהֵיטִיב לָאָדָם וְרוֹצֶה רַק שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל הָאָדָם עַל הַדָּבָר, אָז מַזְמִין לְפָנָיו צַעַר אוֹ פַּחַד מֵעֵין דָּבָר זֶה,
When the Holy One, blessed be He, desires to bestow good upon a person and desires only that the person pray for it, He orchestrates distress or fear akin to that matter,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יְבָמוֹת סד.): מִפְּנֵי מָה הָיוּ אִמָּהוֹת עֲקוּרוֹת וְכוּלֵי.
as our Sages stated (Yevamot 64a): Why were the Matriarchs barren? Because Hashem yearns for their prayers.
אוֹ רוֹאֶה אַחֵר מְעוּנֶּה בְּאוֹתוֹ דָבָר וּמְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עָלָיו כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא נַעֲנֶה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "פַּחַד פָּחַדְתִּי וַיֶּאֱתָיֵנִי]" (אִיּוֹב ג, כה).
Or he witnesses another afflicted in that very matter and pleads for mercy on his behalf so that he himself is answered, as written: "For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me" (Job 3:25).
כִּי כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹצֶה לְהָבִיא לָעוֹלָם אוֹ לָאָדָם, הִיא מִתְפַּשֶּׁטֶת לְכַמָּה גְּוָונִין, וְיֵשׁ בָּהּ הַהֵיפֶךְ גַּם כֵּן חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
For every matter the Blessed Name seeks to bring into the world or unto man extends into various manifestations, containing its opposite as well, Heaven forbid,
כִּדְאָמְרוּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל וְזֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, רטז עַמּוּד ב) בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל שֶׁהָיוּ מְעוּתָּדִים לְקַבֵּל תּוֹרָה אִלּוּ זָכוּ, וְכֵן בְּכָל דּוֹר וּבְכָל אָדָם.
as stated (Shemot Rabbah 30; Zohar III:216b) concerning the Generation of the Flood, that they were destined to receive the Torah had they merited, and so in every generation and within every person.
וּלְכָךְ כְּשֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר מִדָּה זוֹ לְטוֹבָה, מִתְעוֹרֵר גַּם כֵּן הַהֵיפֶךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וּמַרְגִּישׁ פַּחַד וּמִתְפַּלֵּל וּבָא הַטּוֹב.
And therefore, when this attribute awakens toward the good, its opposite is likewise aroused, and he senses fear, prays, and the good arrives.
אֲבָל לְעוֹלָם הוּא בָּא הַדָּבָר שֶׁמִּתְפַּחֵד, רַק שֶׁבָּא הַהֵיפֶךְ, דְּהַיְינוּ כָּל מִינֵי טוֹבָה שֶׁבְּדָבָר זֶה.
Yet in reality the very thing he feared arrives, only that it arrives in its inverted form—namely all manner of goodness within that matter.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סו): צַדִּיקִים תְּחִלָּתָן יִסּוּרִין וְסוֹפָן שַׁלְוָה,
And this is what is written (Bereishit Rabbah 66): the righteous experience afflictions at their outset and tranquility at their end,
פֵּירוּשׁ בְּכָל דָּבָר וְכָל מִדָּה טוֹבָה וְעִנְיָן טוֹב, תְּחִלַּת הַכְּנִיסָה בּוֹ הוּא בְּצַעַר, כְּטַעַם כָּל הַתְחָלוֹת קָשׁוֹת
meaning in every matter, good character trait, and worthy endeavor, the initial entry into it involves distress, because all beginnings are difficult
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (גִּטִּין מג.): אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן וְכוּלֵי],
along the lines of Gittin 43a: a person does not master words of Torah unless he stumbles,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת (ה.): ג' מַתָּנוֹת טוֹבוֹת וְכוּלֵי, וּכִבְרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם: בְּרֵישָׁא וְכוּלֵי (שַׁבָּת עז:).
and as in Berakhot 5a: three precious gifts were given through suffering, and matching creation: first darkness, then light (Shabbat 77b).

לְפִי שֶׁהָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה רוּבּוֹ רַע כַּיָּדוּעַ, וּלְכָךְ כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ, רוֹאֶה הוּא מִקּוֹדֶם כֹּחַ הָרָע שֶׁבּוֹ וּמִצְטַעֵר, וְעַל יְדֵי הַצַּעַר מַמְתִּיקוֹ וּמִיָּד סוֹפוֹ שַׁלְוָה.

Because this world is predominantly coarse and evil, whenever a matter awakens within him, he first perceives the power of evil within it and feels anguish, and through that anguish he sweetens it, and immediately its culmination is tranquility.

וּכְעִנְיַן תְּלָתָא דְּפוּרְעָנוּתָא וְשֶׁבַע דְּנֶחָמָתָא שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, שֶׁהֵם ג' רִאשׁוֹנוֹת וְז' תַּחְתּוֹנוֹת, שֶׁהַהַתְחָלָה חָלוּק לְג' וְהַסּוֹף לְז' כַּיָּדוּעַ.

And this mirrors the three Haftarot of rebuke and seven of consolation instituted by our Sages, corresponding to the three upper and seven lower sefirot, the beginning dividing into three and the end into seven.
וְהַתְחָלַת כָּל פְּעֻלָּה הוּא מִצַּד הֶכְרֵחַ הַפּוֹעֵל שֶׁחָסֵר לְאוֹתָהּ פְּעֻלָּה, אִם כֵּן הַהַתְחָלָה מִצַּד הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁהוּא חָסֵר וְדָחוּק לְכָךְ,
And the start of every action stems from the necessity felt by the actor who lacks that outcome; thus the beginning emerges from deficiency, being pressured toward it,
וּ"מִן הַמֵּצַר קָרָאתִי יָּהּ" (תְּהִלִּים קיח, ה), שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ הַצַּעַר זוֹעֵק לַה', וְעוֹנֵהוּ בַּמֶּרְחָב,
and "Out of the straits I called upon Yah" (Psalms 118:5), where out of distress he cries to Hashem, Who answers him with expansive relief,
שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא נֶחָמָה, דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּתְנַחֵם עַל צַעַר הֶעָבָר, שֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁאֵין צַעַר, כְּעִנְיַן "וְנַסְתֶּם וְאֵין רֹדֵף" (וַיִּקְרָא כו, יז).
which is termed consolation—being comforted over past distress, realizing that in truth there is no distress, in the manner of: "and you shall flee when none pursues you" (Leviticus 26:17).
כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אוֹהֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה, בְּוַדַּאי לֹא קִלְּלָם, רַק בְּכָל קְלָלָה טָמוּן הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ לוֹ רַק עַל יְדֵי הַקְּלָלָה.
For Moses our teacher loved Israel and certainly did not curse them, but within every curse lay hidden the blessing that could not be attained except through that curse.
וּבְקִלְלַת הַנִּיסָה שָׁם הוּא הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁאֵין רוֹדֵף כְּלָל.
And within the curse of fleeing lies the blessing that there is no pursuer at all.
וּכְשֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר הֶאָרָה זוֹ לְהַכִּיר שֶׁאֵין רוֹדֵף כְּלָל, מִתְעוֹרֵר גַּם כֵּן הַהֵיפוּךְ שֶׁהוּא הַנִּיסָה,
And when this illumination awakens to recognize that none pursues, its opposite—the sensation of fleeing—is likewise aroused,
וְעַל יְדֵי הַנִּיסָה מַכִּיר תֵּיכֶף אֲמִיתַּת יִחוּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַד שֶׁאֵין רוֹדֵף כְּלָל.
and through fleeing he instantly perceives the ultimate unity of the Blessed Name, realizing that there is truly no pursuer.
וְכֵן בְּקִלְלַת "וְלֹא תַאֲמִין בְּחַיֶּיךָ" (דְּבָרִים כח, סו), הוֹדִיעֲךָ שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ בְּקַלְקָלָה הֵם קְרוּיִים חַיִּים, וְלֹא כִּרְשָׁעִים שֶׁבְּחַיֵּיהֶם קְרוּיִים מֵתִים.

And likewise with the curse "and you shall have no assurance of your life" (Deuteronomy 28:66), it informs you that even in their fallen state they are called "living," unlike the wicked who in their lifetime are called dead.
אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵם מִגּוֹדֶל הַפַּחַד עַד שֶׁלֹּא יַאֲמִינוּ גַּם בְּכָךְ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם חַיֵּי עוֹלָם בְּהַכִּירָם מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם.
Only that out of the magnitude of fear they do not believe that they possess eternal life when examining their deeds.
וּבְאוֹתוֹ פָּסוּק נִתְגַּלָּה זֶה שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חַיִּים, דְּאֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים קְרוּיִים מֵתִים וְאֵין לָהֶם חַיִּים כְּלָל לְהַאֲמִין בָּהֶם.
And in that very verse it is revealed that all Israel have life, whereas the gentile nations are termed dead and have no true life to believe in.

וּכְשֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר פַּחַד זֶה שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַאֲמִין בְּעַצְמוֹ כְּלָל אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, מִתְעוֹרֵר גַּם כֵּן הַהַבְטָחָה הַבְּרוּרָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְכֵן בְּכָל דָּבָר:

And when this fear awakens wherein he does not believe in himself whether he has a share in the World to Come, there is simultaneously aroused the clear assurance that he does possess a share in the World to Come, and so in every matter.

paragraphs.text: Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 7:1–3, places permitted material things and permitted worldly thought, speech, and action without heavenly intention within kelippat nogah. Even bodily necessities remain at that level when they are not directed toward serving God. Nogah is a mixture, intermediate between the three wholly impure kelippot and holiness; in the World of Action its evil predominates, but its good can be separated, prevail, and rise into holiness. This supplies the kabbalistic setting for the siman’s description without identifying every person or act as wholly evil.

paragraphs.text: Et HaOchel 14:1 reads the Seder as a movement from felt poverty to expansion. Matzah evokes a poor person awaiting heavenly mercy; the Pesach offering’s meat expresses an enlargement of vitality. Likewise, the Exodus account proceeds by question and answer, even when the questioner is wise: a felt lack opens into the expansive answer of Psalm 118:5. This illustrates the siman’s account through a mitzvah’s ordered practice, without identifying the particular benefit that must follow any given distress.

paragraphs.text: Sod Yesharim, The Seventh Day of Pesach 25:4, explains Psalm 118:5 through God’s limitation of His light, which gives Israel a real part in bringing worldly service to completion. It associates the name Yah with hidden worlds and Vav-He with this world and the World to Come. The resulting bond with Israel makes the limitation itself a source of breadth and deliverance. This develops the siman’s account of good concealed within a difficult beginning through the relation that the limitation makes possible.
